definitions.note: Common preposition used for destinations (going to a place) and location (being at a place); also often means “to” before a person (indirect object).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vado a scuola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to school.

definitions.note: Used mainly for dogs.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il cane abbaia quando qualcuno suona il campanello.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog barks when someone rings the doorbell.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund form of "abbaiare"; used for actions in progress (e.g., "sta abbaiando" = "is barking").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il cane sta abbaiando in giardino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is barking in the garden.

definitions.note: Used mainly for dogs.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il cane comincia ad abbaiare quando suona il campanello.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog starts barking when the doorbell rings.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il cane ha abbaiato tutta la notte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog barked all night.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (past continuous/habitual) form of “abbaiare”; often used for an ongoing or repeated action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il cane abbaiava tutta la notte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog was barking all night.

definitions.note: Often used for leaving a person/animal, a place, or giving up a project or plan.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non voglio abbandonare questo progetto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to abandon this project.

definitions.native: to abandon me, to leave me
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non puoi abbandonarmi proprio adesso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can’t abandon me right now.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "abbandonare"; often used with "essere" in passive forms.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La casa è stata abbandonata da anni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The house has been abandoned for years.

definitions.note: Present tense, 2nd person plural (voi).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Perché abbandonate il progetto proprio adesso?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you all abandoning the project right now?

definitions.note: Feminine plural past participle/adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le case abbandonate sono pericolose.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The abandoned houses are dangerous.

definitions.note: Past participle of "abbandonare"; often used like an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hanno trovato un cane abbandonato per strada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They found an abandoned dog on the street.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La casa è abbandonata da anni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The house has been abandoned for years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il giardino è abbandonato e pieno di erbacce.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The garden is neglected and full of weeds.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), third person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo l’incidente, abbandonò l’auto e scappò.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the accident, he abandoned the car and ran away.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular ("he/she/it"), used for actions like lowering something or turning the volume down.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbassa il volume, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Turn down the volume, please.

definitions.note: Present gerund ("-ing" form), often used with "stare" to mean "am/is/are ...-ing".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto abbassando il volume della musica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m turning down the volume of the music.

definitions.note: Used for reducing height/level or making something quieter (e.g., volume).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi abbassare il volume, per favore?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you turn down the volume, please?

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto) of "abbassare"; often used in narratives or in southern Italy.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbassarono la musica perché era troppo alta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They lowered the music because it was too loud.

definitions.note: Plural informal command form (voi).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbassate la voce, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Lower your voices, please.

definitions.note: Feminine plural past participle form, often used like an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le persiane sono abbassate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The shutters are lowered.

definitions.note: Past participle of "abbassare"; often used like an adjective (e.g., "volume abbassato").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho abbassato il volume della musica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I turned down the volume of the music.

definitions.note: “tu” form (2nd person singular), used for the informal “you”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se abbassi la musica, riesco a concentrarmi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you turn down the music, I can concentrate.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) form; often used in narratives and in written Italian.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbassò la voce quando entrò il professore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lowered his voice when the professor came in.

definitions.note: Often used before adjectives/adverbs to mean “quite” (e.g., abbastanza grande = quite big), or after verbs to mean “enough” (e.g., ho mangiato abbastanza = I ate enough).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho studiato abbastanza per l’esame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I studied enough for the exam.

definitions.note: Often used before a noun (like a determiner) or after a verb/adjective to mean “enough.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho abbastanza soldi per il biglietto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have enough money for the ticket.

definitions.note: Common with adjectives/adverbs to mean “quite/fairly” (not necessarily “very”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La casa è abbastanza grande.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The house is quite big.

definitions.note: past participle (masculine plural) of "abbattere"; often used with "essere" in passive forms
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gli alberi sono stati abbattuti dopo la tempesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The trees were felled after the storm.

definitions.note: Past participle of "abbattere"; often used for buildings or trees.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hanno abbattuto il vecchio muro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They knocked down the old wall.

definitions.note: Past participle of "abbattere" used figuratively to describe someone’s mood.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo la notizia, mi sono sentito abbattuto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the news, I felt down.

definitions.note: Used with "tu" as either (1) present subjunctive (after expressions like "spero che...") or (2) the affirmative imperative.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che tu abbi tempo domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you have time tomorrow.

definitions.note: present subjunctive form of "avere"; often used after expressions like "spero che...", "penso che..."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che tu abbia finito il lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you have finished the work.

definitions.note: Used in the present subjunctive (often after "che") to express uncertainty, wishes, or opinions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che lui abbia tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope he has time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo finito il lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have finished the work.

definitions.note: Present tense (noi) of "avere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo due cani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have two dogs.

definitions.note: Used with che in the present subjunctive (e.g., after verbs like 'spero che', 'penso che').
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che abbiano finito il lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope they have finished the work.

definitions.note: Used with "che" to form the present subjunctive (e.g., "che loro abbiano" = "that they have").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che abbiano abbastanza tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope they have enough time.

definitions.note: Used with “voi” (you plural / formal you) as the auxiliary of avere.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che abbiate capito tutto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you have understood everything.

definitions.note: Form used with voi (you plural). It can be the present subjunctive or the imperative of "avere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiate pazienza, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Have patience, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In inverno serve abbigliamento caldo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In winter you need warm clothing.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Marco abbina la camicia blu con i jeans.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Marco matches the blue shirt with the jeans.

definitions.note: Often used to say that something exists in large quantities in a place or situation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In questa zona abbonda l’acqua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this area, water is plentiful.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In estate abbondano i turisti in questa città.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In summer, tourists abound in this city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei abbraccia sua sorella.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She hugs her sister.

definitions.note: Imperative (command) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbraccia tua madre!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hug your mother!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Camminavano abbracciando i bambini dopo la scuola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were walking while hugging the children after school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio abbracciare mia nonna.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to hug my grandma.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “-la” = “her” (also “it” for feminine nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio abbracciarla prima di partire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to hug her before leaving.

definitions.note: simple past (passato remoto), 3rd person plural: “they hugged”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando si rividero, si abbracciarono forte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When they saw each other again, they hugged tightly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ogni volta che ci vedete, ci abbracciate forte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every time you see us, you hug us tightly.

definitions.note: Plural informal command (to more than one person).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ragazzi, abbracciate la nonna!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Kids, hug grandma!

definitions.note: Feminine plural past participle.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le bambine sono state abbracciate dalla mamma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The girls were hugged by their mom.

definitions.note: Often used as a past participle/adjective to describe people who are hugging.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Li ho visti abbracciati davanti alla stazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw them hugging in front of the station.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho abbracciato mia madre dopo il viaggio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hugged my mother after the trip.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti abbraccio forte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hug you tightly.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto); common in stories and in some regions, especially in the South.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei lo abbracciò forte e poi andò via.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She hugged him tightly and then left.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Marta è molto abile a cucinare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Marta is very skilled at cooking.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha molta abilità nel parlare in pubblico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has a lot of skill in public speaking.

definitions.note: third-person singular present (he/she/it lives)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Giulia abita a Roma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Giulia lives in Rome.

definitions.note: Gerund form; often used with "stare" to mean "to be living" / "to be residing."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto abitando a Milano da due mesi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve been living in Milan for two months.

definitions.note: 3rd person plural present tense of "abitare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abitano a Milano da tre anni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They live in Milan and have for three years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gli abitanti di questo paese sono molto gentili.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The inhabitants of this town are very kind.

definitions.note: Used for where someone lives (their place of residence).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abito a Roma da tre anni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I live in Rome and have for three years.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive of "abitare" (used after certain verbs/expressions, often in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pensavo che abitasse a Roma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thought he lived in Rome.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (voi) present tense of "abitare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abitate in centro o in periferia?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you live downtown or in the suburbs?

definitions.note: Past participle of "abitare"; often used with "avere" to form the past tense (e.g., "ho abitato" = "I lived").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho abitato a Milano per due anni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I lived in Milan for two years.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (used for ongoing actions or habitual situations in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da bambino abitava vicino al mare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As a child, he lived near the sea.

definitions.native: lived, used to live, were living
definitions.note: Imperfect past: describes an ongoing situation or habit in the past (often “we used to live”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando eravamo studenti, abitavamo vicino all’università.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When we were students, we lived near the university.

definitions.native: lived, used to live, was living
definitions.note: imperfect past (ongoing or habitual action in the past)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando ero studente, abitavo vicino all’università.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a student, I lived near the university.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dove abiti?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Where do you live?

definitions.note: Plural of "abito"; commonly refers to items of clothing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato degli abiti nuovi per l’inverno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought some new clothes for the winter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abitiamo a Milano da due anni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have lived in Milan for two years.

definitions.note: Not the English word “habit”. (In Italian, “abito” can also be a noun meaning “dress/suit”, but here it’s the verb form.)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abito a Roma da due anni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I live in Rome and have for two years.

definitions.note: Commonly refers to a piece of clothing (e.g., a suit or a formal outfit); for “habit” in Italian, use “abitudine.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per la cerimonia indosso un abito elegante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For the ceremony I’m wearing an elegant suit.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle; often used with “essere” to mean “to be used to.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono abituata a svegliarmi presto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m used to waking up early.

definitions.note: feminine singular (said about a female person or a feminine noun)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono abituata a svegliarmi presto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m used to waking up early.

definitions.note: plural form (e.g., “we/they are used to…”, “the boys/men are used to…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo abituati al freddo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are used to the cold.

definitions.note: Often used with “essere” (e.g., “sono abituato”) and/or with “a” + infinitive/noun (e.g., “abituato a...”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono abituato a svegliarmi presto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m used to waking up early.

definitions.note: Often followed by “a” + infinitive or “a” + noun/pronoun (e.g., “abituato a lavorare”, “abituato al caldo”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono abituato al freddo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m used to the cold.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fare colazione presto è una mia abitudine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Having breakfast early is a habit of mine.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le mie abitudini sono cambiate dopo il trasloco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My habits changed after the move.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Un cane abusato ha bisogno di cure e pazienza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: An abused dog needs care and patience.

definitions.note: Often used for ideas, phrases, or objects used too much.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un argomento abusato: ne parlano tutti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s an overused topic: everyone talks about it.

definitions.note: Used after expressions that trigger the subjunctive (e.g., "spero che...", "è possibile che...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che accada presto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope it happens soon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non so cosa accade qui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t know what’s happening here.

definitions.note: Used like English “happening/occurring” to describe something in progress.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Che cosa sta accadendo qui?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What’s happening here?

definitions.note: Often used for events/situations (similar to “succedere”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Che cosa è accaduto?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What happened?

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive (used after expressions like “it was possible that…”, “it was necessary that…”, “I hoped that…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Speravo che non accadesse nulla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hoped that nothing happened.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A volte accadono cose strane.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sometimes strange things happen.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non so cosa accadrà domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't know what will happen tomorrow.

definitions.note: Past participle of "accadere"; often used with "essere" to form past tenses (e.g., "è accaduto" = "it happened/has happened").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È già accaduto una volta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It has already happened once.

definitions.note: Often used with "a" + noun/pronoun: "accanto a".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siedo accanto a te.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sit next to you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siediti accanto a me.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sit next to me.

definitions.note: Often used with “a” (accedere a un sito/servizio) or with “con” for credentials (accedere con una password).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per accedere al tuo account, inserisci la password.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: To access your account, enter the password.

definitions.note: Used for the (present) subjunctive (e.g., after verbs like “spero che…”) or as a formal imperative (Lei).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che accenda la luce.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you turn on the light.

definitions.note: Often used for turning on lights, devices, or lighting a fire/cigarette.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi accendere la luce, per favore?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you turn on the light, please?

definitions.note: Second-person plural ("you" plural) form; used for addressing more than one person or as polite "you" (voi).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Accendete la luce, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Turn on the light, please.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) present indicative; also used as an informal command (“turn on!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Accendi la luce, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Turn on the light, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hai un accendino?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have a lighter?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho accennato al problema, ma non ho spiegato tutto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hinted at the problem, but I didn’t explain everything.

definitions.note: Also used to mean an accent in someone’s speech (e.g., a regional or foreign accent).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nella parola “perché” c’è un accento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the word “perché” there is an accent mark.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form; used for things like lights, TVs, engines, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La luce è accesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The light is on.

definitions.note: Often used for arguments, debates, or emotions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La discussione è accesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The discussion is heated.

definitions.note: Often used as the feminine plural past participle (e.g., with “essere”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le luci sono accese.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lights are on.

definitions.note: Can also be the passato remoto (historic past), third person singular of “accendere”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Accese la luce e uscì.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She turned on the light and left.

definitions.note: Passato remoto (remote past) of "accendere" (1st person singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Accesi la luce e aprii la finestra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I turned on the light and opened the window.

definitions.note: Past participle of "accendere" used as an adjective (plural masculine; also used for mixed-gender plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho lasciato i fari accesi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I left the headlights on.

definitions.note: past participle of "accendere" (often used with "avere")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho acceso la luce.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I turned on the light.

definitions.note: Often used for lights or devices: "la luce è accesa" (fem.), "il computer è acceso" (masc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il computer è acceso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The computer is on.

definitions.native: bright, intense (of colors, feelings, or tone)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha un colore acceso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It has a bright color.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per accedere al sito serve un accesso autorizzato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: To access the site you need authorized access.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi servono accessori per il telefono.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need accessories for the phone.

definitions.note: Often used for car or appliance parts in everyday Italian.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il meccanico ha ordinato gli accessori per l’auto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mechanic ordered the spare parts for the car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui accetta la proposta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He accepts the proposal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il prezzo è accettabile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The price is acceptable.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 1st person singular of “accettare”; common in written narratives, less in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Accettai l’offerta senza pensarci troppo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I accepted the offer without thinking too much about it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho deciso di accettare la tua proposta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I decided to accept your proposal.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “lo” (= “it” or “him”) attached to the verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devi accettarlo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to accept it.

definitions.note: simple past (passato remoto), 3rd person plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Accettarono l’offerta senza esitazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They accepted the offer without hesitation.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "accettare"; often agrees with a feminine noun like "proposta" (proposal) or "richiesta" (request)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La tua richiesta è stata accettata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your request has been accepted.

definitions.note: Often used for “you (plural) accept” (present) or “accept!” (command to a group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Accettate la carta di credito?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you accept credit cards?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I documenti sono stati accettati.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The documents have been accepted.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho accettato la tua proposta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I accepted your proposal.

definitions.note: Conditional mood (used for polite requests or hypothetical situations).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you accept credit cards?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Accettiamo la tua proposta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We accept your proposal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Accetto la tua proposta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I accept your proposal.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto) form, often used in written narratives (and in everyday speech mainly in some regions).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end, he/she accepted the proposal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo coltello è fatto di acciaio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This knife is made of steel.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho cancellato il file accidentalmente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I deleted the file accidentally.

definitions.note: An exclamation of annoyance or frustration; relatively mild, but still informal.

definitions.note: plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per la pizza, preferisco le acciughe.

definitions.note: Often used for places (a home, a restaurant, a hotel) or an atmosphere; can also describe a person’s manner.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This restaurant is very welcoming.

definitions.note: Past historic/simple past form (passato remoto) of "accogliere", used often in narratives and in some regions for past events.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The director welcomed the visitors at the entrance.

definitions.note: Past participle of "accogliere"; often used with "essere" in passive forms (e.g., "è stato accolto").

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His advice was welcomed with enthusiasm.

definitions.native: have a seat, make yourselves comfortable

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of "accompagnare".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He accompanies his sister to school every morning.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "accompagnare"; agrees with a feminine singular subject/object
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Maria è stata accompagnata a casa da suo fratello.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Maria was accompanied home by her brother.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho accompagnato mia sorella a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I accompanied my sister home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti accompagno alla stazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll accompany you to the station.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person singular: “he/she/it accompanied”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Marco accompagnò sua sorella a casa dopo la festa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Marco accompanied his sister home after the party.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 1st person singular: “I agreed.” Common in writing and narratives.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alla fine acconsentii alla proposta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end I agreed to the proposal.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), used mainly in written Italian and in some regions for past events.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alla fine acconsentimmo a cambiare il programma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end we agreed to change the plan.

definitions.note: Often used with “a” + infinitive (e.g., “acconsentire a fare qualcosa”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha acconsentito a firmare il contratto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He agreed to sign the contract.

definitions.note: Future tense (he/she/it). Often used with “a” + infinitive (e.g., “acconsentire a fare qualcosa”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alla fine acconsentirà a incontrarci domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end, he/she will agree to meet us tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho acconsentito alla proposta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I agreed to the proposal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alla fine acconsentì a venire con noi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end, he/she agreed to come with us.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively as “accontentarsi (di)” = “to be satisfied (with), to make do (with)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cerco di accontentare tutti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I try to satisfy everyone.

definitions.note: Often used for musical instruments (e.g., a guitar).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho accordato la chitarra prima del concerto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I tuned the guitar before the concert.

definitions.note: Used in formal contexts meaning to grant or allow something (e.g., permission, a request).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They granted me a special permit.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo raggiunto un accordo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We reached an agreement.

definitions.note: future tense, 3rd person singular (he/she/it/you formal)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si accorgerà subito dell’errore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She will notice the mistake right away.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto), often used in stories and writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si accorse di aver dimenticato le chiavi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She realized they had forgotten the keys.

definitions.note: Past participle (feminine singular) of the reflexive verb "accorgersi"; often used with "essere" (e.g., "si è accorta").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si è accorta dell’errore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She noticed the mistake.

definitions.note: masculine plural past participle of "accorgersi/accorgere"; used with "essere" in compound tenses
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci siamo accorti dell'errore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We noticed the mistake.

definitions.note: Past participle of "accorgersi/accorgere"; often used with "essere" (e.g., "mi sono accorto").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi sono accorto dell’errore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I noticed the mistake.

definitions.note: Common loanword; often used for online accounts (email, social media, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho creato un account nuovo per il sito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I created a new account for the website.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto), 3rd person singular: “he/she/it accumulated.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Durante l’inverno, accumulò molta legna per il camino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: During the winter, he accumulated a lot of firewood for the fireplace.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sta accusando Marco di aver mentito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is accusing Marco of having lied.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of "accusare"; used with a feminine subject or as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei è stata accusata di furto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was accused of theft.

definitions.note: Past participle of "accusare"; often used like an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’uomo è stato accusato di furto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The man was accused of theft.

definitions.note: plural form of "accusa"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui nega tutte le accuse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He denies all the accusations.

definitions.note: simple past (passato remoto) of "accusare"; common in writing and storytelling
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo accusò di aver mentito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She accused him of having lied.

definitions.note: Often used for the taste of foods and drinks (e.g., wine, lemon).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo vino è troppo acido per me.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This wine is too acidic for me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei un bicchiere d’acqua, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like a glass of water, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio acquistare un nuovo telefono.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to buy a new phone.

definitions.note: Past participle of "acquistare"; used with "avere" to form past tenses (e.g., "ho acquistato").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho acquistato un biglietto online.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a ticket online.

definitions.note: Plural of "acquisto".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho fatto alcuni acquisti online ieri sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I made some purchases online last night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo acquisto è stato un ottimo affare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This purchase was a great deal.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), used mainly in writing and in some regions to talk about completed actions in the distant past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri acquistò un libro in libreria.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday he/she bought a book at the bookstore.

definitions.note: Often used for sounds (a “high-pitched” sound) or pain (a “sharp” pain).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha un dolore acuto al petto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has a sharp pain in his chest.

definitions.note: Used especially for sounds and musical notes.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho sentito un fischio acuto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I heard a high-pitched whistle.

definitions.note: Used in medical contexts (e.g., acute illness).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un'infezione acuta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s an acute infection.

definitions.note: Form of "a" used before vowels (and often before an infinitive), meaning "to/at."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho imparato ad andare in bicicletta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I learned to ride a bike.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of "adatto"; often used with "a" to mean "suitable for".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa soluzione è adatta a noi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This solution is suitable for us.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dobbiamo adattare il progetto alle nuove regole.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to adapt the project to the new rules.

definitions.note: Reflexive: it means “to adapt oneself / to get used to” a new situation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi devo adattare al nuovo lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to adapt to the new job.

definitions.note: past participle of "adattare"; often used with "essere" or "avere" depending on the verb’s use
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho adattato il testo per i bambini.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I adapted the text for children.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo libro è adatto ai bambini.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book is suitable for children.

definitions.note: Used for training people or animals (e.g., a dog), or coaching someone in a skill.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'istruttrice addestra il cane ogni giorno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The instructor trains the dog every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I cani sono addestrati.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dogs are trained.

definitions.note: Often used in an impersonal way with an indirect object: “mi/ti/gli/le/ci/vi/gli addice” = “it suits/be fits me/you/him/her/us/you/them”.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This behavior doesn't suit you.

definitions.note: Often sounds more final than "ciao" (like a permanent goodbye).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Goodbye, friends!

definitions.note: Often a final or emotional goodbye; can also mean “farewell” as in leaving for good.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È difficile dirti addio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s hard to say goodbye to you.

definitions.native: put (someone) to sleep, lulled to sleep
definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto), typically used in storytelling or in some regions in speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Addormentai il bambino con una ninna nanna.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the baby to sleep with a lullaby.

definitions.note: Often used with a reflexive pronoun (mi/ti/si), as in “mi sto addormentando”.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm falling asleep on the couch.

definitions.note: Reflexive infinitive with "mi" (= myself). Often used with modal verbs like "devo", "posso", "voglio".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to fall asleep early tonight.

definitions.native: to fall asleep, to go to sleep

definitions.note: Feminine singular form; often used like an adjective with essere (e.g., è addormentata = is asleep).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La bambina è addormentata sul divano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The little girl is asleep on the couch.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La bambina è addormentata sul divano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The little girl is asleep on the couch.

definitions.note: addressed to more than one person (plural “you”)

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The girls are already asleep.

definitions.note: Masculine plural past participle, often used with "essere" (e.g., "sono addormentati").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I bambini sono già addormentati.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are already asleep.

definitions.note: Informal singular command ("tu") with reflexive "ti".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s late: fall asleep right away.

definitions.note: plural masculine (also used for mixed groups)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I bambini sono già addormentati.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are already asleep.

definitions.note: Past participle often used like an adjective (e.g., “He is asleep”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il bambino è addormentato sul divano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The child is asleep on the couch.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il bambino è addormentato sul divano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The child is asleep on the sofa.

definitions.native: on (me/you/him, etc.), on top of (me/you/him, etc.)

definitions.note: Can refer to a boy or a girl; the form is the same for masculine and feminine.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is a teenager.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei adora il gelato al cioccolato.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kids love ice cream.

definitions.note: Plural of "aereo".

definitions.note: Often used with places/views (e.g., a window, balcony, or room) + “su” (onto/over).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The window overlooks the sea.

definitions.note: feminine singular form

definitions.note: Often used for a commercial deal or transaction; also used broadly for “business” in general.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I have a lot of business to take care of.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a fascinating city.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These stories are really fascinating.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono affascinata dalla storia di questa città.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m fascinated by the history of this city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono affascinato dalla storia di Roma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m fascinated by the history of Rome.

definitions.note: Most often used with negation (e.g., “non ... affatto”) meaning “not at all.”

definitions.note: Often implies grabbing quickly/firmly, sometimes with effort.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho afferrato la valigia e sono uscito.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto), 3rd person singular: “(he/she/it) grabbed/seized.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando vide il bambino cadere, afferrò la sua mano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he saw the child fall, he grabbed his hand.

definitions.note: Past participle of "affettare"; often used with "avere" in compound tenses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho affettato il pane.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sliced the bread.

definitions.note: Often used for warmth or fondness toward someone (not necessarily romantic).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti voglio bene e ti dimostro il mio affetto ogni giorno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I care about you and I show you my affection every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il cuoco affettò il prosciutto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The chef sliced the ham.

definitions.note: Often used with feelings or attitudes (e.g., affettare indifferenza).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Affettò indifferenza, ma era preoccupato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He feigned indifference, but he was worried.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Marco è un collega affidabile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Marco is a reliable colleague.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Queste informazioni non sono affidabili.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This information is not reliable.

definitions.note: Often used as third-person singular present (e.g., “he/she sharpens”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Marco affila il coltello prima di cucinare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Marco sharpens the knife before cooking.

definitions.note: Can also be used as an informal singular command (tu imperative): “Sharpen!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Affila la matita, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sharpen the pencil, please.

definitions.note: gerund of “affilare”; often used with “stare” to mean “to be sharpening.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto affilando il coltello.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m sharpening the knife.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La lama è affilata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The blade is sharp.

definitions.note: Plural form (masculine plural or mixed group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Attento: questi coltelli sono molto affilati.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Careful: these knives are very sharp.

definitions.note: past participle of "affilare" (to sharpen)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho affilato il coltello.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sharpened the knife.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo coltello è molto affilato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This knife is very sharp.

definitions.note: Often used for renting out something you own (e.g., an apartment). For renting from someone, Italians also commonly use “prendere in affitto”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo deciso di affittare il nostro appartamento per l’estate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We decided to rent out our apartment for the summer.

definitions.note: Used for the money you pay to rent a place; for the act of renting, learners will often see "affitto" in phrases like "in affitto" (for rent) or "dare/prendere in affitto" (to rent out/to rent).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pago l’affitto il primo del mese.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I pay the rent on the first of the month.

definitions.note: Often used to describe someone who feels very sad or troubled.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Era afflitto dopo la notizia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was distressed after the news.

definitions.note: Past participle of "affogare". (Not to be confused with "affogato" as a dessert/coffee in English.)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il gatto è affogato nel fiume.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat drowned in the river.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La spiaggia era affollata nel pomeriggio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The beach was crowded in the afternoon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il treno è affollato questa mattina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train is crowded this morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La barca affonda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boat is sinking.

definitions.note: Often used for boats/ships or objects going down in water; can also be used figuratively (e.g., sinking into something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La barca ha iniziato ad affondare durante la tempesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boat started to sink during the storm.

definitions.note: present gerund ("while"/"by" doing something) of "affrettare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto affrettando il passo perché è tardi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m hurrying my pace because it’s late.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/it) present of "affrontare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei affronta il problema con calma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She faces the problem calmly.

definitions.note: Often used for facing a problem, situation, or challenge. It looks like English “affronting,” but in Italian it usually does not mean “insulting.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto affrontando un problema difficile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am facing a difficult problem.

definitions.note: Often used for facing a problem, situation, or challenge.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dobbiamo affrontare questo problema insieme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to face this problem together.

definitions.note: Past participle of "affrontare"; often used with "avere" (e.g., "ho affrontato...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho affrontato il problema subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I faced the problem right away.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le spezie africane sono molto profumate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: African spices are very fragrant.

definitions.note: Commonly used for a personal planner/calendar (not for meeting notes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho dimenticato l’agenda a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I forgot my planner at home.

definitions.note: Often used for someone who represents others professionally (e.g., a real estate agent, travel agent, talent agent).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'agente immobiliare ci mostra un appartamento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The real estate agent is showing us an apartment.

definitions.note: Common in the phrase "agente di polizia".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Un agente ferma le macchine al semaforo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A police officer stops the cars at the traffic light.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il sistema aggiorna l'app automaticamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The system updates the app automatically.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono aggiornamenti sul progetto?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are there any updates on the project?

definitions.note: Often used for software/app updates, and also for a progress/status update (e.g., a work update).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho installato l’ultimo aggiornamento sul telefono.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I installed the latest update on my phone.

definitions.note: Often used for updating software, information, or bringing someone up to date.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo aggiornare il computer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to update the computer.

definitions.native: bring up to date, give an update
definitions.note: Commonly used with people: "aggiornare qualcuno" = to update someone (on a situation).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti aggiorno domani sulla situazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll update you tomorrow on the situation.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho aggiornato l’app sul telefono.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I updated the app on my phone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il sito è aggiornato ogni settimana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The website is updated every week.

definitions.note: Used as a formal command (Lei) and also as the present subjunctive (“that he/she/you add”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aggiunga un po' di sale, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Add a little salt, please.

definitions.note: third-person singular (he/she/it adds) of "aggiungere"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aggiunge un po' di sale alla zuppa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She adds a little salt to the soup.

definitions.note: often used when adding extra information or details
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nel messaggio aggiunge che arriverà tardi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the message, he/she adds that he/she will arrive late.

definitions.note: present gerund of "aggiungere"; often used like "by adding" or "while adding"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto preparando la salsa aggiungendo un po' di sale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm preparing the sauce by adding a little salt.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi aggiungere un po' di sale?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you add a little salt?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei aggiungere un dettaglio importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to include an important detail.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (voi) form, used for commands or present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aggiungrete un po’ di sale, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Add a little salt, please.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) present tense; also used for informal commands (“add!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aggiungi un po’ di sale, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Add a little salt, please.

definitions.note: third-person plural present tense (they add)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alla fine, aggiungono un po' di sale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end, they add a little salt.

definitions.note: simple past (passato remoto), 3rd person singular
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Finì la lettera e aggiunse un post scriptum.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He finished the letter and added a postscript.

definitions.note: past historic (passato remoto), 1st person singular
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alla fine aggiunsi un dettaglio importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end, I added an important detail.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "aggiungere"; agrees with a feminine noun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho ordinato un’insalata con una salsa aggiunta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ordered a salad with an added sauce.

definitions.note: Past participle of "aggiungere"; commonly used with auxiliary verbs (e.g., "ho aggiunto").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho aggiunto lo zucchero al caffè.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I added sugar to the coffee.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È stato aggredito fuori dal supermercato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was attacked outside the supermarket.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La pubblicità è troppo aggressiva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The advertisement is too aggressive.

definitions.note: plural masculine form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quei cani sono aggressivi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those dogs are aggressive.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il cane è aggressivo con gli estranei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is aggressive with strangers.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mia sorella è molto agile e corre veloce.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is very agile and runs fast.

definitions.note: Often used in set phrases like “a proprio agio” (= at ease).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi sento a mio agio con i tuoi amici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel at ease with your friends.

definitions.note: Often used for “act” in the sense of taking action or behaving in a certain way.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dobbiamo agire subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We must act right away.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (lui/lei) present tense of "agire".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando vede un problema, agisce subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he sees a problem, he acts right away.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Agisci subito, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Act right away, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Era molto agitato prima dell’esame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was very anxious before the exam.

definitions.note: Often used for the sea/weather (e.g., “mare agitato”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi il mare è agitato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today the sea is rough.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho agito subito per aiutarti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I acted right away to help you.

definitions.note: Contraction of “a” + “gli”; used before masculine plural nouns (or a masculine singular noun starting with a vowel) that take “gli” as the definite article.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Parlo agli studenti dopo la lezione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I speak to the students after the lesson.

definitions.note: Contraction of “a + gli”; used before masculine plural nouns (or plural forms like “gli amici”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scrivo una lettera agli amici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m writing a letter to my friends.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In questa ricetta ci vuole un po' di aglio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This recipe needs a bit of garlic.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per Pasqua mangiamo l’agnello.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For Easter we eat lamb.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ad agosto andiamo al mare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In August we go to the sea.

definitions.note: Used to show realization, understanding, surprise, relief, or to react emotionally; meaning depends on context and intonation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ah, ora capisco!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ah, now I understand!

definitions.note: Used to express regret or disappointment (often slightly dramatic or literary).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ahimè, oggi non posso venire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Alas, I can't come today.

definitions.note: Contraction of "a" + "i" (plural masculine "the").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vado ai negozi dopo pranzo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to the shops after lunch.

definitions.note: Articulated preposition: a + i (used before masculine plural nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vado ai giardini con Marco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to the gardens with Marco.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Marco aiuta sua sorella con i compiti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Marco helps his sister with her homework.

definitions.note: Used as an informal imperative (“help!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aiuta! Non riesco ad aprire la porta!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Help! I can’t open the door!

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto), 1st person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando eri in difficoltà, ti aiutai subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When you were in trouble, I helped you right away.

definitions.note: Often used as an informal command ("Help him/it!"); "-lo" refers to a masculine singular person or thing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aiutalo a portare queste borse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Help him carry these bags.

definitions.note: Informal command (imperative) with the object pronoun “mi” attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aiutami a portare queste borse, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Help me carry these bags, please.

definitions.note: Gerund: often means “while helping” or “by helping,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto aiutando mia sorella con i compiti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m helping my sister with her homework.

definitions.note: third-person plural present tense (they help)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi aiutano sempre con i compiti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They always help me with my homework.

definitions.note: "-ci" is an object pronoun meaning "us"; in some contexts it can also mean "each other" or "ourselves".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi aiutarci con i compiti?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you help us with our homework?

definitions.note: Infinitive + direct object pronoun "ci" (us). Often used after another verb (e.g., "puoi", "vuoi", "devi").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi aiutarci con i compiti?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you help us with the homework?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi aiutare tua sorella con i compiti?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you help your sister with her homework?

definitions.note: includes the direct object pronoun “la” (= her; also “it” for a feminine noun) attached to the verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Posso aiutarla con i compiti?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can I help her with her homework?

definitions.note: Infinitive + attached direct-object pronoun “la” (meaning “her” or “it” depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio aiutarla domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to help her tomorrow.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “-le” (= them, feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio aiutarle a finire i compiti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to help them finish their homework.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “li” (= “them”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Posso aiutarli con i compiti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can help them with their homework.

definitions.note: Infinitive + attached direct object pronoun “li” (“them”, usually masculine plural or mixed group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio aiutarli con i compiti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to help them with their homework.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “lo” (“him”); it attaches to the infinitive “aiutare”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo aiutarlo con i compiti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to help him with his homework.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “lo” attached to the verb (meaning “him” or “it”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo aiutarlo con i compiti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to help him with his homework.

definitions.note: Object pronoun -mi is attached to the verb (common with infinitives/imperatives).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi aiutarmi, per favore?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you help me, please?

definitions.note: Infinitive with the attached pronoun “mi” (= me).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi aiutarmi con i compiti?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you help me with my homework?

definitions.note: This form includes the pronoun "ti" (= you, informal singular) attached to the verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Posso aiutarti con i compiti?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can I help you with your homework?

definitions.note: Object pronoun “vi” means “you” (plural or formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Posso aiutarvi con i bagagli?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can I help you with the bags?

definitions.note: Used in the imperfect subjunctive (congiuntivo imperfetto), often after "che" to express wishes, doubts, or hopes in the past (e.g., "I hoped he would help").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Speravo che mi aiutasse con i compiti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hoped he would help me with my homework.

definitions.note: Imperfetto congiuntivo, 1st person singular; used after expressions of doubt, desire, necessity, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Volevo che ti aiutassi con i compiti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wanted to help you with your homework.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "aiutare"; often used with "essere" in passive forms.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono stata aiutata da un'amica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was helped by a friend.

definitions.note: second-person plural (you all) form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ragazzi, aiutate la mamma con la spesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Guys, help Mom with the groceries.

definitions.note: Imperative (plural) + "ci" (us).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per favore, aiutateci a trovare la stazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please help us find the station.

definitions.note: Imperative with the attached direct object pronoun “lo” (= him/it).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aiutatelo, per favore!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Help him, please!

definitions.note: Plural/imperative form used to address more than one person (or as a polite/formal 'you'); includes the attached pronoun "me".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aiutatemi, per favore!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Help me, please!

definitions.note: Imperative with the pronoun “ti” attached (used to tell one person to help themselves).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dai, aiutati e finisci i compiti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come on, help yourself and finish your homework.

definitions.note: Past participle (masculine plural), used for a group of males or a mixed group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I turisti sono stati aiutati dalla guida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tourists were helped by the guide.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hai aiutato molto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You helped me a lot.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (past) form: describes an ongoing/repeated action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi aiutava sempre con i compiti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She always helped me with my homework.

definitions.note: second person singular (tu), future tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi aiuterai con i compiti?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Will you help me with my homework?

definitions.note: third-person plural (they) in the future tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani ti aiuteranno con i compiti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow they will help you with your homework.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti aiuterebbe volentieri, ma oggi non può.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She would gladly help you, but today he/she can’t.

definitions.note: First-person singular conditional (io).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se avessi tempo, ti aiuterei volentieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I had time, I would gladly help you.

definitions.note: Conditional mood, 2nd person plural (voi).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se aveste tempo, aiutereste i vostri amici?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you had time, would you help your friends?

definitions.note: Second person singular conditional (used for polite requests or hypothetical situations).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi aiuteresti con i compiti?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Would you help me with my homework?

definitions.note: Second person plural (voi), future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani aiuterete i vostri amici con il trasloco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow you will help your friends with the move.

definitions.note: third-person singular (he/she/it/you formal) future tense of "aiutare"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti aiuterà domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She will help you tomorrow.

definitions.note: first-person singular (io), future tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani ti aiuterò con i compiti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will help you with your homework.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tu) of "aiutare"; often used after expressions like "penso che" / "spero che".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che mi aiuti con i compiti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you help me with my homework.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (lui/lei) of "aiutare"; also used as a formal command (Lei).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È importante che lui ti aiuti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that he helps you.

definitions.note: Present tense, 1st person plural (noi).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aiutiamo i nostri amici con i compiti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We help our friends with their homework.

definitions.note: Form used with the subjunctive (voi), often after expressions like “spero che…”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che voi aiutiate i vostri amici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you help your friends.

definitions.note: Diminutive of "aiuto"; often used to mean a small, informal help (sometimes a slight “nudge”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi dai un aiutino con i compiti?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you give me a little help with my homework?

definitions.note: Verb form: present tense (io) of "aiutare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti aiuto con i compiti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I help you with your homework.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho bisogno di aiuto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need help.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person singular: “he/she/it helped.” Common in writing and storytelling; in everyday speech many people use passato prossimo instead.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando ero piccolo, mio nonno mi aiutò con i compiti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was little, my grandpa helped me with my homework.

definitions.note: Contraction of “a” + “il”; used with masculine singular nouns.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Love life!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono amati da tutti.

definitions.note: past participle of "amare" (used with "avere" to form compound tenses)

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui è un amato insegnante.

definitions.note: Often used for the feel or vibe of a place (e.g., a restaurant, a party).

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La sua ambizione è diventare medico.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s an ambitious project.

definitions.note: Conditional mood (io).

definitions.note: feminine singular form (used with feminine nouns or to refer to a woman)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei è americana.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother has an American friend.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is an American in class today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prendo un americano, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll have an Americano, please.

definitions.note: Future tense (3rd person singular): he/she/it will love.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Un giorno amerà qualcuno davvero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: One day he/she will truly love someone.

definitions.note: Future tense (1st person singular) of "amare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti amerò per sempre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will love you forever.

definitions.note: Most commonly means “you love” (tu ami). It can also mean “(that) I love” in the present subjunctive (che io ami).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu ami la musica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You love music.

definitions.note: Present tense (noi).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Amiamo la pizza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We love pizza.

definitions.note: Feminine form; used for a female friend.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Giulia è la mia migliore amica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Giulia is my best friend.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of “amico”

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Giulia is my friend.

definitions.note: feminine plural of “amica”; used when referring to a group of female friends (or an all-female group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le mie amiche abitano vicino a me.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My (female) friends live near me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È solo un’amichetta di scuola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She’s just a school friend.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il personale del ristorante è molto amichevole.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The restaurant staff is very friendly.

definitions.note: plural form; used for both masculine and feminine plural nouns
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono incontri amichevoli tra vicini.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form of the adjective “amico”.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our neighbors are very friendly.

definitions.note: plural of "amico" (male or mixed-gender group)

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Long-standing friendships are precious.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Marco is a friend of mine.

definitions.note: Often means “I love” (1st person singular, present) in context.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I love you so much.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form (used for a woman or a feminine noun).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is sick today.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mia sorella è ammalata oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is sick today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi sono ammalato, quindi resto a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I’m sick, so I’m staying home.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), often used in stories and in written Italian; in everyday speech people often use the passato prossimo instead.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: During the trip, he/she got sick suddenly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quel virus ammazza molte persone ogni anno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That virus kills many people every year.

definitions.note: Often used as an informal command (tu).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Turn off the engine before getting out of the car.

definitions.note: Often strong and graphic; in everyday speech it can also mean “to kill (someone) off” or “to slaughter.”

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to kill anyone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il cacciatore ha ammazzato un cinghiale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hunter killed a wild boar.
