definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After work I’m exhausted.

definitions.note: Often used informally to mean “I’m going to kill you!” as a joke or threat when annoyed (not always literal).

definitions.note: Past participle (masculine plural) of “ammettere”; often used in passive forms or as an adjective.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He admits that he made a mistake.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I admit that I was wrong.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She admires the view from the terrace.

definitions.note: past imperfect (used for ongoing/repeated action in the past)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da bambino, ammiravo le stelle ogni sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As a child, I admired the stars every evening.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Provo molta ammirazione per il tuo coraggio.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We admire your courage.

definitions.note: Present tense, 1st person singular (io).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I admire you for your courage.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) form; common in written Italian, especially stories and history.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bread is moldy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti amo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I love you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'amore è importante nella vita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Love is important in life.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In 2010 I went to Rome for the first time.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) form of "andare"; common in stories and writing, less common in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri andammo al mare.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio andarmene subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to leave right away.

definitions.note: From the verb phrase “andarsene,” meaning to leave/go away (often with the idea of leaving a place or situation).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo andarmene subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to leave right away.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) of "andare" (3rd person plural), used especially in written narration and in some regions.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After dinner, they went home.

definitions.note: Often used to mean leaving a place (sometimes with the idea of going away for good).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s better to leave right away.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to leave right away.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devi andartene subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to leave right away.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo andarvene adesso.

definitions.note: imperfect subjunctive of “andare”; used after expressions like “volevo che…”, “se…”, “benché…”.

definitions.note: Past participle of "andare" (used with "essere").

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono andato a casa presto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I went home early.

definitions.note: Imperfect past (imperfetto) of “andare”; often used for ongoing or habitual past actions.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (imperfect) of "andare"; used for ongoing/repeated actions in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando eravamo piccoli, andavamo al mare ogni estate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When we were little, we went to the seaside every summer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I bambini andavano a scuola a piedi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children were going to school on foot.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (past habitual/ongoing) form of "andare"; often used for something you used to do or were doing.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was little, I used to go to school on foot.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the run, Maria is very thirsty.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo la corsa sono assetato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the run I’m thirsty.

definitions.note: Often used with “che” + clause (e.g., “assicurati che…” = “make sure that…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi assicuro che la porta sia chiusa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I make sure the door is closed.

definitions.note: Used for insurance (e.g., a car, a house).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio assicurare la macchina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to insure the car.

definitions.note: Often used with "che" + clause (e.g., "assicurarmi che...") to mean “make sure (that...)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo assicurarmi che la porta sia chiusa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to make sure the door is closed.

definitions.note: Second-person plural imperative/reflexive (used to tell a group “you all” to do something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Assicuratevi di chiudere la porta prima di uscire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Make sure to close the door before you go out.

definitions.note: Informal (tu) command form of “assicurarsi,” often used with “di” + infinitive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Assicurati di spegnere le luci prima di uscire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Make sure to turn off the lights before you go out.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il pacco è assicurato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The package is insured.

definitions.native: you assure, you make sure, you insure
definitions.note: Present tense (tu) or present subjunctive (che tu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che tu assicuri tutti che va tutto bene.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you assure everyone that everything is fine.

definitions.note: First-person singular (io) in the present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti assicuro che domani sarò puntuale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I assure you that tomorrow I will be on time.

definitions.note: Often used to mean you check or confirm something so it happens.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Assicuro la porta prima di uscire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I make sure the door is locked before going out.

definitions.note: Commonly spelled “assieme” in older texts; in modern Italian it’s usually spelled “insieme”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Andiamo assieme al cinema stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let's go to the cinema together tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'assistente prepara i documenti per la riunione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The assistant prepares the documents for the meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Grazie per la tua assistenza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thank you for your help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo chiamare l’assistenza clienti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to call customer support.

definitions.note: Often used with “a” + event (e.g., a un concerto). It can look like English “assist,” but here it means “attend.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani assisterà al concerto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow he/she will attend the concert.

definitions.note: Often used with “a” + person (e.g., assisterà sua madre).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti assisterà durante il progetto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She will help you during the project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È stato assistito da un medico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was assisted by a doctor.

definitions.note: In Italian, assistere a means “to attend / witness,” which can be confusing because English “to assist” usually means “to help.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho assistito a una lezione di italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I attended an Italian lesson.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a solo passage in music (or a solo performance).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il chitarrista fa un assolo incredibile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The guitarist plays an incredible solo.

definitions.note: Often used in legal contexts (e.g., a person is found not guilty).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È stato assolto dal tribunale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was acquitted by the court.

definitions.note: Can be used for being forgiven or freed from guilt/blame, including in religious contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il prete lo ha assolto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The priest absolved him.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una verità assoluta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s an absolute truth.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sì, assolutamente!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yes, absolutely!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il silenzio assoluto mi mette a disagio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Absolute silence makes me uncomfortable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Assomigli molto a tua madre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You look a lot like your mother.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo ragazzo assomiglia a suo padre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This boy looks like his father.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I due fratelli assomigliano molto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The two brothers look very alike.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (voi), used when speaking to more than one person; also used as a formal singular in some contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Assomigliate molto a vostra madre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You (all) look a lot like your mother.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (was similar to / used to look like).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da bambino assomigliava a suo padre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As a child, he looked like his father.

definitions.note: Present tense, first person singular (io).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Assomiglio a mio padre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I look like my father.

definitions.note: feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo pranzo mi sento un po' assonnata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After lunch I feel a bit sleepy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo pranzo siamo tutte un po’ assonnate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After lunch we’re all a bit sleepy.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo tutti assonnati questa mattina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re all sleepy this morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo pranzo sono sempre un po' assonnato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After lunch I'm always a bit sleepy.

definitions.note: Used as a gerund ("while assuming/supposing").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Assumendo che tu abbia ragione, cosa facciamo adesso?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Assuming you're right, what do we do now?

definitions.note: Used as a gerund, often in the sense of taking on staff.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stanno assumendo nuove persone in ufficio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are hiring new people at the office.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’azienda vuole assumere due nuove persone.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company wants to hire two new people.

definitions.note: Often used for taking on a role/responsibility or adopting an attitude/position.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo l’errore, ha deciso di assumere la responsabilità.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the mistake, he decided to take responsibility.

definitions.native: to take, to consume (medicine, food, etc.)
definitions.note: Common with medicines: "assumere un farmaco" = to take a drug/medicine.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devi assumere questa medicina due volte al giorno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to take this medicine twice a day.

definitions.note: Here, “la” means “her” (feminine direct object pronoun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'azienda vuole assumerla subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company wants to hire her right away.

definitions.note: Here, “la” can mean “it” (referring to a feminine noun) or “it” in a general sense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non voglio assumerla da solo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to take it on by myself.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non assumo che tu abbia torto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t assume you’re wrong.

definitions.note: Often used in a work context (to hire employees).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi assumo due persone nel mio negozio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I’m hiring two people for my shop.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto), often used in written Italian and for historical narration.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nel 2019 assunse la responsabilità del progetto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In 2019, he/she took on responsibility for the project.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) form, used especially in written Italian and storytelling, often about completed actions in the distant past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nel 2010 assunsi Maria come assistente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In 2010 I hired Maria as an assistant.

definitions.note: Used as the feminine singular past participle of a verb meaning “to hire” (about a woman).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Maria è stata assunta ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Maria was hired yesterday.

definitions.note: Used as the feminine singular past participle of a verb meaning “to assume” (about a feminine noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’ipotesi è stata assunta come vera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hypothesis was assumed to be true.

definitions.note: past participle (feminine plural) of “assumere”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le nuove impiegate sono state assunte ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The new employees were hired yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used with essere (passive): essere assunto = to be hired.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Due nuovi impiegati sono stati assunti ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Two new employees were hired yesterday.

definitions.note: Past participle of assumere in the sense of “to assume” (e.g., an assumed fact).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I dati assunti nel rapporto non sono corretti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The data assumed in the report are not correct.

definitions.note: past participle of "assumere"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho assunto un ruolo nuovo nel progetto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I took on a new role in the project.

definitions.note: past participle of "assumere" (used especially for being hired for a job)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Marco è stato assunto ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Marco was hired yesterday.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa idea è assurda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This idea is absurd.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È assurdo pagare così tanto per un biglietto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s absurd to pay that much for a ticket.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio fratello sogna di diventare astronauta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother dreams of becoming an astronaut.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho messo le penne nell’astuccio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the pens in the pencil case.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha risolto il problema con astuzia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He solved the problem with cleverness.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio fratello è ateo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is an atheist.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mia sorella è un’atleta molto disciplinata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is a very disciplined athlete.

definitions.note: plural of "atleta"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gli atleti si allenano ogni giorno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The athletes train every day.

definitions.note: Often used about a person’s body/build or a sporty style.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha un fisico atletico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has an athletic build.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il cane attacca il ladro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog attacks the thief.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La colla attacca bene.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The glue sticks well.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il cane sta attaccando il postino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is attacking the mail carrier.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto attaccando il poster al muro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m attaching the poster to the wall.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se li provochi, attaccano subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you provoke them, they attack right away.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I bambini attaccano gli adesivi sul quaderno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kids stick the stickers on the notebook.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non possono attaccarci qui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They can’t attack us here.

definitions.native: attach to it, stick to it
definitions.note: Often used when adding something onto something else (e.g., a label, a note).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi attaccarci un’etichetta?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you attach a label to it?

definitions.note: Often used for physically attaching something (with tape, glue, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi attaccare questo foglio al muro?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you stick/attach this sheet to the wall?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hanno deciso di attaccare all’alba.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They decided to attack at dawn.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "attaccare"; used with "essere" to form the passive or as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La foto è attaccata al frigorifero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The photo is stuck to the fridge.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Attaccate le foto al muro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Attach the photos to the wall.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Attaccate il nemico!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Attack the enemy!

definitions.note: Past participle used like an adjective (masculine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I fogli sono attaccati al muro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sheets are attached to the wall.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il poster è attaccato al muro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The poster is attached to the wall.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il villaggio è stato attaccato durante la notte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The village was attacked during the night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’attacco è iniziato all’alba.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The attack began at dawn.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il cane attaccò il ladro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog attacked the thief.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Attaccò il francobollo sulla busta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She stuck the stamp on the envelope.

definitions.note: Often used with “a” + infinitive: “attaccare a” + verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Appena arrivò, attaccò a parlare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As soon as he/she arrived, he/she began to talk.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il suo atteggiamento è molto positivo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His attitude is very positive.

definitions.note: Used with the present subjunctive (e.g., after expressions like “è meglio che…”) or as a formal command (Lei).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È meglio che attenda qui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s better that you wait here.

definitions.note: Often used with "aspettare" as a near-synonym; can be followed by "che" + subjunctive (e.g., "attendo che tu arrivi").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti prego di attendere un momento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please wait a moment.

definitions.note: Second-person plural present tense ("you all" / formal "you").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Attendete qui un momento, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wait here a moment, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Attendiamo il treno alla stazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We wait for the train at the station.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "attento".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei è sempre attenta quando guida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is always careful when she drives.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ascolta attentamente le istruzioni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Listen carefully to the instructions.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of "attento"; used with feminine plural nouns or feminine plural subjects.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le guide sono attente ai dettagli.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The guides are attentive to the details.

definitions.note: masculine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: State attenti quando attraversate la strada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Be careful when you cross the street.

definitions.note: Often used with “a” + noun/infinitive (e.g., “attento a…”) to mean careful/aware about something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stai attento quando attraversi la strada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Be careful when you cross the street.

definitions.note: Often used as an interjection to warn someone or to call for focus (like “Attention!” or “Careful!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Attenzione! C'è una macchina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Watch out! There’s a car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fai attenzione quando attraversi la strada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Pay attention when you cross the street.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo atterrati a Roma alle otto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We landed in Rome at eight.

definitions.note: Often used in set phrases like “in attesa (di ...)” = “waiting (for ...)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’attesa è lunga, ma ne vale la pena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wait is long, but it’s worth it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vivono in un attico con una grande terrazza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They live in a penthouse with a big terrace.

definitions.note: feminine singular form (used with feminine nouns or to describe a woman/girl).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mia sorella è molto attiva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is very active.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho attivato l’abbonamento ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I activated the subscription yesterday.

definitions.note: plural masculine form of "attivo"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I bambini sono molto attivi oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are very active today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa attività è molto interessante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This activity is very interesting.

definitions.note: Often used in the sense of a shop, company, or commercial activity (e.g., “un’attività” = a business).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio zio ha un'attività in centro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My uncle has a business downtown.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi sono molto attivo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I am very active.

definitions.note: Common for things like phones, subscriptions, or accounts (meaning not disabled).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il mio abbonamento è ancora attivo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My subscription is still active.

definitions.note: Often used for an act in a play (e.g., "atto primo" = "act one").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il primo atto della commedia è molto divertente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The first act of the comedy is very funny.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio fratello vuole diventare attore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother wants to become an actor.

definitions.note: plural of "attore"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gli attori sono sul palco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The actors are on the stage.

definitions.note: Often used with a to form the prepositional phrase attorno a (“around”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono molte persone attorno al tavolo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many people around the table.

definitions.note: Often used with "a" as "attorno a" = "around" / "around (something)".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'erano molte persone attorno al tavolo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There were many people around the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una città molto attraente per i turisti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a very attractive city for tourists.

definitions.note: Often used with "da" (attracted by) or "verso" (attracted to).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono attratto dalla musica jazz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m attracted to jazz music.

definitions.note: third-person singular present (he/she/it crosses) of "attraversare"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui attraversa la strada con attenzione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He crosses the street carefully.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 1st person plural of "attraversare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri attraversammo il ponte a piedi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday we crossed the bridge on foot.

definitions.note: gerund ("-ing" form) of "attraversare"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto attraversando la strada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m crossing the street.

definitions.note: Often used for crossing a street, a river, or an area from one side to the other.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo attraversare la strada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to cross the street.

definitions.note: Second-person plural form (used with “voi”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ogni mattina attraversate la strada sulle strisce.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every morning you cross the street on the crosswalk.

definitions.note: Past participle of "attraversare"; often used with "avere" to form the past tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho attraversato la strada con attenzione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I crossed the street carefully.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing/past habitual action).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Attraversava la strada quando ha visto l’amico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was crossing the street when he saw his friend.

definitions.note: Used in the present subjunctive (e.g., after expressions like “è importante che…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È importante che tu attraversi la strada sulle strisce.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that you cross the street at the crosswalk.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Camminiamo attraverso il parco per arrivare a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We walk through the park to get home.

definitions.note: simple past (passato remoto) of "attraversare"; common in written narratives
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il cane attraversò la strada all’improvviso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog crossed the street suddenly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A Roma ci sono molte attrazioni famose.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In Rome there are many famous attractions.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho lasciato gli attrezzi in garage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I left the tools in the garage.

definitions.note: Past participle of "attribuire"; often used with "essere" to form passive or as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il merito è stato attribuito a lei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The credit was attributed to her.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mia sorella vuole diventare attrice.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister wants to become an actress.

definitions.note: Often used in formal or written contexts to mean “current” (e.g., current situation, current government).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La situazione attuale è difficile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The current situation is difficult.

definitions.note: Often used in formal or written Italian.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Attualmente vivo a Milano, ma l’anno prossimo mi trasferisco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I currently live in Milan, but next year I’m moving.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ascolto spesso audiolibri mentre guido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I often listen to audiobooks while I drive.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un risultato molto augurato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a very much hoped-for result.

definitions.note: Used to wish someone well on an occasion (e.g., birthday, holidays) or to congratulate them.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Auguri per il tuo compleanno!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Best wishes for your birthday!

definitions.note: Often used as an exclamation on birthdays/holidays (“Auguri!”) or to congratulate someone (“Auguri per…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Auguri per il tuo compleanno!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Best wishes for your birthday!

definitions.note: Often used in the pattern “ti auguro …” (“I wish you …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti auguro buona fortuna.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wish you good luck.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La lezione è in aula 3.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lesson is in classroom 3.

definitions.note: Third-person singular present of "aumentare" (can also be a formal "you" form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il prezzo aumenta ogni mese.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The price increases every month.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stiamo aumentando i prezzi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are increasing the prices.

definitions.note: Past participle (masculine plural); often used with "essere" to form compound tenses or as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I prezzi sono aumentati di nuovo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The prices have increased again.

definitions.note: Past participle of "aumentare"; often used with "avere" to form the past tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho aumentato il prezzo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I increased the price.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'è stato un aumento dei prezzi quest'anno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There has been an increase in prices this year.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of "autentico".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa borsa è autentica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This bag is authentic.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo ristorante è autentico: qui cucinano come a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This restaurant is authentic: they cook here like at home.

definitions.note: Often used for a professional driver (e.g., bus, taxi, truck), but can also mean a regular driver.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'autista dell'autobus è molto gentile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus driver is very kind.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La mia auto è parcheggiata davanti a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My car is parked in front of the house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vado a scuola in autobus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I go to school by bus.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho chiesto un autografo al cantante dopo il concerto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I asked the singer for an autograph after the concert.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho parcheggiato l’automobile davanti a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I parked the car in front of the house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In questa strada ci sono troppe automobili.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are too many cars on this street.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chi è l’autore di questo libro?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Who is the author of this book?

definitions.note: plural of "autore"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gli autori del libro firmano le copie dopo la presentazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The authors of the book sign copies after the presentation.

definitions.note: Often refers to an institution/official body (e.g., local authorities) or to someone’s power to make decisions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le autorità hanno chiuso la strada per sicurezza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The authorities closed the road for safety.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’autostima è importante per affrontare le difficoltà.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Self-esteem is important for facing difficulties.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prendiamo l’autostrada per arrivare prima.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s take the highway to get there faster.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In autunno le foglie cambiano colore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In autumn the leaves change color.

definitions.note: Often used to encourage someone to continue or to move forward (like “come on!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vai avanti e ti raggiungo tra cinque minuti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Go ahead and I’ll catch up with you in five minutes.

definitions.note: Used to encourage someone to start or continue.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Avanti, prova ancora!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come on, try again!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Avanzate lentamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Move forward slowly.

definitions.note: Usually refers to food left after a meal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Metto gli avanzi in frigo per domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the leftovers in the fridge for tomorrow.

definitions.note: Plural form; commonly used when talking about food left after a meal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Metto gli avanzi in frigo per domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the leftovers in the fridge for tomorrow.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "avaro".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È avara con i soldi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is stingy with money.

definitions.note: Used to describe a person who doesn’t like spending or giving money.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio zio è molto avaro e non offre mai niente a nessuno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My uncle is very stingy and never offers anything to anyone.

definitions.note: In Italian it’s commonly used for an online profile image or a digital character representing a user.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho cambiato il mio avatar sul forum.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I changed my avatar on the forum.

definitions.note: Formal/archaic greeting (from Latin), often used in historical or literary contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ave, Cesare!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hail, Caesar!

definitions.note: Remote past (passato remoto) of "avere"; used mainly in written narratives and in some regions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’anno scorso avemmo molta fortuna.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last year we had a lot of luck.

definitions.note: Gerund of the auxiliary verb "avere"; used to form compound tenses and can also introduce a clause meaning "since/because".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Avendo già finito, possiamo uscire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Having already finished, we can go out.

definitions.note: Gerund of "avere"; often used as an auxiliary to form compound tenses (e.g., "avendo fatto" = "having done").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Avendo finito il lavoro, sono andato a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Having finished the work, I went home.

definitions.note: contracted form of "avere" used as an auxiliary, especially in fixed phrases like "dopo aver..."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo aver finito il lavoro, siamo usciti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After having finished the work, we went out.

definitions.note: Shortened form of "avere", common in writing or set phrases (e.g. "di aver", "aver bisogno").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero di aver tempo domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope to have time tomorrow.

definitions.note: Used as the auxiliary verb "avere" with the clitic "ci" (= there/in it/on it), often before a past participle (e.g., "averci messo" = "to have put/taken [there/on it]").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo averci messo troppo tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I must have taken too much time on it.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary to form compound past tenses with many verbs (especially transitive verbs).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho mangiato una pizza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ate a pizza.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho due fratelli.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have two brothers.

definitions.native: to have it, to have her
definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “la” (= it/her).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo averla finita entro domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to have it finished by tomorrow.

definitions.native: to have it, to have her
definitions.note: Infinitive of "avere" with the direct object pronoun "la" attached ("it/her").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo averla vista ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I must have seen it yesterday.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “le” (= “them”, feminine plural). Often used as an auxiliary in phrases like “dopo averle + past participle”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo averle viste, sono tornato a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After having seen them, I went back home.

definitions.note: Infinitive of "avere" with the direct object pronoun "li" attached (= “them”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo averli pronti entro stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to have them ready by this evening.

definitions.note: Infinitive of "avere" with the direct object pronoun "lo" attached (="it").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È importante averlo sempre con te.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important to always have it with you.

definitions.note: Infinitive of "avere" with the direct object pronoun "lo" ("it") attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei averlo subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to have it right away.

definitions.note: Infinitive of "avere" with the direct object pronoun "lo" attached ("it").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei averlo subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to have it right away.

definitions.note: Used as the auxiliary "avere" with the object pronoun "mi" attached (enclitic), often before a past participle (e.g., "avermi detto").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dovresti avermi chiamato prima.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You should have called me earlier.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “mi” (“me”) attached to “avere” (“to have”), often used as an auxiliary before a past participle (e.g., “avermi visto” = “having seen me” / “have seen me”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Potresti avermi visto ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You might have seen me yesterday.

definitions.native: to have some (of it/them), to have any (of it/them)
definitions.note: This is the infinitive of “avere” with the particle “ne”, used to refer to an unspecified amount (e.g., “some/any of it/them”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei averne di più.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to have more of it/them.

definitions.note: Used with a past participle to form a perfect infinitive with the object pronoun “ti” (e.g., “averti visto” = “to have seen you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi dispiace non averti avvisato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm sorry I didn't warn you.

definitions.note: This is the infinitive "avere" with the attached direct object pronoun "ti" (= you, informal singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono felice di averti qui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m happy to have you here.

definitions.note: Includes the attached pronoun "vi" (usually “you” plural, or sometimes “there”); often used before a past participle, e.g. "avervi visto" = “having seen you”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono felice di avervi incontrato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m happy to have met you.

definitions.note: Imperfetto congiuntivo (subjunctive imperfect) of "avere"; used after expressions like "volevo che...", "era importante che...".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Volevo che avesse più tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wanted him/her to have more time.

definitions.note: Imperfetto congiuntivo (subjunctive imperfect) of "avere"; often used after expressions of doubt, desire, or possibility in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pensavo che avesse ragione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thought he/she was right.

definitions.note: Past subjunctive (congiuntivo imperfetto) of “avere”, used in dependent clauses (e.g., after “se” or verbs of doubt/wishing).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se avessero tempo, verrebbero con noi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If they had time, they would come with us.

definitions.note: Third-person plural imperfect subjunctive of "avere"; often used after expressions of doubt, desire, or necessity.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dubito che avessero abbastanza tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I doubt they had enough time.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive (io/tu/lui/lei) of the auxiliary “avere”, used in hypothetical or dependent clauses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se avessi tempo, verrei con te.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I had time, I would come with you.

definitions.note: Used in the imperfect subjunctive (e.g., after "se" = "if", or after expressions like "pensavo che...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se avessi tempo, verrei con te.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I had time, I would come with you.

definitions.note: Subjunctive form of the auxiliary "avere", often used after expressions like "se" (if) or after verbs that trigger the subjunctive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se avessimo tempo, andremmo al mare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If we had time, we would go to the beach.

definitions.note: First-person plural (noi) imperfect subjunctive of “avere”. Often used after expressions of doubt, desire, or necessity, or in hypothetical clauses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se avessimo più tempo, faremmo un viaggio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If we had more time, we would take a trip.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 2nd person plural; used mainly in writing and in some regions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando aveste finito, usciste in silenzio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When you had finished, you left quietly.

definitions.note: Second person plural, past historic (passato remoto) of "avere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nel 2010 aveste un'idea brillante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In 2010 you had a brilliant idea.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary with a past participle (passato prossimo); 2nd person plural (voi).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Avete già finito i compiti?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Have you already finished the homework?

definitions.note: Second-person plural (“you all”); can also be used as an auxiliary verb (e.g., to form the past tense).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Avete già mangiato?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Have you already eaten?

definitions.note: Imperfect (past) form of the auxiliary verb used to form compound tenses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aveva già finito quando sono arrivato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He had already finished when I arrived.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (past) form of "avere"; often used for ongoing/repeated past situations or background description.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando ero piccolo, aveva sempre un sorriso per tutti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was little, he/she always had a smile for everyone.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (imperfect past) of the auxiliary verb “avere”; used to form compound tenses and also to mean possession in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando eravamo piccoli, avevamo un cane.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When we were little, we had a dog.

definitions.note: imperfect tense (used for ongoing/repeated past actions or descriptions)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Avevamo una casa al mare quando ero piccolo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had a house by the sea when I was little.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (past imperfect) of the auxiliary verb "avere"; often used to form past tenses with a past participle.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Avevano già finito quando siamo arrivati.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They had already finished when we arrived.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (past habitual/ongoing) form of “avere” for “they/you (plural, formal)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando erano piccoli, avevano un cane.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When they were little, they had a dog.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (past imperfect), 2nd person plural (voi). Often used as an auxiliary to form compound tenses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Avevate già finito quando sono arrivato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You had already finished when I arrived.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (past habitual/ongoing). Used with “voi”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando eravate bambini, avevate molti giocattoli.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When you were children, you had many toys.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (tu). Often used to describe an ongoing state in the past or a habitual past action; can also be used as an auxiliary to form past tenses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando ero piccolo, avevi sempre tempo per me.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was little, you always had time for me.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) of the imperfect tense of "avere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Avevi già finito i compiti?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Had you already finished your homework?

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (used for ongoing/repeated past situations or background).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando ero piccolo, avevo un cane.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was little, I had a dog.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary to form compound past tenses (passato prossimo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Avevo già finito quando sei arrivato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had already finished when you arrived.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (imperfect) of “avere”; used for ongoing states/habits in the past or background descriptions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando ero piccolo, avevo un cane.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was little, I had a dog.

definitions.note: Future tense (informal singular: tu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani avrai molto tempo libero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow you will have a lot of free time.

definitions.note: third-person plural (loro) future tense of "avere"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani avranno molto lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow they will have a lot of work.

definitions.note: Conditional (third person singular) of the auxiliary verb “avere”; used to form the conditional perfect (e.g., “avrebbe detto” = “would have said”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Avrebbe voluto venire, ma era troppo tardi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She would have wanted to come, but it was too late.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (lui/lei) of the conditional tense of "avere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Avrebbe voluto aiutarti, ma non poteva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She would have wanted to help you, but he/she couldn’t.

definitions.note: Third-person plural conditional of the auxiliary verb "avere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Avrebbero finito prima, ma il treno era in ritardo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They would have finished earlier, but the train was late.

definitions.note: Conditional present (io). Used to form the conditional perfect: avrei + past participle.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Avrei voluto chiamarti ieri, ma ero troppo stanco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would have liked to call you yesterday, but I was too tired.

definitions.note: Conditional present (noi) of the auxiliary verb “avere”; used to form the conditional perfect (e.g., “avremmo detto” = “we would have said”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Avremmo finito prima, ma c'era troppo traffico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We would have finished earlier, but there was too much traffic.

definitions.note: Conditional mood (present conditional) of "avere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Avremmo più tempo se finissimo prima.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We would have more time if we finished earlier.

definitions.note: Future simple of "avere" (used for possession and also as an auxiliary in compound tenses).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani avremo più tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will have more time.

definitions.note: Second person plural (voi) conditional present of the auxiliary verb “avere”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se me lo aveste detto prima, avreste avuto più tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you had told me earlier, you would have had more time.

definitions.note: Second person singular (tu), conditional mood, used as an auxiliary with a past participle (e.g., avresti detto...).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Avresti dovuto chiamarmi prima.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You should have called me earlier.

definitions.note: Second person singular (tu) of the conditional present of “avere” (used for hypotheticals and in the conditional perfect with a past participle).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se avresti tempo, mi aiuteresti?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you would have time, would you help me?

definitions.note: Second person plural (voi), future tense of "avere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani avrete più tempo per studiare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow you will have more time to study.

definitions.note: Third-person singular future tense of the auxiliary verb “avere” (used to form compound tenses).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Avrà finito entro stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She will have finished by this evening.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular future (lui/lei/Lei).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani avrà più tempo per studiare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow he/she will have more time to study.

definitions.note: First-person singular (io) of the future tense of "avere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani avrò più tempo per studiare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will have more time to study.

definitions.note: Past participle of "avere"; used with "essere" or "avere" to form compound tenses (e.g., "ho avuto").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho avuto un problema ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had a problem yesterday.

definitions.note: feminine singular form; can be used as a past participle or as an adjective
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’acqua era avvelenata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The water was poisoned.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form (often used like an adjective) of the past participle of "avvelenare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non mangiare quelle bacche: potrebbero essere avvelenate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t eat those berries: they could be poisoned.

definitions.note: Imperative form for "you all" (2nd person plural) of "avvelenare"; used to give a command to more than one person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non avvelenate il pozzo!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t poison the well!

definitions.note: Often used as a past participle (with essere/avere) or as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il cibo era avvelenato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The food was poisoned.

definitions.note: Passato remoto (literary/simple past), 3rd person singular: he/she/it poisoned.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il re avvelenò il nemico durante la cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The king poisoned the enemy during dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La nostra vacanza è stata una vera avventura.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our vacation was a real adventure.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Durante le vacanze abbiamo vissuto tante avventure.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: During the holidays we lived through many adventures.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Luca è molto avventuroso e ama viaggiare da solo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Luca is very adventurous and loves to travel alone.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "avvenire"; often used with "essere" (e.g., "è avvenuta")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La riunione è avvenuta ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The meeting happened yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used intransitively for hopes, dreams, or predictions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I suoi sogni si avverano finalmente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His dreams finally come true.

definitions.note: Used transitively when someone makes a wish, plan, or dream become reality.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Con il loro aiuto, avverano il progetto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With their help, they make the project come true.

definitions.note: Used especially with "(si) è avverato" to talk about dreams, hopes, or predictions becoming reality.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il suo sogno si è avverato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His dream came true.

definitions.native: will come true, will make (something) come true
definitions.note: Future tense, 3rd person plural (they). Often used for wishes, dreams, predictions, or promises that become reality.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I tuoi sogni si avvereranno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your dreams will come true.

definitions.note: Often used with "che" in the subjunctive to express a hope, wish, or possibility (e.g. "Spero che...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che i tuoi genitori avverino i tuoi desideri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope your parents fulfill your wishes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se piove, la partita avverrà domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If it rains, the match will happen tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il nostro avversario è molto forte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our opponent is very strong.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho ricevuto un avvertimento dal professore per essere arrivato tardi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I received a warning from the teacher for arriving late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti avverto: la strada è scivolosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I warn you: the road is slippery.

definitions.note: Often used for giving notice or letting someone know (sometimes formally).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per favore, avvertimi se arrivi tardi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please let me know if you arrive late.

definitions.note: Infinitive with the attached pronoun “le”; depending on context it can mean “her” (to her) or “them” (feminine plural). Often means “to warn/notify”. Can be confused with English “advertise” (false friend).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo avvertirle che siamo in ritardo.
