definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il treno parte dal binario 4.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train leaves from platform 4.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho letto una biografia di Leonardo da Vinci.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I read a biography of Leonardo da Vinci.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Studio biologia all’università.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I study biology at university.

definitions.note: Often used for food/products made without synthetic pesticides or fertilizers.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compro frutta biologica al mercato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I buy organic fruit at the market.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mia sorella è biologo e lavora in un laboratorio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is a biologist and works in a lab.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form; used for a woman or feminine noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mia sorella è bionda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is blonde.

definitions.note: Common term for a ballpoint pen; often used like a brand name.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi presti la tua biro?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you lend me your ballpoint pen?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prendo una birra, grazie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll have a beer, thanks.

definitions.note: plural of "birra"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei due birre, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like two beers, please.

definitions.note: Plural of “biscotto”. In Italy it can refer to many kinds of cookies; “biscotti” can also mean the specific twice-baked almond cookies common in English.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato dei biscotti al supermercato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought some cookies at the supermarket.

definitions.note: In American English, it’s usually “cookie”; in British English, often “biscuit.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vuoi un biscotto con il tè?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you want a cookie with your tea?

definitions.native: it is necessary, you have to, one must
definitions.note: Impersonal form (used without a specific subject), often followed by an infinitive (e.g., “bisogna studiare”) or by “che” + subjunctive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bisogna studiare per l’esame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to study for the exam.

definitions.note: Impersonal form (used with an infinitive or with “che” + subjunctive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bisogna studiare ogni giorno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s necessary to study every day.

definitions.native: one should, it would be necessary
definitions.note: Impersonal form (no real subject); often followed by an infinitive (e.g., "bisognerebbe fare...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bisognerebbe studiare un po’ ogni giorno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: One should study a little every day.

definitions.note: plural of "bisogno".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I bambini hanno bisogni diversi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Children have different needs.

definitions.note: Often used with "avere" (to have) and "di" (of): "avere bisogno di" = "to need."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho bisogno di aiuto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo visto un bisonte allo zoo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We saw a bison at the zoo.

definitions.note: plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nel parco vivono molti bisonti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many bison live in the park.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per cena prendo una bistecca con le patate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For dinner I’m having a steak with potatoes.

definitions.note: Past participle of "bloccare"; often used with "essere" or as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La macchina è bloccata nel traffico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car is stuck in traffic.

definitions.note: feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La porta è bloccata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The door is blocked.

definitions.note: plural masculine form; can also be used in mixed-gender groups
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo bloccati nel traffico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re stuck in traffic.

definitions.note: Past participle of "bloccare"; often used with "avere" to form the past tense (passato prossimo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho bloccato il numero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I blocked the number.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il traffico è bloccato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Traffic is blocked.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto), often used in narratives and in some regions more than in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La polizia bloccò la strada per un incidente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police blocked the road because of an accident.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho aperto un blog per condividere le mie ricette.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I started a blog to share my recipes.

definitions.note: Invariable adjective: it does not change for gender or number (e.g., una macchina blu, due macchine blu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La tua giacca è blu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your jacket is blue.

definitions.note: Commonly invariable in Italian (the same form for masculine/feminine and singular/plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il blu è il mio colore preferito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Blue is my favorite color.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Apri la bocca, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Open your mouth, please.

definitions.note: Often used about failing a school year or an exam.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Marco è stato bocciato all’esame di matematica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Marco failed the math exam.

definitions.note: Used for ideas, proposals, or requests that are not accepted.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il progetto è stato bocciato dal consiglio comunale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The project was rejected by the city council.

definitions.note: Often used for a small mouthful or a small tasty morsel.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vuoi un bocconcino di torta?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you want a little bite of cake?

definitions.note: Often used for a bite of food (or, figuratively, something hard to swallow).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho preso un boccone di panino e poi sono uscito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I took a bite of my sandwich and then I went out.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hanno organizzato un boicorraggio contro l’azienda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They organized a boycott against the company.

definitions.note: Usually for utilities (electricity, gas, water) or services.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo pagare la bolletta della luce entro domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to pay the electricity bill by tomorrow.

definitions.note: Can be used literally (water/food boiling) and figuratively (e.g., emotions “boiling”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’acqua sta per bollire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The water is about to boil.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho bollito le patate per cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I boiled the potatoes for dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La polizia ha trovato una bomba vicino alla stazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police found a bomb near the station.

definitions.note: Often used for an extra benefit or incentive (e.g., a discount, perk, or tax-related bonus).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Con questo abbonamento hai un bonus di 10 euro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With this subscription you get a 10-euro bonus.

definitions.note: Often considered vulgar or offensive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La polizia ha chiuso un bordello in centro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police shut down a brothel downtown.

definitions.note: Colloquial; can sound vulgar (like saying “what a mess!” in a strong way).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In cucina c’è un bordello: piatti ovunque e niente è in ordine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There’s a mess in the kitchen: dishes everywhere and nothing is in order.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il bordo del tavolo è rovinato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The edge of the table is damaged.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho messo il telefono nella borsa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the phone in my bag.

definitions.note: Often used in phrases like “la Borsa di Milano” (Milan Stock Exchange).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi la borsa è in calo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today the stock market is down.

definitions.note: Plural of "borsa".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato due borse nuove.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought two new bags.

definitions.note: In Italian, "la borsa" can mean the stock exchange; "borse" is the plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le borse europee sono in calo oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: European stock exchanges are down today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I borseggiatori lavorano spesso nelle zone turistiche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Pickpockets often operate in tourist areas.

definitions.note: Often refers to a small handbag/purse; depending on context it can also mean a small pouch/bag.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato una borsetta nera per la sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a small black handbag for the evening.

definitions.note: plural of "bosco"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono molti boschi vicino al paese.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many woods near the town.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'è un sentiero nel bosco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a path in the woods.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La botte è piena di vino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The barrel is full of wine.

definitions.note: Often used as the plural of "botta" (a blow/hit).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha preso molte botte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He took a lot of hits.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato una bottiglia d'acqua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a bottle of water.

definitions.note: plural of "bottiglia"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato due bottiglie d’acqua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought two bottles of water.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi manca un bottone della camicia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m missing a button on my shirt.

definitions.note: Often used in Italian to refer to the sport and also to the bowling alley (the place).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sabato sera andiamo a giocare a bowling.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On Saturday night we’re going to play bowling.

definitions.note: Plural of "braccio" (arm).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho le braccia stanche dopo la palestra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My arms are tired after the gym.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hanno regalato un braccialetto d’argento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They gave me a silver bracelet as a gift.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi fa male il braccio destro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My right arm hurts.

definitions.note: used in Italian as a masculine noun: il braille
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Legge in braille perché è cieco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He reads in Braille because he is blind.

definitions.note: Often used for animals like wolves or sheep; for fish you more often hear "banco" (school of fish).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Un branco di lupi attraversa la foresta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A pack of wolves crosses the forest.

definitions.note: In Italian, this is a masculine noun and is often used as a loanword from English.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo cena prendo un brandy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After dinner I have a brandy.

definitions.note: Adjective meaning 'from Brazil'.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho un collega brasiliano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a Brazilian coworker.

definitions.note: feminine singular form; often used to compliment a woman or girl (e.g., “Brava!” = “Well done!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Marta è brava a cucinare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Marta is good at cooking.

definitions.note: Plural form (masculine or mixed group) of "bravo".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siete brave in matematica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are good at math.

definitions.note: Plural form (masculine plural, or mixed-gender plural). Often used to praise someone (e.g., kids): “Bravi!” = “Good job!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siete stati bravi oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You were good today.

definitions.note: Superlative form of "bravo"; often used as praise ("Well done!").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sei bravissimo a cucinare!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re very good at cooking!

definitions.note: Often used to praise someone (especially after a performance): “Bravo!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sei davvero bravo a cucinare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re really good at cooking.

definitions.note: Used as an interjection to praise someone (like saying “Bravo!” in English).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bravo! Hai fatto un ottimo lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Well done! You did a great job.

definitions.note: A typical Italian cured meat, often served sliced thin (e.g., with arugula and lemon).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei un panino con la bresaola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like a sandwich with bresaola.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il film è breve, ma molto interessante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie is short, but very interesting.

definitions.note: plural form (masculine or feminine) of "breve".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scrivi frasi brevi, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Write short sentences, please.

definitions.note: Used in Italian mainly to refer to the card game.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I miei nonni giocano a bridge ogni domenica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandparents play bridge every Sunday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La stella brilla nel cielo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The star shines in the sky.

definitions.note: Often used for something that shines (like a light or a color) or for someone very intelligent.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha avuto un'idea brillante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She had a brilliant idea.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gli occhi dei bambini sono brillanti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children's eyes are bright.

definitions.note: Often used to propose a toast (like “cheers!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È il tuo compleanno: brindiamo!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s your birthday: let’s toast!

definitions.note: used for things or people from Great Britain/the UK; agrees in gender and number (britannica/britannici/britanniche)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Un giornale britannico ha pubblicato la notizia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A British newspaper published the news.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho i brividi perché fa freddo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have chills because it’s cold.

definitions.note: Often used for a shiver from cold, fear, or excitement.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho sentito un brivido di freddo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I felt a shiver of cold.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi riempire la brocca d’acqua, per favore?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you fill the pitcher of water, please?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi piacciono i broccoli al vapore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like steamed broccoli.

definitions.note: In Italian it’s commonly used as an English loanword, especially for web browsers.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quale browser usi di solito?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Which browser do you usually use?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il legno brucia facilmente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wood burns easily.

definitions.note: Imperative form (command) of "bruciare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Attento: brucia!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Careful: it burns!

definitions.note: simple past (passato remoto), 1st person singular; common in narratives and in some regions
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bruciai la lettera e non ne parlai più.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I burned the letter and I never talked about it again.

definitions.note: present gerund (used like “burning” or “while burning”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto bruciando la cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m burning dinner.

definitions.note: Can be used both transitively (to burn something) and intransitively (to be burning).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Attento: puoi bruciare la cena se non controlli il forno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Careful: you can burn dinner if you don’t check the oven.

definitions.note: past historic (passato remoto), third person plural; often used in narratives and historical accounts
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Durante la notte bruciarono le vecchie lettere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: During the night, they burned the old letters.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "bruciare" (used with feminine nouns, or in compound tenses with "essere" when agreeing with a feminine subject)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La torta è bruciata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cake is burned.

definitions.note: Can mean "you (plural) burn/are burning" (present tense).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se bruciate la carta, fate fumo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you burn the paper, you make smoke.

definitions.note: Can also be a plural command (imperative) addressed to more than one person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bruciate queste lettere subito!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Burn these letters right away!

definitions.note: Past participle of "bruciare"; often used as an adjective (e.g. "pane bruciato").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il pane è bruciato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bread is burnt.

definitions.note: Can also be used figuratively to mean “ruined/spoiled” (e.g., a plan).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il pane è bruciato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bread is burnt.

definitions.note: Often used for a burning sensation in the body (e.g., heartburn, irritation).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho un bruciore allo stomaco dopo aver mangiato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a burning sensation in my stomach after eating.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto), third person singular: “(he/she/it) burned.” Common in storytelling and in some regions; in everyday speech many people use passato prossimo instead.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La candela bruciò tutta la notte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The candle burned all night.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "brutto"; used to describe a feminine noun (or something referred to as feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quella macchina è brutta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That car is ugly.

definitions.note: feminine plural form of “brutto”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quelle scarpe sono brutte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those shoes are ugly.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form of "brutto"; can also be used for mixed-gender groups.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quei palazzi sono brutti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those buildings are ugly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quel palazzo è brutto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That building is ugly.

definitions.note: Often used about experiences, situations, or feelings (not just appearance).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo avuto una brutta giornata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had a bad day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’è una buca nella strada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There’s a hole in the road.

definitions.note: Often used for puncturing something like a tire, a balloon, or skin (e.g., with a needle).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho bucato una gomma con un chiodo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I punctured a tire with a nail.

definitions.note: Commonly used in phrases like “fare il bucato” (to do the laundry).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi devo fare il bucato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I have to do the laundry.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono molte buche sulla strada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many potholes on the road.

definitions.note: plural of "buco"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono dei buchi nella strada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are holes in the road.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'è un buco nel muro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There’s a hole in the wall.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il buddhismo è una religione e una filosofia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Buddhism is a religion and a philosophy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il buddismo è una religione e una filosofia nata in Asia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Buddhism is a religion and a philosophy that began in Asia.

definitions.note: Often refers to the (water) buffalo in Italy, for example in connection with mozzarella di bufala.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nel parco abbiamo visto un bufalo enorme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the park we saw a huge buffalo.

definitions.note: Commonly used in Italian as a loanword, especially in computing for a software error.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'è un bug nel programma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There’s a bug in the program.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non dire una bugia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t tell a lie.

definitions.note: feminine form of "bugiardo"; used for a woman or girl
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non credere a quella bugiarda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t believe that liar.

definitions.note: plural masculine form of "bugiardo"; can refer to a mixed-gender group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I bugiardi non dicono mai tutta la verità.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Liars never tell the whole truth.

definitions.note: masculine noun; for a woman, you usually say “bugiarda”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non credere a Marco: è un bugiardo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t believe Marco: he’s a liar.

definitions.note: Plural of “bugia” (a lie).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non dire bugie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don't tell lies.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "buio"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La stanza è buia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The room is dark.

definitions.note: Often used with "fare" or "essere" to talk about it being dark.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fuori è buio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It's dark outside.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho paura del buio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m afraid of the dark.

definitions.note: Can refer to a man from Bulgaria; for a woman, use “bulgara”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio vicino è un bulgaro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My neighbor is a Bulgarian.

definitions.note: Informal; from the English word “bully”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da ragazzo mi sono sentito bullizzato a scuola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As a kid, I felt bullied at school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Durante la guerra si nascosero in un bunker.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: During the war they hid in a bunker.

definitions.note: In golf, a "bunker" is a sand trap.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La mia palla è finita nel bunker.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My ball ended up in the sand trap.

definitions.note: Short form of "buono", used before many masculine singular nouns (e.g., "buon giorno", "buon amico").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Buon viaggio!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Have a good trip!

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "buono".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La pizza è buona.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pizza is good.

definitions.note: Used as a greeting or farewell in the evening, especially when someone is going to sleep.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Buonanotte, a domani!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Good night, see you tomorrow!

definitions.note: Used as a greeting when going to bed or saying goodbye late at night.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Buonanotte, a domani!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Good night, see you tomorrow!

definitions.note: Used as a greeting in the evening; can also be used when leaving in the evening.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Buonasera, come sta?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Good evening, how are you?

definitions.note: feminine plural form of "buono"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho ricevuto buone notizie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I received good news.

definitions.note: Used as a polite greeting, especially in the morning and early afternoon.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Buongiorno! Come stai?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Good morning! How are you?

definitions.note: plural masculine form of "buono"; can also be used for a mixed-gender group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono buoni amici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are good friends.

definitions.note: often used to talk about food; plural masculine form of "buono".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questi biscotti sono davvero buoni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These cookies are really good.

definitions.note: Often used before a noun (e.g., "un buon libro") and can shorten to "buon" before many masculine singular nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo pane è buono.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This bread is good.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi sono di buonumore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I'm in a good mood.

definitions.note: Often used to describe someone who seems unfriendly or stern, but not necessarily mean.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il nuovo vicino è un po' burbero, ma in realtà è gentile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The new neighbor is a bit grumpy, but actually he's kind.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi passarmi il burro, per favore?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you pass me the butter, please?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il burro cammina lentamente lungo la strada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The donkey walks slowly along the road.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prendo il bus alle otto per andare a scuola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I take the bus at eight to go to school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Qualcuno bussa alla porta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Someone is knocking at the door.

definitions.note: Used as an informal command (imperative) to one person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bussa prima di entrare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Knock before you come in.

definitions.note: Gerund form, often used to mean “while knocking” or “(I’m) knocking” with “stare” (e.g., “sto bussando”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto bussando alla porta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m knocking on the door.

definitions.note: past participle of "bussare"; often used with "avere" (e.g., "ho bussato" = "I knocked").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho bussato alla porta, ma nessuno ha risposto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I knocked on the door, but nobody answered.

definitions.note: Often used in the present subjunctive (e.g., after expressions like “spero che…”), and also as the formal (Lei) imperative: “Bussi!” = “Knock!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che tu bussi prima di entrare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you knock before coming in.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho messo la lettera nella busta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the letter in the envelope.

definitions.note: Often used for a paper or plastic shopping bag.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi dai una busta, per favore?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you give me a bag, please?

definitions.note: Diminutive of “busta”; often used for a small paper envelope.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi ha lasciato una bustarella con i documenti sulla scrivania.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He left me a small envelope with the documents on the desk.

definitions.note: Informal: money given secretly (literally “an envelope”) to get an illegal favor.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il funzionario ha accettato una bustarella per accelerare la pratica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The official accepted a bribe to speed up the paperwork.

definitions.note: Can also be used as an informal command ("throw!", "throw it away!") depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui butta la bottiglia nel cestino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He throws the bottle in the trash can.

definitions.note: Can be either present tense (“you all throw”) or an imperative (“throw!” to more than one person).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Buttate via la spazzatura, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Throw away the trash, please.

definitions.note: Past participle (feminine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le carte buttate a terra erano tutte bagnate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cards thrown on the ground were all wet.

definitions.note: Past participle (plural) of "buttare"; often used with an object pronoun (e.g., "li buttati").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Li ho buttati via perché erano rotti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I threw them away because they were broken.

definitions.note: Past participle of "buttare"; often used with "avere" to form the past tense (e.g., "ho buttato").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho buttato la carta nel cestino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I threw the paper in the trash can.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Perché butti via il cibo?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why do you throw away the food?

definitions.note: Present tense (io). Often used for throwing something away (e.g., in the trash) depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Butto la carta nel cestino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I throw the paper in the trash can.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto) of "buttare"; common in narratives and some regions, while spoken Italian often uses passato prossimo.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui buttò la palla nel cestino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He threw the ball into the bin.

definitions.note: refers to the Kabyle people/culture from Kabylia (Algeria)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Una donna cabila vive in Algeria.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A Kabyle woman lives in Algeria.

definitions.note: Often used in reference to North African or Arab/Berber tribal groups.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In passato molte persone vivevano in una cabila nel deserto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the past, many people lived in a tribe in the desert.

definitions.note: Often used for small enclosed spaces like a phone booth, voting booth, shower stall, or changing room; can also mean the cabin of a vehicle (e.g., elevator, plane, truck).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci vediamo davanti alla cabina telefonica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: See you in front of the phone booth.

definitions.note: Informal/childish word; can be considered rude depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il bambino deve fare la cacca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The child has to poop.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per favore, non cacci il cane dal parco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please, don’t chase the dog out of the park.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La caccia è vietata in questo parco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hunting is forbidden in this park.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo a caccia di un buon ristorante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re on the hunt for a good restaurant.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In autunno molti vanno a cacciare nel bosco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In autumn many people go hunting in the woods.

definitions.native: to chase away, to drive out
definitions.note: Often used for forcing someone/something to leave a place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il proprietario ha cacciato via i ladri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The owner chased the thieves away.

definitions.native: driven out, chased away, kicked out
definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "cacciare"; used with a feminine subject/object.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La ragazza è stata cacciata dal locale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The girl was kicked out of the place.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'ho cacciato di casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I kicked him out of the house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il cacciatore è nel bosco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hunter is in the woods.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi puoi passare il cacciavite, per favore?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you pass me the screwdriver, please?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il proprietario cacciò gli intrusi dalla casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The owner chased the intruders out of the house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da giovane cacciò nel bosco con suo padre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he was young, he hunted in the woods with his father.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho un cactus sul davanzale della finestra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a cactus on the windowsill.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hanno trovato un cadavere nel parco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They found a corpse in the park.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) of "cadere" (used mainly in writing and in some regions for past events).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri cadde un albero durante il temporale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday a tree fell during the storm.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto) of "cadere"; common in narratives and written Italian.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alla fine della battaglia, caddero in silenzio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the end of the battle, they fell in silence.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto) of “cadere”; common in narratives and in some regions in speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri caddi dalle scale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I fell down the stairs.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Attento: cade il vaso!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Careful: the vase is falling!

definitions.note: Often used in the expression “che cosa cade?” meaning “what’s happening?”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Che cosa cade? Perché urlano tutti?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What’s happening? Why is everyone shouting?

definitions.note: present gerund of "cadere"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stavo cadendo dalle scale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was falling down the stairs.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Attento: potresti cadere!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Careful: you might fall!

definitions.note: third-person plural ("they")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In autunno le foglie cadono dagli alberi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In autumn the leaves fall from the trees.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se non lo tieni bene, cadrà.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you don’t hold it well, it will fall.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "cadere"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La foglia è caduta dall’albero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The leaf has fallen from the tree.

definitions.note: feminine plural past participle of "cadere"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le foglie sono cadute ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The leaves fell yesterday.

definitions.note: Past participle (masculine plural) of "cadere"; used with "essere" to form compound tenses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono caduti dalle scale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They fell down the stairs.

definitions.note: past participle of "cadere"; commonly used with "essere" (e.g., "è caduto")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il vaso è caduto dal tavolo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The vase fell off the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non bevo caffè la sera perché la caffeina mi tiene sveglio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t drink coffee in the evening because caffeine keeps me awake.

definitions.note: In Italian, this often refers to a place focused on coffee (like an espresso bar).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci vediamo in caffetteria alle tre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: See you at the café at three.

definitions.note: Plural of caffettiera; often refers to stovetop moka pots in Italy.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In cucina ci sono due caffettiere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the kitchen there are two coffee makers.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prendo un caffè, grazie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll have a coffee, please.

definitions.native: to poop, to take a shit
definitions.note: Vulgar/very informal; use more neutral “fare la cacca” or “andare di corpo” in polite contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho dovuto cagare in un bagno pubblico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had to take a shit in a public bathroom.

definitions.note: vulgar/slang.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scusa, ho cagato nel bagno sbagliato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry, I pooped in the wrong bathroom.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La cagna ha avuto cinque cuccioli.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The female dog had five puppies.

definitions.note: Often used as a strong insult; can be vulgar/offensive when referring to a person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non chiamarla cagna: è offensivo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t call her a bitch: it’s offensive.

definitions.note: Diminutive/affectionate form of "cane" (dog).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Che cagnolino carino!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What a cute little dog!

definitions.note: Very vulgar; used to talk about defecating or (figuratively) to express contempt/fear in an offensive way.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scusa, devo andare in bagno: cago e torno subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry, I have to go to the bathroom: I’ll take a shit and be right back.

definitions.note: Often used as the plural (voi) command: “Lower/Drop (it)!” It can also be the (voi) form in the present subjunctive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Calate la voce, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Lower your voice, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha dato due calci alla palla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gave two kicks to the ball.

definitions.note: Infinitive of "calciare" with the attached pronoun "mi" (= "me").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non devi calciarmi!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You must not kick me!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho calciato la palla nel cortile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I kicked the ball into the yard.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio fratello è un calciatore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is a soccer player.

definitions.note: Plural of "calciatore"; in Italian, "calcio" usually refers to soccer (not American football).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I calciatori entrano in campo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soccer players walk onto the field.

definitions.note: In Italy, "calcio" usually refers to soccer (what Americans call "soccer").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio fratello gioca a calcio ogni sabato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother plays soccer every Saturday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il latte è ricco di calcio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Milk is rich in calcium.

definitions.note: Passato remoto (simple past), used mainly in writing (and more in some regions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alla fine della partita, calciò il pallone fuori dal campo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the end of the game, (he/she) kicked the ball out of the field.

definitions.note: gerund form; often used like “while calculating” or “by calculating”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto calcolando il totale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m calculating the total.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho dimenticato la calcolatrice a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I forgot the calculator at home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho fatto i calcoli e il totale è giusto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I did the calculations and the total is correct.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per domani devo finire questi calcoli di matematica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For tomorrow I have to finish these math problems.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo fare un calcolo veloce.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to do a quick calculation.

definitions.note: In Italian, this meaning is usually used in the plural (calcoli), especially in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio zio ha avuto un calcolo al rene.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My uncle had a kidney stone.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "caldo" (used with feminine nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La minestra è calda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soup is hot.

definitions.note: feminine plural form of “caldo”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le giornate estive sono molto calde qui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The summer days are very hot here.

definitions.note: masculine plural form of "caldo"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi i panini sono ancora caldi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today the sandwiches are still warm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi l’acqua è calda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today the water is warm.

definitions.note: Often used with the article: "il caldo" = "the heat" (especially hot weather).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non sopporto il caldo in estate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t stand the heat in summer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho appeso un calendario in cucina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hung a calendar in the kitchen.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nel giardino ci sono calendule gialle e arancioni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the garden there are yellow and orange marigolds.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hai una calligrafia molto chiara.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have very clear handwriting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mantieni la calma, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stay calm, please.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of the adjective “calmo”; used with feminine nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La situazione è calma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The situation is calm.

definitions.note: Often used with a direct object (calmare qualcuno/qualcosa) or reflexively as calmarsi (“to calm down”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo calmare il bambino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to calm the child.

definitions.note: Reflexive: it means becoming calm (not calming someone else).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo la lezione di yoga, mi calmo e mi sento meglio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the yoga class, I calm down and I feel better.

definitions.note: Reflexive form ("to calm yourself down"); used with "tu".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Calmarti: respira lentamente e conta fino a dieci.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Calm down: breathe slowly and count to ten.

definitions.note: Often used for a brief period when things (like the sea, wind, or a situation) become calmer.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo la tempesta, c’è stata una breve calmata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the storm, there was a brief lull.

definitions.note: Plural informal command (to “you all”); reflexive: “calm yourselves.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Calmatevi e ascoltatemi un attimo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Calm down and listen to me for a moment.

definitions.note: Informal (used with "tu"); also used reflexively ("calmarsi").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Calmati, per favore: va tutto bene.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Calm down, please: everything is fine.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi la situazione è più calme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today the situation is calmer.

definitions.note: Plural form of the noun “calmo” (state of calm).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo la tempesta ci sono stati alcuni calmi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the storm there were a few moments of calm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Rimani calmo e respira lentamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stay calm and breathe slowly.

definitions.note: As a noun, it’s used mainly in set phrases (often about the sea or weather), e.g. “il calmo del mare”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo la tempesta, è tornato il calmo del mare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the storm, the calm of the sea returned.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto), 3rd person singular: “he/she/it calmed down” or “he/she/it soothed (someone/something)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando vide che i bambini stavano bene, si calmò.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he saw that the children were fine, he calmed down.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il calore del sole è piacevole in inverno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The warmth of the sun is pleasant in winter.

definitions.note: Often used for people, welcomes, greetings, and receptions (a friendly, heartfelt warmth).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci hanno fatto un caloroso benvenuto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They gave us a warm welcome.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho calpestato una foglia secca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I stepped on a dry leaf.

definitions.note: plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi servono delle calze pulite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need some clean socks.

definitions.note: plural of "calzino".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato dei calzini nuovi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought some new socks.

definitions.note: Often used as the formal (Lei) imperative (“change!”) and also in the present subjunctive (e.g., “che io cambi” = “that I change”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cambi idea, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Change your mind, please.

definitions.note: Often used for “he/she/it changes” (present tense).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il tempo cambia spesso in montagna.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The weather often changes in the mountains.

definitions.note: Can also be the command “change!” (tu imperative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cambia strada, è più veloce.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Change roads/route, it’s faster.

definitions.note: past historic (passato remoto), 1st person singular
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri cambiai idea all’ultimo minuto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I changed my mind at the last minute.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono stati molti cambiamenti quest'anno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There have been many changes this year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo bisogno di un cambiamento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need a change.

definitions.note: Present tense (noi) and can also be used as an invitation/command meaning “let’s …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cambiamo strada perché c’è traffico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We change streets because there’s traffic.

definitions.note: gerund form of "cambiare"; often used like English “-ing” or after "stare" (e.g., "sto cambiando" = "I’m changing").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto cambiando idea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m changing my mind.

definitions.note: third-person plural ("they") present tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le cose cambiano in fretta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Things change quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio cambiare lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to change jobs.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi cambiare questi euro in dollari?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you exchange these euros into dollars?

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “lo” (“it”, masculine singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dobbiamo cambiarlo prima di partire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to change it before leaving.

definitions.note: Reflexive form with mi (“myself”); commonly used for changing clothes.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo cambiarmi prima di uscire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to get changed before going out.

definitions.note: past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo la discussione, cambiarono idea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the discussion, they changed their minds.

definitions.note: Includes the pronoun "ti" (= you). Depending on context, it can also mean "change yourself" (e.g., getting changed).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo cambiarti subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to change you right away.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "cambiare"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La situazione è cambiata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The situation has changed.

definitions.note: Often used as an imperative addressed to more than one person ("you all").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cambiate idea!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Change your mind!

definitions.note: Used for the main city where a country's government is based.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Roma è la capitale d'Italia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Rome is the capital of Italy.

definitions.note: Money or assets used for investment or business.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo bisogno di più capitale per avviare l'azienda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need more capital to start the company.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il capitalismo è un sistema economico basato sulla proprietà privata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Capitalism is an economic system based on private property.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sta capitando qualcosa di strano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Something strange is happening.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il capitano della squadra parla con l’allenatore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The team captain talks with the coach.

definitions.note: Verb form of "capitare" (often used to mean that something happens by chance). Not related to "captain" in this use.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A volte capitano degli imprevisti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sometimes unexpected things happen.

definitions.note: Often used with "a" + person ("capita a me" = "it happens to me").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Può capitare un imprevisto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Something unexpected can happen.

definitions.native: to drop by, to end up (somewhere)
definitions.note: Often used with "in/da" to say you go somewhere by chance.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri sono capitato in quel bar per caso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I happened to end up in that bar by chance.

definitions.note: Imperfetto congiuntivo (subjunctive imperfect) of "capitare"; used after expressions of possibility, doubt, or conditions (often translated as “if … happened”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se capitasse un imprevisto, chiamami subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If something unexpected happened, call me right away.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "capitare"; used with a feminine subject (often with "essere": "è capitata").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi è capitata un’occasione interessante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: An interesting opportunity came up for me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi è capitato di perdere il treno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I happened to miss the train.

definitions.note: Second person plural (voi) form of "capire".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Capite quello che sto dicendo?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you (all) understand what I’m saying?

definitions.note: Often used to mean something occurs by chance or unexpectedly.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se capiterà un imprevisto, ti chiamo subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If something unexpected happens, I’ll call you right away.

definitions.note: Subjunctive form of "capitare"; often used after expressions like "spero che..." (I hope that...).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che tu capiti qui domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you happen to come by here tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used on its own as an informal reply meaning “Got it!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho capito la lezione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I understood the lesson.

definitions.note: Plural of "capitolo".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho letto i primi due capitoli del libro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I read the first two chapters of the book.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho letto il primo capitolo del libro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I read the first chapter of the book.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto) of "capitare"; common in writing, storytelling, and in some regions in speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: E poi capitò una cosa strana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: And then something strange happened.

definitions.note: Imperfetto: often describes an ongoing past situation (“I was understanding”) or a repeated/habitual past (“I used to understand”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: All'inizio non capivo, ma poi capivo meglio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At first I didn’t understand, but then I understood better.

definitions.note: Often used both literally (body part) and in common expressions like "in cima a" or "a capo" depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi fa male il capo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My head hurts.

definitions.note: Common in work contexts (e.g., "il capo" = the boss).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il capo è in riunione adesso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss is in a meeting right now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo romanzo è un capolavoro della letteratura italiana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This novel is a masterpiece of Italian literature.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'è una piccola cappella vicino al castello.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a small chapel near the castle.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In inverno porto spesso cappelli di lana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In winter I often wear wool hats.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato un cappello nuovo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a new hat.

definitions.note: plural of "cappotto"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In inverno metto sempre i cappotti nell’armadio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In winter I always put the coats in the wardrobe.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho bisogno di un cappotto perché fa freddo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a coat because it’s cold.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prendo un cappuccino e un cornetto, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'll have a cappuccino and a croissant, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La capra mangia l’erba.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The goat eats the grass.

definitions.note: plural of “capra”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le capre mangiano l’erba nel prato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The goats eat the grass in the meadow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho avuto un capriccio e ho comprato un gelato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had a whim and I bought an ice cream.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto) form; common in written Italian and storytelling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando vide la lettera, capì subito la verità.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he saw the letter, he understood the truth right away.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of "caro"; meaning depends on context (person vs. price).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cara Maria, come stai?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Dear Maria, how are you?

definitions.note: Used to describe something that costs a lot (feminine singular).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This bag is very expensive.

definitions.note: Plural form of "caramella".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vuoi delle caramelle?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you want some candies?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha un carattere molto gentile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has a very kind personality.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cerco di mangiare meno carboidrati la sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I try to eat fewer carbohydrates in the evening.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il carbone è un elemento chimico fondamentale per la vita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Carbon is a chemical element that is fundamental for life.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In inverno, alcune case si scaldano ancora con il carbone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È stato mandato in carcere per furto.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cardinal celebrated Mass in the cathedral.

definitions.note: feminine plural form of "caro"; often used when addressing a group of women or talking about feminine plural nouns (e.g., "amiche").

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Dear friends, thank you for being here.

definitions.note: feminine plural form of "caro"; used with feminine plural nouns (e.g., "scarpe", "case").

definitions.note: Plural form of the adjective.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La batteria è quasi senza carica.

definitions.note: Often used for an official role (e.g., in government or a company).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has an important position in the local government.

definitions.note: Often used for loading items into/onto something (e.g., a truck) or loading a file/page in computing.

definitions.note: Common in computing/online contexts (uploading files, photos, videos).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm about to upload a photo to Instagram.

definitions.note: Form used for ‘you (plural) load’ (present tense) and also for the plural command ‘load!’

definitions.note: Past participle of "caricare"; often used for uploading files/photos online.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I uploaded the photo to the website.

definitions.note: Often used for a phone/laptop battery charger; in some contexts it can also mean a magazine (for a firearm), but that meaning is not typically taught at beginner level.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I forgot the phone charger at home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il camion trasporta un carico pesante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The truck is carrying a heavy load.

definitions.note: Passato remoto (simple past), often used in stories or in some regions instead of the present perfect.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il camionista caricò le scatole sul camion.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The truck driver loaded the boxes onto the truck.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of "carino"; often used as a friendly compliment.

definitions.note: Plural feminine form of "carino"; used for people, pets, or things you find pleasant or charming.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your photos are really cute.

definitions.note: plural form; can describe people or things

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your children are really cute.

definitions.note: Often used to describe a person, pet, or thing in an affectionate way.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha molto carisma e la gente lo ascolta.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un insegnante molto carismatico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a very charismatic teacher.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non mangio carne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't eat meat.

definitions.note: Used to address someone in letters/emails or to show affection.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Caro Marco, come stai?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Dear Marco, how are you?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo ristorante è caro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This restaurant is expensive.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei una carota, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like a carrot, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compro delle carote per la zuppa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m buying some carrots for the soup.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio zio è carpentiere e costruisce mobili su misura.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My uncle is a carpenter and builds custom-made furniture.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il carro è pieno di fieno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cart is full of hay.

definitions.note: Often used for a horse-drawn vehicle; it can also mean a (train) coach/car.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo saliti sulla carrozza numero cinque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We got on coach number five.

definitions.note: Plural of "carrozza"; often refers to horse-drawn carriages or (in modern use) train cars/coaches.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le carrozze del treno sono molto affollate oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train cars are very crowded today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La carrozzina è nel bagagliaio della macchina.

definitions.note: Often used for a wheelchair (e.g., in “carrozzina per disabili”).

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi serve della carta per stampare questo documento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need some paper to print this document.

definitions.note: Often used for things like ID cards, credit cards, or business cards.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho dimenticato la carta di credito a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I forgot my credit card at home.

definitions.note: Plural of "carta" in the sense of playing cards or cards in general.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hai delle carte da gioco?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have any playing cards?

definitions.note: Plural of "carta" in the sense of a map (as in "carta geografica").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo comprato due carte della città.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We bought two maps of the city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho firmato tutte le carte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I signed all the papers.

definitions.note: Often used for a paper folder or binder; in computing, it can also mean a file folder (directory).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho messo i documenti nella cartella blu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the documents in the blue folder.

definitions.note: Plural of "cartellino"; often used for small labels or name tags.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho stampato i cartellini con i nomi per la riunione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I printed the name tags for the meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a map of the city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi serve un cartone per spedire questo pacco.

definitions.note: Common in the expression “cartone animato” (animated cartoon).

definitions.note: Imperative (tu) of "chiamare" with the direct object pronoun "la" (feminine: “her/it”).
