definitions.note: Imperative with the attached pronoun “-le” (feminine plural), referring to “them” (feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se hai bisogno di aiuto, chiamale subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you need help, call them right away.

definitions.note: Informal (tu) imperative with the direct object pronoun “lo” attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se hai un problema, chiamalo subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you have a problem, call him right away.

definitions.note: Informal (tu) command form; used to tell someone to call you.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se hai bisogno di aiuto, chiamami.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you need help, call me.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) form; common in storytelling and in some regions of Italy.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri chiamammo un taxi per andare in aeroporto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday we called a taxi to go to the airport.

definitions.note: present gerund of "chiamare"; often used to mean “by calling” / “while calling.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto chiamando un taxi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m calling a taxi.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (present tense) of "chiamare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi chiamano ogni sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They call me every evening.

definitions.note: Often used for calling someone on the phone, calling out to someone, or calling someone by a name.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti chiamo stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll call you tonight.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “la” (= her/it, feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo chiamarla stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to call her tonight.

definitions.note: "-le" is a pronoun meaning "them" (feminine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo chiamarle stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to call them tonight.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “li” = “them” (masculine plural; can also refer to a mixed group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo chiamarli prima di partire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to call them before leaving.

definitions.note: Infinitive with the direct object pronoun “lo” attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo chiamarlo più tardi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to call him later.

definitions.note: Infinitive with the attached pronoun “mi” (“me”). Often used after modal verbs like “puoi” (can) or “vuoi” (want).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi chiamarmi domani?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you call me tomorrow?

definitions.note: Infinitive with the object pronoun “mi” attached (“me”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi chiamarmi domani?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you call me tomorrow?

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto), third person plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri sera chiamarono un taxi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night they called a taxi.

definitions.note: Infinitive with the attached object pronoun “-ti” (= you).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo chiamarti stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to call you tonight.

definitions.note: Includes the object pronoun “vi” (= you all).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo chiamarvi domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to call you (all) tomorrow.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "chiamare"; used with "essere" in compound tenses or as an adjective
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La mia amica è stata chiamata per il colloquio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My friend was called for the interview.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho ricevuto una chiamata ieri sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I received a call last night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi chiamate ogni giorno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You call me every day.

definitions.note: Plural of "chiamata".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho ricevuto tre chiamate oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I received three calls today.

definitions.note: 2nd-person plural (voi) command with the direct object pronoun “la” attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chiamatela subito!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Call her right away!

definitions.note: Imperative with an attached pronoun: said to more than one person ("you all").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se li vedi, chiamateli subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you see them, call them right away.

definitions.note: Imperative addressed to “voi” (you all): “call me.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se avete bisogno di aiuto, chiamatemi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you need help, call me.

definitions.note: past participle used for masculine plural (or mixed-gender) groups
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I ragazzi sono stati chiamati dal preside.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boys were called by the principal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho chiamato Maria ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I called Maria yesterday.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (past) form: used for ongoing/repeated actions or background description in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri sera mi chiamava ogni mezz'ora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night he/she was calling me every half hour.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (past habitual/ongoing): describes an action that was repeated or in progress in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando eri piccolo, ti chiamavamo ogni sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When you were little, we used to call you every evening.

definitions.note: imperfect tense (they)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri mi chiamavano ogni cinque minuti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday they were calling me every five minutes.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) in the future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi chiamerai domani mattina?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Will you call me tomorrow morning?

definitions.note: Second person singular (tu), conditional present.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi chiameresti domani?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Would you call me tomorrow?

definitions.note: Future tense, 2nd person plural (voi).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani chiamerete i nonni per salutarli.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow you (all) will call Grandma and Grandpa to say hello to them.

definitions.note: Third-person singular future tense (he/she/it will call).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani ti chiamerà alle otto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow he/she will call you at eight.

definitions.note: First person singular (io), future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti chiamerò domani mattina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will call you tomorrow morning.

definitions.note: Used in the present subjunctive (e.g., after expressions like “it’s important that…”) and also as a formal (Lei) command: “Chiami!” = “Call!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È importante che tu mi chiami stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that you call me tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chiamiamo il medico subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We call the doctor right away.

definitions.note: Used with "voi" in the present subjunctive (e.g., after expressions like "è importante che...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È importante che voi chiamiate prima di arrivare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that you call before arriving.

definitions.note: First-person singular (io). Often used to say your name: “Mi chiamo …” = “My name is …”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chiamo mia madre ogni sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I call my mother every evening.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto), used mainly in written Italian and for past events felt as distant (common in stories and in some regions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri sera Marco chiamò sua madre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night Marco called his mother.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "chiaro".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La spiegazione è chiara.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The explanation is clear.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chiaramente non ho capito la domanda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Clearly, I didn’t understand the question.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of “chiaro”; can describe something that is clear (easy to understand) or light in color.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi piacciono le pareti chiare in cucina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like light-colored walls in the kitchen.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi piace la chiarezza con cui spieghi le cose.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like the clarity with which you explain things.

definitions.note: Plural form (masculine plural, or mixed-gender plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi piacciono i colori chiari.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like light colors.

definitions.note: past participle of "chiarire"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho chiarito il problema con l’insegnante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I clarified the problem with the teacher.

definitions.note: Often means “light” in color (not dark).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il cielo è chiaro oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sky is clear today.

definitions.note: Used as an invariable adjective, often placed after the noun (e.g., "punto chiave").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo è un punto chiave del discorso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is a key point of the speech.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho perso la chiave di casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I lost the house key.

definitions.note: Often used in expressions like “parola chiave” (keyword) or “punto chiave” (key point).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La comunicazione è la chiave del successo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Communication is the key to success.

definitions.note: Plural of "chiave".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho dimenticato le chiavi a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I forgot the keys at home.

definitions.note: Usually the 3rd-person singular present subjunctive of "chiedere" (e.g. after "che"); it can also be used as a formal command (Lei).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È importante che chieda aiuto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that he/she asks for help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi chiede un favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She asks me for a favor.

definitions.note: gerund of "chiedere"; often used to mean "while asking" or to describe the action of asking.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto chiamando il professore, chiedendo un consiglio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m calling the professor, asking for some advice.

definitions.note: Often used with “a” + person (chiedere a qualcuno) and sometimes with “di” + verb (chiedere di fare qualcosa).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Posso chiedere un favore?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can I ask a favor?

definitions.note: Infinitive of "chiedere" with the indirect object pronoun "gli" attached (= to him).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo chiedergli un favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to ask him a favor.

definitions.note: Infinitive form with attached pronouns: -gli = to him, -lo = it.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo chiederglielo domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to ask him for it tomorrow.

definitions.note: "le" is an indirect object pronoun meaning "to her" or "to you" (formal, Lei).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei chiederle una cosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'd like to ask you something.

definitions.native: to ask for it, to ask him
definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun "lo" (= "it" or "him").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo chiederlo al professore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to ask him (the professor).

definitions.note: Infinitive of "chiedere" with the indirect object pronoun "mi" attached ("me").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi chiedermi un consiglio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can ask me for advice.

definitions.note: Infinitive with the attached pronoun “ti” (= you).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo chiederti una cosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to ask you something.

definitions.note: Can mean “to ask yourself” (literally “to ask to yourself”), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devi chiederti se è davvero necessario.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to ask yourself whether it’s really necessary.

definitions.native: to ask you (plural/formal), to ask yourselves
definitions.note: Enclitic form of "chiedere" + "vi". "Vi" can mean "you" (plural or formal) or "yourselves" depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei chiedervi una cosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to ask you something.

definitions.note: "vi" refers to "you" (plural, or polite/formal singular) and is attached as a pronoun to the verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei chiedervi una cosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to ask you something.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani ti chiederà un favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow he/she will ask you a favor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani chiederò al professore una spiegazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will ask the professor for an explanation.

definitions.note: Second-person plural ("you" plural) present tense; also used as the formal "you" (plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Che cosa chiedete?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What are you asking?

definitions.note: Second-person plural ("you" plural) present tense; also used as the formal "you" (plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chiedete un caffè al bar?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you requesting a coffee at the bar?

definitions.note: Second-person plural imperative (addressing more than one person, like “you all”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chiedetegli di aspettare qui un momento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ask him to wait here for a moment.

definitions.note: Imperative form with the indirect object pronoun "-le" attached ("to her" or "to them" feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chiedetele scusa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Apologize to her.

definitions.note: Imperative (voi): a command or request addressed to more than one person; "-lo" = "it".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se non mi credete, chiedetelo al direttore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you don’t believe me, ask the director for it.

definitions.note: Plural imperative (voi) with an object pronoun: “ask me”. Often used to address more than one person or in formal contexts (e.g., customer service).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se avete dubbi, chiedetemi pure.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you have doubts, feel free to ask me.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (imperfect tense): often used for ongoing/repeated past actions or background context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi chiedeva sempre come stavo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She always asked me how I was doing.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (past, ongoing/habitual) of "chiedere"; often used for a polite/softened request.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chiedevo un'informazione, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was asking for some information, please.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) present tense of “chiedere”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chiedi sempre aiuto quando ne hai bisogno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You always ask for help when you need it.

definitions.note: Informal (tu) command form of "chiedere" with the indirect object pronoun "gli" (“to him”) attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chiedigli di venire domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ask him to come tomorrow.

definitions.note: Imperative form with the indirect object pronoun “le” (“to her” or “to them,” feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chiedile se viene domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ask her if she’s coming tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m asking you a favor.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I already asked the office for the information.

definitions.note: past participle of “chiedere” (often used with “avere”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti ho chiesto un favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I asked you a favor.

definitions.note: Often used for the spicy pepper itself; can also refer to chili powder in some contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aggiungo un po' di chili alla salsa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I add a little chili pepper to the sauce.

definitions.note: Plural of “chilo” (kilogram).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato due chili di mele.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought two kilos of apples.

definitions.note: Commonly used to mean a kilogram (1,000 grams), especially for food and body weight.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like a kilo of apples, please.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The beach is ten kilometers from here.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the shop there are many guitars.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio fratello è chitarrista in una band.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is a guitarist in a band.

definitions.note: Often used after "che" in the present subjunctive (e.g., "È importante che..."); it can also be used as a formal command (Lei) meaning "close!".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È importante che chiuda la porta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that you close the door.

definitions.note: third-person singular present (also used for formal "you") of "chiudere"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui chiude la porta ogni sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He closes the door every evening.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 1st person plural of "chiudere"; common in writing and storytelling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chiudemmo la porta e tornammo in casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We closed the door and went back inside.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto chiudendo la finestra perché fa freddo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m closing the window because it’s cold.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi chiudere la porta, per favore?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La porta può chiudersi da sola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The door can close by itself.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chiudete la porta, per favore.

definitions.note: feminine plural form (used with feminine plural nouns)

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il negozio è chiuso oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The shop is closed today.

definitions.note: Often used on shop/restaurant doors or signs to mean “(we’re) closed.”

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought some onions at the market.

definitions.native: we will start, we will begin

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le condizioni del contratto sono chiare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The conditions of the contract are clear.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase "condizioni di salute".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le sue condizioni sono migliorate dopo l’operazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His condition improved after the operation.

definitions.note: Usually used in the plural (as here), especially in the expression “le mie condoglianze”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le porgo le mie condoglianze per la sua perdita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I offer you my condolences for your loss.

definitions.note: In Italian it often refers both to the building with multiple owners and to the homeowners’ association/management of shared areas.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abito in un condominio con dieci appartamenti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I live in a condominium building with ten apartments.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La sua condotta è stata impeccabile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His conduct was impeccable.

definitions.note: Past participle of "condurre" (often used with "avere" to form the past tense).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho condotto la riunione ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I led the meeting yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Conduce l’auto con prudenza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She drives the car carefully.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts (e.g., in traffic rules or on forms).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il conducente deve indossare la cintura di sicurezza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The driver must wear a seat belt.

definitions.note: Can also mean “I drive” (more formal/less common than “guido”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Io conduco il gruppo verso l’uscita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I lead the group toward the exit.

definitions.note: Often used for leading people or managing an activity (e.g., a meeting, an investigation, a TV/radio show).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei conduce una riunione ogni lunedì.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She leads a meeting every Monday.

definitions.note: Used with vehicles (synonym: guidare).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non so condurre la macchina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't know how to drive the car.

definitions.note: Passato remoto of "condurre" (often used in stories/historical narration).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il capitano condusse i soldati al castello.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The captain led the soldiers to the castle.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani partecipo a una conferenza sul clima.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I'm attending a conference about the climate.

definitions.note: plural of "conferenza"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani ho due conferenze all’università.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I have two conferences at the university.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho ricevuto la conferma della prenotazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I received the confirmation of the reservation.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi confermare la prenotazione, per favore?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you confirm the reservation, please?

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 1st person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alla fine confessai tutto alla polizia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end I confessed everything to the police.

definitions.note: Often used for confessing a mistake, wrongdoing, or a secret.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo confessare che ho sbagliato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to confess that I was wrong.

definitions.note: Used especially in a religious context, when a priest listens to someone’s confession.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il prete confessa i fedeli ogni sabato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The priest hears the faithful people’s confessions every Saturday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho confessato tutto alla polizia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I confessed everything to the police.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha fatto una confessione alla polizia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He made a confession to the police.

definitions.note: Often used in religious contexts to refer to a statement of belief.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La sua confessione di fede è stata molto sincera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His confession of faith was very sincere.

definitions.note: simple past (passato remoto), often used in narratives and in some regions
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alla fine confessò la verità.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end, he/she confessed the truth.

definitions.note: Often used for fruit preserves (similar to jam); in everyday Italian people may also say "marmellata" even when it isn’t citrus.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A colazione mangio pane e confettura di fragole.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For breakfast I eat bread and strawberry jam.

definitions.note: Often used with “con” (with) to say two places share a border.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'Italia confina con la Francia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Italy borders France.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il fiume segna il confine tra i due paesi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The river marks the border between the two countries.

definitions.note: plural of "confine"; often used for national or regional borders
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I confini tra i due paesi sono ben definiti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The borders between the two countries are well defined.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In quella regione ci sono molti conflitti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In that region there are many conflicts.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il conflitto tra i due paesi è durato molti anni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The conflict between the two countries lasted many years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A volte confondo i nomi delle persone.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sometimes I confuse people’s names.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa sedia è molto confortevole.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This chair is very comfortable.

definitions.note: Often used in the expression “nei confronti di” meaning “towards / regarding” someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non fare confronti con gli altri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t make comparisons with others.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il confronto tra i due prezzi è facile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The comparison between the two prices is easy.

definitions.note: Often used for an exchange of views between people (sometimes on TV or in politics).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo avuto un confronto in riunione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had a discussion in the meeting.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono confusa: puoi spiegarmelo di nuovo?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m confused: can you explain it to me again?

definitions.note: feminine plural form of "confuso".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le istruzioni sono confuse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The instructions are confused.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo un po' confusi, puoi ripetere?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re a bit confused—can you repeat?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'è molta confusione in questa stanza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a lot of confusion in this room.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho confuso i nomi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I mixed up the names.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono confuso: non capisco la domanda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m confused: I don’t understand the question.

definitions.note: Often used for official/authorized leave (e.g., maternity leave, sick leave, military discharge/leave).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho chiesto un congedo di due settimane dal lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I asked for two weeks of leave from work.

definitions.note: Gerund form; often means “(while) freezing” or “(by) freezing,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto congelando l'acqua per fare dei cubetti di ghiaccio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm freezing the water to make ice cubes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il pesce è congelato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fish is frozen.

definitions.note: third-person plural simple past (passato remoto): “they congratulated”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alla fine della gara, i compagni la congratularono per la vittoria.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the end of the race, her teammates congratulated her on the victory.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ogni anno voi congratulate gli studenti migliori.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every year you congratulate the best students.

definitions.note: Informal (tu) command; reflexive form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Congratulati per il tuo successo!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Congratulate yourself on your success!

definitions.note: Used to congratulate someone on an achievement or happy event.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Congratulazioni per il nuovo lavoro!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Congratulations on the new job!

definitions.note: Often used for a political legislative body (like the U.S. Congress) or a formal meeting/conference.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il congresso approva una nuova legge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Congress approves a new law.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono due conigli nel giardino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are two rabbits in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho visto un coniglio nel giardino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw a rabbit in the garden.

definitions.note: Often used for internet/phone connections, as well as general links between people or things.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non ho connessione a internet in questo momento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t have an internet connection right now.

definitions.note: Often used for being connected to the internet/network; also used more generally for things that are linked.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il computer è connesso a Internet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The computer is connected to the internet.

definitions.note: Often used like an adjective (e.g., ‘connected/online’), even though it’s the past participle of “connettere”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il computer è connesso a Internet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The computer is connected to the internet.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) form, common in narration and written stories.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nel 2010 conobbe sua moglie a Roma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In 2010 he met his wife in Rome.

definitions.native: they met, they got to know
definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) form of "conoscere"; often used in written narratives to describe a completed event in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Durante il viaggio conobbero una guida molto gentile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: During the trip they met a very kind guide.

definitions.native: I met, I got to know
definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), often used in books and storytelling for completed actions in the distant past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nel 2010 conobbi mia moglie a Firenze.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In 2010 I met my wife in Florence.

definitions.note: Used as the present subjunctive of "conoscere" (e.g., after expressions like "spero che..."); it can also be a formal (Lei) command meaning "know"/"get to know" depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che lei conosca la risposta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you know the answer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui conosce bene questa città.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He knows this city well.

definitions.native: we met, we got to know, we found out
definitions.note: Passato remoto (remote past): commonly used in stories and in some regions, especially in southern Italy; in everyday speech many speakers prefer passato prossimo.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A Firenze conoscemmo una guida molto gentile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In Florence we met a very kind guide.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha una buona conoscenza della storia italiana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has a good knowledge of Italian history.

definitions.note: A person you know, but not well (not a close friend).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È solo una conoscenza, non un amico stretto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s just an acquaintance, not a close friend.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho molte conoscenze in questa città.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have many acquaintances in this city.

definitions.note: Plural form; often refers to pieces/areas of knowledge (e.g., knowledge in a subject).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le sue conoscenze di inglese sono ottime.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His/Her knowledge of English is excellent.

definitions.native: to know, to be acquainted with
definitions.note: Used for knowing a person/place or being familiar with something (not for knowing a fact—that’s usually "sapere").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Conosco bene questa città.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I know this city well.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “la” (= her).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei conoscerla meglio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to get to know her better.

definitions.native: to know them, to meet them
definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “le” attached to the verb (= “them”, feminine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei conoscerle meglio prima di decidere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to get to know them better before deciding.

definitions.note: includes the direct object pronoun "li" (= "them") attached to the verb
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio conoscerli meglio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to know them better.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “li” = “them” (masculine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei conoscerli meglio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to know them better.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “lo” (= him/it).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei conoscerlo meglio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to know him better.

definitions.native: to meet you, to know you
definitions.note: Often used when meeting someone for the first time (e.g., “Piacere di conoscerti”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono felice di conoscerti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m happy to meet you.

definitions.native: to meet you, to get to know you
definitions.note: Often used in the phrase "Piacere di conoscerti" (“Nice to meet you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Piacere di conoscerti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Nice to meet you.

definitions.native: to meet you (all), to get to know you (all)
definitions.note: Includes the pronoun "vi" (= you, plural; also used as formal "you").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono felice di conoscervi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m happy to meet you (all).

definitions.native: to know you, to meet you
definitions.note: Includes the pronoun “vi” (= you all / you plural; also used as formal “you” in some contexts).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono felice di conoscervi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m happy to meet you.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form of “conoscere”; often used after expressions like “volevo che...” (I wanted that...) or “se...” (if...).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Volevo che lui conoscesse la verità.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wanted him to know the truth.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form (used in situations like “if I/you knew…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se conoscessi la risposta, te la direi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I knew the answer, I would tell you.

definitions.note: Passato remoto (voi); mostly used in writing or in some regions in spoken Italian.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando vi trasferiste a Roma, conosceste molta gente nuova.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When you moved to Rome, you met a lot of new people.

definitions.native: you (plural) know, you (plural) are familiar with
definitions.note: Second-person plural (voi) form; used for knowledge/familiarity with people, places, or things.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Conoscete Roma?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you (all) know Rome?

definitions.note: imperfect tense (he/she/it)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non conosceva nessuno in quella città.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She didn’t know anyone in that city.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense: often describes a past habit or an ongoing state in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da bambini conoscevamo tutti i vicini.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When we were kids, we knew all the neighbors.

definitions.note: Imperfetto, 3rd person plural (they). Often describes a past state or repeated/habitual action.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da bambini conoscevano tutti i vicini del quartiere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As children, they knew all the neighbors in the neighborhood.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (voi): often implies “used to know” or “were knowing” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando eravate piccoli, conoscevate tutti i vicini.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When you were little, you knew all the neighbors.

definitions.note: Second-person singular, imperfect (tu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando eri piccolo, conoscevi già tutte le strade del quartiere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When you were little, you already knew all the streets in the neighborhood.

definitions.note: Imperfect past (io): used for ongoing/habitual situations in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da bambino, conoscevo tutti i vicini.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As a child, I knew all the neighbors.

definitions.note: Informal ("tu") form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Conosci questo posto?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you know this place?

definitions.note: Informal ("tu") command (imperative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Conosci la verità!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Know the truth!

definitions.note: Present tense (noi). Can also mean “we meet / we get to know” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Conosciamo bene questo quartiere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We know this neighborhood well.

definitions.note: Used with "voi"; this form is typically the present subjunctive (e.g., after "che", "spero che").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che conosciate già la città.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you already know the city.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of "conoscere"; often agrees with a feminine direct object (e.g., "l'ho conosciuta" = "I met her").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’ho conosciuta ieri alla festa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I met her yesterday at the party.

definitions.note: feminine plural form (used with feminine plural nouns; also as a past participle in passive/compound forms)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono persone molto conosciute in città.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are very well-known people in the city.

definitions.note: past participle of "conoscere"; often used with "avere" in compound tenses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Li ho conosciuti ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I met them yesterday.

definitions.note: Past participle of "conoscere"; often used like an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un attore molto conosciuto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s a very well-known actor.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “famous” or “widely known,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un autore conosciuto in tutta Italia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a well-known author throughout Italy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Conosco bene questa città.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I know this city well.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Conoscono bene questa città.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They know this city well.

definitions.note: Often used both for winning something (a prize, a position) and for winning someone over (earning someone’s affection or trust).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha conquistato la medaglia d’oro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He won the gold medal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono consapevole del problema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m aware of the problem.

definitions.note: plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo consapevoli del problema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are aware of the problem.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La consegna è prevista per domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The delivery is scheduled for tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used for delivering packages or handing in homework/documents.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Consegna i compiti domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: (He/She) hands in the homework tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used for delivering something (a package, goods) or handing something in (an assignment, documents).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo consegnare il pacco entro domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to deliver the package by tomorrow.

definitions.native: to deliver it, to hand it in
definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “lo” (“it”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo consegnarlo entro domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to hand it in by tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used to tell a group of people what to do ("you" plural), e.g. as an imperative.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Consegnate il modulo entro domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hand in the form by tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho consegnato il pacco al vicino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I delivered the package to the neighbor.

definitions.note: Often used with informal "tu" (present tense). It can also appear in the present subjunctive (e.g., after "che" or in conditional sentences).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se consegni il modulo oggi, ti rispondo domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you hand in the form today, I’ll reply to you tomorrow.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto), 3rd person singular (he/she/it). Often used in narratives; in everyday speech many speakers prefer the passato prossimo.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il corriere consegnò il pacco nel pomeriggio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The courier delivered the package in the afternoon.

definitions.note: Plural of "conseguenza".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ogni scelta ha conseguenze.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every choice has consequences.

definitions.note: Often used in legal/official contexts, especially for consent (permission).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho bisogno del tuo consenso per usare questa foto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need your consent to use this photo.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo metodo conserva il cibo più a lungo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This method preserves the food longer.

definitions.note: Often used for keeping something in good condition (food, documents, memories).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devi conservare questi documenti in un posto sicuro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to keep these documents in a safe place.

definitions.note: Often used for political views; can also describe a cautious/traditional approach in general.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio nonno è molto conservatore in politica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather is very conservative in politics.

definitions.note: Often refers to a person with conservative political views.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio zio è un conservatore e vota sempre per i partiti di destra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My uncle is a conservative and always votes for right-wing parties.

definitions.note: A professional who preserves, restores, or looks after artworks or historical objects (e.g., in a museum).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il conservatore del museo sta restaurando un dipinto antico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The museum conservator is restoring an old painting.

definitions.note: Can be present tense (“he/she considers”) or an informal command (“consider!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Marco considera l'idea interessante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Marco considers the idea interesting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Considerando il traffico, partiamo prima.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Considering the traffic, let's leave earlier.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Considerano questa opzione la migliore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They consider this option the best.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo considerare tutte le opzioni prima di decidere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to consider all the options before deciding.

definitions.native: you consider, you take into account
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Considerate tutti i dettagli prima di decidere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You consider all the details before deciding.

definitions.note: can be used as a plural or formal command (imperative)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Considerate le conseguenze prima di agire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Consider the consequences before acting.

definitions.note: Often used as a past participle (e.g., with "sono"), or as an adjective meaning "regarded as".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questi libri sono considerati molto importanti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These books are considered very important.

definitions.note: Plural imperative (addressing more than one person).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Considerati fortunati: avete trovato i biglietti all’ultimo minuto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Consider yourselves lucky: you found the tickets at the last minute.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È considerato un esperto.
