definitions.note: Often used for a sudden fall in prices, the market, or the economy.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo la notizia, c’è stato un crollo in borsa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the news, there was a crash on the stock market.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto) of "crollare"; often used in written narratives and in some regions of Italy.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il ponte crollò durante la tempesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bridge collapsed during the storm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un momento cruciale per il progetto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a crucial moment for the project.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "crudo".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preferisco la verdura cruda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prefer raw vegetables.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preferisco le verdure crude.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prefer raw vegetables.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È stato crudele con il cane.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was cruel to the dog.

definitions.note: plural form (masculine or feminine)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non essere crudeli con gli animali.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t be cruel to animals.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La crudeltà contro gli animali è inaccettabile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Cruelty against animals is unacceptable.

definitions.note: Often used for food (e.g., raw meat/fish/vegetables).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preferisco il pesce crudo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prefer raw fish.

definitions.note: Used for things like a harsh truth or a harsh reality.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una verità cruda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a harsh truth.

definitions.note: Plural of "cubetto"; often used for small food pieces (e.g., diced ham, cheese cubes, ice cubes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Taglia il formaggio a cubetti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Cut the cheese into cubes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Metti due cucchiai di zucchero nel caffè.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put two spoons of sugar in the coffee.

definitions.note: plural of "cucchiaino" (a small spoon, often used for stirring coffee or for tea)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi servono due cucchiaini per il caffè.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need two teaspoons for the coffee.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi dai un cucchiaio, per favore?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you give me a spoon, please?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il cane dorme nella sua cuccia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog sleeps in its doghouse/pet bed.

definitions.note: Often used for dogs (“puppy”), but can refer to the young of other animals too.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il cucciolo dorme nella sua cuccia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The puppy sleeps in its doghouse.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La cucina è molto piccola, ma luminosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kitchen is very small, but bright.

definitions.note: Often used to mean the activity or style of cooking (e.g., "cucina italiana").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi piace la cucina italiana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like Italian cooking.

definitions.note: Verb form of "cucinare". Not the noun "cucina" meaning "kitchen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mia sorella cucina spesso la sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister cooks often in the evening.

definitions.note: past historic (passato remoto), 1st person singular
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri sera cucinai la pasta per tutti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night I cooked pasta for everyone.

definitions.note: present gerund (used with "stare" to mean "(is/are) cooking")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto cucinando la pasta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm cooking pasta.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi piace cucinare la pasta la domenica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like to cook pasta on Sundays.

definitions.native: cook for me, cook for myself
definitions.note: Infinitive with the attached pronoun “mi” (“me”). Depending on context it can mean someone cooks for you or you cook for yourself.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi cucinarmi qualcosa di semplice?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you cook me something simple?

definitions.note: 2nd-person plural (voi) form; used for “you (all) cook/are cooking.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Di solito cucinate la pasta per cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Usually you (all) cook pasta for dinner.

definitions.note: 2nd-person plural command; used to tell a group to cook.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ragazzi, cucinate voi stasera!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Guys, you (all) cook tonight!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho cucinato la pasta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I cooked the pasta.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il pesce è già cucinato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fish is already cooked.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho cucinato il pollo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I cooked the chicken.

definitions.note: Third-person singular future tense (he/she/it will cook).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stasera cucinerà la pasta per tutti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tonight, he/she will cook pasta for everyone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cucini spesso a casa?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you often cook at home?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi cucino la pasta per cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I cook pasta for dinner.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri sera cucinò la pasta per tutti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night he/she cooked pasta for everyone.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto), 3rd person singular: “he/she cooked.” Common in writing and in some regions; in speech many people use passato prossimo instead.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri sera cucinò una pasta deliziosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night he/she cooked a delicious pasta dish.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: So cucire un bottone.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can sew a button.

definitions.note: Plural form of "cuffia"; in everyday Italian, "cuffie" is commonly used to mean headphones (or a headset).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho dimenticato le cuffie a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I forgot my headphones at home.

definitions.note: female form; used for a female cousin.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mia cugina vive a Milano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My cousin lives in Milan.

definitions.note: Plural of "cugina"; used for female cousins.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le mie cugine vivono a Roma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My female cousins live in Rome.

definitions.note: plural of "cugino"; can refer to male cousins or a mixed-gender group
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I miei cugini abitano a Firenze.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My cousins live in Florence.

definitions.note: male cousin; feminine is "cugina".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Marco è mio cugino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Marco is my cousin.

definitions.note: Used mainly in more formal Italian; it refers back to a person or thing already mentioned and is often used after a preposition (e.g., di cui, a cui, con cui).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La ragazza di cui parli è mia sorella.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The girl you’re talking about is my sister.

definitions.note: Often used with di (e.g., il ragazzo di cui conosco il padre = the boy whose father I know).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un amico di cui mi fido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s a friend I trust.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il bambino dorme nella culla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The baby sleeps in the cradle.

definitions.note: Often used for a baby’s small bed (like a cradle/crib).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo comprato una culla nuova per il neonato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We bought a new crib for the newborn.

definitions.note: Vulgar/informal; avoid in polite situations. A more polite word is "sedere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi fa male il culo dopo quel giro in bici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My butt hurts after that bike ride.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi piace conoscere la cultura italiana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like getting to know Italian culture.

definitions.note: Feminine form of "cuoco"; refers to a woman who cooks (professionally or at home).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mia madre è una cuoca bravissima.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My mother is a really great cook.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (io/lui/lei) of "cuocere"; also used as a formal (Lei) command.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che cuocia la pasta al dente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope (that) he/she cooks the pasta al dente.

definitions.note: third-person plural present tense of "cuocere"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le verdure cuociono in dieci minuti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The vegetables cook in ten minutes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato un cuociriso per fare il riso più facilmente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a rice cooker to make rice more easily.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio padre è cuoco in un ristorante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My father is a cook in a restaurant.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho il cuore pieno di gioia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My heart is full of joy.

definitions.note: Plural of "cuore".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo disegnato due cuori sul biglietto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We drew two hearts on the card.

definitions.note: Commonly used in Italian as an English loanword.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per dessert ho preso un cupcake al cioccolato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For dessert I got a chocolate cupcake.

definitions.note: Often used for dim light, colors, sounds, or an overall mood/atmosphere.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La stanza è cupa e silenziosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The room is dark and quiet.

definitions.note: Often used both for taking care of someone/something and for medical care.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Grazie per la tua cura.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thank you for your care.

definitions.note: Common in medical contexts (e.g., a treatment for an illness).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa cura funziona bene.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This treatment works well.

definitions.note: Can also be used as the informal singular command “take care of!” (tu imperative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei cura sempre i suoi figli.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She always takes care of her children.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il medico cura i pazienti con molta attenzione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor treats the patients with a lot of care.

definitions.native: to take care of, to look after
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo curare mia nonna questo pomeriggio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to take care of my grandma this afternoon.

definitions.note: Used especially in the medical sense (treat an illness, a patient).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il medico sta curando la mia tosse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor is treating my cough.

definitions.note: Past participle of "curare". It can look like English "curate," but the common meaning is about caring for/treating (often medically), not selecting/organizing content.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho curato il paziente per tre mesi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I treated the patient for three months.

definitions.note: Plural form of "cura".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le cure per i bambini richiedono molta pazienza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Caring for children requires a lot of patience.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mia sorella è molto curiosa e fa sempre domande.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is very curious and always asks questions.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le bambine sono curiose di sapere la verità.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The girls are curious to know the truth.

definitions.note: plural masculine form (also used for mixed-gender groups)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I bambini sono curiosi e fanno molte domande.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are curious and ask a lot of questions.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per curiosità, ho aperto la finestra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Out of curiosity, I opened the window.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono curioso di sapere cosa è successo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m curious to know what happened.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A cena abbiamo mangiato un curry di verdure.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For dinner we ate a vegetable curry.

definitions.note: plural of "cuscino"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sul letto ci sono due cuscini.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are two pillows on the bed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato un cuscino nuovo per il letto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a new pillow for the bed.

definitions.note: Often used for someone who looks after a building (e.g., a school or apartment building).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il custode apre la scuola alle sette.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The caretaker opens the school at seven.

definitions.note: Often used for a protective case (for glasses, a phone, an instrument, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato una custodia per il mio telefono.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a case for my phone.

definitions.note: Used in contexts like legal custody or being in police custody.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo l’arresto, l’uomo è rimasto in custodia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the arrest, the man remained in custody.

definitions.note: Elided form of “ci” before a vowel (common in “c’è” = “there is/are”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’è un supermercato vicino a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There’s a supermarket near home.

definitions.note: Elided form of “ci” before a vowel.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’hanno detto di aspettare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They told us to wait.

definitions.note: Contraction of “di” used before a vowel (e.g., d’Italia, d’accordo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono d'accordo con te.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I agree with you.

definitions.note: used to indicate origin or starting point
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vengo da Roma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m from Rome.

definitions.note: used with people to mean “at/to someone’s home, office, etc.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stasera vado da Lucia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tonight I’m going to Lucia’s place.

definitions.note: used with time expressions to show how long something has been happening
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Studio italiano da due anni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve been studying Italian for two years.

definitions.note: used to indicate the agent in passive sentences
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il libro è stato scritto da Maria.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book was written by Maria.

definitions.note: Imperative form of "dare" with the pronoun "ci" (to us).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dacci una mano, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Give us a hand, please.

definitions.note: Contraction of “da” + “gli” (plural masculine “the”); used before plural masculine nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vengo dagli amici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m coming from my friends.

definitions.note: Imperative form of "dare" with the indirect object pronoun "gli" (= to him). Often written without the accent; with the accent it’s "dàgli".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dagli un bicchiere d’acqua, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Give him a glass of water, please.

definitions.note: Contraction of "da + i" ("from/by/at" + masculine plural "the").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vengo dai miei amici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m coming from my friends’ place.

definitions.note: contraction of “da + i” (used before a masculine plural noun)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vengo dai miei amici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m coming from my friends’ place.

definitions.note: Often used to encourage someone, show impatience, or urge them to do something (informal in tone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dai, sbrigati!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come on, hurry up!

definitions.note: 2nd-person singular ("you") of dare in the present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi dai un bicchiere d’acqua, per favore?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you give me a glass of water, please?

definitions.note: Imperative (command) to one person; often used on its own like “come on!”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dai il libro a Marco!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Give the book to Marco!

definitions.note: Contraction of "da" + "il".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vengo dal supermercato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m coming from the supermarket.

definitions.note: Contraction of "da" + "il"; used before masculine singular nouns starting with most consonants.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vengo dal supermercato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m coming from the supermarket.

definitions.note: Contraction of "da" + "la"; used before a feminine singular noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vengo dalla stazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I come from the station.

definitions.note: Contraction of "da" + "la"; can indicate the agent in passive constructions (before a feminine singular noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La lettera è stata scritta dalla segretaria.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The letter was written by the secretary.

definitions.note: Contraction of "da" + "la" (feminine singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vengo dalla stazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m coming from the station.

definitions.note: Contraction of "da" + "la" (feminine singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vengo dalla stazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m coming from the station.

definitions.note: Contraction of "da" + "le" (feminine plural "the"). Used before feminine plural nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Torno dalle mie amiche domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m coming back from my (female) friends tomorrow.

definitions.note: Contraction of "da" + "le" (plural feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vengo dalle montagne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I come from the mountains.

definitions.note: Contraction of "da" + "le" (feminine plural "the").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vengo dalle montagne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I come from the mountains.

definitions.note: Imperative form of "dare" with the attached indirect object pronoun "le" (= to her).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dalle questo messaggio, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Give her this message, please.

definitions.note: Contraction of “da + lo” (used before a masculine singular noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Torno dallo psicologo alle cinque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm coming back from the psychologist's at five.

definitions.note: Imperative of "dare" + the direct object pronoun "lo".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dallo a me, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Give it to me, please.

definitions.note: Refers to a person who has color blindness.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio fratello è daltonico e fa fatica a distinguere il rosso dal verde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is color-blind and has trouble telling red from green.

definitions.note: Imperative with pronouns: dammi (to me) + la (it, feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dammela subito, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Give it to me right away, please.

definitions.note: Informal (tu) command form of "dare" with pronouns attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dammelo, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Give it to me, please.

definitions.native: give me some, give me some of it
definitions.note: Informal singular imperative of "dare" with pronouns attached (="da' + me + ne").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dammene un po', per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Give me some, please.

definitions.note: Informal (tu) command form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dammi il libro, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Give me the book, please.

definitions.note: gerund of "dare"; often used to mean "while giving" or "by giving" depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto dando un libro a Marco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m giving a book to Marco.

definitions.note: Often used in strong language or to express anger/frustration (like “damn”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa macchina è dannata: non parte mai!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This car is damned: it never starts!

definitions.note: Informal/emphatic; often used to intensify a statement (similar to “really” or “so” in tone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fa dannatamente freddo oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s damn cold today.

definitions.note: Often used in exclamations or as a mild insult; can also mean “cursed” in a more literal/religious sense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Che giornata dannata!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What a damned day!

definitions.note: Used as a mild swear word to express anger or frustration.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dannazione! Ho dimenticato le chiavi a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Damn! I forgot my keys at home.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of "danneggiare"; often used like an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La valigia è danneggiata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The suitcase is damaged.

definitions.note: Can be present tense (voi) or the plural informal imperative.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se le usate male, danneggiate le cuffie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you use them badly, you damage the headphones.

definitions.note: Feminine plural past participle, often used like an adjective or with 'essere'.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le valigie sono arrivate danneggiate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The suitcases arrived damaged.

definitions.note: Often used like an adjective (past participle of "danneggiare").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il telefono è danneggiato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The phone is damaged.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il pacco è arrivato danneggiato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The package arrived damaged.

definitions.note: simple past (passato remoto) form; common in narration and written Italian
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La grandine danneggiò le auto parcheggiate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hail damaged the parked cars.

definitions.note: Plural of "danno".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’incidente ha causato molti danni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The accident caused a lot of damage.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il temporale ha causato molti danni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The storm caused a lot of damage.

definitions.note: third-person plural ("they") present tense of "dare"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi danno un libro ogni anno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They give me a book every year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi piace la danza classica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like classical dance.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui danza sul palco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He dances on the stage.

definitions.note: present gerund of "danzare"; used to mean "while dancing" or to form progressive tenses with "stare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto danzando con i miei amici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m dancing with my friends.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti va di danzare con me?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you feel like dancing with me?

definitions.note: past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri sera danzarono fino a mezzanotte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night they danced until midnight.

definitions.note: Often used for "you (plural) dance/are dancing" or as an imperative meaning "dance!" (to a group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ragazzi, danzate con me!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Guys, dance with me!

definitions.note: past participle of "danzare"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho danzato tutta la notte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I danced all night.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (past imperfect): describes an ongoing or habitual action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri sera danzava con gli amici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night he/she was dancing with friends.

definitions.note: Usually used as present subjunctive (e.g., "che tu danzi").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che tu danzi con noi stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you dance with us tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ogni sabato sera danziamo con gli amici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every Saturday evening we dance with friends.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho cercato dappertutto, ma non trovo le chiavi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I looked everywhere, but I can’t find the keys.

definitions.note: Second person singular (tu), simple future of "dare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi darai una mano domani?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Will you give me a hand tomorrow?

definitions.note: Third-person plural future tense (they will give).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani daranno i compiti agli studenti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow they will give the homework to the students.

definitions.note: Infinitive of "dare" with the pronoun "ci" attached (="to us").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi darci una mano?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you give us a hand?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi puoi dare una mano?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you give me a hand?

definitions.note: Conditional tense (third person singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti darebbe una mano se potesse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She would help you if he/she could.

definitions.note: Second person singular of the conditional present (tu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi daresti una mano con i compiti?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Would you give me a hand with the homework?

definitions.note: second-person plural (voi) future tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi darete una mano domani?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Will you give me a hand tomorrow?

definitions.native: to give him, to give to him
definitions.note: Infinitive with the indirect object pronoun “gli” (“to him”) attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio dargli un regalo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to give him a gift.

definitions.note: This is the verb "dare" with the indirect object pronoun "le" (= to her) attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio darle un regalo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to give her a gift.

definitions.note: Combination of the verb "dare" (to give) + the direct object pronoun "lo" (it).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi darlo a Marco?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you give it to Marco?

definitions.note: Combination of "dare" + indirect object pronoun "mi" (to me) + direct object pronoun "lo" (it).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi darmelo, per favore?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you give it to me, please?

definitions.note: Infinitive of "dare" with the indirect object pronoun "mi" (“me”) attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi darmi una mano?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you give me a hand?

definitions.note: Infinitive of "dare" with the indirect object pronoun "mi" attached ("to me").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi darmi una mano?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you give me a hand?

definitions.native: to happen, to occur; (può darsi) maybe
definitions.note: Often used impersonally in expressions like “può darsi (che…)” meaning “maybe / it’s possible (that…)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Può darsi che oggi piova.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Maybe it will rain today.

definitions.native: to make an effort, to work hard
definitions.note: Common in the expression “darsi da fare”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per finire in tempo, dobbiamo darsi da fare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: To finish on time, we have to work hard.

definitions.note: includes the indirect object pronoun “ti” = “to you” (informal singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio darti un consiglio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to give you some advice.

definitions.note: Includes the pronoun “vi” = “to you” (plural, or formal “you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Posso darvi una mano?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can I give you a hand?

definitions.native: to give you (plural), to give to you
definitions.note: Includes the pronoun "vi" (= to you / you all).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Posso darvi una mano?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can I give you a hand?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani darà il libro a Marco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow he/she will give the book to Marco.

definitions.note: First-person singular (io) future tense of "dare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te lo darò domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will give it to you tomorrow.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of "dare"; often used in the passive (e.g., "è stata data" = "was given").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La risposta è stata data ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The answer was given yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used for calendar dates (e.g., birthdays). It may look like English “data”, but English “data” is usually “dati” in Italian.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Qual è la data di nascita?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is the date of birth?

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of the adjective/past participle "dato".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una spiegazione data dall’insegnante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s an explanation given by the teacher.

definitions.note: Second-person plural form of "dare" ("you all / you (plural) give"; also used as the plural imperative "give!").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi date un consiglio?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you give me some advice?

definitions.note: Command form (imperative) addressed to more than one person (voi).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dateci un minuto, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Give us a minute, please.

definitions.note: Imperative (voi) form with the indirect object pronoun “gli” attached; means “give to him.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dategli il libro, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Give him the book, please.

definitions.note: Imperative form with the pronoun “-le” attached (usually “them,” feminine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Datele a Maria, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Give them to Maria, please.

definitions.note: Imperative (plural “you”): used to tell more than one person to give something to the speaker.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Datemi un minuto, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Give me a minute, please.

definitions.note: 2nd person plural imperative of "dare" with the reflexive pronoun "vi" (“to yourselves”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Datevi un po’ di tempo per riposare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Give yourselves a bit of time to rest.

definitions.note: past participle of "dare" (masculine plural)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Li ho già dati a Marco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve already given them to Marco.

definitions.note: plural of "dato" (in the sense of information/data)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho salvato i dati sul computer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saved the data on the computer.

definitions.note: Past participle of "dare"; often used with "avere" to form the past tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti ho dato le chiavi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I gave you the keys.

definitions.note: the fruit of the date palm; plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi piacciono i datteri con le noci.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like dates with walnuts.

definitions.note: Informal (tu) imperative of "dare" with the reflexive pronoun "ti" ("to yourself").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Datti una possibilità.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Give yourself a chance.

definitions.note: Likely a misspelling of “davanti” (“in front (of)”), but “davanri” itself isn’t standard Italian.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non so cosa significhi “davanri”.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t know what “davanri” means.

definitions.note: Often used with "a" (davanti a + noun/pronoun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’è un parco davanti alla scuola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There’s a park in front of the school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La fermata dell’autobus è proprio davanti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus stop is right in front.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Davvero non lo so.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I really don't know.

definitions.note: Subjunctive form of "dovere"; often sounds formal/literary. In everyday Italian you more often see "debba" in set phrases or formal writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È possibile che debba partire domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s possible that I have to leave tomorrow.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (they). Often used after expressions like "è necessario che" (it’s necessary that).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È importante che debbano partire presto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that they must leave early.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho molti debiti e devo risparmiare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have many debts and I have to save money.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho un debito con la banca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a debt with the bank.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi sento debole oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel weak today.

definitions.note: Often used with a possessive (e.g., "il mio debole") to mean something you can’t resist or a personal weak point.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il mio debole è il cioccolato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My weakness is chocolate.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In squadra non c’è spazio per un debole.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There’s no room in the team for a weakling.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La debolezza dei muscoli può causare dolore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Muscle weakness can cause pain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ognuno ha le proprie debolezze.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Everyone has their own weaknesses.

definitions.note: plural form of "debole"; can describe people, things, or arguments.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho le braccia deboli dopo la palestra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My arms are weak after the gym.

definitions.note: Used as a plural noun meaning “weak people / the weak ones.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dobbiamo proteggere i deboli.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We must protect the weak.

definitions.note: Often used for drinks like coffee (e.g., caffè decaffeinato).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei un caffè decaffeinato, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like a decaffeinated coffee, please.

definitions.note: Often used for the most senior person in a group (e.g., the dean of a faculty, or the longest-serving member).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il decano della facoltà terrà il discorso inaugurale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dean of the faculty will give the opening speech.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form; often used in formal contexts (e.g., legal or medical) to refer to someone who has died.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La signora Rossi è deceduta ieri sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Mrs. Rossi passed away last night.

definitions.note: More formal than "morto"; often used in official or medical contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio nonno è deceduto nel 2018.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather died in 2018.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Negli ultimi decenni, la città è cambiata molto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In recent decades, the city has changed a lot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cerco un ristorante decente vicino a qui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m looking for a decent restaurant near here.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 1st person plural of "decidere"; common in writing and storytelling, less common in everyday conversation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alla fine decidemmo di partire il giorno dopo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end we decided to leave the next day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo decidere cosa fare domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to decide what to do tomorrow.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of "decidere"; used when the direct object is feminine (often shown by "la" / "l'" before the verb).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'ho decisa ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I decided it yesterday.

definitions.note: Used to emphasize a strong opinion or clear degree (often like “definitely” in conversation).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Decisamente sì, voglio venire con voi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Definitely yes, I want to come with you.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) form, often used in narratives and in some regions instead of the passato prossimo.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo una lunga discussione, decise di accettare l’offerta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After a long discussion, he/she decided to accept the offer.

definitions.note: Passato remoto (simple past) of "decidere"; often used in narratives and in some regions more than in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alla fine decisero di partire il giorno dopo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end they decided to leave the next day.

definitions.note: Past historic/simple past form of "decidere" (used often in writing and storytelling, especially in some regions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Decisi di partire il giorno dopo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I decided to leave the next day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una decisione importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s an important decision.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dobbiamo prendere decisioni importanti oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to make important decisions today.

definitions.note: past participle of "decidere"; also commonly used as an adjective meaning "decided" or "determined".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho deciso di partire domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I decided to leave tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often followed by “a” + infinitive to mean “determined to (do something)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono deciso a partire domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m determined to leave tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto decorando la torta per il compleanno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m decorating the cake for the birthday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo decorato la torta per il compleanno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We decorated the cake for the birthday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho decorato l'albero di Natale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I decorated the Christmas tree.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo comprato una decorazione per l’albero di Natale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We bought a decoration for the Christmas tree.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le decorazioni di Natale sono già appese.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Christmas decorations are already hung up.

definitions.note: simple past (passato remoto), often used in narratives and in some regions instead of the present perfect
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per la festa, Giulia decorò la sala con luci e fiori.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For the party, Giulia decorated the room with lights and flowers.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho dedicato questa canzone a mia madre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I dedicated this song to my mother.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person singular (he/she/it dedicated). Common in narratives and written Italian; in speech many people use passato prossimo instead.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dedicò il libro a sua madre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He dedicated the book to his mother.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lavora con grande dedizione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She works with great dedication.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa è la versione definitiva del documento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is the final version of the document.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Definitivamente voglio provare questo ristorante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I definitely want to try this restaurant.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts or in obituaries to refer to someone who has died.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il defunto era molto rispettato in città.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The deceased person was very respected in the city.

definitions.note: Contraction of "di" + "gli" (plural masculine "the"); used for "of the" or as a partitive meaning "some".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho bisogno degli appunti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need some notes.

definitions.note: Plural partitive article (di + gli); used before masculine plural nouns (especially starting with z, s+consonant, gn, ps, x, y, or a vowel).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei degli spaghetti, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like some spaghetti, please.

definitions.note: Plural form used to mean “of the” before masculine plural nouns (di + gli), often in expressions like “the color of the eyes”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi piace il colore degli occhi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like the color of the eyes.

definitions.note: Contraction of “di” + plural “gli”; used before masculine plural nouns starting with a vowel or with s+consonant, z, gn, ps, pn, x, y.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho bisogno degli amici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need (some) friends.

definitions.note: Contraction of "di" + "gli". Used as an indefinite plural article before masculine plural nouns (often meaning "some"), and also used to mean "of the" in expressions like "uno degli..." (= "one of the...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei comprare degli spaghetti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to buy some spaghetti.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of “degno” (used with feminine nouns or feminine subjects)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei è degna di fiducia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is worthy of trust.

definitions.note: Often used with “di” + noun or infinitive (e.g., “degno di fiducia”, “degno di nota”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È degno di fiducia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is worthy of trust.

definitions.note: Articulated preposition: di + i.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho paura dei cani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m afraid of dogs.

definitions.note: Partitive plural (masculine); used with plural countable nouns to mean an indefinite quantity.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei comprare dei libri in italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to buy some books in Italian.

definitions.note: Contraction of "di" + "i". Often used as a partitive article meaning “some”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei dei biscotti, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like some cookies, please.

definitions.note: Masculine plural partitive article; used to mean an unspecified amount.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei comprare dei pomodori.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to buy some tomatoes.

definitions.note: Contraction of "di" + "i"; used to mean "of the" before a masculine plural noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Parliamo dei libri che hai letto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s talk about the books you’ve read.

definitions.note: Contraction of "di" + "il".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Parliamo del film stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s talk about the movie tonight.

definitions.note: Contraction of "di + il"; used with masculine singular nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il colore del cielo è bellissimo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The color of the sky is beautiful.

definitions.note: Contraction of "di" + "il" (used before a masculine singular noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il libro del ragazzo è sul tavolo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boy's book is on the table.

definitions.note: Contraction of "di + il"; used before a masculine singular noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il libro del ragazzo è sul tavolo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boy’s book is on the table.

definitions.note: Plural of "delegato" (a person chosen to represent a group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I delegati hanno votato a favore della proposta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The delegates voted in favor of the proposal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I delfini nuotano vicino alla barca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dolphins swim near the boat.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo visto un delfino vicino alla barca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We saw a dolphin near the boat.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of “delicato”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una situazione delicata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a delicate situation.

definitions.note: Often used for things that need careful handling, or for sensitive situations/topics.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo bicchiere è molto delicato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This glass is very delicate.

definitions.note: Can describe people (easily upset) or situations/topics that require tact.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un argomento delicato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a sensitive topic.

definitions.note: Often used figuratively to mean “wild/crazy” (e.g., a frantic pace or a chaotic scene).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo la febbre alta, era ancora delirante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the high fever, he was still delirious.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of “delizioso” (used with feminine singular nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa torta è deliziosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This cake is delicious.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le torte sono deliziose.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cakes are delicious.

definitions.note: plural masculine form; can also be used for a mixed-gender group
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questi biscotti sono deliziosi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These cookies are delicious.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo dolce è delizioso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This dessert is delicious.

definitions.note: Contraction of “di + la”; used with feminine singular nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La copertina della rivista è rossa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cover of the magazine is red.

definitions.note: Contraction of "di" + feminine singular "la"; used before a feminine singular noun (e.g., "della casa").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La chiave è della macchina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The key is from the car.

definitions.note: contraction of “di” + “la” (feminine singular)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono della città.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m from the city.

definitions.note: Contraction of "di" + feminine singular "la" (often translated as “of the” or “from the” depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il colore della macchina è rosso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The color of the car is red.

definitions.note: Contraction of "di" + "la"; used before feminine singular nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho bisogno della chiave.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need the key.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form. Can be a partitive article (“some”) or a contraction of “di + le” (“of the”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei delle mele, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like some apples, please.

definitions.note: Contraction of "di" + "le" (feminine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho bisogno delle chiavi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need the keys.

definitions.note: Feminine plural partitive article (di + le), used before feminine plural nouns to mean an unspecified amount.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei delle fragole, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like some strawberries, please.

definitions.note: Feminine plural contracted preposition (di + le).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Parliamo delle regole della classe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s talk about the class rules.

definitions.note: Contraction of "di" + "le". Often used as a partitive meaning "some" with feminine plural nouns, or as "of the".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei delle mele, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like some apples, please.

definitions.note: Often used in legal contexts (e.g., accusations that harm someone’s reputation).
