definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Direbbe che è una buona idea?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Would you say it’s a good idea?

definitions.note: conditional form, often used to give a polite suggestion or opinion
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Direi che possiamo andare adesso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would say we can go now.

definitions.note: First-person plural simple future of “dire.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani diremo la verità a tutti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will tell everyone the truth.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto), often used in written stories and history.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il maestro diresse l’orchestra per tutta la serata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The conductor directed the orchestra for the whole evening.

definitions.note: Second-person plural conditional (voi).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Che cosa direste se vi dicessi la verità?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What would you say if I told you the truth?

definitions.note: second-person singular conditional (tu)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Che cosa diresti se ti dicessi la verità?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What would you say if I told you the truth?

definitions.note: second-person plural (voi) future tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani direte la verità a tutti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow you will tell the truth to everyone.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "diretto"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo preso la strada diretta per il centro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We took the direct road to the city center.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi parlare direttamente con il manager.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can speak directly with the manager.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Riceviamo informazioni dirette dalla fonte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We receive direct information from the source.

definitions.note: plural masculine form of "diretto"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo preso voli diretti per Roma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We took direct flights to Rome.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo è un volo diretto per Roma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is a direct flight to Rome.

definitions.note: Often used for routes/directions (e.g., “go straight”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vai diretto e poi gira a sinistra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Go straight and then turn left.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho diretto la riunione ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I directed the meeting yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il direttore della scuola parla con i genitori.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The school principal talks with the parents.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non so in che direzione andare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t know which direction to go.

definitions.note: Often used to refer to the people who run an organization (e.g., a school or company).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La direzione ha deciso di chiudere l’ufficio alle 17.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Management decided to close the office at 5 p.m.

definitions.note: Plural of "direzione".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scusi, può darmi delle direzioni per arrivare alla stazione?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Excuse me, can you give me directions to get to the station?

definitions.note: Plural, often used in the sense of "organizational departments" (e.g., school, company).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le direzioni dell’azienda si incontrano ogni lunedì.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company’s departments meet every Monday.

definitions.note: Infinitive "dire" + indirect object pronoun "gli" (= to him).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio dirgli la verità.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to tell him the truth.

definitions.note: Infinitive of "dire" with attached object pronouns: "gli" (to him/her/them) + "lo" (it).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo dirglielo subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to tell him/her/them right away.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei dirige il team con molta calma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She leads the team very calmly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo visto un dirigibile volare sopra la città.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We saw an airship flying over the city.

definitions.note: Plural form of "diritto".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tutti hanno gli stessi diritti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Everyone has the same rights.

definitions.note: Often used for a legal right or entitlement; also used in plural (diritti) for “rights.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hai il diritto di sapere la verità.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have the right to know the truth.

definitions.note: Infinitive of "dire" with the direct-object pronoun "la" attached (="it", feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non so come dirla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t know how to say it.

definitions.note: Literally "to tell to her" ("le" = to her, indirect object pronoun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio dirle la verità.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to tell her the truth.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun "lo" (= "it").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo dirlo subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to say it right away.

definitions.note: Infinitive of "dire" with attached pronouns: mi (to me) + lo (it).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi dirmelo domani?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you tell it to me tomorrow?

definitions.note: Combination of the infinitive "dire" + the indirect object pronoun "mi" (to me).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi dirmi la verità?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you tell me the truth?

definitions.note: Literally “dire” (to say/tell) + the object pronoun “mi” (me) attached to the end.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi dirmi la verità?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you tell me the truth?

definitions.note: Infinitive with attached pronouns: "dir" (dire) + "te" (to you, informal) + "lo" (it).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Volevo dirtelo ieri, ma non ho avuto tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wanted to tell it to you yesterday, but I didn’t have time.

definitions.note: Includes the indirect object pronoun “ti” (= “to you”, informal singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo dirti una cosa importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to tell you something important.

definitions.note: Made of "dire" + "ve" (to you, plural / to you all) + "lo" (it).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo dirvelo subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to tell it to you right away.

definitions.note: Includes the pronoun “vi” (= “you” plural, and sometimes polite singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo dirvi una cosa importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to tell you something important.

definitions.note: Includes the pronoun “vi” (= you plural; also used as formal “you” in some contexts).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei dirvi la verità.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to tell you the truth.

definitions.note: Third-person singular future tense of "dire"; can mean "he/she/it will say."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dirà la verità domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She will tell the truth tomorrow.

definitions.native: I will say, I will tell
definitions.note: First-person singular future tense of "dire".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te lo dirò domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will tell you tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La città sta migliorando i servizi per le persone con disabilità.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The city is improving services for people with disabilities.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono molti disaccordi tra i due partiti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many disagreements between the two parties.

definitions.note: Often used for a mild setback or displeasure.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Con mio grande disappunto, il treno è stato cancellato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: To my great disappointment, the train was canceled.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'uomo era disarmato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The man was unarmed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo la tempesta, la città era un disastro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the storm, the city was a disaster.

definitions.note: Plural of "disco".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato due dischi in vinile al mercato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought two vinyl records at the market.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A scuola la disciplina è importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At school, discipline is important.

definitions.note: Common in academic contexts to mean an area of study.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La biologia è una disciplina scientifica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Biology is a scientific subject.

definitions.note: Often used for music: a CD/record, or a disco (dance club) depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato un disco nuovo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a new record.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I discorsi del sindaco sono sempre molto chiari.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mayor's speeches are always very clear.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non voglio fare discorsi adesso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to have conversations right now.

definitions.note: Often used for a formal speech or a topic being discussed (e.g., "un discorso interessante" = an interesting discussion/topic).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il presidente ha fatto un discorso breve.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The president gave a short speech.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stasera andiamo in discoteca con gli amici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tonight we’re going to the nightclub with friends.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha risposto in modo discreta durante la riunione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She answered in a discreet way during the meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Parla discretamente al telefono in treno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He speaks discreetly on the phone on the train.

definitions.note: Often describes a person who is tactful and doesn’t attract attention.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio fratello è molto discreto e non parla mai dei fatti degli altri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is very discreet and never talks about other people’s business.

definitions.note: Commonly used to say something is okay or fairly good (not excellent).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il ristorante è discreto, ma non è il migliore della città.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The restaurant is decent, but it’s not the best in the city.

definitions.note: Often used in the sense of being tactful or keeping something confidential.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti chiedo la massima discrezione su questa notizia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ask you for the utmost discretion about this news.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La discriminazione sul lavoro è illegale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Discrimination at work is illegal.

definitions.note: simple past (passato remoto), often used in narratives and in some regions
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Durante la riunione, il direttore discusse i risultati con il team.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: During the meeting, the director discussed the results with the team.

definitions.note: past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo la riunione, discussero a lungo del progetto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the meeting, they discussed the project for a long time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo avuto una discussione molto interessante in classe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had a very interesting discussion in class.

definitions.note: plural of "discussione"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo avuto molte discussioni su questo argomento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had many discussions about this topic.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo discusso del problema ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We discussed the problem yesterday.

definitions.note: gerund form (used for actions in progress or as “by/while …-ing”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stiamo discutendo del problema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are discussing the problem.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani discuteranno del progetto in riunione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow they will discuss the project in the meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dobbiamo discutere del progetto domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to discuss the project tomorrow.

definitions.note: Can also mean “designs” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mia sorella disegna un gatto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister draws a cat.

definitions.note: Informal (tu) command form with the object pronoun “mi” (= me).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Disegnami un gatto, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Draw me a cat, please.

definitions.note: Gerund form: often used like “(while) drawing.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto disegnando un gatto sul quaderno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m drawing a cat in my notebook.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi piace disegnare animali.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like to draw animals.

definitions.note: Form of "disegnare" used with "voi" (you plural): can mean "you draw" or the command "draw!" (to a group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Disegnate un cerchio sul foglio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Draw a circle on the sheet.

definitions.note: Past participle of "disegnare" (to draw); commonly used with "avere" in the passato prossimo.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho disegnato un cane.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I drew a dog.

definitions.note: Often means “you draw” (present tense). The same form is also used in the present subjunctive (e.g., after “spero che…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Disegni molto bene.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You draw very well.

definitions.note: plural of "disegno"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I bambini hanno fatto dei disegni a scuola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children made some drawings at school.

definitions.note: plural of "disegno"; can mean plans/designs in a general sense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi piacciono i disegni di questo tessuto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like the designs of this fabric.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho fatto un disegno di un gatto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I made a drawing of a cat.

definitions.note: Often used for the idea/plan behind how something is made or organized.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il disegno della sedia è molto moderno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The chair’s design is very modern.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto), often used in stories and historical narration.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da bambino, mio nonno disegnò una mappa del suo paese.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he was a child, my grandfather drew a map of his town.

definitions.note: feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono disgustata da quello che ha detto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m disgusted by what he said.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Che odore disgustoso!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What a disgusting smell!

definitions.note: Informal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il bagno è disgustoso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bathroom is gross.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il bambino è disobbediente e non ascolta mai.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The child is disobedient and never listens.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hai disobbedito ai tuoi genitori.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You disobeyed your parents.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mia sorella è disoccupata da due mesi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister has been unemployed for two months.

definitions.note: plural masculine form (can also refer to a mixed-gender group)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Molti giovani sono disoccupati.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many young people are unemployed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono disoccupato da due mesi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve been unemployed for two months.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La disoccupazione è aumentata quest’anno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Unemployment has increased this year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'è disordine in camera mia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There’s a mess in my room.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono troppo disorganizzato per trovare le chiavi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m too disorganized to find my keys.

definitions.note: Used for someone who has lost their sense of direction or feels mentally confused.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo il lungo viaggio mi sentivo disorientato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the long trip, I felt disoriented.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi sento disperata perché non trovo le chiavi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel desperate because I can't find the keys.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho cercato disperatamente le chiavi ovunque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I desperately looked for the keys everywhere.

definitions.note: plural masculine form (also used for mixed-gender groups).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eravamo disperati e non sapevamo cosa fare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We were desperate and we didn’t know what to do.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono disperato: ho perso il portafoglio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m desperate: I lost my wallet.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La disperazione lo ha spinto a chiedere aiuto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Desperation pushed him to ask for help.

definitions.note: Used mainly in the expression “mi dispiace” = “I’m sorry.” Literally means “it displeases me / I’m sorry about it.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi dispiace, oggi non posso venire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m sorry, I can’t come today.

definitions.native: would you mind, would it bother you
definitions.note: Often used in polite requests (literally: “would displease”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti dispiacerebbe chiudere la finestra?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Would you mind closing the window?

definitions.note: Often used like "Mi dispiaceva..." = "I was sorry..." (literally: "it was displeasing to me").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi dispiaceva per quello che era successo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was sorry about what had happened.

definitions.note: Used to apologize or to express regret; feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono dispiaciuta per il ritardo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m sorry about the delay.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo davvero dispiaciute per il ritardo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re really sorry for the delay.

definitions.note: often used to say you’re sorry about something (e.g., a problem, bad news, or not being able to do something)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo dispiaciuti per il ritardo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re sorry for the delay.

definitions.note: Often used to apologize or express regret; agrees with the speaker (e.g., dispiaciuto/dispiaciuta).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono dispiaciuto per il ritardo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm sorry for the delay.

definitions.note: Often used with "di" ("dispone di...") to mean "has/has available".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’hotel dispone di una piscina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hotel has a pool (available).

definitions.note: Often used for people as well: it can mean “free/able to help” (e.g., available to meet).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani sono disponibile per una riunione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I’m available for a meeting.

definitions.note: plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I biglietti sono ancora disponibili.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tickets are still available.

definitions.note: often used about people being ready to help
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I miei colleghi sono sempre disponibili a darmi una mano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My colleagues are always willing to give me a hand.

definitions.note: Often used for arranging things or organizing them in a certain order.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È importante disporre i libri in ordine alfabetico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important to arrange the books in alphabetical order.

definitions.note: Common in the expression "disporre di" (= to have/possess something available).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devi disporre di un documento valido per viaggiare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You need to have a valid document available in order to travel.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo dispositivo funziona anche senza internet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This device works even without internet.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La disposizione dei tavoli nella sala è molto comoda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The arrangement of the tables in the room is very convenient.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase “a disposizione” (“available / at your disposal”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Resto a tua disposizione per qualsiasi domanda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I remain available to you for any question.

definitions.note: Often used in more formal contexts (e.g., rules or official texts).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seguiamo le disposizioni del regolamento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We follow the provisions of the regulations.

definitions.note: feminine singular form (used with a feminine person or thing)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei è disposta ad aiutarti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is willing to help you.

definitions.note: feminine plural; often used with “a” + infinitive (e.g., disposte a fare qualcosa)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le studentesse sono disposte a lavorare dopo le lezioni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The (female) students are willing to work after class.

definitions.note: feminine plural; used for how things are placed or organized
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le sedie sono disposte in cerchio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The chairs are arranged in a circle.

definitions.note: Often used with “a” + infinitive (e.g., “disposti a fare…” = willing to do…).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo disposti a cambiare idea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are willing to change our mind.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I tavoli sono disposti in cerchio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tables are arranged in a circle.

definitions.note: Often used with “a” + infinitive (e.g., “disposto a fare…” = “willing to do…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono disposto a parlare con te domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m willing to talk to you tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alcune persone disprezzano chi è diverso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Some people despise those who are different.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (ongoing/repeated action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da ragazzo, disprezzava la scuola e non studiava mai.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As a boy, he used to despise school and he never studied.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non disprezzo nessuno, ma non sono d’accordo con te.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t despise anyone, but I don’t agree with you.

definitions.note: Simple past in a literary/narrative tense (passato remoto), common in stories and formal writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Poi disse la verità a tutti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Then he said the truth to everyone.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person plural of "dire"; common in written Italian and narratives.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dissero la verità a tutti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They told everyone the truth.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 1st person singular of "dire"; common in writing and in some regions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri dissi la verità a tutti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I told everyone the truth.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hanno dissotterrato un vaso antico nel giardino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They unearthed an ancient vase in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La scuola è distante da casa mia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The school is far from my house.

definitions.note: Often used to describe someone’s attitude or behavior (not physically far away).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da qualche giorno è distante e parla poco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For the past few days he’s been distant and doesn’t talk much.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La distanza tra casa mia e la scuola è di due chilometri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The distance between my house and the school is two kilometers.

definitions.note: plural of "distanza"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le distanze tra le città in Italia possono essere piccole.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The distances between cities in Italy can be small.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È importante distinguere tra fatti e opinioni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important to distinguish between facts and opinions.

definitions.note: "-la" is a direct object pronoun meaning “her” or “it” (feminine singular).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't distinguish her from her sister.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non voglio distrarre gli studenti durante la lezione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to distract the students during the lesson.

definitions.note: Often used with “l’attenzione” (attention) or “da” (from) to mean redirecting attention.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cerco di distrarre la mia attenzione dai pensieri negativi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I try to divert my attention from negative thoughts.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei oggi è molto distratta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very distracted today.

definitions.note: feminine plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le studentesse erano distratte durante la lezione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The students were distracted during the lesson.

definitions.note: plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siete sempre distratti quando parlo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are always distracted when I speak.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi sono molto distratto e dimentico tutto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I'm very distracted and I forget everything.

definitions.note: Often used for administrative areas (e.g., a city district) or in set phrases like "distretto industriale" (industrial district).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abito nel distretto 5 della città.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I live in district 5 of the city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il volantino è stato distribuito ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The flyer was distributed yesterday.

definitions.note: Used with the present subjunctive (e.g., after expressions like "è possibile che...") or as a formal command (Lei).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È possibile che il fuoco distrugga la casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s possible that the fire destroys the house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sta distruggendo il vecchio edificio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is destroying the old building.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non voglio distruggere questo edificio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to destroy this building.

definitions.note: second-person singular (“you”); can be used as present tense or as a command.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Perché distruggi sempre le tue cose?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why do you always destroy your things?

definitions.note: Passato remoto (simple past); can mean “I destroyed” or “he/she/it destroyed” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La tempesta distrusse il ponte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The storm destroyed the bridge.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of “distruggere”; often used with “essere” (e.g., “è distrutta”) or as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo l’incendio, la casa è distrutta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the fire, the house is destroyed.

definitions.note: feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La città è distrutta dopo il terremoto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The city is destroyed after the earthquake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho distrutto il documento per errore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I destroyed the document by mistake.

definitions.note: Can look like English “distracted,” but it means “destroyed.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo l’incendio, il negozio era completamente distrutto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the fire, the shop was completely destroyed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi disturba il rumore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The noise bothers me.

definitions.note: (tu) informal imperative
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Disturba pure, se hai bisogno di aiuto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Go ahead and interrupt if you need help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scusa, ti sto disturbando?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry, am I disturbing you?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quel film è davvero disturbante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That movie is really disturbing.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scusa per l’ora: non voglio disturbarci.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry for the time: I don’t want to bother us.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scusa, non voglio disturbare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry, I don't want to bother you.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “la” (= her / it [feminine]).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scusa, non volevo disturbarla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry, I didn’t mean to bother her.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun "lo" (= him/it) attached to the infinitive "disturbare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non voglio disturbarlo mentre lavora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to disturb him while he’s working.

definitions.native: to bother me, to disturb me
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi evitare di disturbarmi mentre lavoro?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you avoid bothering me while I’m working?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono stata disturbata dal rumore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was disturbed by the noise.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono disturbato dal rumore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m disturbed by the noise.

definitions.note: Often used in the present subjunctive (e.g., after phrases like “spero che…”, “penso che…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che non disturbi nessuno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope it doesn’t bother anyone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi dispiace per il disturbo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m sorry for the disturbance.

definitions.note: Often used in medical/psychological contexts (e.g., a sleep disorder).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha un disturbo del sonno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She has a sleep disorder.

definitions.note: Plural of "dito" (finger).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi fanno male le dita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My fingers hurt.

definitions.note: second-person plural (voi) present tense: “you (all) say/tell”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Che cosa dite?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What are you saying?

definitions.note: second-person plural (voi) imperative: “say/tell (you all)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dite la verità.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tell the truth.

definitions.note: imperative; informal plural (voi)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diteci la verità, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tell us the truth, please.

definitions.note: Plural informal/formal command to “you all/you (plural)”, with the object pronoun “gli” = “to him”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ditegli di venire domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tell him to come tomorrow.

definitions.note: Form of "dire" with the indirect object pronoun "le" attached (to her / to them, feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ditele la verità.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tell her the truth.

definitions.note: Informal plural command (to “you” plural). Includes the direct object pronoun “lo” (= “it”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se lo sapete, ditelo subito!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you know it, say it right away!

definitions.note: Imperative: polite/plural “you” (voi) + “to me” (mi) + “it” (lo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ditemelo subito, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tell it to me right away, please.

definitions.note: Plural informal command (voi) + object pronoun mi (“to me”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ditemi la verità, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tell me the truth, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi sono tagliato un dito mentre cucinavo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I cut a finger while I was cooking.

definitions.note: Often used for a business/company name or in contexts like trades/services (e.g., a construction firm).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La ditta ha consegnato i mobili ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company delivered the furniture yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sediamo sul divano dopo cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We sit on the sofa after dinner.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) form; common in written narratives.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nel 1990 divenne medico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In 1990, he became a doctor.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person plural of "divenire"; common in written narratives and history.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Con il tempo divennero amici inseparabili.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Over time they became inseparable friends.

definitions.note: Third-person singular present tense of "diventare" (used for “he/she/it becomes”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Con il freddo, l’acqua diventa ghiaccio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With the cold, water becomes ice.

definitions.note: past historic (passato remoto), 1st person singular of "diventare"; common in writing and storytelling, less in everyday speech
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A diciotto anni diventai maggiorenne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At eighteen I became an adult.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto diventando più paziente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m becoming more patient.

definitions.note: third-person plural (they)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Con l’esperienza diventano più sicuri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With experience, they become more confident.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio diventare medico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to become a doctor.

definitions.note: simple past (passato remoto), 3rd person plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nel 1990 diventarono amici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In 1990 they became friends.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "diventare"; used with "essere" (e.g., "è diventata")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È diventata famosa in poco tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She became famous in a short time.

definitions.note: Used as the (voi) plural imperative: “become!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diventate più pazienti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Become more patient.

definitions.note: Used as the feminine plural past participle (e.g., in compound tenses), agreeing with a feminine plural subject.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le cose sono diventate più complicate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Things have become more complicated.

definitions.note: past participle plural masculine of "diventare"; used with "essere" in compound tenses and as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo diventati amici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We became friends.

definitions.note: past participle of "diventare" (typically used with "essere" in compound tenses)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono diventato medico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I became a doctor.

definitions.note: Second person plural (voi), future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se studierete con costanza, diventerete più sicuri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you study consistently, you will become more confident.

definitions.note: Third-person singular future tense of "diventare" (used for he/she/it, or a singular subject).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tra pochi anni, questo quartiere diventerà molto più moderno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In a few years, this neighborhood will become much more modern.

definitions.note: present subjunctive form (used after expressions like "spero che...", "penso che...")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che tu diventi più sicuro di te.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you become more confident.

definitions.note: First-person singular (io) present tense of "diventare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando studio tanto, divento più sicuro di me.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I study a lot, I become more confident.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto) form; common in narratives, storytelling, and some regions of Italy.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo molti anni, diventò medico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After many years, he became a doctor.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "diverso".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho un'idea diversa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a different idea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devi fare diversamente se vuoi ottenere un risultato migliore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to do it differently if you want to get a better result.

definitions.note: feminine plural form of "diverso".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo idee diverse su questo argomento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have different ideas on this topic.

definitions.note: feminine plural form (used with feminine plural nouns)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho letto diverse storie interessanti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I read various interesting stories.

definitions.note: plural masculine form of "diverso"; used with masculine plural nouns or mixed-gender groups
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo idee diverse su questo argomento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have different ideas about this topic.

definitions.note: plural masculine form used before a masculine plural noun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho letto diversi libri quest'estate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I read various books this summer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La diversità culturale arricchisce la società.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Cultural diversity enriches society.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi mi sento diverso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I feel different.

definitions.note: Often used in the plural (diversi/diverse) to mean “several” or “various.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho visitato diversi musei a Roma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I visited various museums in Rome.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che il film ti diverta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope the movie amuses you.

definitions.note: Often used with "stare" to form the present progressive (e.g., "stiamo divertendo" = "we are entertaining").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stiamo divertendo i bambini con un gioco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are entertaining the children with a game.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il film è davvero divertente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie is really funny.

definitions.note: plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quei video sono davvero divertenti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those videos are really funny.

definitions.note: Passato remoto (simple past), 1st person singular: used mostly in writing and in some regions; often replaced by passato prossimo in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alla festa divertii tutti con una barzelletta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the party, I entertained everyone with a joke.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La festa è stata un vero divertimento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The party was real fun.

definitions.note: Past historic/remote past meaning “we had fun.” In modern spoken Italian, many speakers often use passato prossimo instead.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri sera divertimmo molto alla festa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night we had a lot of fun at the party.

definitions.note: Uses the pronoun “ci” meaning “us” (direct object).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi divertirci con una barzelletta?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you entertain us with a joke?

definitions.note: Often used reflexively as "divertirsi" = "to have fun".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo film riesce a divertire tutta la famiglia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This movie manages to entertain the whole family.

definitions.note: Reflexive form meaning “to enjoy myself.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio divertirmi alla festa stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to have fun at the party tonight.

definitions.note: Passato remoto (simple past), 3rd person plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I bambini si divertirono al parco tutto il pomeriggio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children had fun at the park all afternoon.

definitions.note: Reflexive verb; used with reflexive pronouns (mi, ti, si, ci, vi, si).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È importante divertirsi ogni tanto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important to have fun every now and then.

definitions.note: Infinitive of "divertire" with the object pronoun "ti" (= you).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio divertirti un po'.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to entertain you a bit.

definitions.native: to entertain you, to amuse you
definitions.note: Contains the pronoun "vi" (= you plural/formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio divertirvi con un gioco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to entertain you with a game.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle; often used with essere (e.g., "sono divertita")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri sera mi sono divertita molto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night I had a lot of fun.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri sera ero molto divertita alla festa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night I was really having fun at the party.

definitions.note: Often used with a direct object (someone you entertain). For “have fun,” Italian typically uses the reflexive form “divertirsi” (e.g., “divertitevi”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Divertite i bambini con un gioco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Entertain the children with a game.

definitions.note: feminine plural form (used with feminine plural nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le attività del pomeriggio sono state divertite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The afternoon activities were fun.

definitions.note: Often used as an informal (tu) command with the attached pronoun “-ti”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Divertiti alla festa!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Have fun at the party!

definitions.note: Can also be the masculine plural past participle (e.g., used with “essere”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I bambini erano divertiti dallo spettacolo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children were amused by the show.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I bambini sono divertiti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are amused.

definitions.note: Past participle of "divertire"; often used with "essere" in the reflexive form "divertirsi" (to have fun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi sono divertito alla festa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had fun at the party.

definitions.note: Often used to describe someone who is having fun or finds something funny.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono molto divertito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m very amused.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively as “mi diverto” = “I have fun.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diverto i bambini con una storia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I entertain the children with a story.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person singular of “divertire”. Often used in written narratives; in speech many speakers use passato prossimo instead.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alla festa si divertì molto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the party, he/she had a lot of fun.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 1st person plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri dividemmo la torta in otto fette.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday we divided the cake into eight slices.

definitions.note: Often used with "in" + plural to mean “to divide into …” (e.g., "dividere in due").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dobbiamo dividere la torta in otto fette.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to divide the cake into eight slices.

definitions.note: In everyday Italian, it often means “to share” in the sense of sharing something with someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Possiamo dividere la pizza?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can we share the pizza?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La linea rossa divise la pagina in due parti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The red line divided the page into two parts.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) form of "dividere" (used mostly in writing and in some regions to talk about the distant past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alla fine, divisi la torta in sei fette.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end, I divided the cake into six slices.

definitions.note: Past participle of "dividere"; often used with "essere" (e.g., "sono divisi").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I due gruppi sono divisi da una parete.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The two groups are divided by a wall.

definitions.note: past participle of "dividere"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho diviso la torta in otto fette.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I divided the cake into eight slices.

definitions.note: Past participle of "divorare"; often used to mean something was eaten very quickly or greedily.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He devoured the pizza in five minutes.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My aunt has been divorced for many years.

definitions.note: masculine plural adjective

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My parents are divorced.

definitions.note: Past participle (masculine singular) of "divorziare"; used with essere in compound tenses and often also as an adjective.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve been divorced for two years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio zio è divorziato da tre anni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My uncle has been divorced for three years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo dieci anni di matrimonio, hanno deciso di chiedere il divorzio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After ten years of marriage, they decided to file for divorce.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto) form: “(he/she) divorced.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo molti anni insieme, divorziò e si trasferì in un'altra città.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After many years together, he/she divorced and moved to another city.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il lupo divorò la preda in pochi minuti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wolf devoured the prey in a few minutes.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a dictionary to study Italian.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother DJs on weekends.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: DNA contains genetic information.

definitions.note: This form means “I give”.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dobbiamo andare a casa adesso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to go home now.

definitions.note: Present indicative, 1st person plural of "dovere".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to study for the exam.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that you (all) must finish today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Faccio una doccia ogni mattina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I take a shower every morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I docenti preparano le lezioni per domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teachers are preparing the lessons for tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo inviare la documentazione al Comune entro domani.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho bisogno del tuo documento d’identità.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need your ID document.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho dodici anni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am twelve years old.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il mio dog si chiama Max.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo tè è molto dolce.
