definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She has a gentle voice.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Parla dolcemente ai bambini.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She speaks sweetly to the children.

definitions.note: Plural of "dolcetto"; often used for small treats (like candies or little desserts).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I bambini vogliono dei dolcetti dopo cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children want some sweets after dinner.

definitions.note: plural form (masculine or feminine) of "dolce"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi piacciono i dolci al cioccolato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like sweet things with chocolate.

definitions.note: Plural of "dolce" (noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per Natale preparo sempre dei dolci fatti in casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For Christmas I always make homemade desserts.

definitions.note: Usually used in the plural to mean candy/sweet treats in general.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per Halloween compriamo dolciumi per i bambini.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For Halloween we buy sweets for the kids.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho cambiato cento dollari in euro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I changed one hundred dollars into euros.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho cambiato cento euro in dollari.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I changed one hundred euros into dollars.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho un forte dolore alla schiena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a strong pain in my back.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho dolori alla schiena da ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve had back pain since yesterday.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "doloroso"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La ferita è ancora dolorosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wound is still painful.

definitions.note: often used to describe something emotionally painful; feminine singular form of "doloroso"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È stata una notizia dolorosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was sad news.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È stato un ricordo doloroso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was a painful memory.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un momento doloroso per tutti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a sorrowful moment for everyone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho una domanda per te.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a question for you.

definitions.note: Common in formal contexts (e.g., job or document applications).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho compilato la domanda per il passaporto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I filled out the passport application.

definitions.note: plural of "domanda"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho due domande per te.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have two questions for you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani vado al lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I’m going to work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani ho un appuntamento dal medico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I have a doctor’s appointment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domattina ho un colloquio alle nove.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow morning I have an interview at nine.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci vediamo domenica mattina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: See you Sunday morning.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo comprato delle cose domestiche per la cucina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We bought some household items for the kitchen.

definitions.note: Often used for things related to the home (e.g., chores, appliances).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le faccende domestiche richiedono tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Household chores take time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa squadra domina la partita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This team dominates the match.

definitions.note: Used as a title before a man's first name, especially for Catholic priests.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Don Marco celebra la messa ogni domenica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don Marco celebrates Mass every Sunday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ogni mese dona dei vestiti a un’associazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every month, he/she donates some clothes to an organization.

definitions.native: to donate, to give (as a gift)
definitions.note: Often used for giving money, blood, or organs; also for giving something as a present.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ogni anno doniamo soldi a un'associazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every year we donate money to an organization.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (voi). Often used formally to address one person, or to address multiple people.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Donate questi vestiti alla Caritas?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you donating these clothes to Caritas?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho donato i vestiti che non uso più.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I donated the clothes I don’t use anymore.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo ricevuto molti doni per il matrimonio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We received many gifts for the wedding.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quella donna parla italiano molto bene.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That woman speaks Italian very well.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In questa azienda lavorano molte donne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many women work at this company.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il suo dono mi ha reso molto felice.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His gift made me very happy.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person singular: “he/she gave/donated.” Common in writing and stories; in everyday speech many people use the passato prossimo instead.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il signor Rossi donò molti libri alla biblioteca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Mr. Rossi donated many books to the library.

definitions.note: Can be used as a preposition (followed by a noun) or as an adverb (alone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo la lezione, vado a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the lesson, I go home.

definitions.note: Used both for time (“after/later”) and in set phrases like “a dopo” (“see you later”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci vediamo dopo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: See you later.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopodomani parto per Roma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I leave for Rome the day after tomorrow.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form (used with feminine singular nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho preso una porzione doppia di pasta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I took a double portion of pasta.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho controllato la prenotazione: era doppiata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I checked the reservation: it was doubled.

definitions.note: Used for movies/TV when the audio has been replaced with another language.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho visto la serie in versione doppiata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I watched the series in the dubbed version.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei un espresso doppio, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like a double espresso, please.

definitions.note: Often used to mean a “double room” in a hotel (e.g., prenotare un doppio).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho prenotato un doppio per due notti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I booked a double room for two nights.

definitions.note: Used as present subjunctive (e.g., after che) and also as the formal (Lei) imperative: Dorma!
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che dorma bene stanotte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope he/she sleeps well tonight.

definitions.note: third-person singular (lui/lei) present tense of "dormire"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio fratello dorme ancora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is still sleeping.

definitions.note: gerund (present participle) of "dormire"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto dormendo sul divano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m sleeping on the couch.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) present tense of "dormire".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Perché dormi così poco?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why do you sleep so little?

definitions.note: Present tense (noi).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Di solito dormiamo otto ore a notte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We usually sleep eight hours a night.

definitions.note: Passato remoto (simple past) of "dormire"; common in writing and in some regions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri sera dormii otto ore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night I slept eight hours.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio dormire otto ore stanotte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to sleep eight hours tonight.

definitions.note: Third-person singular future tense (lui/lei/Lei).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani dormrà otto ore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow he/she will sleep eight hours.

definitions.note: Used with "voi" (you all / you plural; also formal "you" in some contexts).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voi dormite otto ore ogni notte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You sleep eight hours every night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho dormito otto ore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I slept eight hours.

definitions.note: Often refers to a shared sleeping room (e.g., in a school/hostel), but it can also mean a bedroom in general depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In ostello dormo in un dormitorio con altre sei persone.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the hostel I sleep in a dormitory with six other people.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense; describes an ongoing/background action in the past (“was sleeping”) or a habitual past action (“used to sleep”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando sono arrivato, lui dormiva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I arrived, he was sleeping.

definitions.note: Present tense (io).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dormo otto ore ogni notte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sleep eight hours every night.

definitions.note: third-person plural (they sleep) of "dormire".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I bambini dormono presto la sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children sleep early in the evening.

definitions.note: Passato remoto (simple past), common in narratives and in some regions of Italy.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo il viaggio, dormì per dieci ore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the trip, (he/she) slept for ten hours.

definitions.note: Commonly used for a bump in the road (e.g., a speed bump).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Rallenta: c’è un dosso sulla strada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Slow down: there’s a bump in the road.

definitions.note: Often used with “di” + noun (e.g., “dotato di pazienza” = “gifted with patience”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un ragazzo molto dotato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a very gifted boy.

definitions.note: Shortened form of “dottore”, used especially before a man’s name (e.g., Dottor Rossi).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Buongiorno, dottor Bianchi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Good morning, Dr. Bianchi.

definitions.note: In everyday Italian, it’s commonly used to address a medical doctor; it can also be used for someone with a university degree (especially a PhD), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il dottore mi visita alle dieci.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor examines me at ten.

definitions.note: Often used as a title for a woman with a university degree as well (like “Dr.”), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La dottoressa visita i pazienti ogni mattina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The (female) doctor sees patients every morning.

definitions.note: plural of “dottore”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I dottori dicono che devo riposare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctors say that I need to rest.

definitions.note: Used in questions and in relative clauses to indicate a place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dove abiti?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Where do you live?

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 1st person plural (“we”); common in writing and storytelling, often replaced by “abbiamo dovuto” in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dovemmo tornare a casa presto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had to go back home early.

definitions.note: Used as a modal (auxiliary) verb to express obligation or necessity; it’s typically followed by an infinitive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo studiare stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to study tonight.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary to express obligation or necessity.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo studiare stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to study tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È mio dovere aiutare gli altri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It is my duty to help others.

definitions.note: Plural of "dovere" in the sense of obligations/responsibilities.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho molti doveri a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have many duties at home.

definitions.note: Used in the past subjunctive (imperfetto congiuntivo), often after “se” (if) to express a hypothetical necessity.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se dovesse piovere, resteremmo a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If it should rain, we would stay at home.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive of "dovere"; used after expressions like "se" (if) or "penso che" (I think that) to talk about a hypothetical duty/necessity.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se dovessi partire domani, ti avviserei subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I should have to leave tomorrow, I’d let you know right away.

definitions.note: Used with another verb (e.g., “dovete + infinitive”) to express obligation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dovete finire i compiti prima di uscire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to finish your homework before going out.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (voi); can also mean “you owe” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dovete studiare per l'esame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to study for the exam.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), used mainly in writing and for events in the distant past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dovette partire subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He had to leave immediately.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person plural; used mainly in writing and storytelling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dovettero partire subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They had to leave immediately.

definitions.note: past historic (passato remoto) form; common in narratives and writing
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dovetti partire subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had to leave immediately.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary with an infinitive to express obligation/necessity in the past (imperfect).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Doveva studiare, ma era troppo stanco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He had to study, but he was too tired.

definitions.note: Imperfect past form; often used to describe an ongoing obligation in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Doveva studiare, ma era troppo stanco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He had to study, but he was too tired.

definitions.note: Past imperfect (noi): used to express an obligation in the past; often corresponds to “had to” or “were supposed to.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dovevamo partire alle otto, ma abbiamo perso il treno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had to leave at eight, but we missed the train.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense, 3rd person plural (they). Used as an auxiliary with another verb (often in the infinitive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dovevano partire presto, ma hanno perso il treno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They had to leave early, but they missed the train.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (past) form used with "voi" (you all / formal you).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dovevate studiare di più per l'esame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You had to study more for the exam.

definitions.note: imperfect (past); used with another verb in the infinitive
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dovevi studiare per l’esame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You had to study for the exam.

definitions.note: Imperfect of the auxiliary verb "dovere"; often used for past obligations, or obligations that were ongoing/habitual in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dovevo studiare ieri sera, ma ero troppo stanco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had to study last night, but I was too tired.

definitions.note: Future tense (tu form) of "dovere"; used to express obligation or necessity.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani dovrai alzarti presto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow you will have to get up early.

definitions.note: Future tense (3rd person plural) of the auxiliary verb "dovere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani dovranno partire presto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow they will have to leave early.

definitions.note: Often used to give advice or express what is expected/supposed to happen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dovrebbe partire presto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: should leave early.

definitions.note: Used with another verb in the infinitive to express obligation or advice (conditional form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dovrebbero studiare di più.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They should study more.

definitions.note: Conditional form of "dovere" used to express advice/obligation or something you would be expected to do (often translated as “should”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dovrei studiare di più.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I should study more.

definitions.note: First-person plural conditional of "dovere" (we should). Often used for advice or polite suggestions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dovremmo partire presto domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We should leave early tomorrow.

definitions.native: we will have to, we must
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani dovremo partire presto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will have to leave early.

definitions.note: Second person plural (voi) of "dovere"; used to give advice or say what is expected.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dovreste studiare un po' di più.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You should study a bit more.

definitions.note: Can express a conditional obligation for "voi" (you all).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per arrivare in tempo, dovreste partire adesso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: To arrive on time, you would have to leave now.

definitions.note: Second-person singular conditional of "dovere" (used to give advice or express what is expected).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dovresti studiare un po' di più.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You should study a bit more.

definitions.native: will have to, will need to
definitions.note: Second-person plural (voi) future tense of the auxiliary verb "dovere"; used to express obligation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani dovrete alzarvi presto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow you will have to get up early.

definitions.note: Future tense form of "dovere" used as an auxiliary to express obligation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dovrà finire il lavoro entro stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Will have to finish the work by this evening.

definitions.native: will have to, will need to
definitions.note: Future tense (io): used to express obligation or necessity.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani dovrò studiare per l’esame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will have to study for the exam.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form (often used like an adjective) meaning something is required to be paid or given.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La somma dovuta è di 50 euro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The amount owed is 50 euros.

definitions.note: feminine plural form (past participle) of "dovere"; often used like an adjective meaning something is owed or required.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le tasse dovute devono essere pagate entro fine mese.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The taxes due must be paid by the end of the month.

definitions.note: Past participle of "dovere", often used like an adjective meaning something is required/owed.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I pagamenti sono dovuti entro domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The payments are due by tomorrow.

definitions.note: Past participle of "dovere" used in compound tenses to express necessity.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho dovuto lavorare fino a tardi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had to work until late.

definitions.note: Often used like an adjective to describe money or something that must be given or paid.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non ho ancora pagato i soldi dovuti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I still haven’t paid the money owed.

definitions.note: Often used in set phrases like “il dovuto rispetto” (“the respect that is due”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti pagherò la somma dovuta entro domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll pay you the amount due by tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato una dozzina di uova.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a dozen eggs.

definitions.note: Plural of "dozzina".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ne ho comprate due dozzine per la festa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought two dozen for the party.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nella storia c'è un drago che vive in una grotta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the story there is a dragon that lives in a cave.

definitions.note: Common in Italian as an English loanword, especially meaning an alcoholic mixed drink (a cocktail).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prendo un drink al bar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll have a drink at the bar.

definitions.note: Common in the expression “dare una dritta” (to give someone a tip).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi dai una dritta per trovare casa a Milano?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you give me a tip for finding a place to live in Milan?

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "dritto"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La strada è dritta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The road is straight.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le linee dritte sono più facili da disegnare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Straight lines are easier to draw.

definitions.note: As an adverb, it describes the direction or way of moving/looking (e.g., “go straight”, “look straight ahead”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vai dritto fino al semaforo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Go straight until the traffic light.

definitions.note: Often used in the plural (droghe) to mean illegal drugs.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La polizia ha trovato della droga in macchina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police found drugs in the car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hanno drogato il cane.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They drugged the dog.

definitions.note: Plural of "droga"; can mean medicines or (more commonly) illegal drugs depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La polizia ha trovato droghe nello zaino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police found drugs in the backpack.

definitions.note: Plural of "dubbio".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho dei dubbi su questa decisione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have some doubts about this decision.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho un dubbio su questa risposta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a doubt about this answer.
