definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They arrived yesterday.

definitions.note: Gerund form of the auxiliary verb “essere”; often used to give a reason or context (“since/being…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Essendo arrivato tardi, ha perso il treno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Being late, he missed the train.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È essenziale bere acqua ogni giorno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s essential to drink water every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per me l’onestà è essenziale in un’amicizia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For me, honesty is necessary in a friendship.

definitions.note: Plural form; used for masculine or feminine plural nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questi documenti sono essenziali per la domanda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These documents are essential for the application.

definitions.note: Used to say that someone/something exists or is present (often corresponds to “there is/there are”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono due sedie in cucina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are two chairs in the kitchen.

definitions.note: Used as the auxiliary “to be” in many compound tenses (especially with movement verbs and reflexive verbs).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo essere arrivato tardi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I must have arrived late.

definitions.note: Irregular verb; often used as an auxiliary in compound tenses (e.g., with many verbs of movement and change of state).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio essere felice.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to be happy.

definitions.native: to be it, to be so
definitions.note: Infinitive of "essere" with the direct object pronoun "lo" attached ("it").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non voglio esserlo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to be it.

definitions.note: Infinitive of "essere" with the indirect object pronoun "mi" attached (= “to me”). Often used as part of a compound tense with a past participle (as an auxiliary).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deve essermi sfuggito il tuo messaggio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I must have missed your message.

definitions.note: This is the infinitive essere with the clitic pronoun ne attached; ne often means “of it/of them” (or “about it/them”) depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo esserne sicuro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to be sure of it.

definitions.note: Used in the perfect infinitive with reflexive verbs (e.g., after having done something to yourself).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo essersi svegliato, ha fatto colazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After waking up, he had breakfast.

definitions.note: Infinitive of "essere" with the attached pronoun "ti" (= to you). Often used in phrases like "esserti utile" (to be useful to you) or "esserti d’aiuto" (to help you).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio esserti d’aiuto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to help you.

definitions.note: Subject pronoun; more formal/literary than "loro" and used mostly in writing or for emphasis.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Essi arrivano domani mattina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They arrive tomorrow morning.

definitions.note: Subject pronoun for masculine plural (or mixed-gender groups); often omitted in Italian when the subject is clear.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Essi sono arrivati in ritardo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They arrived late.

definitions.note: Subject pronoun (masculine singular), used mainly for animals or things; less common for people (who usually take “lui”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il cane è stanco: esso dorme sul divano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is tired: it sleeps on the sofa.

definitions.note: used for the cardinal direction; often in phrases like “a est di …” (“to the east of …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La finestra guarda a est.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The window faces east.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In estate fa molto caldo qui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the summer it’s very hot here.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È stato un viaggio estenuante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was an exhausting trip.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'è un estintore vicino alla porta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a fire extinguisher near the door.

definitions.note: Often used in more formal contexts (e.g., “vacanze estive”, “orario estivo”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Durante l'orario estivo, il negozio chiude alle otto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: During summer hours, the shop closes at eight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non parlo con gli estranei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t talk to strangers.

definitions.note: Can also mean an outsider (someone not part of a group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'è un estraneo alla porta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a stranger at the door.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho estratto un dente ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had a tooth extracted yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono estremamente felice di vederti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m extremely happy to see you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha esultato dopo il gol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She exulted after the goal.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "eterno".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La nostra amicizia è eterna.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our friendship is eternal.

definitions.note: Plural of "etichetta".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le etichette sulle bottiglie sono chiare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The labels on the bottles are clear.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A che età hai iniziato a studiare italiano?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At what age did you start studying Italian?

definitions.note: the official currency used in many European countries
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo libro costa dieci euro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book costs ten euros.

definitions.note: plural form of "europeo" (a person from Europe)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gli europei parlano molte lingue diverse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Europeans speak many different languages.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hanno evacuato l’edificio dopo l’allarme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They evacuated the building after the alarm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono molti eventi in città questo fine settimana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many events in the city this weekend.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani c'è un evento in centro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow there’s an event downtown.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È evidente che hai ragione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s obvious that you’re right.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present (he/she/it avoids) of "evitare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Evita sempre le discussioni inutili.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He always avoids useless arguments.

definitions.note: Gerund form (often used like “while avoiding” / “by avoiding”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto guidando evitando le strade trafficate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm driving while avoiding the busy streets.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cerco di evitare lo zucchero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I try to avoid sugar.

definitions.note: Often used with “che” + subjunctive or with “di” + infinitive to mean preventing something from happening.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dobbiamo evitare che succeda di nuovo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to prevent it from happening again.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle (used with a feminine noun, or with “essere” in compound tenses)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quella situazione è stata evitata grazie al tuo consiglio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That situation was avoided thanks to your advice.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (voi) present indicative, or plural imperative.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Evitate di fare rumore durante la lezione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Avoid making noise during the lesson.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho evitato la discussione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I avoided the discussion.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tu) or present indicative (tu). The meaning depends on context (e.g., after expressions like “è meglio che…” it’s subjunctive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che tu eviti di fare tardi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you avoid being late.

definitions.note: Present tense (io): “I avoid.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Evito di mangiare troppo tardi la sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I avoid eating too late in the evening.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto) form, common in written narratives and in some regions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando vide il cane, evitò la strada principale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he saw the dog, he avoided the main road.

definitions.note: Invariable; used before a noun (e.g., "ex marito") or alone as a noun (e.g., "il mio ex").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho visto la mia ex ragazza ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw my ex-girlfriend yesterday.

definitions.note: Commonly used as a noun, often with the article (e.g., "il mio ex").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho incontrato il mio ex al supermercato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ran into my ex at the supermarket.

definitions.note: Used with a time expression to mean “... ago” (e.g., due anni fa = two years ago).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’ho visto due giorni fa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw him two days ago.

definitions.note: Often used in expressions about weather or conditions (e.g. "Fa caldo" = "It’s hot").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui fa la spesa il sabato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He does the grocery shopping on Saturday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio padre lavora in una fabbrica di automobili.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My father works in a car factory.

definitions.note: Past participle of "fabbricare". Often a false friend with English "fabricate" (which can mean "make up" a story).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho fabbricato un tavolo di legno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I made a wooden table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il fabbro ripara il cancello di ferro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The blacksmith repairs the iron gate.

definitions.note: plural of "faccia"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho visto tante facce nuove alla festa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw lots of new faces at the party.

definitions.note: Often used for a situation or issue to deal with; also commonly used in the plural (faccende) for chores/housework.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una faccenda complicata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a complicated matter.

definitions.note: Plural; often used for household tasks or things you need to take care of.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo fare le faccende prima di uscire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to do the chores before going out.

definitions.note: This is the informal imperative form "fa'" (from "fare") + the pronoun "ci". Very common in expressions like "farci caso" (= to notice/pay attention).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Facci caso: la porta è aperta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Notice it: the door is open.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha una faccia stanca oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has a tired face today.

definitions.note: Form of the verb "fare" used in the present subjunctive (e.g., "che io faccia...") and also as the formal (Lei) command (e.g., "Faccia così!").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È importante che tu lo faccia oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that you do it today.

definitions.note: Present tense (noi) of "fare"; can also be used as an informal suggestion like "let’s".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Facciamo la spesa domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’ll do the grocery shopping tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used in the subjunctive after expressions like “è importante che…” (“it’s important that…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È importante che lo facciano oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that they do it today.

definitions.note: Used in the present subjunctive (e.g., after expressions like “è importante che...”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È importante che facciate attenzione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that you pay attention.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi faccio la spesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I do the grocery shopping.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) form of "fare" used mainly in written narratives and in some regions in speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'anno scorso facemmo un viaggio in Sicilia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last year we took a trip to Sicily.

definitions.note: present gerund of "fare"; often used to mean "while doing/making" or to form the progressive with "stare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto facendo la cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m making dinner.

definitions.note: imperfect subjunctive (io/lui/lei) of "fare"; used after expressions of doubt, desire, or necessity, often meaning "were to do/make" in English.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pensavo che lui lo facesse per aiutarmi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thought he did it to help me.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive (used after expressions like "se" = "if", in hypothetical or reported situations in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se facessero più attenzione, non sbaglierebbero così spesso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If they paid more attention, they wouldn’t make mistakes so often.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive of "fare" (used in clauses like "se..." = "if..." or after expressions of doubt/wish). Often translates as "(if) I/you/he/she were to do" or "(if) I/you/he/she did" depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se lo facessi, sarebbe più facile per tutti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you/I/he/she did it, it would be easier for everyone.

definitions.note: Used in the imperfect subjunctive (often after expressions like "era importante che...", "volevo che...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Era importante che lo facessimo subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was important that we do it right away.

definitions.native: was doing, used to do, made
definitions.note: Imperfect tense (third person singular: “he/she/it”); often used for ongoing actions in the past or habitual past actions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri faceva freddo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday it was cold.

definitions.native: we were doing, we used to do, we made
definitions.note: Imperfetto (past habitual/ongoing): often translates as “we were…” or “we used to…”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da piccoli facevamo i compiti insieme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When we were little, we used to do our homework together.

definitions.native: were doing, did, were making, made
definitions.note: Imperfetto (past habitual/ongoing): used for actions that were repeated or in progress in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da piccoli, facevano i compiti insieme ogni pomeriggio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When they were little, they used to do their homework together every afternoon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo esercizio è facile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This exercise is easy.

definitions.note: plural form (used with masculine or feminine plural nouns)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questi esercizi sono facili.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These exercises are easy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi farlo facilmente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can do it easily.

definitions.note: plural of "fagiolo"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A cena mangio fagioli e insalata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For dinner I eat beans and salad.

definitions.note: second-person singular (tu) present of "fare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Che cosa fai oggi?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What are you doing today?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prendo un falafel con insalata, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll have a falafel with salad, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nel cielo vola un falco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A falcon is flying in the sky.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il falegname ha riparato la porta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The carpenter fixed the door.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando il sistema falla, perdiamo i dati.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When the system fails, we lose the data.

definitions.note: Informal command (tu) with the direct object pronoun “la” (“it” referring to something feminine, e.g. una torta).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non pensarci troppo: falla adesso!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t think about it too much: do it now!

definitions.note: From the verb "fallare" (to fail).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se falli oggi, puoi riprovare domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you fail today, you can try again tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il progetto si è concluso con un fallimento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The project ended in failure.

definitions.note: Used in legal/financial contexts (a company or person cannot pay their debts).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’azienda ha dichiarato fallimento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company declared bankruptcy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho studiato molto, ma ho paura di fallire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I studied a lot, but I'm afraid of failing.

definitions.note: Often used for a business or company.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'azienda ha fallito l'anno scorso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company went bankrupt last year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se non studi, fallirà l’esame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you don’t study, you will fail the exam.

definitions.note: Can mean to fail at something or (for a person/company) to go bankrupt; context makes it clear.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se non paga i debiti, l’azienda fallisce.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If it doesn’t pay its debts, the company goes bankrupt.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho fallito l’esame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I failed the exam.

definitions.note: Informal command (tu) of “fare” with the direct object pronoun “lo” attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se vuoi, fallo adesso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you want, do it now.

definitions.note: Imperative form of “fare” + “lo” (“it”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fallo adesso!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do it now!

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) of “fallire” (3rd person singular), common in narratives and some regions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il piano fallì all'ultimo momento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plan failed at the last moment.

definitions.note: feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa notizia è falsa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This news is false.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa informazione è false.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This information is false.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form; also used for mixed-gender plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I documenti sono falsi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The documents are false.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hanno falsificato i documenti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They forged the documents.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa notizia è falsa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This news is false.

definitions.note: Used as a noun, often with an article (e.g., "un falso", "il falso").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quel dipinto è un falso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That painting is a forgery.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha una buona fama nel quartiere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has a good reputation in the neighborhood.

definitions.note: Not to be confused with English "fame" (Italian for "fame" is "fama").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho molta fame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m very hungry.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La mia famiglia vive a Milano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My family lives in Milan.

definitions.note: plural of "famiglia"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In questo quartiere ci sono molte famiglie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this neighborhood there are many families.

definitions.note: Often used with “a” to mean “familiar with”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa parola mi è familiare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This word is familiar to me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un problema familiare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a family problem.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questi volti mi sono familiari.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These faces are familiar to me.

definitions.note: Often used for knowing something well or being comfortable with it; it can also mean an overly casual manner.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho poca familiarità con questo argomento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have little familiarity with this topic.

definitions.note: Informal (tu) imperative of "fare" with attached pronouns: mi (= to/for me) + lo (= it).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fammelo vedere, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Show it to me, please.

definitions.note: Informal command: imperative of “fare” + “mi” (“me”). Often used like “Fammi un favore” = “Do me a favor.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fammi un favore, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do me a favor, please.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "famoso".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa attrice è famosa in tutto il mondo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This actress is famous all over the world.

definitions.note: feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quelle attrici sono molto famose.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those actresses are very famous.

definitions.note: masculine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quei cantanti sono molto famosi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those singers are very famous.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Roma è famosa per i suoi monumenti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Rome is famous for its monuments.

definitions.note: Commonly used loanword in Italian (especially for sports, music, movies, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono un fan del Milan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m a fan of Milan.

definitions.note: Very vulgar/offensive; used as an insult or to tell someone to go away.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vaffanculo!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Fuck you!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo la pioggia, le scarpe erano piene di fango.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the rain, the shoes were full of mud.

definitions.note: third-person plural (they/you all) of "fare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fanno colazione alle sette.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They have breakfast at seven.

definitions.note: Used with a time expression or context to describe an action in progress in the present.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Che cosa fanno adesso?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What are they doing now?

definitions.note: Informal and insulting.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non fare il fannullone: aiutami a pulire la cucina!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t be a lazy good-for-nothing—help me clean the kitchen!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi piace leggere romanzi di fantascienza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like reading science fiction novels.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da bambina aveva molta fantasia e inventava storie ogni sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As a child she had a lot of imagination and made up stories every evening.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho visto un fantasma in quel castello.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw a ghost in that castle.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Di notte, i fantasmi mi fanno paura.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At night, ghosts scare me.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La tua idea è fantastica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your idea is fantastic.

definitions.note: feminine plural form of "fantastico".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le idee sono fantastiche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ideas are fantastic.

definitions.note: plural masculine form (or plural mixed-gender group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I tuoi amici sono fantastici!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your friends are fantastic!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il film è fantastico!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie is fantastic!

definitions.note: Shortened form of “fare”, commonly used before pronouns (e.g., farlo, farla) and in some fixed expressions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo farlo oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to do it today.

definitions.native: you will do, you will make
definitions.note: Second person singular (tu) in the future tense of "fare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani farai i compiti dopo cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow you will do your homework after dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani faranno la spesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow they will do the grocery shopping.

definitions.native: to make it, to manage, to succeed
definitions.note: Commonly used with expressions like “non farcela” (not to manage / not to make it).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non so se posso farcela da solo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t know if I can make it on my own.

definitions.note: From "fare" + the pronoun "ci" (“to us” / “us”). Often used in requests like "farci un favore" (“do us a favor”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi farci un favore?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you do us a favor?

definitions.note: Often used both literally (a heavy load) and figuratively (a worry or responsibility).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo fardello è troppo pesante da portare da solo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This burden is too heavy to carry alone.

definitions.note: Very common verb. False friend: it does not mean English “fare.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo fare i compiti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to do my homework.

definitions.note: Conditional mood (present conditional), third person singular (lui/lei/Lei).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se avesse tempo, farebbe una torta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If he had time, he would make a cake.

definitions.note: Third-person plural conditional ("they"/"you all" formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se avessero tempo, farebbero una torta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If they had time, they would make a cake.

definitions.native: I would do, I would make
definitions.note: First-person singular conditional (io).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Io lo farei subito, ma non ho tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would do it right away, but I don’t have time.

definitions.note: First-person plural conditional (noi).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se avessimo più tempo, faremmo una passeggiata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If we had more time, we would take a walk.

definitions.native: we will do, we will make
definitions.note: First-person plural future tense of "fare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani faremo una torta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will make a cake.

definitions.native: you would do, you would make
definitions.note: Second person plural (voi) of the conditional tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Che cosa fareste voi al mio posto?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What would you do in my place?

definitions.native: you would do, you would make
definitions.note: Second-person singular conditional (tu form) of "fare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Che cosa faresti al mio posto?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What would you do in my place?

definitions.native: you (plural) will do, you (plural) will make
definitions.note: Second person plural (voi) future tense of "fare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani farete i compiti dopo cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow you will do the homework after dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nel giardino c'è una farfalla gialla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a yellow butterfly in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nel giardino ci sono molte farfalle colorate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the garden there are many colorful butterflies.

definitions.native: to do (something) to him, to make him
definitions.note: Combination of fare + gli (“to him”). Often used before another verb (e.g., “fargli vedere” = “to show him”, literally “to make him see”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo fargli una domanda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to ask him a question.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi serve la farina per fare la pizza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need flour to make pizza.

definitions.note: Combination of "fare" + the direct object pronoun "la" (“it” for a feminine noun, or “her”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo farla oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to do it today.

definitions.note: Clitic pronoun “la” is attached to the verb and usually means “it” (referring to a feminine noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo farla subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to do it right away.

definitions.native: to do them, to make them
definitions.note: Infinitive "fare" with the direct object pronoun "le" (= them, feminine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo farle oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to do them today.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun "li" = "them" (masculine plural, also used for mixed groups).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo farli oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to do them today.

definitions.note: "fare" + the direct object pronoun "lo" (“it”) attached to the end.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo farlo oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to do it today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vado in farmacia a comprare delle medicine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to the pharmacy to buy some medicine.

definitions.note: Fare + the clitic pronoun “mi” (“me”). Often used in requests (e.g., “farmi un favore” = “do me a favor”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi farmi un favore?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you do me a favor?

definitions.note: From "fare" with the clitic pronoun "mi" attached (meaning "to me / me"). Often used with another noun (e.g., "un favore").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi farmi un favore?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you do me a favor?

definitions.native: do with it, make of it
definitions.note: From "fare" + the pronoun "ne" (referring to something previously mentioned, often meaning “of it/with it”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Che vuoi farne?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What do you want to do with it?

definitions.note: Pronominal/reflexive form of "fare"; often used to describe a change or transformation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Con il tempo, tutto può farsi più facile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With time, everything can become easier.

definitions.note: Used when you arrange for someone else to do something for you (often with an infinitive, e.g. "farsi tagliare").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani mi faccio tagliare i capelli.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I’m getting my hair cut.

definitions.native: to do/make for you, to make you
definitions.note: Infinitive "fare" with the attached pronoun "ti" ("to you/you"). Meaning depends on context (e.g. "farti un regalo" = do/make something for you; "farti ridere" = make you laugh).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio farti un regalo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to give you a gift.

definitions.native: to make you (plural), to do for you (plural)
definitions.note: Includes the clitic pronoun “vi” = “you (plural)” (also used as formal “you”). Often used before another verb (e.g., “farvi vedere” = “to show you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Posso farvi una domanda?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can I ask you a question?

definitions.native: to do/make for you (plural); to make you (plural) (do something)
definitions.note: From "fare" + the clitic pronoun "vi" (“you” plural). In some contexts "vi" can also mean “there,” but here it commonly means “to/for you (all).”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Posso farvi una domanda?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can I ask you a question?

definitions.note: 3rd person singular future of "fare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani farà i compiti dopo scuola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow he/she will do the homework after school.

definitions.native: I will do, I will make
definitions.note: First person singular (io) in the future tense of "fare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani farò la spesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will do the grocery shopping.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il medico ha messo una fasciatura sul mio polso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor put a bandage on my wrist.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il suo fascino è irresistibile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His charm is irresistible.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo nella fase finale del progetto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are in the final phase of the project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi dà fastidio quando parlano tutti insieme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It annoys me when they all talk at the same time.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa musica è fastidiosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This music is annoying.

definitions.note: feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le zanzare sono molto fastidiose d’estate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Mosquitoes are very annoying in the summer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il rumore del traffico è fastidioso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The traffic noise is annoying.

definitions.note: Verb form of "fare" used with "voi" (you plural). Also looks like the English word "fate" (destiny), but it does not mean that.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Che cosa fate oggi?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What are you doing today?

definitions.note: Imperative with the clitic pronoun “ci” (= us). Often used before another verb: “Fateci + infinitive” = “Let us / Make us (do something)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fateci entrare, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let us in, please.

definitions.note: Plural command form with an attached pronoun: fate + la (“you all do/make” + “it/her”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fatela adesso!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do it now!

definitions.note: Command form (plural “you”) with the object pronoun “li” (“them”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Avete tante cose da fare oggi: fateli subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have lots of things to do today: do them right away.

definitions.note: Imperative for “voi” (you plural); “-lo” = “it” attached to the verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fatelo adesso, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do it now, please.

definitions.native: do it for me, make it for me
definitions.note: Plural command (addressed to "voi") with the indirect object pronoun "mi" (= to/for me).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fatemi un favore, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do me a favor, please.

definitions.note: Imperative for “voi” (you all) with the attached pronoun “vi” (“yourselves” / “to you all”), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fatevi avanti, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come forward, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho finito il lavoro con molta fatica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I finished the work with a lot of effort.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "fare"; it agrees with a feminine singular subject/object (often with "essere" or used as an adjective).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La torta è fatta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cake is done.

definitions.note: feminine singular form (used with feminine nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La torta è già fatta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cake is already made.

definitions.note: Feminine plural past participle of "fare"; used with feminine plural nouns (often in passive or compound tenses).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le torte sono state fatte ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cakes were made yesterday.

definitions.note: Plural imperative (voi). Not to be confused with the noun “fatti” meaning “facts.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fatti sentire quando arrivi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let me hear from you when you arrive.

definitions.note: Past participle plural. Not to be confused with the noun “fatti” meaning “facts.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo già fatti i compiti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’ve already done the homework.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I fatti sono chiari.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The facts are clear.

definitions.note: Past participle of "fare"; used with auxiliary verbs (e.g., "ho fatto" = "I have done/made").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho già fatto i compiti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve already done my homework.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un fatto importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s an important fact.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono molti fattori che influenzano questa decisione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many factors that influence this decision.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio nonno vive in una fattoria in Toscana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather lives on a farm in Tuscany.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In Toscana ci sono molte fattorie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In Tuscany there are many farms.

definitions.note: Often used for traditional children’s stories; it can also mean a made-up story that teaches a lesson (like a fable).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La mamma legge una favola ai bambini prima di dormire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Mom reads a fairy tale to the children before they go to sleep.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hai fatto un lavoro favoloso!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You did a fabulous job!

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase “per favore” = “please.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi fai un favore?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you do me a favor?

definitions.note: Often used with “a” + noun/pronoun (e.g., “favorevole a…” = “in favor of…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono favorevole a questa proposta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am in favor of this proposal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi mandarmi il contratto via fax?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you send me the contract by fax?

definitions.note: Often used for a cloth handkerchief; in everyday speech it can also mean a paper tissue depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hai un fazzoletto?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have a tissue?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il mio compleanno è a febbraio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My birthday is in February.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho la febbre da ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve had a fever since yesterday.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) form; common in storytelling and some regions, less in everyday spoken Italian.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri fece una torta per la sua famiglia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday he/she made a cake for his/her family.

definitions.note: past historic (passato remoto), third-person plural (they)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alla fine fecero una scelta difficile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end they made a difficult choice.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) form of “fare”; common in writing, storytelling, and some regions for past events.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri feci una torta per il compleanno di mia sorella.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I made a cake for my sister’s birthday.

definitions.note: Often used for religious faith, but can also mean trust/belief in someone or something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho fede in te.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have faith in you.

definitions.note: Often used about a person (or even a dog) who is loyal; it can also describe being faithful in a relationship.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un amico fedele.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a faithful friend.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Apprezzo la tua fedeltà.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I appreciate your loyalty.

definitions.note: Often refers to federal law enforcement agents.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I federali stanno indagando sul caso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The federal agents are investigating the case.

definitions.note: Commonly used as a loanword in Italian, especially in work/school and tech contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi puoi dare un feedback su questo progetto?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you give me some feedback on this project?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il fegato è un organo molto importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The liver is a very important organ.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono felice di vederti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m happy to see you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vivono felicemente insieme da molti anni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They have lived happily together for many years.

definitions.note: plural form (masculine or feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo felici di vederti oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re happy to see you today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La felicità viene dalle piccole cose.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Happiness comes from the little things.

definitions.note: Used for animals and for people in a general/biological sense; when talking about a woman as a person, "donna" is often more natural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il veterinario dice che il gatto è una femmina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The vet says the cat is a female.

definitions.note: Often used with a disparaging tone (diminutive, sometimes sexist).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Smettila di dire a tuo figlio che è una femminuccia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop telling your son that he's a little girl.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo è un fenomeno interessante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is an interesting phenomenon.

definitions.note: In informal Italian, it can also mean someone who is exceptionally good at something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Marco è un fenomeno a calcio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Marco is a phenomenon at soccer.

definitions.note: Usually used in the plural to mean time off work.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ad agosto siamo in ferie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In August we’re on vacation.

definitions.note: Often used for physical wounds; can also be used figuratively for hurting someone’s feelings.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non volevo ferire nessuno con quelle parole.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn’t mean to hurt anyone with those words.

definitions.note: past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person plural (they)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nella battaglia ferirono tre soldati.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the battle they wounded three soldiers.

definitions.note: Future tense (3rd person singular) of "ferire".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se lo colpisci, lo ferirà.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you hit him, it will hurt him.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa ferita ferisce ancora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This wound still hurts.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "ferire"; used with feminine singular nouns (or as a feminine singular adjective).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo la caduta, Maria è ferita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the fall, Maria is injured.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La ferita sulla mano sta guarendo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wound on my hand is healing.

definitions.note: feminine singular form (used to describe a female person or a feminine noun)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo l'incidente, lei è ferita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the accident, she is injured.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (“you all”) form of "ferire"; can be present tense or an imperative, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non ferite gli animali.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t hurt the animals.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le ferite si sono infettate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wounds got infected.

definitions.note: feminine plural adjective
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le persone ferite sono state portate in ospedale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The injured people were taken to the hospital.

definitions.note: past participle (often used like an adjective)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo l’incidente, ci sono due feriti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the accident, there are two injured people.

definitions.note: plural form (masculine or mixed group)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo l’incidente, ci sono stati tre feriti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the accident, there were three injured people.

definitions.note: plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I feriti sono stati portati in ospedale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The injured people were taken to the hospital.

definitions.note: past participle of "ferire"; often used like an adjective
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi sono ferito al dito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I injured my finger.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il cane è ferito alla zampa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is injured in its paw.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular (he/she/it) of "fermare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’autobus ferma davanti alla stazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus stops in front of the station.

definitions.note: Informal singular command (tu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ferma la macchina qui, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop the car here, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La macchina è ferma al semaforo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car is stopped at the traffic light.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 1st person singular; common in narration and in some regions, less in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi fermai davanti alla porta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I stopped in front of the door.

definitions.note: Gerund of "fermare"; it means "stopping" or "by stopping". Not related to "firmare" (to sign).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto fermando la macchina davanti a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm stopping the car in front of the house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi fermarci un momento?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you stop us for a moment?

definitions.note: Here “ci” means “there/at that point,” often used with words like “qui/lì.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dobbiamo fermarci qui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to stop here.

definitions.note: Often used with a direct object to mean “to stop something/someone.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi fermare la macchina qui?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you stop the car here?

definitions.note: Used especially with police/authorities as the subject.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La polizia ha fermato due sospetti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police arrested two suspects.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “la” (“it” for a feminine noun, or “her”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi fermarla, per favore?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you stop it/her, please?

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “le” = “them” (feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dobbiamo fermarle subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to stop them right away.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “li” (“them”, masculine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devi fermarli prima che escano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to stop them before they go out.

definitions.note: Infinitive of "fermare" with the direct object pronoun "lo" attached ("him/it").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo fermarlo prima che entri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to stop him before he goes in.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs like "dovere" (e.g., "devo fermarmi") to mean stopping oneself / coming to a stop.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo fermarmi qui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to stop here.

definitions.note: Reflexive verb; used for stopping oneself (or a vehicle) rather than stopping something else.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dobbiamo fermarci qui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to stop here.

definitions.note: Reflexive form meaning “stop yourself”; can also be used like “stop” (e.g., “to stop/come to a stop”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devi fermarti qui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to stop here.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "fermare"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'ho fermata davanti a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I stopped it in front of the house.

definitions.note: Often used for a stop of a vehicle (e.g., bus stop) or a brief stop during a trip.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La prossima fermata è Piazza Garibaldi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The next stop is Garibaldi Square.

definitions.note: Can be used as “you (plural) stop” (present) or as a plural command (“stop!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fermate la macchina!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop the car!

definitions.note: Imperative (voi): used to tell more than one person to stop.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fermatevi qui, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop here, please.

definitions.note: Commonly used as an informal command to one person (tu).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop here!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il treno si è fermato alla stazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train stopped at the station.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police stopped (detained) a man near the bank.

definitions.note: feminine plural form of “fermo”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le mani sono ferme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hands are still.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se vedete un semaforo rosso, fermerete la macchina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you see a red traffic light, you will stop the car.

definitions.note: Future tense (he/she/it will stop). Often used for stopping a vehicle or stopping an action.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus will stop at the next stop.

definitions.note: Future tense (he/she/it will close), used especially for closing a shop or business for the day.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The shop will close at eight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fermerò la macchina davanti al semaforo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will stop the car at the traffic light.

definitions.note: Often used as the (informal) imperative “stop!”; it can also mean “you stop” in the present tense, depending on context.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop the car here, please.

definitions.note: Present tense (io) form of "fermare"; often used for stopping something/someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fermo la macchina qui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I stop the car here.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Resta fermo, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stay still, please.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Keep a firm grip on the railing.

definitions.note: Used as an interjection to tell someone to stop or hold still.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop! Don’t move!

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus stopped in front of the station.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I left the iron on the table.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form; used to describe something related to the railway/railroad (often in fixed phrases like “stazione ferroviaria”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The railway station is close to the city center.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa valle è molto fertile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This valley is very fertile.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto), used especially in written stories and in some regions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Durante la rissa, lo ferì al braccio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: During the brawl, he hurt him in the arm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stasera facciamo una festa per il tuo compleanno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tonight we’re having a party for your birthday.

definitions.note: plural of "festa".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A dicembre ci sono molte feste in città.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In December there are many celebrations in the city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Festeggiamo il tuo compleanno stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re celebrating your birthday tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stiamo festeggiando il tuo compleanno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are celebrating your birthday.

definitions.note: third-person plural (they) of "festeggiare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi festeggiano il compleanno di Marco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today they celebrate Marco’s birthday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Festeggiamo il tuo compleanno stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re celebrating your birthday tonight.

definitions.note: past participle of "festeggiare"; often used with "avere" to form past tenses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo festeggiato il tuo compleanno ieri sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We celebrated your birthday last night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani c'è un festival di musica in centro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow there is a music festival downtown.

definitions.note: Often used for a slice of bread, cake, meat, cheese, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei una fetta di torta, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like a slice of cake, please.

definitions.note: Plural of "fetta".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei due fette di pane, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like two slices of bread, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La fiamma della candela è piccola ma luminosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The candle’s flame is small but bright.

definitions.note: Plural of "fiamma".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le fiamme erano alte e luminose.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The flames were tall and bright.

definitions.note: plural of fiammifero
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hai dei fiammiferi per accendere la candela?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have any matches to light the candle?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hai un fiammifero?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have a match?

definitions.note: Plural form of "fianco"; in the body, "i fianchi" commonly means "hips."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi fanno male i fianchi dopo la corsa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My hips hurt after the run.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi fa male il fianco destro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My right side hurts.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non ho più fiato dopo la corsa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't have any breath left after the run.

definitions.note: plural of "fibra"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questi alimenti contengono molte fibre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These foods contain a lot of fiber.

definitions.note: Plural of "fico" (the fruit).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In estate mangio spesso fichi freschi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In summer I often eat fresh figs.

definitions.note: Used with a reflexive pronoun (mi/ti/si/ci/vi/si), e.g. “si fida” = “(he/she) trusts”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non si fida di me.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She doesn’t trust me.

definitions.note: the period/status of being engaged (to be married)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hanno annunciato il loro fidanzamento ieri sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They announced their engagement last night.

definitions.note: Often used for a woman you are engaged to (fiancée), but it can also mean “girlfriend” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La mia fidanzata vive a Milano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My girlfriend lives in Milan.

definitions.note: Feminine form; often used as a noun meaning “girlfriend” or “fiancée.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei è fidanzata da due anni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has been engaged for two years.

definitions.note: Female form: a woman someone is dating or engaged to; which meaning depends on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La mia fidanzata vive a Milano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My girlfriend lives in Milan.

definitions.note: Plural masculine; can refer to a group of male partners/fiancés or a mixed group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I fidanzati sono arrivati insieme alla festa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boyfriends/fiancés arrived together at the party.

definitions.note: used to describe someone who is engaged to be married (masculine singular)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui è fidanzato con Giulia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is engaged to Giulia.

definitions.note: Often means “boyfriend”; it can also mean “fiancé” when you are engaged.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il mio fidanzato vive a Milano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My boyfriend lives in Milan.

definitions.note: with ci, it means “for us to trust” (1st-person plural reflexive)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È difficile fidarci di lui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s hard for us to trust him.

definitions.note: More commonly used in the reflexive form “fidarsi” (e.g., “mi fido di te” = “I trust you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fido in te.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I trust you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fido il mio segreto a te.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I entrust my secret to you.

definitions.note: In modern Italian this verb is uncommon; people usually say "affidare". The reflexive form "fidarsi" means "to trust".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non fidare i tuoi soldi a degli sconosciuti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t entrust your money to strangers.

definitions.note: Used with "di" to say who/what you trust: "fidarmi di..."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo fidarmi di te.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to trust you.

definitions.note: Reflexive verb; typically used with "di" or "a" (e.g., "fidarsi di qualcuno", "fidarsi a qualcuno").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi fido di te.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I trust you.

definitions.note: Reflexive verb form (fidarsi) with the pronoun “ti” = “you”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non posso fidarti la mia password.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t trust you with my password.

definitions.note: Often used in the sense of depending on someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Posso fidarti questo compito?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can I rely on you with this task?

definitions.note: Includes the clitic pronoun “vi” (= you plural), so it often means “for you (all) to trust” (e.g., “fidarvi di qualcuno” = to trust someone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È difficile fidarvi di qualcuno che mente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s hard for you to trust someone who lies.

definitions.note: Past participle (feminine singular) of the reflexive verb “fidarsi”; often used with “essere” in compound tenses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi sono fidata di lui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I trusted him.

definitions.note: Form of the reflexive verb "fidarsi" (often used with "di": "fidarsi di qualcuno" = to trust someone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vi fidate di lui?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you trust him?

definitions.note: Imperative (plural): used to tell a group to trust; can mean “trust each other” or “trust yourselves,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fidatevi di me: vi aiuterò.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Trust me: I will help you.

definitions.note: Informal ("tu") imperative of the reflexive verb "fidarsi"; often used to reassure someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fidati, andrà tutto bene.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Trust me, everything will be fine.

definitions.note: Past participle of "fidarsi" (to trust / to rely on someone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi sono fidato di lui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I trusted him.

definitions.note: From the reflexive verb "fidarsi"; it’s typically used with a reflexive pronoun (e.g., "si fidava") and often with "di" ("to trust someone").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si fidava di me.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She trusted me.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense: often means “we used to trust” or “we were trusting,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci fidavamo di lui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We trusted him.

definitions.note: Used with the reflexive pronoun (si): “si fidavano (di ...)” = “they trusted (someone/something)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si fidavano di lui anche quando era difficile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They trusted him even when it was difficult.

definitions.note: From "fidarsi" (to trust); often used with "mi" (I trusted) or "di" (I trusted in).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi fidavo di lui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I trusted him.

definitions.note: Usually used with the reflexive pronoun: "si fiderà" (= he/she will trust).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si fiderà di te.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She will trust you.

definitions.note: Often used with a pronoun, e.g. “ti fidi di …?” / “mi fidi?” = “do you trust … / do you trust me?”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi fidi?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you trust me?

definitions.note: Usually used with a reflexive pronoun (e.g., “ci fidiamo”) and often followed by “di” + infinitive or “di” + noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci fidiamo di te.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We trust you.

definitions.note: From the reflexive verb “fidarsi”; it’s usually used with a reflexive pronoun (e.g., “mi fido”) and often with “di” (“mi fido di…” = “I trust…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi fido di te.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I trust you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho fiducia in te.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I trust you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono fiera di te.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m proud of you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha uno sguardo fiera e deciso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a fierce, determined look.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are proud of their work.

definitions.note: Rare/learned usage (often as a noun phrase: "il fieri" = the process of becoming/coming into being). It can look like English "fiery" but is unrelated.

definitions.note: masculine plural form of "fiero"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono fieri del loro lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are proud of their work.

definitions.note: Often used with “di” to say what someone is proud of (e.g., “fiero di te”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono fiero di te.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m proud of you.

definitions.note: Plural of "figlio".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have two children: a boy and a girl.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mia figlia ha otto anni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My daughter is eight years old.

definitions.note: plural of "figlia"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho due figlie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have two daughters.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio figlio ha otto anni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My son is eight years old.

definitions.note: Somewhat old-fashioned or affectionate; in modern everyday speech, "figlio" is more common.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un bravo figliolo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s a good son.

definitions.note: Informal/slang.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saved the file on the desktop.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stasera voglio vedere un film.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tonight I want to watch a movie.

definitions.note: past participle of "filmare"; often used with "avere" in compound tenses.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I filmed the concert with my phone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: All’università studio filosofia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At university I study philosophy.

definitions.note: Often used to mean the basic guiding principles or way of thinking behind a person, group, or project.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our approach is to put the customer first.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio fratello vuole diventare filosofo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother wants to become a philosopher.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll stay here until tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used after the noun in Italian (e.g., "la scena finale").

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is the final scene of the movie.

definitions.note: As a noun, it often refers to the last part of an event, show, or piece of music (e.g., the final act or closing section).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ending of the movie is surprising.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Queste sono le decisioni finali.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These are the final decisions.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Finalmente ho finito i compiti!

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company’s financial situation is stable.

definitions.note: feminine plural form (used with feminine plural nouns).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We discussed the financial strategies for next year.

definitions.note: Used to introduce a subordinate clause; often followed by the subjunctive when expressing a goal or expectation (e.g., waiting until something happens).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll stay here until you come back.

definitions.note: Often used in the sense of “I’m fine / it’s fine.”

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Everything’s fine: it’s fine like this.

definitions.note: Used for textures/materials (e.g., sand, salt, flour).
