definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prefer fine salt.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alla fine del film, tutti piangono.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the end of the movie, everyone cries.

definitions.note: gerund form, often used with "stare" to mean "to be [verb]-ing"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto finendo il lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m finishing the work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Apri la finestra, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Open the window, please.

definitions.note: plural of "finestra"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le finestre sono aperte perché fa caldo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The windows are open because it’s hot.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a small window, especially the window of a vehicle.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi sono addormentato vicino al finestrino del treno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I fell asleep near the train window.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui finge di essere malato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He pretends to be sick.

definitions.note: gerund form of “fingere” (used like “pretending / while pretending”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha risposto fingendo di non sapere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He answered pretending not to know.

definitions.note: Often used with “di” + infinitive (e.g., “fingere di dormire” = “to pretend to sleep”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha finto di non sentire la domanda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He pretended not to hear the question.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (past) form, used for an ongoing or habitual action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fingeva di non sapere nulla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She was pretending not to know anything.

definitions.note: past historic (passato remoto), 1st person singular
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Finii il lavoro ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I finished the work yesterday.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 1st person plural of "finire"; common in written narratives, less common in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Finimmo i compiti prima di cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We finished the homework before dinner.

definitions.native: you will finish, you will end
definitions.note: Second person singular (tu) future tense of "finire".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Finirai i compiti prima di cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will finish your homework before dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo finire i compiti prima di uscire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to finish my homework before going out.

definitions.native: to stop it, to quit it
definitions.note: Often used to tell someone to stop doing something annoying: «Finirla!» = “Stop it!/Cut it out!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devi finirla con queste scuse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You need to stop it with these excuses.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “lo” (= “it”, masculine singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo finirlo entro stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to finish it by tonight.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto), 3rd person plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo la cena, finirono il lavoro in silenzio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After dinner, they finished the work in silence.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular future (he/she/it will finish/end).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il film finirà alle dieci.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie will end at ten.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Finirò i compiti dopo cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will finish the homework after dinner.

definitions.note: Used as the present subjunctive (e.g. after expressions like 'spero che...') or as the formal imperative (Lei).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che finisca presto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope it finishes soon.

definitions.note: third-person singular (he/she/it) present tense of "finire"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il film finisce alle dieci.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie ends at ten.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci vediamo giovedì.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: See you on Thursday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La ruota gira velocemente.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La tua risposta è giusta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your answer is right.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non è giusto trattare così le persone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho già finito i compiti.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho già mangiato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve already eaten.

definitions.note: Used to agree or confirm, often in a casual tone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Già, hai ragione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yes, you’re right.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scendi giù, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come down, please.

definitions.note: Often used to indicate movement or direction downward, or to tell someone/something to go down.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scendi giù!

definitions.note: Indirect object pronoun. In spoken Italian, it’s also often used to mean “to them,” though in more formal Italian you’ll see “loro” or “a loro.”

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I gave him the book.

definitions.note: masculine plural definite article (used before most consonants; also used before vowels and some consonant clusters like s+consonant, z, gn, ps)

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The students are in class.

definitions.native: to him it, to her it
definitions.note: Combination of object pronouns: gli/le (to him/to her) + la (it, feminine). Often used with verbs like dare (to give) or dire (to tell).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'll give it to him/her tomorrow.

definitions.native: to him it, it to him

definitions.native: to him it, to him that, to him this
definitions.note: Combined pronoun: indirect object "gli" (to him) + direct object "lo" (it/that). It usually comes before the verb (or attached to an infinitive/imperative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Glielo do domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll give it to him tomorrow.

definitions.native: to him/her/them of it, some of it

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll give him one of them.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: D'inverno indosso spesso un golf nero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In winter I often wear a black turtleneck sweater.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio padre è un golfista e gioca ogni domenica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My father is a golfer and he plays every Sunday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi fa male il gomito destro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My right elbow hurts.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa palla è fatta di gomma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This ball is made of rubber.

definitions.note: Common in the plural: le gomme = tires (of a car).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo cambiare le gomme della macchina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to change the car’s tires.

definitions.note: In Italian, "gomma" can also mean an eraser (for pencils).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho dimenticato la gomma a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I forgot the eraser at home.

definitions.note: Plural of "gomma". Often means erasers in a school context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi servono due gomme per cancellare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need two erasers to erase.

definitions.note: Plural of "gomma". Commonly used for car/bike tires.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo cambiare le gomme della macchina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to change the car's tires.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo comprato una piscina gonfiabile per il giardino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We bought an inflatable pool for the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato una gonna nera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a black skirt.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato due gonne nuove.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought two new skirts.

definitions.note: Commonly used in Italian, especially in entertainment/news contexts (e.g., celebrity gossip).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non ascolto il gossip in ufficio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t listen to gossip at the office.

definitions.note: Not related to English “gotta” (= “got to”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio nonno soffre di gotta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather suffers from gout.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il governatore ha annunciato nuove misure per la sicurezza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The governor announced new measures for safety.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il governo ha annunciato nuove misure economiche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The government announced new economic measures.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una serata gradevole.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a pleasant evening.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts (e.g., “di tuo gradimento” = “to your liking”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che la proposta sia di tuo gradimento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope the proposal meets your approval.

definitions.note: Often used for temperature or angles.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi ci sono trenta gradi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today it’s thirty degrees.

definitions.note: Often used for school marks/grades.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho preso un buon grado all’esame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got a good grade on the exam.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo esercizio è di un grado più difficile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This exercise is one level more difficult.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La situazione è migliorata gradualmente nel corso dell’anno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The situation improved gradually over the course of the year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho graffiato la macchina per sbaglio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I scratched the car by accident.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto studiando la grammatica italiana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m studying Italian grammar.

definitions.note: Shortened form of "grande", used before many singular nouns (especially masculine) in fixed/common phrases.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un gran problema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a big problem.

definitions.note: Also used to mean “grown-up/adult” in contexts like “when I grow up” (da grande).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La casa è molto grande.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The house is very big.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Che grandezza di scarpe porti?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What shoe size do you wear?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La grandezza di questa artista è evidente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The greatness of this artist is obvious.

definitions.note: plural form (masculine or feminine) of "grande".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato due pizze grandi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought two large pizzas.

definitions.note: Often used to describe something impressive or spectacular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È stato un grandioso spettacolo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was a magnificent show.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il grano cresce nei campi in estate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wheat grows in the fields in summer.

definitions.note: Often used for food ("fatty/greasy"); when describing a person it can sound rude/offensive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa salsa è troppo grassa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This sauce is too greasy.

definitions.note: plural form of the adjective (masculine plural)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cerco di evitare i cibi grassi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I try to avoid fatty foods.

definitions.note: Often used both literally (body/food) and figuratively (e.g., “a fat salary/joke”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo formaggio è molto grasso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This cheese is very fatty.

definitions.note: Commonly used to talk about fat in food or on the body; it can also mean “grease” in some contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'è troppo grasso in questa carne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There's too much fat in this meat.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "grato".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono grata per il tuo aiuto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am grateful for your help.

definitions.note: Often used in more formal/literary contexts, meaning something is pleasing or welcome.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La tua visita è stata grata a tutti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your visit was welcome to everyone.

definitions.note: feminine plural form of "grato" (used with feminine plural nouns/pronouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo grate per il tuo aiuto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are grateful for your help.

definitions.note: plural form (masculine or mixed) of "grato"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo grati per il tuo aiuto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are grateful for your help.

definitions.note: Usually means “at no cost” (free of charge).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'ingresso è gratis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Admission is free.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti do un campione gratis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'll give you a free sample.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'ingresso è gratis oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Admission is free today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Provo molta gratitudine per il tuo aiuto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel a lot of gratitude for your help.

definitions.note: Often used with “a” or “per” (e.g., “grato a/di/per”). Slightly formal compared to “contento” or “felice”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti sono molto grato per il tuo aiuto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m very grateful to you for your help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho grattato la macchina mentre parcheggiavo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I scratched the car while I was parking.

definitions.note: Often used for food like cheese (e.g., formaggio grattato).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho grattato il formaggio sulla pasta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I grated the cheese on the pasta.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il gatto grattò la porta per entrare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat scratched the door to come in.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form; used for something offered at no cost.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’entrata è gratuita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Admission is free.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’ingresso al museo è gratuito, quindi oggi possiamo entrare gratuitamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Admission to the museum is free, so today we can go in for free.

definitions.note: Often used for services/entry/items that cost no money.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'ingresso al museo è gratuito oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Entry to the museum is free today.

definitions.note: Used for situations, problems, illnesses, or consequences.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un problema grave.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a serious problem.

definitions.note: Often used to describe the seriousness or severity of a problem, injury, or situation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È rimasto gravemente ferito nell’incidente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was seriously injured in the accident.

definitions.note: Plural form (masculine or feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le conseguenze sono gravi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The consequences are serious.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Durante la gravidanza, è importante mangiare in modo sano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: During pregnancy, it’s important to eat healthily.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La gravità tiene i pianeti in orbita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Gravity keeps the planets in orbit.

definitions.note: Often used to talk about the seriousness of a situation or problem.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non capisci la gravità della situazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You don’t understand the seriousness of the situation.

definitions.note: Used as an interjection to express gratitude (even though the lemma is the noun “grazia”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Grazie per l’aiuto!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thanks for the help!

definitions.note: Often used with "a" before a noun/pronoun: "grazie a" = "thanks to".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Grazie a te, ho trovato la strada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thanks to you, I found the way.

definitions.note: Often used on its own; can be strengthened as “grazie mille” (“thanks a lot”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Grazie per il tuo aiuto!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thank you for your help!

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Che gattina graziosa!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What a cute kitten!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La ballerina si muoveva graziosamente sul palco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dancer moved gracefully on the stage.

definitions.note: Often used when someone does something in a courteous way (similar to “kindly” in English).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi ha risposto graziosamente, anche se era di fretta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She replied to me kindly, even though he/she was in a hurry.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La cucina greca è molto famosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Greek cuisine is very famous.

definitions.note: Can describe something from Greece (language, people, culture).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto imparando il greco a scuola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m learning Greek at school.

definitions.note: Can refer to a Greek person or, more generally, something/someone from Greece; it can also be used as an adjective in other contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Un greco vive nel mio palazzo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A Greek person lives in my building.

definitions.note: Often used to mean the Greek language, especially in phrases like “parlare greco”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Studio il greco all’università.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I study Greek at university.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mia madre indossa un grembiule quando cucina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My mother wears an apron when she cooks.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il bambino dorme nel grembo della madre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The child sleeps in the mother's lap.

definitions.note: Often used in a more literary sense to mean someone’s bosom/embrace (a place of protection or closeness).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cercò rifugio nel grembo della famiglia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He sought refuge in the bosom of his family.

definitions.note: Often used for “he/she shouts” (present tense of “gridare”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui grida quando è arrabbiato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He shouts when he’s angry.

definitions.note: Can also be the informal (tu) command form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Grida più forte!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Shout louder!

definitions.note: present gerund ("-ing" form) of "gridare"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È entrato in casa gridando il mio nome.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He came into the house shouting my name.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non gridare, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t shout, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho gridato perché non mi sentiva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I shouted because he/she couldn’t hear me.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (past) tense; describes an ongoing or repeated action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il bambino gridava perché aveva paura.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The child was shouting because he was scared.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person singular: “(he/she) shouted.” Common in written narration; in speech you’ll often hear “ha gridato.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando vide il cane, gridò e scappò.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he saw the dog, he shouted and ran away.

definitions.note: plural form (masculine) of "grigio"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato dei pantaloni grigi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought some gray pants.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of “grigio”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La macchina è grigia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car is gray.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi il cielo è grigio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today the sky is gray.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Metti le verdure sulla griglia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put the vegetables on the grill.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stasera voglio grigliare il pesce.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tonight I want to grill the fish.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho grigliato le verdure per cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I grilled the vegetables for dinner.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto), 3rd person singular: “he/she/it grilled.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri sera grigliò la carne in giardino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night he grilled the meat in the yard.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci vuole grinta per finire questa gara.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It takes grit to finish this race.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "grosso".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato una pizza grossa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a big pizza.

definitions.note: feminine plural form; used to agree with feminine plural nouns
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato delle mele grosse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought some big apples.

definitions.note: masculine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato due libri grossi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought two big books.

definitions.note: Often implies something physically big/thick or “a lot” in size/amount; can be used before or after the noun depending on meaning.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha un cane grosso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has a big dog.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo entrati in una grotta vicino al mare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We went into a cave near the sea.

definitions.note: Plural of "gruppo".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono tre gruppi nella classe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are three groups in the class.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo un gruppo di amici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are a group of friends.

definitions.note: Present tense (he/she/it earns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guadagna bene con questo lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He earns well with this job.

definitions.note: Often used for earning money (a salary, income), but can also mean earning/obtaining something through effort.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guadagno 1.500 euro al mese.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I earn 1,500 euros a month.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho guadagnato molti soldi quest’anno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I earned a lot of money this year.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past, ongoing/habitual action).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando lavorava in banca, guadagnava bene.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he worked at the bank, he was earning well.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quanto guadagni al mese?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How much do you earn per month?

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person singular: used mainly in writing and in Southern Italy to talk about completed actions in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nel 2010 guadagnò molti soldi con quel lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In 2010, he/she earned a lot of money with that job.

definitions.note: Plural of "guaio".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non voglio guai con la polizia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want trouble with the police.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono nei guai se arrivo tardi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m in trouble if I arrive late.

definitions.note: plural of "guancia".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi fanno male le guance quando sorrido troppo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My cheeks hurt when I smile too much.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi fa male la guancia destra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My right cheek hurts.

definitions.note: plural of "guanto"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho dimenticato i guanti a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I forgot my gloves at home.

definitions.note: informal (tu) command
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guarda questa foto!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Look at this photo!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui guarda la TV ogni sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He watches TV every evening.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto) of "guardare"; common in written narratives and in some regions of Italy.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guardai fuori dalla finestra e vidi la pioggia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I looked out the window and saw the rain.

definitions.note: Informal (tu) form: command (imperative) + object pronoun mi (“me”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guardami negli occhi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Look me in the eyes.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 1st person plural of “guardare”; often used in writing and in some regions in speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri guardammo un film a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday we watched a movie at home.

definitions.note: Often used with "stare" to talk about what you are doing right now (present continuous).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto guardando la TV.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m watching TV.

definitions.note: gerund form with the direct object pronoun “li” = “them” (masculine plural, or mixed group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stavo guardandoli dalla finestra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was watching them from the window.

definitions.note: Gerund of "guardare" with the direct object pronoun "li" (= them, masculine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto imparando molto guardandoli lavorare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m learning a lot by watching them work.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present of "guardare" (they).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guardano un film in salotto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They’re watching a movie in the living room.

definitions.note: Often means “to watch” with TV/films/sports, and “to look at” with people or things.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guardiamo un film stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re watching a movie tonight.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “la” (= her; also “it” for feminine nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio guardarla negli occhi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to look at her in the eyes.

definitions.note: includes the object pronoun "le" = "them" (feminine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio guardarle domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to look at them tomorrow.

definitions.native: to watch him/it, to look at him/it
definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “lo” (= him/it, masculine singular) attached to the verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio guardarlo adesso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to watch him/it now.

definitions.native: to look at me, to watch me
definitions.note: Infinitive with an attached indirect object pronoun: "-mi" = "me".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi guardarmi un attimo?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you look at me for a moment?

definitions.note: Infinitive "guardare" with the object pronoun "mi" attached ("me").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi guardarmi un attimo?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you look at me for a moment?

definitions.note: Used for a place or service where you leave coats and bags (e.g., in a theater), or for a wardrobe/closet in general.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi lasciare il cappotto al guardaroba.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can leave your coat at the cloakroom.

definitions.note: past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guardarono il film fino alla fine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They watched the movie until the end.

definitions.note: Infinitive "guardare" with the object pronoun "ti" (= you).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio guardarti negli occhi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to look you in the eyes.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "guardare"; it often agrees with a feminine direct object pronoun (e.g., "l'ho guardata").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’ho guardata tutta la sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I watched her all evening.

definitions.note: 2nd person plural present (also used as the polite form with "voi").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guardate questo video!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Watch this video!

definitions.note: Command form addressed to more than one person ("you all"); includes the object pronoun "it".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guardatelo bene prima di decidere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Look at it carefully before deciding.

definitions.note: Plural informal command (voi); can also mean “watch me” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guardatemi, ho qualcosa di importante da dirvi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Look at me, I have something important to tell you.

definitions.note: Plural informal command (to “voi”); can mean literally “look at yourselves” or more generally “be careful / watch out.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guardatevi allo specchio!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Look at yourselves in the mirror!

definitions.note: Informal singular command (tu), reflexive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guardati allo specchio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Look at yourself in the mirror.

definitions.note: Often used as a warning (informal singular command: tu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guardati dalla macchina!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Watch out for the car!

definitions.note: Often confused with English “guard/guarded,” but it usually means “watched/looked at.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho guardato un film ieri sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I watched a movie last night.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing or habitual action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guardava la TV quando ho chiamato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She was watching TV when I called.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (past habitual/ongoing): often implies something happening repeatedly or in progress in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da piccoli, guardavamo i cartoni animati ogni mattina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When we were kids, we watched cartoons every morning.

definitions.note: imperfect tense (3rd person plural): describes an ongoing or habitual action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I bambini guardavano la TV dopo cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children were watching TV after dinner.

definitions.native: I was watching, I was looking at
definitions.note: Imperfetto (past) form: often used for an ongoing or habitual action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guardavo la TV quando mi hai chiamato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was watching TV when you called me.

definitions.note: Third-person singular future tense of "guardare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani guarderà un film a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow he/she will watch a movie at home.

definitions.note: Often used as a polite/formal command (addressing someone as “Lei”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guardi qui, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Look here, please.

definitions.note: Often used for a person who watches over or protects something; in some contexts it can also refer to being on duty (e.g., "di guardia" = on duty).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'è una guardia all'ingresso dell'edificio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a guard at the entrance of the building.

definitions.note: Can also mean “let’s watch/look (at) …” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guardiamo un film stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re watching a movie tonight.

definitions.note: Plural of "guardia".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: All'ingresso ci sono due guardie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are two guards at the entrance.

definitions.note: Present tense (io) form of "guardare"; often used for looking at something or watching (e.g., TV).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guardo la TV dopo cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I watch TV after dinner.

definitions.note: Passato remoto (simple past), common in writing and in some regions for past events.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guardò il film fino alla fine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She watched the movie until the end.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero di guarire presto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope to recover soon.

definitions.note: Future tense (third person singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Con un po' di riposo, guarirà presto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With a bit of rest, he/she will recover soon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo una settimana di riposo, sono guarito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After a week of rest, I recovered.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La guerra è finita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The war is over.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le guerre nel mondo causano sofferenza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wars in the world cause suffering.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il guerriero proteggeva il villaggio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The warrior protected the village.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Di notte ho sentito un gufo nel bosco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At night I heard an owl in the woods.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La guida ci spiega la storia del museo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The guide explains the history of the museum to us.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato una guida di Roma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a guidebook to Rome.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Marco guida l’auto ogni giorno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Marco drives the car every day.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto), often used in narratives; in conversation you’ll usually hear the passato prossimo instead.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri guidai fino a Roma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I drove all the way to Rome.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto), often used in narratives.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guidai il gruppo attraverso il bosco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I guided the group through the woods.

definitions.note: gerund of "guidare"; often used like English “while driving” or “by driving.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto ascoltando un podcast guidando.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm listening to a podcast while driving.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: So guidare, ma non ho la macchina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can drive, but I don’t have a car.

definitions.note: Used for leading a person/group or guiding (e.g., a tour, a discussion).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'insegnante guida gli studenti durante l'esercizio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher guides the students during the exercise.

definitions.note: Present tense, second-person plural (voi).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guidate piano, c’è molta nebbia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Drive slowly, there’s a lot of fog.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho guidato tutta la notte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I drove all night.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (past habitual/ongoing).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri sera guidava troppo veloce.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night he was driving too fast.

definitions.note: first-person singular (io), past imperfect tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guidavo piano perché pioveva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was driving slowly because it was raining.

definitions.native: will drive, will guide, will lead
definitions.note: Future tense (3rd person singular) of "guidare"; it can refer to driving a vehicle or guiding/leading someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani guiderà lui fino a Firenze.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow he will drive as far as Florence.

definitions.note: Form of "guidare" used for (1) the present subjunctive (e.g., "che io/tu/lui guidi") and (2) the informal (tu) imperative ("guidi!" = "drive!"), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che tu guidi piano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you drive slowly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Di solito guido io.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I usually drive.

definitions.note: Often used with a direct object (e.g., people) or with "a" + place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guido i turisti nel museo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I guide the tourists in the museum.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri Marco guidò fino a Roma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday Marco drove to Rome.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il cane è al guinzaglio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is on a leash.

definitions.note: past participle (masculine plural) of “gustare”; often used in the passive (e.g., “sono stati gustati”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I piatti sono stati gustati da tutti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dishes were enjoyed by everyone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gusti il vino prima di comprarlo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You taste the wine before buying it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In gelateria ci sono molti gusti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the ice cream shop there are many flavors.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ognuno ha i suoi gusti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Everyone has their own preferences.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo gelato ha un gusto molto dolce.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This ice cream has a very sweet taste.

definitions.note: Often used in expressions like "mi piace" / "non mi piace" or "a mio gusto" (in my opinion).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A mio gusto, questa pasta è troppo salata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In my opinion, this pasta is too salty.

definitions.note: Auxiliary form of "avere" used to build the passato prossimo (e.g., "ha mangiato" = "has eaten").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha finito il lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has finished the work.

definitions.note: Also used as the auxiliary “has” with a past participle (passato prossimo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Marco ha due sorelle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Marco has two sisters.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary with a past participle to form compound tenses (e.g., passato prossimo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hai già finito i compiti?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Have you already finished your homework?

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) form of "avere" in the present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hai tempo oggi?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have time today?

definitions.note: Used mainly for food/products permitted under Islamic dietary rules.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preferisco un ristorante halal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prefer a halal restaurant.

definitions.note: Common loanword in Italian, especially for hotels, cinemas, and large buildings.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci vediamo nell’hall dell’hotel alle otto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: See you in the hotel lobby at eight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prendo un hamburger e una bibita, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll have a hamburger and a drink, please.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary with a past participle to form compound tenses (e.g., passato prossimo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hanno già finito il lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They have already finished the work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hanno due cani e un gatto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They have two dogs and a cat.

definitions.note: German exclamation; in Italian it’s mainly seen in historical/political contexts (e.g., Nazi slogans).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sul manifesto c'era scritto: «Heil!».
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On the poster it said: “Hail!”.

definitions.note: Used to get someone’s attention or as an informal greeting.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hey, scusa, sai che ore sono?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hey, sorry, do you know what time it is?

definitions.note: Refers to the head covering worn by some Muslim women.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Indossa l’hijab quando esce di casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wears a hijab when she leaves the house.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary with a past participle to form the present perfect (passato prossimo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho finito i compiti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have finished my homework.

definitions.note: Also used as an auxiliary with a past participle to form the past tense (passato prossimo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho due fratelli.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have two brothers.

definitions.note: From Tolkien’s stories; used as a common noun for that fictional race.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nel libro, lo hobbit parte per un lungo viaggio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the book, the hobbit sets off on a long journey.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il mio hobby è la fotografia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My hobby is photography.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gioco a hockey ogni sabato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I play hockey every Saturday.

definitions.note: Used in Italian mainly in contexts like events, flights, restaurants, or promotions (often as an English loanword).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'hostess ci ha accolti all'ingresso dell'evento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hostess welcomed us at the entrance of the event.

definitions.note: English loanword used in informal Italian.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui è proprio un hot.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s really a hottie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo prenotato un hotel vicino alla stazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We booked a hotel near the station.

definitions.note: Plural masculine definite article (plural form of “il”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I ragazzi studiano in biblioteca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boys are studying in the library.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo visto un enorme iceberg in lontananza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We saw a huge iceberg in the distance.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo l’ictus, ha iniziato la riabilitazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the stroke, he started rehabilitation.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have an idea for the project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo posto è ideale per una vacanza tranquilla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This place is ideal for a quiet vacation.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il mio ideale è aiutare gli altri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My ideal is to help others.

definitions.note: plural of "idea"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho molte idee per il progetto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have many ideas for the project.

definitions.note: feminine singular form.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your signature is identical to mine.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I due documenti sono identici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The two documents are identical.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The suspect was identified by the police.

definitions.note: simple past (passato remoto), 3rd person singular
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La polizia identificò il sospetto grazie alle telecamere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police identified the suspect thanks to the cameras.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha perso la carta d’identità.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lost his ID card.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase “carta d’identità” (identity card).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi serve un documento d’identità per il check-in.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need an ID for check-in.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s an idiotic decision.

definitions.note: Often insulting; can also be used jokingly among friends depending on tone and context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non essere un idiota: guarda dove cammini!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t be an idiot: watch where you’re walking!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non ascoltare quegli idioti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t listen to those idiots.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dire una cosa del genere è un'idiozia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Saying something like that is idiocy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri sono andato al supermercato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I went to the supermarket.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui ignora il problema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He ignores the problem.

definitions.note: Informal singular command (tu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ignora i commenti negativi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ignore the negative comments.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 1st person plural.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha continuato a parlare, ignorando le mie domande.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti prego, non ignorare i miei messaggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please, don’t ignore my messages.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La tua email è stata ignorata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your email was ignored.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ignorate i commenti cattivi e continuate a lavorare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ignore the nasty comments and keep working.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form (used to agree with feminine plural nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le tue richieste sono state ignorate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your requests were ignored.

definitions.note: Past participle (masculine plural) of "ignorare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I loro avvertimenti sono stati ignorati.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Their warnings were ignored.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ignore the mean comments and keep studying.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti ignorerò se continui a urlare.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ignoro la risposta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't know the answer.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He ignored the message and left the house.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Chapter II: The basic rules.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book is on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È illegale parcheggiare qui.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He parked illegally in front of the entrance.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La firma sul documento è illeggibile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The signature on the document is illegible.

definitions.note: A Muslim religious leader (especially one who leads prayers in a mosque).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The imam leads the prayer in the mosque.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are all embarrassed in this situation.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This team is unbeatable.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ran into an old friend at the supermarket.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi sono imbattuto in un vecchio amico al supermercato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ran into an old friend at the supermarket.

definitions.note: Often insulting when used about a person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una cosa imbecille da fare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a stupid thing to do.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non fare l’imbecille!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t be an idiot!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hai imbrogliato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You tricked me.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The seller tricked the tourists with a fake price.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to mail this letter before five o’clock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho mangiato una fetta di pane imburrato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ate a slice of buttered bread.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preferisco il pane imburrato a colazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prefer buttered bread for breakfast.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night he buttered the bread and put it in the oven.

definitions.note: Present gerund of "imitare"; often means “while/by imitating.”

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s learning Italian by imitating native speakers’ pronunciation.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I bambini imitano spesso i loro genitori.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Children often imitate their parents.

definitions.note: informal singular command (tu)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Immagina di vivere vicino al mare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Imagine living near the sea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prova a immaginare come sarà il futuro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Try to imagine what the future will be like.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would never have imagined something like that.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With a bit of imagination, you can make up a nice story.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa immagine è molto bella.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This image is very beautiful.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form (used after expressions like “penso che…”, “non credo che…”) for “tu” or “lui/lei/Lei”.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw some beautiful images from your trip.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I imagine you’re right.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quel comportamento è immaturo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That behavior is immature.

definitions.note: feminine singular form.
