definitions.example_sentence_native_language: An immediate answer is needed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chiamami immediatamente, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Call me immediately, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo bisogno di una risposta immediata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need an immediate response.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il mare è immenso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sea is immense.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Rimase immobile davanti alla porta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He stayed motionless in front of the door.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È stato un comportamento immorale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was immoral behavior.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo il vaccino, sono immune alla malattia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the vaccine, I am immune to the disease.

definitions.note: Often used for someone who feels self-conscious or uncomfortable, especially in social situations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi sento impacciato quando parlo in pubblico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel awkward when I speak in public.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il suo aiuto è stato impagabile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His help was priceless.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo la notizia, è rimasta impallidita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the news, she remained pale.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando sentì la notizia, impallidì.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he heard the news, he turned pale.

definitions.note: present tense, 3rd person singular (he/she/it learns)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Impara l’italiano guardando film e ascoltando musica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He learns Italian by watching movies and listening to music.

definitions.note: imperative (tu): used to give an informal command
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Impara queste parole e ripeti dopo di me.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Learn these words and repeat after me.

definitions.note: simple past (passato remoto), used often in written narratives and in some regions instead of the passato prossimo
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da bambino imparai a nuotare al mare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As a child, I learned to swim at the sea.

definitions.note: past historic (passato remoto), 1st person plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Imparammo l’italiano in pochi mesi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We learned Italian in a few months.

definitions.note: gerund/present participle of "imparare"; often used with "stare" to mean "to be (in the process of) learning"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto imparando l'italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am learning Italian.

definitions.note: third-person plural present (they learn)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A scuola imparano l'italiano molto velocemente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At school they learn Italian very quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto imparando l’italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m learning Italian.

definitions.note: 2nd person plural present indicative of "imparare" (used for "you" plural: you all / you formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Imparate l’italiano a scuola?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you learn Italian at school?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho imparato l'italiano a scuola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I learned Italian at school.

definitions.note: Used to say someone (feminine singular) is related to someone else by family ties, often through marriage.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei è imparentata con una famiglia importante del paese.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is related to an important family in the town.

definitions.note: feminine plural; often used for families or people connected through marriage
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le due famiglie sono imparentate da generazioni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The two families have been related by marriage for generations.

definitions.note: Often used to say two families are connected through marriage.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono imparentati con la famiglia Rossi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are related to the Rossi family (by marriage).

definitions.note: Third-person singular future tense (lui/lei/Lei).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Imparerà l’italiano in pochi mesi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She will learn Italian in a few months.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Impari l'italiano molto in fretta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You learn Italian very quickly.

definitions.note: Present tense (noi) of "imparare"; can also be used as an invitation/encouragement (“let’s…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Impariamo l’italiano insieme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We learn Italian together.

definitions.note: Present tense (io).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Imparo l'italiano ogni giorno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I learn Italian every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il giudice deve essere imparziale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The judge must be impartial.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person singular (he/she learned).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da piccolo imparò a nuotare in mare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As a child, he learned to swim in the sea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il nuovo progetto avrà un grande impatto sull’ambiente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The new project will have a big impact on the environment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il bambino era impaurito dal temporale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The child was scared of the thunderstorm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono impaziente di vedere il film stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m impatient to see the movie tonight.

definitions.note: plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo impazienti di iniziare la lezione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are impatient to start the lesson.

definitions.native: to go crazy, to go mad
definitions.note: Often used both literally (to become mentally unstable) and figuratively (to lose control, e.g. from stress or excitement).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando ha sentito la notizia, ha impazzito dalla gioia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he heard the news, he went crazy with joy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo la notizia, lei è impazzita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the news, she went crazy.

definitions.note: Past participle (masculine plural) of "impazzire"; often used with "essere" (e.g., "sono impazziti").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono impazziti quando hanno sentito la notizia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They went crazy when they heard the news.

definitions.note: past participle of "impazzire"; often used with "essere" (e.g., "sono impazzito")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono impazzito quando ho perso le chiavi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I went crazy when I lost my keys.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) form; often used in narratives, especially in writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando vide la notizia, impazzì dalla rabbia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he saw the news, he went crazy with anger.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il servizio è stato impeccabile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The service was impeccable.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La pioggia impedì la partita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rain prevented the match.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi sono impegnata e non posso uscire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I’m busy and I can’t go out.

definitions.note: Used for a woman; often said as "essere impegnata".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei è impegnata: si sposa l’anno prossimo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She’s engaged: she’s getting married next year.

definitions.note: Plural feminine form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi siamo tutte impegnate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today we’re all busy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo molto impegnati oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are very busy today.

definitions.note: Often used to say someone is occupied (e.g., already has plans or is unavailable).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi sono impegnato e non posso venire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I’m busy and I can’t come.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho un impegno domani mattina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a commitment tomorrow morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo impegno richiede tempo e attenzione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This task requires time and attention.

definitions.note: reflexive gerund; describes an action in progress or happening at the same time as another action
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha tentato di scappare impiccandosi alla ringhiera del balcone.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tried to escape by hanging himself from the balcony railing.

definitions.note: Often used as a past participle in passive constructions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È stato impiccato per i suoi crimini.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was hanged for his crimes.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) form; often used in storytelling or historical accounts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nel romanzo, il re impiccò il traditore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the novel, the king hanged the traitor.

definitions.note: plural form of "impiegato" (often office workers or staff in a business).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gli impiegati dell’ufficio arrivano alle nove.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The office employees arrive at nine.

definitions.note: Often refers to an office worker (as opposed to a manual laborer).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio padre è un impiegato in banca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My father is an employee at a bank.

definitions.note: Plural of "impiego".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha cambiato impieghi tre volte quest’anno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She changed jobs three times this year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto cercando un impiego a tempo pieno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m looking for a full-time job.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo lavoro implica molte responsabilità.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This job involves a lot of responsibilities.

definitions.note: gerund form of "imporre"; used for actions in progress (often translated with “-ing”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stai imponendo troppe regole ai bambini.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are imposing too many rules on the children.

definitions.note: Often used impersonally, like “non importa” = “it doesn’t matter.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non importa se arrivi tardi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It doesn’t matter if you arrive late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’Italia importa petrolio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Italy imports oil.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un documento importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s an important document.

definitions.note: plural (masculine or feminine), used with plural nouns
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questi documenti sono importanti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These documents are important.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa decisione ha molta importanza per noi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This decision is very important for us.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'Italia importa molto petrolio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Italy imports a lot of oil.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase “importa” (it matters) or “non importa” (it doesn’t matter).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non importa se arrivi in ritardo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It doesn’t matter if you arrive late.

definitions.note: Used in the subjunctive (e.g., after se “if”, or in hypothetical situations).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se l'azienda importasse più caffè, i prezzi scenderebbero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If the company imported more coffee, prices would go down.

definitions.note: From importare meaning “to matter”; often used with an implied subject like “it”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non credo che importasse davvero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t think it really mattered.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa frutta è importata dal Brasile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This fruit is imported from Brazil.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (past habitual/ongoing): often used like “it mattered” / “it used to matter.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non mi importava cosa dicevano gli altri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn’t care what the others said.

definitions.note: conditional (present) form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se avesse più soldi, importerebbe più prodotti dall’Italia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If he had more money, he would import more products from Italy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che l’azienda importi caffè dal Brasile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope the company imports coffee from Brazil.

definitions.note: Often used with an indirect object (e.g., “mi/ti/gli importa” = “I/you/he cares”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non credo che ti importi davvero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t think you really care.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È impossibile finire tutto oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s impossible to finish everything today.

definitions.note: plural (masculine or feminine), used with plural nouns
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questi esercizi sono impossibili.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These exercises are impossible.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si è finto medico, ma era un impostore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He pretended to be a doctor, but he was an impostor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi sento impotente davanti a questa situazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel powerless in the face of this situation.

definitions.note: Often refers to swearing or using strong language (sometimes blaspheming), especially when angry.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stava imprecando contro il traffico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She was cursing at the traffic.

definitions.note: Often used for swearing angrily (sometimes against someone/something: “imprecare contro …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nel traffico ha cominciato a imprecare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In traffic, he started swearing.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È stato uno spettacolo impressionante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was an impressive show.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio impressionare i miei genitori con i miei voti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to impress my parents with my grades.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “la” (= her).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio impressionarla con il mio italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to impress her with my Italian.

definitions.note: Includes the attached pronoun “-le” (= them, feminine), meaning you are impressing a group of women/things referred to with feminine plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio impressionarle con il mio italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to impress them with my Italian.

definitions.note: Verb with the direct object pronoun "li" attached ("them").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio impressionarli con il mio italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to impress them with my Italian.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle (often used like an adjective)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono impressionata dal tuo italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m impressed by your Italian.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono rimasta impressionata dal concerto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was impressed by the concert.

definitions.note: Second-person plural form: used for “you (all) impress” and also as a plural command “impress!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando parlate in pubblico, impressionate tutti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When you speak in public, you impress everyone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le ragazze sono impressionate dalla notizia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The girls are impressed by the news.

definitions.note: Used for a group of men or a mixed group (masculine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo rimasti impressionati dal panorama.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We were impressed by the view.

definitions.note: masculine plural adjective
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo rimasti impressionati dalla tua presentazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We were impressed by your presentation.

definitions.note: Past participle of "impressionare"; often used like an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono impressionato dal tuo italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m impressed by your Italian.

definitions.note: often used with “da” to say what impressed someone (e.g., “impressionato da…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono impressionato dal tuo italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m impressed by your Italian.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Che impressione ti ha fatto il nuovo insegnante?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What impression did the new teacher make on you?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quali sono le tue impressioni sul nuovo insegnante?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What are your impressions of the new teacher?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il tempo oggi è imprevedibile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The weather today is unpredictable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il giornalista è stato imprigionato per settimane.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The journalist was imprisoned for weeks.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È improbabile che piova oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s unlikely that it will rain today.

definitions.note: Plural of "impronta"; often used for footprints or marks left on a surface.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono impronte sulla neve.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are footprints in the snow.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È stata una decisione improvvisa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was a sudden decision.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Improvvisamente ha iniziato a piovere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Suddenly, it started to rain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo organizzato un pranzo improvvisato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We organized an improvised lunch.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È stato imprudente guidare così veloce.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was careless to drive that fast.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A volte sono troppo impulsivo e parlo senza pensare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sometimes I'm too impulsive and I speak without thinking.

definitions.note: Often combines with the definite article (e.g., nel, nello, nella, nei, negli, nelle).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono in casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm at home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il suo comportamento è inaccettabile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His behavior is unacceptable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non posso contare su di lui: è inaffidabile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t count on him: he’s unreliable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa barca è inaffondabile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This boat is unsinkable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È successo qualcosa di inaspettato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Something unexpected happened.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La strega ha lanciato un incantesimo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The witch cast a spell.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo trovato un hotel incantevole sul lago.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We found a charming hotel on the lake.

definitions.note: Often used with “di” + infinitive (e.g., “incapace di parlare”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono incapace di ricordare il suo nome.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m unable to remember his name.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form (often used like an adjective; from the verb “incastrare”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La chiave è incastrata nella serratura.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The key is stuck in the lock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il cassetto è incastrato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The drawer is stuck.

definitions.note: Common in informal contexts, especially about a person being made to seem responsible for a crime.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È stato incastrato per un furto che non ha commesso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was framed for a theft he didn’t commit.

definitions.note: Very informal and vulgar; stronger than “arrabbiato.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono incazzato per quello che è successo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm pissed off about what happened.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'è un incendio nel palazzo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a fire in the building.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono incerto su quale strada prendere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m unsure about which road to take.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto), often used in narratives; commonly with "si" as "si inchinò" = "(he/she) bowed."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si inchinò davanti al re.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He bowed before the king.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo comprare l’inchiostro per la stampante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to buy ink for the printer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho inciampato sul gradino e sono quasi caduto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I tripped on the step and almost fell.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono inciampato sul marciapiede.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I tripped on the sidewalk.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto), 3rd person singular: “he/she tripped.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mentre correva, inciampò in una pietra e cadde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: While he was running, he tripped over a stone and fell.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’è stato un incidente sulla strada stamattina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There was an accident on the road this morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono stati due incidenti sulla strada stamattina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There were two accidents on the road this morning.

definitions.note: Used mainly for women; for animals, Italian often uses "gravida".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mia sorella è incinta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is pregnant.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il prezzo include la colazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The price includes breakfast.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form (past participle) of “includere”; often used like an adjective or with “essere”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La colazione è inclusa nel prezzo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Breakfast is included in the price.

definitions.note: Past participle of "includere"; often used like an adjective (e.g., in prices or lists).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il prezzo è già incluso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The price is already included.

definitions.note: Can be used as "you (plural) glue/stick" (present) or as a plural command ("glue!/stick!").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voi incollate le foto nell’album.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You glue the photos into the album.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che tu incolli bene l’etichetta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you glue the label on well.

definitions.note: Often used with "di": "incolpare qualcuno di qualcosa" (to blame/accuse someone of something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Marco incolpa sua sorella dell’errore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Marco blames his sister for the mistake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non puoi incolpare me per quello che è successo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can’t blame me for what happened.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non puoi incolparla per quello che è successo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can’t blame her for what happened.

definitions.note: “lo” is a direct object pronoun meaning “him” or “it” (masculine singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non puoi incolparlo per quello che è successo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can’t blame him for what happened.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Incolparono Marco dell’incidente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They blamed Marco for the accident.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Incolpate sempre gli altri per i vostri errori.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You always blame others for your mistakes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’uomo è stato incolpato dell’incidente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The man was blamed for the accident.

definitions.note: Subjunctive form (present) of "incolpare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non credo che tu incolpi sempre gli altri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t think you always blame others.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non ti incolpo per l'errore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t blame you for the mistake.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The newspaper blamed the mayor for the mistake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un collega incompetente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s an incompetent colleague.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La domanda è incompleta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The question is incomplete.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È inconcepibile che nessuno abbia chiamato i soccorsi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s inconceivable that nobody called for help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Era completamente inconsapevole del problema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was completely unaware of the problem.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Marco incontra spesso i suoi amici al bar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Marco often meets his friends at the café.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) form, often used in stories and in some regions for completed past actions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri incontrai Marco al mercato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I met Marco at the market.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto) form meaning “we met/encountered.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri incontrammo Marco per caso al mercato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday we met Marco by chance at the market.

definitions.note: usually means meeting someone (in person), by chance or by arrangement
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si incontrano ogni venerdì al bar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They meet every Friday at the café.

definitions.note: can also mean coming across something (often a problem or difficulty)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In viaggio incontrano molti problemi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On the trip they encounter many problems.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Possiamo incontrarci domani alle tre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We can meet each other tomorrow at three.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vuoi incontrarci dopo il lavoro?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you want to meet us after work?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani devo incontrare un amico in centro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I have to meet a friend downtown.

definitions.note: Includes the direct-object pronoun “la” (= her; or “it” for a feminine noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non vedo l’ora di incontrarla di persona.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t wait to meet her in person.

definitions.note: The pronoun "-le" means "them" (feminine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero di incontrarle domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope to meet them tomorrow.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “li” (= “them”, masculine plural; can also refer to a mixed group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo incontrarli domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to meet them tomorrow.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “lo” (= him/it, masculine singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero di incontrarlo domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope to meet him tomorrow.

definitions.note: simple past (passato remoto), 3rd person plural: “they met”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si incontrarono per caso al mercato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They met by chance at the market.

definitions.note: Includes the clitic pronoun “ti” (= you, informal singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero di incontrarti domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope to meet you tomorrow.

definitions.note: With the enclitic pronoun "-vi" meaning "you" (plural, or formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero di incontrarvi domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope to meet you tomorrow.

definitions.note: With the enclitic "-vi" meaning "there" (in that place).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Possiamo incontrarvi davanti alla stazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We can meet there in front of the station.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive of "incontrare" (used in hypotheticals or after certain past-tense expressions, often with "se" = "if").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se lo incontrasse, gli parlerebbe subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If he met him, he would talk to him right away.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "incontrare"; often agrees with a feminine direct object (or with "essere" in some contexts).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’ho incontrata ieri al mercato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I met her yesterday at the market.

definitions.note: Used with "voi" (you plural) as present tense (you meet) or as an imperative (meet!).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani incontrate i vostri amici in centro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow you meet your friends downtown.

definitions.note: Feminine plural past participle of "incontrare" (often used with "essere" in compound tenses for feminine plural subjects).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siete già incontrate al lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You already met at work.

definitions.note: Past participle masculine plural (often referring to people).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Li ho già incontrati ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I already met them yesterday.

definitions.note: Informal plural command (imperative) used as a reflexive form: “(you all) meet up / meet each other.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Incontrati con i tuoi amici alle otto!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Meet up with your friends at eight!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho incontrato Marco ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I met Marco yesterday.

definitions.note: third-person plural (they) in the future tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani incontreranno il nuovo insegnante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow they will meet the new teacher.

definitions.native: we will meet, we will run into
definitions.note: future tense, 1st person plural (noi).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani incontreremo i nostri amici al parco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will meet our friends at the park.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/it) future tense of "incontrare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani incontrerà il nuovo insegnante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow he/she will meet the new teacher.

definitions.note: second-person singular (tu) present tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ogni volta che vieni qui, incontri qualcuno che conosci.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every time you come here, you meet someone you know.

definitions.note: Present tense (noi) of "incontrare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci incontriamo al bar alle otto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We meet at the bar at eight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Incontro spesso i miei amici al bar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I often meet my friends at the café.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani ho un incontro con il mio insegnante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I have a meeting with my teacher.

definitions.note: Often used for an arranged meeting, including a romantic one.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stasera ho un incontro con una ragazza conosciuta online.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tonight I have a date with a girl I met online.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person singular: “he/she met” in storytelling and written narratives.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri al mercato incontrò un vecchio amico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday at the market he/she met an old friend.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei mi incoraggia a parlare italiano ogni giorno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She encourages me to speak Italian every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le tue parole sono davvero incoraggianti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your words are really encouraging.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle; often used with "essere" in passive or as an adjective
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È stata incoraggiata dai suoi amici a continuare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was encouraged by her friends to keep going.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi ha incoraggiato a continuare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She encouraged me to keep going.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto), third person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il suo insegnante lo incoraggiò a continuare a studiare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His teacher encouraged him to keep studying.

definitions.note: Often used to describe a person or habit that won't change.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un bugiardo incorreggibile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s an incorrigible liar.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo errore è incorreggibile senza rifare tutto da capo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This mistake is impossible to correct without redoing everything from scratch.

definitions.note: Used for a person who has lost consciousness (e.g., after an accident).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo l’incidente era incosciente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the accident he was unconscious.

definitions.note: Used to describe someone who acts without thinking about consequences.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È stato un gesto incosciente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was a reckless act.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una storia incredibile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s an incredible story.

definitions.note: plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono storie incredibili.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are incredible stories.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha finito il lavoro incredibilmente in fretta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He finished the work incredibly fast.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho incrociato Marco per strada stamattina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ran into Marco on the street this morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci vediamo all’incrocio tra Via Roma e Via Milano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: See you at the intersection between Via Roma and Via Milano.

definitions.note: Often used literally for eggs (or in science/medicine for cells, samples, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per far nascere i pulcini, bisogna incubare le uova.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: To hatch the chicks, you need to incubate the eggs.

definitions.note: Figurative: to keep something inside for a long time (e.g., resentment, a plan, an idea).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È meglio non incubare rancore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s better not to harbor resentment.

definitions.note: Plural of "incubo".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho avuto incubi tutta la notte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had nightmares all night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho fatto un incubo stanotte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had a nightmare last night.

definitions.note: Often used figuratively for a very difficult or stressful situation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo traffico è un incubo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This traffic is a nightmare.

definitions.note: Often means “made curious” or “piqued (in your interest)” rather than simply “curious” as a personality trait.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono incuriosito da questa storia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m intrigued by this story.

definitions.note: Gerund/present participle form, often used after "stare" (e.g., "sto indagando" = "I’m investigating").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La polizia sta indagando sul furto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police are investigating the theft.

definitions.note: Often used for official investigations (e.g., police or judicial).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La polizia ha aperto un'indagine sull'incidente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police opened an investigation into the accident.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo l’università, ero molto indebitato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After university, I was very in debt.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono ancora indeciso su cosa ordinare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m still undecided about what to order.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei è indiana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is Indian.

definitions.note: Plural of “indiano”. Depending on context, it can mean people from India or Native Americans.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gli indiani vivono in molte regioni del mondo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Indians live in many regions of the world.

definitions.note: Can describe a person or something from India; it also commonly refers to Indigenous peoples of the Americas in older usage (context matters).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un ristorante indiano molto buono.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a very good Indian restaurant.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto indicando la strada sulla mappa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m indicating the route on the map.

definitions.native: to point out to me, to show me, to tell me
definitions.note: Combined form: indicare + mi (“to me”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi indicarmi la strada per la stazione?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you show me the way to the station?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il percorso è stato indicato sulla mappa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The route was indicated on the map.

definitions.note: imperfect tense (they)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sulla mappa indicavano il percorso più breve.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On the map, they were indicating the shortest route.

definitions.note: Often used for directions (e.g., on the street) or instructions (e.g., for a task).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi puoi dare delle indicazioni per arrivare alla stazione?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you give me directions to get to the station?

definitions.note: Past simple (passato remoto) form, common in narratives and more formal/written Italian.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il professore indicò l’errore sulla lavagna.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The professor pointed out the mistake on the board.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs of movement (e.g., andare/tornare indietro).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fai un passo indietro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take a step back.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono rimasto indietro con i compiti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I fell behind with my homework.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il cucciolo era indifeso sotto la pioggia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The puppy was defenseless in the rain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono indifferente a quello che dicono gli altri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm indifferent to what other people say.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È stata una serata indimenticabile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was an unforgettable evening.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mia sorella è molto indipendente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is very independent.

definitions.note: Past participle (feminine singular) of "indirizzare"; often used with essere or as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La lettera è stata indirizzata al nuovo ufficio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The letter was addressed to the new office.

definitions.note: Plural of "indirizzo"; can refer to postal/email addresses or (in context) directions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho salvato tutti i tuoi indirizzi nel telefono.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saved all your addresses in my phone.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a postal or email address.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Qual è il tuo indirizzo?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is your address?

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una domanda indiscreta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s an indiscreet question.

definitions.note: Plural of "individuo".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In questa foto ci sono molti individui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this photo there are many individuals.

definitions.note: Plural of "indizio".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La polizia sta cercando nuovi indizi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police are looking for new clues.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo indizio ci aiuterà a risolvere il caso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This clue will help us solve the case.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Indossa sempre scarpe comode.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: (He/She) always wears comfortable shoes.

definitions.note: gerund form; used to mean “while wearing/putting on” or to form progressive tenses (stare + gerund).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sta entrando indossando un cappotto nero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s coming in wearing a black coat.

definitions.note: third-person plural ("they")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Indossano il cappotto perché fa freddo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are wearing their coat because it’s cold.

definitions.note: Used mainly for clothing and accessories (e.g., shoes, a jacket, glasses).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi indosso una giacca perché fa freddo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I’m wearing a jacket because it’s cold.

definitions.note: Depending on context, it can mean “you (plural) wear/are wearing” or a command “wear!/put on!” (plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Indossate la giacca, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put on the jacket, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho indossato la giacca prima di uscire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put on the jacket before going out.

definitions.note: imperfect past (ongoing/repeated action in the past)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri sera indossava un cappotto nero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night he/she was wearing a black coat.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Perché non indossi la giacca?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why don’t you wear the jacket?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Indossiamo le giacche perché fa freddo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We wear our jackets because it’s cold.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi indosso una giacca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I’m wearing a jacket.

definitions.native: on me, on you, on (someone), on (oneself)
definitions.note: Used to say something is being worn or carried on the body; the exact person depends on context (e.g., ce l’ho indosso = “I have it on me”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non ho soldi indosso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t have any money on me.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto), 3rd person singular: “he/she/it put on / wore” (common in storytelling and some regions; often replaced by passato prossimo in everyday speech).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Indossò il cappotto e uscì.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He put on his coat and went out.

definitions.note: Used as the present tense (he/she/it guesses) or as the informal command “guess!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Indovina chi viene a cena stasera!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Guess who’s coming to dinner tonight!

definitions.note: Also used for correctly guessing an answer (like “to figure out”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Riesci a indovinare la risposta?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you guess the answer?

definitions.note: Second-person plural (“you all”); can be used as present tense (“you guess”) or as a command (“guess!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Indovinate la risposta!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Guess the answer!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hai indovinato la risposta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You guessed the answer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho un indovinello per te: che cosa ha le chiavi ma non apre nessuna porta?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a riddle for you: what has keys but doesn't open any door?

definitions.note: Often used as “(tu) indovini” = “you guess” or in phrases like “che indovini…” (“that you/he/she guesses”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Indovini la risposta?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you guess the answer?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’industria automobilistica è molto importante in Italia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car industry is very important in Italy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Era inevitabile che arrivassimo in ritardo con tutto quel traffico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was inevitable that we would arrive late with all that traffic.

definitions.note: Often used critically to describe immature behavior.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il suo comportamento è davvero infantile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His behavior is really childish.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La mia infanzia è stata felice.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My childhood was happy.

definitions.note: Commonly used for a heart attack; in medical contexts it can also refer more generally to an infarction.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio nonno ha avuto un infarto l'anno scorso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather had a heart attack last year.

definitions.note: Gerund form; often means “while annoying/bothering” or “by annoying/bothering,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stai infastidendo tua sorella con tutte queste domande.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re annoying your sister with all these questions.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi dà fastidio quando la gente mi infastidisce mentre lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It bothers me when people annoy me while I’m working.

definitions.note: used for something/someone that irritates or makes you uncomfortable
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il rumore mi infastidisce.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The noise annoys me.

definitions.note: Often used for mild annoyance (like being disturbed or irritated).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti infastidisco se parlo troppo?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do I bother you if I talk too much?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quei rumori mi infastidiscono quando studio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those noises annoy me when I study.

definitions.note: feminine singular
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono un po' infastidita dal rumore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm a bit annoyed by the noise.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le ragazze sono infastidite dal rumore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The girls are annoyed by the noise.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Erano infastiditi dal rumore del traffico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were annoyed by the noise of the traffic.

definitions.note: Often used for someone who feels irritated (e.g., by noise, a comment, or a situation).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono infastidito dal rumore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m annoyed by the noise.

definitions.note: Often used to confirm or explain what was just said; it can also introduce a reason or clarification.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non posso venire; infatti sono malato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't come; in fact, I'm sick.

definitions.note: Often used for a romantic partner who cheats, but can also describe someone who is disloyal in general.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha scoperto che il marito era infedele.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She found out that her husband was unfaithful.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono infelice perché mi manca la mia famiglia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m unhappy because I miss my family.

definitions.note: Plural form (masculine or feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono infelici perché hanno perso il lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are unhappy because they lost their job.

definitions.note: Can describe physical position/level (“lower”) or quality/status (“inferior”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La temperatura oggi è inferiore a quella di ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The temperature today is lower than yesterday’s.

definitions.note: feminine form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mia sorella è un'infermiera in ospedale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is a nurse in the hospital.

definitions.note: Male form; the feminine is "infermiera".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio fratello è infermiere in ospedale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is a nurse in the hospital.

definitions.note: past participle used with feminine singular nouns (or as feminine singular with essere in compound tenses)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La cucina è infestata di formiche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kitchen is infested with ants.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La cucina è infestata di formiche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kitchen is infested with ants.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il virus ha infettato molte persone.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The virus has infected many people.
