definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The finger is infected and it hurts.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Attenzione: questo liquido è infiammabile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Warning: this liquid is flammable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Infine siamo arrivati a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Finally we arrived home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'universo sembra infinite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The universe seems infinite.

definitions.note: Commonly used in Italian as an English loanword, especially for social media personalities.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei lavora come influencer su Instagram.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She works as an influencer on Instagram.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho l’influenza e devo restare a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have the flu and I have to stay home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La pubblicità può influenzare le nostre scelte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Advertising can influence our choices.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono stato influenzato da lui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was influenced by him.

definitions.note: Often used with “informare qualcuno di/che …” (to inform someone of/that …).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti informo che domani la riunione è alle 10.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m informing you that tomorrow the meeting is at 10.

definitions.note: As an adjective, it means “computer-related/IT.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio fratello lavora in un'azienda informatica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother works at an IT company.

definitions.note: past participle of "informare"; also commonly used as an adjective meaning "well-informed"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono stato informato del cambiamento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have been informed about the change.

definitions.note: often used with “su” + topic (“informed about”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono informato sulla situazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m informed about the situation.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho bisogno di un'informazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need some information.

definitions.note: Plural form; often used where English still says “information.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi servono più informazioni su questo corso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need more information about this course.

definitions.note: Often used as a formal (Lei) command (“please inform/let me know”), or as a present subjunctive form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi informi appena arriva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let me know as soon as you arrive.

definitions.note: simple past (passato remoto) of "informare"; often used in written or formal storytelling contexts
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il direttore informò i dipendenti del cambiamento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The director informed the employees about the change.

definitions.note: Often used for rules/laws (like English “infringes/violates”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chi infrange la legge paga una multa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Anyone who breaks the law pays a fine.

definitions.note: Often used for breaking rules/laws (“infrangere la legge”, “infrangere le regole”), as well as physically breaking something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non devi infrangere le regole.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You must not break the rules.

definitions.note: Literary/formal past tense (passato remoto) of "infrangere"; often used for laws/rules or for breaking something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui infranse la legge e fu arrestato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He broke the law and was arrested.

definitions.note: Past participle of "infrangere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha infranto il vetro con una pietra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He broke the glass with a stone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non voglio ingannare nessuno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to deceive anyone.

definitions.note: feminine singular form (used about a woman or a feminine noun)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi sono sentita ingannata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I felt deceived.

definitions.note: 2nd person plural (voi), present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se mentite, ingannate tutti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you lie, you deceive everyone.

definitions.note: 2nd person plural (voi) imperative.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non ingannate i vostri amici!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t deceive your friends!

definitions.note: Feminine plural past participle (often used like an adjective).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le clienti si sono sentite ingannate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The (female) customers felt deceived.

definitions.note: past participle used for masculine plural (also used in plural mixed groups).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci siamo sentiti ingannati.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We felt deceived.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi sento ingannato da quello che mi hai detto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel deceived by what you told me.

definitions.note: past simple (passato remoto), 3rd person singular
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi ingannò e poi sparì.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He deceived me and then disappeared.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio fratello è ingegnere e lavora in una grande azienda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is an engineer and works at a large company.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non voglio ingelosire Marco parlando troppo del mio ex.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to make Marco jealous by talking too much about my ex.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei è troppo ingenua e si fida di tutti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is too naive and trusts everyone.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “naive” (too trusting).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un po' ingenuo e crede a tutto quello che sente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s a bit naive and believes everything he hears.

definitions.note: past historic (passato remoto), used often in writing and storytelling, especially for completed actions in the distant past
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando entrò in chiesa, si inginocchiò in silenzio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he entered the church, he knelt down in silence.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una critica ingiusta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s an unjust criticism.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una legge ingiusta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s an unjust law.

definitions.note: Used for both the adjective (“English”) and the language (“English”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto studiando l'inglese a scuola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m studying English at school.

definitions.note: Can also mean “an English person” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Studio l’inglese a scuola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I study English at school.

definitions.note: plural form (masculine or mixed group)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I turisti inglesi sono arrivati ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The English tourists arrived yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used both literally (food/drink) and figuratively (accept something unpleasant or hold back words/feelings).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non riesco a ingoiare questa pillola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t swallow this pill.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho ingoiato la pillola con un bicchiere d’acqua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I swallowed the pill with a glass of water.

definitions.note: Past simple (passato remoto), 3rd person singular: “he/she swallowed.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo il boccone troppo grande, ingoiò con difficoltà.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the bite that was too big, he/she swallowed with difficulty.

definitions.note: gerund form; often used with "stare" to mean "is/are gaining weight"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto ingrassando ultimamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve been gaining weight lately.

definitions.note: Most commonly means “you start” (present tense, tu). It can also be the present subjunctive form (that I/you/he/she start) and can be used as a formal command (“start,” to Lei).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu inizi alle otto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You start at eight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gli inizi sono difficili.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Beginnings are difficult.

definitions.note: third-person singular present tense of "iniziare" (also used for formal "you")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La lezione inizia alle nove.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lesson starts at nine.

definitions.note: Passato remoto form (often used in narratives and in some regions instead of the passato prossimo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri iniziai a leggere questo libro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I began reading this book.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo è solo un passo iniziale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is only an initial step.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Inizialmente volevo andare in treno, ma poi ho cambiato idea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Initially I wanted to go by train, but then I changed my mind.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto) of "iniziare"; common in narratives and in some regions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Iniziammo il viaggio all’alba.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We started the trip at dawn.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Iniziamo la lezione alle nove.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We start the lesson at nine.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le lezioni iniziano alle otto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The classes start at eight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani iniziamo il corso di italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we start the Italian course.

definitions.note: simple past (passato remoto), 3rd person plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Iniziarono il viaggio all'alba.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They started the trip at dawn.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of "iniziare"; often used with "essere" (e.g., "è iniziata") or as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La riunione è iniziata alle nove.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The meeting started at nine.

definitions.note: 2nd person plural form (used for “you all” in the present tense).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Iniziate alle otto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You start at eight.

definitions.note: Can also be used as a 2nd person plural command (“you all”): “Start!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Iniziate adesso!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Start now!

definitions.note: Feminine plural past participle (agrees with a feminine plural noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le lezioni sono iniziate ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lessons started yesterday.

definitions.note: Past participle of "iniziare"; commonly used in compound tenses (e.g., with "ho").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho iniziato il corso ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I started the course yesterday.

definitions.note: Third-person singular future tense (he/she/it will).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La lezione inizierà alle nove.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lesson will start at nine.

definitions.note: First-person singular present tense ("I start / I begin").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Inizio a lavorare domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I start working tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'inizio del film è molto interessante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The beginning of the movie is very interesting.

definitions.note: simple past (passato remoto) of "iniziare"; often used in storytelling, writing, and some regions of Italy
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il concerto iniziò alle otto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The concert started at eight.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: “innamorarsi (di)” = “to fall in love (with)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quel posto mi ha fatto innamorare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That place made me fall in love.

definitions.note: Reflexive form with "mi" (“me”). Often used with "di" + person/thing you fall in love with.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho paura di innamorarmi di nuovo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m afraid of falling in love again.

definitions.note: feminine singular form (used for a woman/girl).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono innamorata di te.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m in love with you.

definitions.note: feminine singular form (used for a woman/girl)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei è innamorata di Marco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is in love with Marco.

definitions.note: From the verb "innamorare" (to make someone fall in love). Often used with an object (who you make fall in love).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Con la vostra gentilezza innamorate tutti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With your kindness, you make everyone fall in love.

definitions.note: feminine plural form (used with a group of women or feminine nouns)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le ragazze sono innamorate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The girls are in love.

definitions.note: Plural form; used for two or more people (or mixed gender) who are in love.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono due ragazzi innamorati.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are two boys in love.

definitions.note: Masculine singular form (feminine: innamorata). Often used with essere: sono innamorato di…
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono innamorato di te.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am in love with you.

definitions.note: Often used with “di” (innamorato di qualcuno/qualcosa) to mean “in love with someone/something.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono innamorato di te.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m in love with you.

definitions.native: to irritate, to annoy, to get on someone's nerves
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quel rumore continuo mi innervosisce.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That constant noise irritates me.

definitions.note: Often used like an adjective meaning “irritated/annoyed”; it doesn’t mean “nervous” in English.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono innervosito dal rumore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m annoyed by the noise.

definitions.note: Can describe a person who is not guilty or something that is harmless/inoffensive; agrees in gender and number with the noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui è innocente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is innocent.

definitions.note: plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I bambini erano innocenti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children were innocent.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La sua innocenza era evidente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His innocence was obvious.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non è velenoso: è innocuo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s not poisonous; it’s harmless.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo progetto è molto innovativo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This project is very innovative.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani piove; inoltre, farà freddo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow it will rain; in addition, it will be cold.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La sua assenza è passata inosservata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Her absence went unnoticed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quel rumore nella notte era inquietante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That noise in the night was disturbing.

definitions.note: Often used for someone who can’t relax or feels worried.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo la notizia, Marco era inquieto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the news, Marco was restless.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per pranzo mangio un'insalata con pomodori e tonno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For lunch I eat a salad with tomatoes and tuna.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei insegna italiano a scuola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She teaches Italian at school.

definitions.note: Imperative form used to give an instruction to “you” (tu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Insegna a tuo fratello come si fa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Teach your brother how to do it.

definitions.note: Imperative form with the object pronoun “mi” attached (“me”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Insegnami come si dice questa parola in italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Teach me how to say this word in Italian.

definitions.note: This form is non-standard; the correct spelling is usually “insegniamo”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Insegnamo italiano a scuola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We teach Italian at school.

definitions.note: gerund form of “insegnare” (used like “-ing” in English, often with “stare”: “sto insegnando” = “I am teaching”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto insegnando italiano a un gruppo di principianti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m teaching Italian to a group of beginners.

definitions.note: third-person plural (they)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Insegnano italiano a scuola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They teach Italian at school.

definitions.note: Used for both male and female teachers; the article (il/la) usually shows gender.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La mia insegnante di italiano è molto paziente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My Italian teacher is very patient.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gli insegnanti spiegano la lezione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teachers explain the lesson.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mia madre insegna matematica in una scuola superiore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My mother teaches math in a high school.

definitions.note: Often used with “a” + person + “di” + infinitive: “insegnare a qualcuno a fare qualcosa” = “to teach someone to do something.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi ha insegnato a guidare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/she taught me to drive.

definitions.native: to teach her, to teach them
definitions.note: Includes the indirect object pronoun “le” (= to her / to them).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio insegnarle l'italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to teach her Italian.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi insegnarmi l’italiano?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you teach me Italian?

definitions.note: Infinitive with the object pronoun "mi" (me) attached at the end.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi insegnarmi a cucinare la pasta?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you teach me how to cook pasta?

definitions.note: Includes the attached pronoun "ti" (= "you" singular, informal): "insegnare + ti".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio insegnarti l'italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to teach you Italian.

definitions.native: to teach you (plural), to teach you (formal)
definitions.note: Object pronoun form: insegnare + vi (“to you” plural or formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio insegnarvi l'italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to teach you Italian.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voi insegnate italiano a scuola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You teach Italian at school.

definitions.note: Used as an imperative addressed to more than one person (plural “you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Insegnate ai bambini a leggere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Teach the children to read.

definitions.note: past participle of "insegnare"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho insegnato italiano per due anni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I taught Italian for two years.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (past habitual/ongoing).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da giovane, insegnava italiano a scuola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he was young, he taught/was teaching Italian at school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani insegnerà italiano ai nuovi studenti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow, he/she will teach Italian to the new students.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Insegni italiano a scuola?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you teach Italian at school?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Insegno italiano in una scuola serale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I teach Italian at an evening school.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto), used especially in written narratives and in some regions for completed actions in the distant past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da giovane, mio nonno insegnò italiano in una scuola di campagna.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he was young, my grandfather taught Italian in a rural school.

definitions.note: gerund form (used like “while …-ing” or “by …-ing”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stavo correndo, inseguendo l'autobus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was running, chasing the bus.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il cane insegue la palla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog chases the ball.

definitions.note: past participle of "inseguire"; commonly used with "avere" to form the past tense (e.g., "ha inseguito" = "has chased")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La polizia ha inseguito il ladro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police chased the thief.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto), common in writing and in some regions; often corresponds to English simple past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il cane inseguì la palla nel giardino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog chased the ball in the garden.

definitions.note: Often used for someone who is not considerate of other people’s feelings; it can also mean “numb” (without physical sensation) depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È stato insensibile e mi ha ferito con le sue parole.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was insensitive and hurt me with his words.

definitions.note: plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono due amici inseparabili.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are two inseparable friends.

definitions.note: Used as a formal command (Lei) and also as the present subjunctive form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Inserisca la password, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please enter the password.

definitions.note: Often used as a command (like on a website or device): “Inserisci …” = “Enter/Insert …”. Depending on context it can also mean “you insert/enter”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Inserisci la password.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Enter the password.

definitions.note: Can be used for “you (plural) insert/enter” (present) or as a polite/plural command “insert/enter!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Inserite la password e premete Invio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Enter the password and press Enter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho inserito il tuo nome nel modulo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I entered your name on the form.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In estate ci sono molti insetti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In summer there are many insects.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'è un insetto sul vetro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There's an insect on the glass.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of “insicuro.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei si sente insicura quando parla in pubblico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She feels insecure when she speaks in public.

definitions.note: Can describe a person (lacking confidence) or a situation (not safe/certain), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi sento insicuro quando devo parlare in pubblico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel insecure when I have to speak in public.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Andiamo insieme al cinema stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s go to the cinema together tonight.

definitions.note: Often used for suggesting something indirectly (sometimes with a negative tone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stai insinuando che io abbia mentito?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you insinuating that I lied?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un cliente insistente e chiama ogni giorno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s a persistent customer and calls every day.

definitions.note: Often followed by “su” + noun/pronoun (e.g., “insistere su qualcosa”) or “che” + clause.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Insisto che tu venga con noi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I insist that you come with us.

definitions.note: simple past (passato remoto), 3rd person singular
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei insistette per avere un rimborso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She insisted on getting a refund.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho insistito per avere una risposta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I insisted on getting an answer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Insisto: voglio parlare con il direttore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I insist: I want to speak with the manager.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person singular; common in written narratives, less in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui insisté per avere un altro giorno di tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He insisted on having one more day of time.

definitions.note: feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono insoddisfatta del mio lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m dissatisfied with my job.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono insoddisfatto del servizio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m dissatisfied with the service.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "insolito"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una situazione insolita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s an unusual situation.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un comportamento insolito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s unusual behavior.

definitions.note: Often used as a filler to sum up, to show hesitation, or mild impatience (similar to “come on” or “anyway,” depending on tone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Insomma, che facciamo stasera?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: So, what are we doing tonight?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Soffro di insonnia da qualche settimana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve been suffering from insomnia for a few weeks.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo rumore è insopportabile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This noise is unbearable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il tempo oggi è instabile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The weather today is unstable.

definitions.note: Often used for setting up software/apps or putting equipment in place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo installare questa app sul mio telefono.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to install this app on my phone.

definitions.note: past participle of "installare"; often used with "essere" or "avere" in compound tenses
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho installato l'app sul mio telefono.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I installed the app on my phone.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tu); often used after expressions like "è importante che...".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È importante che tu installi l’app prima della lezione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that you install the app before the lesson.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stai insultando tuo fratello.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re insulting your brother.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non devi insultare le persone solo perché sei arrabbiato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You must not insult people just because you are angry.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi ha insultato davanti a tutti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He insulted me in front of everyone.

definitions.note: Past historic/remote past (passato remoto), common in storytelling and in some regions for the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Durante la discussione, lui insultò il suo collega.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: During the argument, he insulted his colleague.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Io preparo la cena; intanto tu puoi apparecchiare la tavola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'll make dinner; meanwhile you can set the table.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “for now” when a situation is temporary.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Intanto restiamo qui e aspettiamo notizie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For now we’ll stay here and wait for news.

definitions.note: Plural form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo letto i documenti integrali.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We read the whole documents.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una studentessa molto intelligente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is a very intelligent student.

definitions.note: plural form (masculine or feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le studentesse sono molto intelligenti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The female students are very intelligent.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La sua intelligenza mi impressiona.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His intelligence impresses me.

definitions.note: Often used to clarify what someone means (e.g., “Che cosa intende?” = “What do you mean?”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Che cosa intende con questa frase?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What does he/she mean by this sentence?

definitions.note: Second-person plural (voi). Often used to ask for clarification: “What do you mean?”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Che cosa intendete dire?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What do you mean to say?

definitions.note: Imperfetto (past habitual/ongoing): often used for something someone meant/intended at that time, or used to mean repeatedly.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non intendeva offenderti, era solo una battuta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He didn’t mean to offend you; it was just a joke.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (past, ongoing/repeated), 1st person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non intendevo offenderti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn't mean to offend you.

definitions.note: Second-person singular present tense (tu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Che cosa intendi dire?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What do you mean to say?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Intendo dire che non è colpa tua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I mean to say that it's not your fault.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Intendo studiare italiano ogni giorno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I intend to study Italian every day.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "intenso".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È stata una giornata intensa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was an intense day.

definitions.note: Often used with things like rain, traffic, pain, or work to mean very strong or severe.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri sera c'è stata una pioggia intensa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night there was heavy rain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha lavorato intensamente per finire il progetto in tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He worked intensely to finish the project on time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È stato un allenamento intenso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was an intense workout.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non è stato un errore: è stato un gesto intenzionale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It wasn’t a mistake: it was an intentional gesture.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La mia intenzione è aiutarti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My intention is to help you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le mie intenzioni sono buone.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My intentions are good.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho letto il libro interamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I read the book entirely.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo argomento mi interessa molto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This topic interests me a lot.

definitions.note: Common in expressions like “non mi interessa” = “I don’t care / it doesn’t matter to me.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non mi interessa il prezzo; voglio solo qualità.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The price doesn’t matter to me; I just want quality.

definitions.note: Used with an indirect object (e.g., mi/ti/gli/le/ci/vi): “mi interessano” = “I’m interested in / they interest me.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi interessano i film italiani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m interested in Italian films.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo libro è molto interessante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book is very interesting.

definitions.note: plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questi libri sono molto interessanti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These books are very interesting.

definitions.note: Commonly used like “interessare a qualcuno” (“to interest someone”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo argomento interessa molti studenti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This topic interests many students.

definitions.note: feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono molto interessata a imparare l’italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m very interested in learning Italian.

definitions.note: feminine plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo interessate al corso di italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are interested in the Italian course.

definitions.note: masculine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo interessati al corso di italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are interested in the Italian course.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono interessato a imparare l’italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m interested in learning Italian.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho un grande interesse per la musica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a great interest in music.

definitions.note: Often used in the plural ("interessi") to mean someone’s personal interests or hobbies.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo molti interessi in comune.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have many interests in common.

definitions.note: Usually appears in phrases like “che ti interessi” (“that it interests you”), i.e., the present subjunctive of “interessare.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non credo che ti interessi questo film.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t think this movie interests you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I miei interessi includono la musica e lo sport.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My interests include music and sports.

definitions.note: Often used in the plural when talking about money (e.g., bank interest).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La banca applica interessi al prestito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bank charges interest on the loan.

definitions.note: Often used with “con” to mean “interfere with.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non voglio interferire con le tue decisioni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to interfere with your decisions.

definitions.note: Often used for non-physical things (e.g., feelings, thoughts), but can also describe the inside part of something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La pace interiore è importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Inner peace is important.

definitions.note: A constructed international auxiliary language.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto studiando l’interlingua per comunicare con persone di paesi diversi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m studying Interlingua to communicate with people from different countries.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un progetto internazionale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s an international project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Uso internet per studiare italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I use the internet to study Italian.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho letto l’intero libro in due giorni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I read the whole book in two days.

definitions.note: Used in math to mean a whole number (not a fraction).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieci è un numero intero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ten is an integer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei interpreta il ruolo principale nel film.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She interprets (plays) the main role in the film.

definitions.note: Can mean either “you (plural) interpret” (present) or “interpret!” (plural command), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Interpretate questo grafico con attenzione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Interpret this graph carefully.

definitions.note: In Italian, “interprete” is used both for a language interpreter and, more generally, a performer/interpreter of a role (e.g., in theater or film).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo bisogno di un interprete per la riunione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need an interpreter for the meeting.

definitions.note: gerund form; often used with "stare" to mean "is/are questioning" or "is/are interrogating"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto interrogando il testimone.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am questioning the witness.

definitions.note: Often used in formal or police/legal contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La polizia deve interrogare il sospetto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police must question the suspect.

definitions.note: past participle (masculine singular) of "interrogare"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'uomo è stato interrogato dalla polizia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The man was questioned by the police.

definitions.note: Often used for interrupting a person/speech or stopping an activity before it finishes.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi dispiace interrompere, ma devo andare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry to interrupt, but I have to go.

definitions.note: Includes the attached object pronoun "mi" (= me).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi lasciarmi finire senza interrompermi?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you let me finish without interrupting me?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo interrotto la riunione perché mancava la corrente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We interrupted the meeting because the power was out.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person singular of "interrompere"; common in writing and storytelling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il rumore improvviso interruppe la lezione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sudden noise interrupted the lesson.

definitions.note: Often used for intervening in a situation (e.g., a conflict) or taking action to help or change something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La polizia è dovuta intervenire per fermare la rissa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police had to intervene to stop the brawl.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani dobbiamo intervistare tre candidati per il lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we have to interview three candidates for the job.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho intervistato Maria per il giornale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I interviewed Maria for the newspaper.

definitions.note: Plural feminine form of "intimo".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo avuto conversazioni intime.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had intimate, private conversations.

definitions.note: Plural form; can refer to close personal relationships or to private/confidential matters, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo avuto momenti intimi in cui abbiamo parlato dei nostri sogni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had intimate moments where we talked about our dreams.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quel ragazzo mi intimidisce.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That boy intimidates me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non intimidisci nessuno con quelle minacce.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You don’t intimidate anyone with those threats.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tra loro c’è molta intimità.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a lot of intimacy between them.

definitions.note: Often used to mean a person’s private life or private space.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho bisogno di un po’ di intimità.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a bit of privacy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il rumore qui di notte è intollerabile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The noise here at night is unbearable.

definitions.note: Often used for someone who is confused or groggy (for example, after waking up or after a shock).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi sono svegliato intontito e ho dimenticato dove ero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I woke up dazed and forgot where I was.

definitions.note: Often used with "a" ("intorno a" = "around").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’è molta gente intorno alla fontana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many people around the fountain.

definitions.note: Often used with "a" ("intorno a") to mean "around" a place or topic.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'è molta gente intorno alla stazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are lots of people around the station.

definitions.note: Often used for food poisoning (being sick from something you ate or drank). It can look like English “intoxicated,” but it usually does not mean “drunk.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo le ostriche, mi sono sentito intossicato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the oysters, I felt poisoned (like I had food poisoning).

definitions.note: Often used for food poisoning (intossicazione alimentare).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha avuto un’intossicazione dopo aver mangiato pesce.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He had food poisoning after eating fish.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La volpe è intrappolata nella rete.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fox is trapped in the net.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le persone sono rimaste intrappolate nell’ascensore per mezz’ora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The people were trapped in the elevator for half an hour.

definitions.note: plural masculine form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo rimasti intrappolati in ascensore per mezz’ora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We were trapped in the elevator for half an hour.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi sono sentito intrappolato in quella situazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I felt trapped in that situation.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una ragazza intraprendente e trova sempre una soluzione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is an enterprising, resourceful girl and she always finds a solution.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una storia intrigata, ma alla fine si capisce tutto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s an intricate story, but in the end you understand everything.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un problema intrigato, ma possiamo risolverlo insieme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a complicated problem, but we can solve it together.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le sue intuizioni ci hanno aiutato a risolvere il problema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His intuitions helped us solve the problem.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo consiglio è inutile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This advice is useless.

definitions.note: plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questi documenti sono inutili.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These documents are useless.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho aspettato invano per un'ora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I waited in vain for an hour.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Con il tempo, tutti noi invecchiamo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With time, we all age.

definitions.note: Past participle of “invecchiare”; often used like an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un vino invecchiato in botte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a wine aged in a barrel.

definitions.note: Often used with "di" to mean "instead of" (e.g., "invece di").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vado a piedi invece.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going on foot instead.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui è molto calmo; lei, invece, è sempre nervosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s very calm; she, on the other hand, is always nervous.

definitions.note: Often used with "invece di" + infinitive to mean "instead of".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Io prendo un tè; lui, invece, prende un caffè.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m having tea; he, instead, is having coffee.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "inventare"; often used like an adjective
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una storia inventata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a made-up story.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho inventato una storia per i bambini.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I made up a story for the children.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person singular: “he/she/it invented.” Common in written narratives and history; in conversation many speakers use passato prossimo instead.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Leonardo inventò molte macchine straordinarie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Leonardo invented many extraordinary machines.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo comprato dei vestiti invernali.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We bought some winter clothes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In inverno fa freddo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In winter it’s cold.

definitions.note: Often used for stories, explanations, or situations that are hard to believe.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La sua scusa è davvero inverosimile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His excuse is really unbelievable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto investendo in un fondo indicizzato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m investing in an index fund.

definitions.note: Used for accidents involving a car, bike, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stava guidando troppo veloce e rischiava di investendo un pedone.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was driving too fast and risked running over a pedestrian.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'investigatore ha trovato nuove prove.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The investigator found new evidence.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gli investigatori stanno cercando nuove prove.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The investigators are looking for new evidence.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La polizia ha aperto un’investigazione sul furto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police opened an investigation into the theft.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio investire in un fondo indicizzato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to invest in an index fund.

definitions.native: to hit (with a vehicle), to run over
definitions.note: Commonly used in news and everyday speech for traffic accidents.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’auto ha investito un ciclista all’incrocio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car hit a cyclist at the intersection.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo investiti molti soldi nel progetto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We invested a lot of money in the project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Due pedoni sono stati investiti sulle strisce.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Two pedestrians were hit on the crosswalk.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho già investito tutti i miei risparmi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve already invested all my savings.

definitions.note: Often used with “di” to indicate the role or responsibility (e.g., “investito di un incarico”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È stato investito di un incarico importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was appointed to an important assignment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi invia il documento oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She sends me the document today.

definitions.note: Commonly used for sending emails, messages, documents, or packages.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi inviarmi il file per email?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you send me the file by email?

definitions.note: Past participle of "inviare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho inviato un'email al professore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sent an email to the professor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È molto invidiato dai colleghi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very envied by his colleagues.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti invidio perché parli italiano benissimo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I envy you because you speak Italian really well.

definitions.note: feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei è invidiosa del successo di sua sorella.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is envious of her sister’s success.

definitions.note: Used with the subjunctive (e.g., after expressions like “spero che…”, “è importante che…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che tu invii il modulo oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you send the form today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa squadra sembra invincibile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This team seems invincible.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il gas è invisibile, quindi fai attenzione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The gas is invisible, so be careful.

definitions.note: Can also be the (tu) imperative form: “invite!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Luca invita sempre gli amici a cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Luca always invites his friends to dinner.

definitions.note: Past simple (passato remoto), 1st person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri invitai Luca a cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I invited Luca to dinner.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto), 1st person plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri invitammo tutti i vicini a cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday we invited all the neighbors to dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vuoi invitare Maria alla festa?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you want to invite Maria to the party?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I miei amici mi invitarono a cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My friends invited me to dinner.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of “invitare”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Giulia è stata invitata alla festa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Giulia was invited to the party.

definitions.note: Can be used for "you (plural) invite" (present) or as a command "invite!" (plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani invitate tutti i vostri amici alla festa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow you invite all your friends to the party.

definitions.note: past participle (plural) of “invitare”; often used with “essere” to form the passive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siete invitati alla festa di sabato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are invited to Saturday’s party.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gli ospiti sono già arrivati: sono tutti invitati.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The guests have already arrived: they are all invited.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho invitato Marco alla festa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I invited Marco to the party.
