definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa è una leggenda antica del paese.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is an ancient legend from the town.

definitions.note: gerund of "leggere"; often used like "while reading" or to talk about an action in progress
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto leggendo un libro interessante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am reading an interesting book.

definitions.note: feminine singular form; used for things that are not heavy, or for something mild/soft (e.g., a light breeze).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato una valigia leggera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a light suitcase.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi piace leggere prima di dormire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like to read before going to sleep.

definitions.note: plural masculine form of "leggero"; used for more than one masculine noun or a mixed group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preferisco i piatti leggeri a cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prefer light meals for dinner.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “la” (= it, feminine singular; sometimes “her” depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio leggerla stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to read it tonight.

definitions.note: Infinitive "leggere" + direct object pronoun "lo" (“it”, usually referring to a masculine noun or a whole idea).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo leggerlo oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to read it today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La porta è leggermente aperta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The door is slightly open.

definitions.note: Used with the pronoun "mi" (= to me). Often means reading something aloud for me.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi leggermi questa storia?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you read this story to me?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo zaino è leggero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This backpack is light.

definitions.note: Often used for things like food, a meal, wine, or exercise.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preferisco una cena leggera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prefer a light dinner.

definitions.note: third-person singular (he/she/it) future tense of “leggere”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani leggerà il giornale in treno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow, he/she will read the newspaper on the train.

definitions.note: Second-person plural ("you all").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Leggete spesso prima di dormire?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you (all) often read before going to sleep?

definitions.note: Imperative, second-person plural (addressing more than one person).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Leggete queste istruzioni con attenzione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Read these instructions carefully.

definitions.note: imperfect tense (ongoing or habitual action in the past)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando ero piccolo, mio nonno leggeva il giornale ogni mattina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was little, my grandfather used to read the newspaper every morning.

definitions.note: First-person singular imperfect tense of "leggere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da bambino leggevo ogni sera prima di dormire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As a child, I used to read every evening before going to sleep.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le leggi cambiano nel tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Laws change over time.

definitions.note: present tense (2nd person singular): “you read”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu leggi il giornale ogni mattina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You read the newspaper every morning.

definitions.note: imperative (2nd person singular): used to give a command
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Leggi questo messaggio, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Read this message, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ogni sera leggiamo un capitolo prima di dormire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every evening we read a chapter before going to sleep.

definitions.note: Used to make a suggestion in the 1st person plural ("let's...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È tardi: leggiamo solo una pagina e poi andiamo a dormire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s late: let’s read just one page and then let’s go to sleep.

definitions.note: Informal command (tu) with the direct object pronoun “lo” = “it” (masculine singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se hai tempo, leggilo stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you have time, read it tonight.

definitions.note: Present tense, 1st person singular (io).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La sera leggo un libro prima di dormire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the evening I read a book before going to sleep.

definitions.note: third-person plural ("they") present tense of "leggere"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ogni sera leggono un capitolo prima di dormire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every evening they read a chapter before going to sleep.

definitions.note: Usually refers to wood used as fuel (e.g., for a fireplace or stove).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: D'inverno compriamo la legna per il camino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In winter we buy firewood for the fireplace.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il tavolo è fatto di legno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The table is made of wood.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person singular of “legare”; often used in storytelling or written narratives.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Con una corda legò il pacco e lo mise sul tavolo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With a rope, he tied the package and put it on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei è italiana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is Italian.

definitions.note: stressed pronoun; often used after prepositions or for emphasis
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vado al cinema con lei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to the cinema with her.

definitions.note: formal/polite “you” (often written “Lei”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei vuole un caffè?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Would you like a coffee?

definitions.note: feminine singular form of the adjective
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La connessione oggi è lenta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The connection is slow today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cammina lentamente perché la strada è scivolosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He walks slowly because the road is slippery.

definitions.note: Often used when something changes little by little over time.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La situazione sta migliorando lentamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The situation is improving gradually.

definitions.note: feminine singular form (used with feminine nouns)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La tartaruga è molto lente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The turtle is very slow.

definitions.note: masculine plural form of the adjective
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I computer sono lenti oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The computers are slow today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il treno è lento oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train is slow today.

definitions.note: Plural form of “lenzuolo”; commonly used when talking about bed linen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cambio le lenzuola ogni settimana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I change the sheets every week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho cambiato il lenzuolo del letto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I changed the bed sheet.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il leone vive nella savana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lion lives in the savanna.

definitions.note: plural of “leone”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I leoni vivono in gruppo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Lions live in groups.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il leopardo corre veloce nella savana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The leopard runs fast in the savanna.

definitions.note: Past historic/simple past form of "leggere" (passato remoto), used mainly in narratives and in some regions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri sera lesse un capitolo prima di dormire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night he/she read a chapter before going to sleep.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person plural: used mainly in written stories and in some regions to talk about completed actions in the distant past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo cena, lessero un capitolo del libro e poi andarono a dormire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After dinner, they read a chapter of the book and then went to sleep.

definitions.note: simple past (passato remoto), 1st person singular: “I read” (often used in stories and written Italian)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lessi il libro in due giorni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I read the book in two days.

definitions.note: Most often a written message you send (by mail or as a formal written communication).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho scritto una lettera a mia nonna.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wrote a letter to my grandmother.

definitions.note: Often used about translations or meanings (e.g., "traduzione letterale").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa è una traduzione letterale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is a literal translation.

definitions.note: Often also used informally for emphasis, even when not strictly “literally.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'ho preso alla lettera, letteralmente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I took it at face value, literally.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto leggendo una rivista letteraria.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m reading a literary magazine.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: All’università studio letteratura italiana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At university I study Italian literature.

definitions.note: Plural of "lettera"; can mean letters of the alphabet or letters/mail, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo scrivere tre lettere oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to write three letters today.

definitions.note: past participle of "leggere"; used with "avere" to form compound tenses
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho letto questo libro due volte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have read this book twice.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il mio letto è molto comodo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My bed is very comfortable.

definitions.note: Often refers to a person who reads (books, newspapers, etc.), but can also be used for a device (e.g., a card reader) depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio padre è un grande lettore di romanzi storici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My father is a great reader of historical novels.

definitions.note: plural of "lettore"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I lettori leggono in silenzio in biblioteca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The readers read quietly in the library.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La lettura mi rilassa la sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Reading relaxes me in the evening.

definitions.native: get up, move out of the way
definitions.note: Informal plural command (voi); reflexive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Levatevi, per favore: devo passare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Move, please: I need to get through.

definitions.note: Informal singular command (tu) with the reflexive pronoun attached (ti), from "levarsi".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Levati dal letto, è tardi!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Get out of bed, it’s late!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi ho una lezione di italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I have an Italian lesson.

definitions.note: Plural of "lezione".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi ho due lezioni all’università.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I have two lessons at the university.

definitions.note: masculine plural direct object pronoun (used for male or mixed-gender groups)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Li vedo ogni giorno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see them every day.

definitions.note: masculine plural direct object pronoun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Li vedo domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see them tomorrow.

definitions.note: Plural of "libbra"; usually refers to the unit of weight (lb).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il pacco pesa due libbre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The package weighs two pounds.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il giudice libera l’imputato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The judge frees the defendant.

definitions.note: feminine singular form (used with feminine nouns or for a woman speaking about herself)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani sono libera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m free tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used in politics to describe progressive or left-leaning ideas (depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio padre è molto liberale su molte questioni sociali.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My father is very liberal on many social issues.

definitions.note: Often means “freely” in the sense of without constraints (or with freedom of expression).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi parlare liberamente qui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can speak freely here.

definitions.note: Form used with voi (“you” plural) in the present tense; it can also be the voi imperative (“free!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se liberate i prigionieri, finisce la guerra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you free the prisoners, the war will end.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il prigioniero è stato liberato ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The prisoner was freed yesterday.

definitions.note: feminine plural of "libero"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In questo paese, le persone sono libere di parlare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this country, people are free to speak.

definitions.note: Often used in the subjunctive after "che" (e.g., "che tu liberi..."); the same form is also used as the formal command with "Lei" (e.g., "Liberi...!").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che tu liberi il cane.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you free the dog.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo liberi domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are free tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti libero subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll free you right away.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “available” (not busy), especially when talking about time.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi sono libero dopo le sei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I'm free after six.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La libertà è un diritto fondamentale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Freedom is a fundamental right.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto), 3rd person singular: “he/she/it freed/released.” Common in written narratives and historical accounts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il comandante liberò i prigionieri al tramonto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The commander freed the prisoners at sunset.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'è una libreria vicino a casa mia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There’s a bookstore near my house.

definitions.note: Plural of "libro".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato due libri ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought two books yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto leggendo un libro interessante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m reading an interesting book.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per guidare serve la licenza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: To drive you need a license.

definitions.note: Used in set phrases like “in licenza” for time off, especially in work or military contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi sono in licenza e non lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I’m on leave and I’m not working.

definitions.note: Used mainly for ending someone’s job (laying them off/firing them).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'azienda ha deciso di licenziare dieci dipendenti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company decided to fire ten employees.

definitions.note: Past participle of "licenziare"; often used like an adjective (feminine singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Maria è stata licenziata ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Maria was fired yesterday.

definitions.note: Form used with "you" (plural) in Italian (voi). It can also be used as a command ("Fire!" / "Dismiss!").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani licenziate due dipendenti?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you firing two employees tomorrow?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono stati licenziati la settimana scorsa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were fired last week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gli autisti licenziati possono guidare l’autobus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The licensed drivers can drive the bus.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Marco è stato licenziato ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Marco was fired yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used for products or software (e.g., “software licenziato”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo software è licenziato per uso commerciale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This software is licensed for commercial use.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il direttore lo licenziò senza preavviso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The manager fired him without notice.

definitions.note: In Italy, a liceo is an academically oriented type of high school (there are different kinds, e.g. classico, scientifico, linguistico).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mia sorella frequenta il liceo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister goes to high school.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "lieto"; often used with "essere" or "sono".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono lieta di conoscerti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m happy to meet you.

definitions.note: plural masculine form of "lieto"; can also be used for a mixed-gender plural group
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo lieti di conoscerti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are happy to meet you.

definitions.note: Often used in a slightly formal/literary way; common in phrases like “lieto fine” (happy ending).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo lieti di aiutarti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are happy to help you.

definitions.note: feminine plural form of “limitato”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo risorse limitate, quindi dobbiamo scegliere con attenzione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have limited resources, so we have to choose carefully.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “restricted” or “small in amount/number.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo un numero limitato di posti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have a limited number of seats.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'è un limite a tutto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a limit to everything.

definitions.note: Often used for borders between areas or properties, especially in the plural: "i limiti".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il fiume segna il limite tra le due regioni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The river marks the boundary between the two regions.

definitions.note: Plural of "limite".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono limiti di velocità su questa strada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are speed limits on this road.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei una limonata, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like a lemonade, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei un tè al limone, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like a lemon tea, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato dei limoni al mercato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought some lemons at the market.

definitions.note: Often used for water, skies, or anything transparent/pure; can also be used figuratively (e.g., a “clear” idea).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'acqua del lago è limpida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lake water is clear.

definitions.note: Often used for both a drawn line and a telephone line/service.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Traccia una linea dritta sul foglio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Draw a straight line on the sheet of paper.

definitions.note: plural of "linea"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho disegnato tre linee sul foglio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I drew three lines on the sheet of paper.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto imparando una nuova lingua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m learning a new language.

definitions.note: Can refer to the physical organ in your mouth.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi fa male la lingua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My tongue hurts.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Parlo tre linguaggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I speak three languages.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto studiando il linguaggio italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m studying the Italian language.

definitions.note: Often used to refer to someone’s choice of words or style of speaking (e.g., polite vs. rude).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non mi piace il suo linguaggio: è troppo aggressivo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t like his language: it’s too aggressive.

definitions.note: plural of "lingua"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A scuola studiamo tre lingue.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At school we study three languages.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mia sorella è una linguista e studia il giapponese.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is a linguist and she studies Japanese.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: All’università studio linguistica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At university I study linguistics.

definitions.note: Often used in Italian in computing/online contexts, like in English.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi mandi il link del sito?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you send me the link to the website?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In laboratorio lavoriamo con liquidi pericolosi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the lab we work with dangerous liquids.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preferisco un sapone liquido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prefer a liquid soap.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'è del liquido sul pavimento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is some liquid on the floor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi piace la liquirizia, ma è molto dolce.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like licorice, but it’s very sweet.

definitions.note: Plural of "liquore"; refers to alcoholic drinks such as liqueurs or spirits.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preferisco i liquori dolci dopo cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prefer sweet liqueurs after dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho una lista di cose da fare oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a list of things to do today.

definitions.note: Looks like English “litigate,” but in everyday Italian it usually means “to argue/quarrel,” not specifically to take legal action.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Litiga spesso con suo fratello per sciocchezze.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He often argues with his brother over silly things.

definitions.note: Gerund of "litigare"; often used to mean "while arguing" or "arguing" (as an ongoing action).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stanno litigando per soldi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are arguing about money.

definitions.note: Used for people having an argument (often verbal); can also imply a quarrel or dispute.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I miei vicini litigano spesso per il rumore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My neighbors often argue about the noise.

definitions.note: Often used for a verbal quarrel; can also mean to have a fight with someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non voglio litigare con te.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to argue with you.

definitions.note: past participle of "litigare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho litigato con mia sorella ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I argued with my sister yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei un litro di latte, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like a liter of milk, please.

definitions.note: Plural of "livello".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo gioco ha tre livelli.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This game has three levels.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il livello dell’acqua è troppo alto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The water level is too high.

definitions.note: Often used to talk about a level of schooling or study (e.g., first year, second year).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio fratello è al secondo livello di inglese.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is in the second level of English.

definitions.note: Often refers to bruises on the skin after a bump or hit.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo la caduta, aveva lividi sulle braccia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the fall, he had bruises on his arms.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho un livido sul braccio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a bruise on my arm.

definitions.note: Masculine singular definite article used before s + consonant (lo studente), z (lo zaino), gn (lo gnomo), ps (lo psicologo), x/y (lo yogurt), and i + vowel (lo iode).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo studente è in classe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The student is in class.

definitions.note: masculine singular direct object pronoun; usually placed before the verb
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo vedo ogni giorno.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Manca il sale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The salt is missing.

definitions.note: Often used with an indirect object (e.g., “mi mancano…” = “I miss…” / “I’m missing…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mancano due sedie in cucina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Two chairs are missing in the kitchen.

definitions.note: Used for something absent or not present (e.g., a missing item or information).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nel modulo manca una firma: è mancante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On the form, one signature is missing: it’s missing.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'è una mancanza di acqua in questa zona.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a lack of water in this area.

definitions.note: Often used with an indirect object (mi/ti/gli/le/ci/vi) to mean “to miss (someone/something)” or “to lack/need.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi manca la mia famiglia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I miss my family.

definitions.note: Often used to talk about a missed call or a missed appointment (e.g., "chiamata mancata").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho visto una chiamata mancata sul telefono.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw a missed call on the phone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voi mi mancate molto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I miss you a lot.

definitions.note: Past participle (plural masculine) of "mancare"; often used with "essere" to mean that someone/something is missing or absent.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono mancati tre studenti oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Three students were absent today.

definitions.note: Past participle of "mancare"; often used in compound tenses (e.g., "ho mancato...") or as an adjective (e.g., "un'occasione mancata").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho mancato il treno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I missed the train.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mancava un ingrediente nella ricetta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: An ingredient was missing from the recipe.

definitions.note: Often used with an indirect object pronoun (mi, ti, gli/le, ci, vi, gli) to mean someone missed something/someone (literally: something/someone was missing to them).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi mancava mia madre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I missed my mother.

definitions.note: Often used to say something wasn’t there or wasn’t enough (a shortage or an absence).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alla fine della giornata mancavano due sedie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the end of the day, two chairs were missing.

definitions.note: Plural of “mancia”; money given as a tip (often in restaurants, taxis, hotels).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo lasciato alcune mance al cameriere e al barista.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We left a few tips for the waiter and the bartender.

definitions.native: you will miss, you will be missing, you will be absent
definitions.note: From "mancare": it can mean "to be missing/absent" or "to miss (someone/something)" depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi mancherai tantissimo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will miss you so much.

definitions.native: will be missing, will be absent
definitions.note: Future tense of "mancare"; often used to say that someone/something won’t be there or is lacking.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani Luca mancherà alla riunione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow Luca will be absent from the meeting.

definitions.note: Often used with an indirect object: “mi mancherai” = “I will miss you.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi mancherai quando partirai.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will miss you when you leave.

definitions.native: are missing, are absent; are lacking
definitions.note: Often used with an indirect object pronoun: “Mi manchi” means “I miss you” (literally “You are missing to me”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi manchi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I miss you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho lasciato una mancia al cameriere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I left a tip for the waiter.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) form; common in narratives and written Italian.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alla fine mancò un ingrediente, quindi non facemmo la torta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end an ingredient was missing, so we didn’t make the cake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui manda un messaggio ogni sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He sends a message every evening.

definitions.note: Informal singular command (tu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Manda la foto a tua madre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Send the photo to your mother.

definitions.note: Imperative (tu) form of "mandare" + "ci" (= to us/us).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mandaci una foto, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Send us a photo, please.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) form; common in written narratives, less common in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gli mandai un messaggio ieri sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sent him a message last night.

definitions.note: Imperative (tu) of "mandare" + the direct object pronoun "la" (= it/her), written together.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mandala subito, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Send it right away, please.

definitions.note: Informal (tu) imperative of "mandare" with the direct object pronoun "lo" attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mandalo subito!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Send it right away!

definitions.note: informal (tu) imperative with pronouns: me + la
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mandamela subito, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Send it to me right away, please.

definitions.note: Informal singular imperative (tu) with the object pronoun "mi" attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mandami un messaggio quando arrivi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Send me a message when you arrive.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti mando un messaggio più tardi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll send you a message later.

definitions.note: Often used with an object + place or activity (e.g., mandare i bambini a scuola).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ogni mattina mando i bambini a scuola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every morning I send the kids to school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei un mandarino, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like a mandarin, please.

definitions.note: This is mandare + the indirect object pronoun le (“to her”), attached to the infinitive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo mandarle un messaggio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to send her a message.

definitions.note: This can also be mandare + the direct object pronoun le (“them”, feminine plural), attached to the infinitive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le foto sono pronte: devo mandarle subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The photos are ready: I have to send them right away.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “lo” (= it/him, masculine singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo mandarlo oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to send it today.

definitions.note: Verb + object pronoun: "mandare" + "mi" (to me).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi mandarmi un messaggio?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you send me a message?

definitions.note: Includes the indirect object pronoun “ti” (= to you).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Posso mandarti il link più tardi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can I send you the link later?

definitions.note: Can be the present tense form meaning “you (plural) send” (and it can also be used as the “you all” imperative: “send!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi mandate un messaggio quando arrivate?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Will you send me a message when you arrive?

definitions.note: Imperative (plural): used to tell two or more people to send something to “us”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mandateci una foto, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Send us a photo, please.

definitions.note: Imperative with attached object pronoun “la” (= it/her).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mandatela subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Send it right away.

definitions.note: Imperative (plural) with the direct object pronoun “le” (“them”, feminine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mandatele subito, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Send them right away, please.

definitions.note: This is an informal plural command ("you all"), with "me" attached (mi).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mandatemi una foto, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Send me a photo, please.

definitions.note: past participle (masculine plural) of "mandare"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho già mandato i documenti: sono mandati.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve already sent the documents: they are sent.

definitions.note: imperative (2nd person plural) of "mandare" (you all send)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mandati subito una foto, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Send a photo right away, please.

definitions.note: Past participle of "mandare" (used with "avere" in compound tenses).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho mandato un messaggio a Luca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sent Luca a message.

definitions.note: Often used for an official authorization or assignment (e.g., a political or institutional mandate).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il governo ha ricevuto un mandato chiaro dagli elettori.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The government received a clear mandate from the voters.

definitions.note: Used for the period of time someone holds an official position.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il suo mandato finisce a giugno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His term ends in June.

definitions.note: future tense (tu form) of "mandare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi manderai una cartolina?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Will you send me a postcard?

definitions.note: third-person singular (lui/lei/Lei) future tense of "mandare"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani manderà un messaggio a sua madre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow he/she will send a message to his/her mother.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti manderò un messaggio stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will send you a message tonight.

definitions.note: Form of "mandare" used for 2nd person singular ("you") and also for the formal "Lei" form, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi mandi il documento oggi?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you send me the document today?

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto) form, used especially in writing and in some regions to talk about completed actions in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri Carlo mandò una lettera a sua nonna.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday Carlo sent a letter to his grandmother.

definitions.note: future tense (tu form)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani mangerai con noi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow you will eat with us.

definitions.note: future tense (they will)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani mangeranno la pizza a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow they will eat pizza at home.

definitions.note: Conditional present (used for hypothetical situations or polite requests).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Io mangerebbe una pizza, ma non ho fame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would eat a pizza, but I'm not hungry.

definitions.note: Future tense (1st person plural) of "mangiare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani mangeremo presto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will eat early.

definitions.note: future tense, 2nd person plural (voi)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani mangerete al ristorante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow you will eat at the restaurant.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular future (lui/lei).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani mangerà con noi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow he/she will eat with us.

definitions.note: First person singular (io), future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani mangerò presto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will eat early.

definitions.note: Present tense, informal singular (tu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sei sicuro che mangi abbastanza verdura?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you sure you eat enough vegetables?

definitions.note: Present subjunctive, informal singular (tu), often used after expressions like “penso che…”, “è importante che…”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È importante che mangi qualcosa prima di uscire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that you eat something before going out.

definitions.note: Present tense (3rd person singular): he/she/it eats.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Luca mangia una mela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Luca eats an apple.

definitions.note: Informal singular command (imperative): “Eat!” (said to one person).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mangia la pasta, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Eat the pasta, please.

definitions.note: Past remote (passato remoto), used mainly in narratives and in parts of Italy (especially in the South); in everyday speech many people use the passato prossimo instead.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri mangiai una pizza enorme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I ate a huge pizza.

definitions.note: simple past (passato remoto), “we” form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri mangiammo in un piccolo ristorante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday we ate in a small restaurant.

definitions.note: Present tense (noi). Can also be used as an informal suggestion: “let’s eat.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mangiamo a casa stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re eating at home tonight.

definitions.note: present gerund (used like “while eating” / “(I’m) eating”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto mangiando una pizza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m eating a pizza.

definitions.note: third-person plural present tense (they eat; also formal you-plural)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I bambini mangiano la pizza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children eat pizza.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi piace mangiare la pizza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like to eat pizza.

definitions.note: Infinitive with the attached direct-object pronoun “la” (“it” referring to something feminine, e.g. la pizza).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non voglio mangiarla adesso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to eat it now.

definitions.note: Infinitive with the direct object pronoun "lo" attached ("it", masculine singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non voglio mangiarlo adesso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to eat it now.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto), third person plural: “they ate.” Common in narratives and in some regions; in everyday speech many learners will more often hear passato prossimo (hanno mangiato).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo la partita, mangiarono una pizza insieme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the game, they ate a pizza together.

definitions.note: past participle of "mangiare"; it can agree in gender/number when used with "essere" or as an adjective
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La torta è già stata mangiata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cake has already been eaten.

definitions.note: Depending on context, it can mean “you (plural) eat” (present tense) or “eat!” (plural command).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voi mangiate spesso la pasta a pranzo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You often eat pasta for lunch.

definitions.note: Often used with a direct object pronoun (e.g., li = them): “Li ho mangiati” = “I ate them.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Li ho mangiati tutti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ate them all.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho già mangiato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have already eaten.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (past) tense: describes an ongoing, habitual, or background action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando l’ho chiamato, mangiava.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I called him, he was eating.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (past habitual/ongoing).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da bambini, mangiavano sempre la pasta la domenica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As children, they always ate pasta on Sundays.

definitions.native: I was eating, I used to eat
definitions.note: Imperfetto (1st person singular) of "mangiare"; used for ongoing or habitual actions in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando ero piccolo, mangiavo sempre la pasta a pranzo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was little, I always ate pasta for lunch.

definitions.note: Used mainly as the present subjunctive (“(that) they eat”), and can also be used as a 3rd-person plural command (“let them eat”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che mangino presto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope they eat soon.

definitions.note: present tense (io): “I eat / I’m eating” depending on context
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mangio una pizza stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m eating a pizza tonight.

definitions.note: Third-person singular, simple past (passato remoto); common in writing and in some regions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri Marco mangiò una pizza intera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday Marco ate a whole pizza.

definitions.note: plural of "mano".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi lavo le mani prima di mangiare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wash my hands before eating.

definitions.note: Plural of "manica".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa camicia ha le maniche troppo lunghe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This shirt has sleeves that are too long.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non mi piace la tua maniera di parlare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t like your way of speaking.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto manipolando il file per correggere un errore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m manipulating the file to fix an error.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi fa male la mano destra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My right hand hurts.

definitions.note: Often used for a living space under a sloped roof (an attic apartment).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vivo in una mansarda luminosa in centro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I live in a bright attic apartment downtown.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È importante mantenere la calma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important to keep calm.

definitions.note: Infinitive + direct object pronoun "la" (her/it, feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo mantenerla al caldo finché non arriva il medico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to keep her warm until the doctor arrives.

definitions.note: Often used to mean providing for someone economically.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non è facile mantenerla mentre studia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It isn't easy to support her financially while she studies.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mantenete la calma, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Keep calm, please.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (io/lui/lei). Often used after expressions like "voglio che..." or "è importante che...".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È importante che mantenga la calma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that he/she keeps calm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mantengo la promessa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I keep the promise.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) form, used mainly in writing or narratives (especially in central/southern Italy).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mantenne la promessa fino alla fine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He kept the promise until the end.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il giardino è stato mantenuto bene.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The garden was kept well maintained.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei mantiene la calma anche sotto pressione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She keeps calm even under pressure.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se vuoi dimagrire, mantieni una dieta equilibrata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you want to lose weight, keep a balanced diet.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho letto il manuale di istruzioni prima di usare la macchina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I read the instruction manual before using the machine.

definitions.note: Often used in cooking to refer to beef (the meat).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi cucino il manzo con le patate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I’m cooking beef with potatoes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho bisogno di una mappa della città.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a map of the city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani corro una maratona.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I’m running a marathon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa marca è molto conosciuta in Italia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This brand is very well known in Italy.

definitions.note: Often used for an official mark or a stamped mark on something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sul documento c’è la marca dell’ufficio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is the office stamp on the document.

definitions.note: Plural feminine form of “marcio” (used with feminine plural nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Butta via le mele marce.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Throw away the rotten apples.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo marchio è molto conosciuto in Italia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This brand is very well known in Italy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Camminiamo sul marciapiede, non in strada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s walk on the sidewalk, not in the street.

definitions.note: Also commonly used figuratively to mean “corrupt” (e.g., a rotten system).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa mela è marcia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This apple is rotten.

definitions.note: Used figuratively for people, institutions, or situations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il sistema è marcio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The system is corrupt.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In estate andiamo al mare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In summer we go to the sea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Con l’alta marea, il porto si riempie d’acqua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With the high tide, the harbor fills with water.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preferisco la margarina al burro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prefer margarine to butter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In molti paesi la marijuana è illegale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In many countries marijuana is illegal.

definitions.note: Usually used in phrases like "marina militare" (navy).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio nonno ha lavorato nella marina per molti anni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather worked in the navy for many years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio nonno era un marinaio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather was a sailor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho cucinato il pollo marinato al limone.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I cooked the chicken marinated with lemon.

definitions.note: Informal, from the expression “marinare la scuola” (to skip school).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi ho marinato lezione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I skipped class.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I mariti cucinano mentre le mogli apparecchiano la tavola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The husbands cook while the wives set the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio marito lavora in centro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My husband works downtown.

definitions.note: Commonly used in Italian as an English loanword, especially in business contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lavoro nel marketing di una grande azienda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I work in the marketing department of a large company.

definitions.note: In everyday Italian, marmellata is often used like “jam” in general (even for non-citrus fruits).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A colazione mangio pane con la marmellata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For breakfast I eat bread with jam.

definitions.note: Invariable adjective (doesn’t change for masculine/feminine or singular/plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato delle scarpe marrone.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought some brown shoes.

definitions.note: plural form of the color adjective “marrone”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato delle scarpe marroni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought some brown shoes.

definitions.note: Commonly used in Italian as an English loanword.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nel cioccolato caldo metto due marshmallow.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put two marshmallows in my hot chocolate.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci vediamo martedì.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: See you on Tuesday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi serve un martello per piantare questo chiodo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a hammer to hammer in this nail.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il martire è ricordato per il suo coraggio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The martyr is remembered for his courage.

definitions.note: Plural form (masculine or feminine) of “marziale”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A scuola fanno attività marziali il venerdì.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At school they do martial activities on Fridays.

definitions.note: A soft Italian cream cheese often used in desserts like tiramisù.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per il tiramisù serve il mascarpone.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For tiramisu you need mascarpone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi fa male la mascella quando mastico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My jaw hurts when I chew.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per Carnevale indosso una maschera rossa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For Carnival I wear a red mask.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a girl or young woman who behaves or dresses in a stereotypically boyish way; can be teasing or mildly insulting depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da piccola era un maschiaccio e giocava sempre a calcio con i ragazzi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When she was little, she was a tomboy and always played soccer with the boys.

definitions.note: Used for males of people or animals; for humans it can be a bit more technical than “uomo/ragazzo” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il cucciolo maschio è più grande della femmina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The male puppy is bigger than the female one.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei un massaggio, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like a massage, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi la temperatura massima è di 30 gradi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today the maximum temperature is 30 degrees.

definitions.note: Also used as an adjective meaning “maximum, highest,” but here it’s the noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il massimo è trenta persone.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The maximum is thirty people.

definitions.note: gerund form; often used to mean “while chewing” or “(I/he/she/etc.) am/is chewing,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non parlare con la bocca piena: stai masticando.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t talk with your mouth full: you’re chewing.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devi masticare bene il cibo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to chew your food well.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi ho due ore di matematica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I have two hours of math.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato un materasso nuovo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a new mattress.

definitions.note: Used especially for a school/university subject or field of study.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La matematica è una materia difficile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Math is a difficult subject.

definitions.note: Can refer to physical substance in general.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa sostanza è una materia molto resistente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This substance is a very strong material.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi serve del materiale per il progetto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need some material for the project.

definitions.note: plural of "materiale"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci servono più materiali per finire il progetto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need more materials to finish the project.

definitions.note: Plural; commonly used for school/university subjects.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quest’anno ho molte materie difficili a scuola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This year I have many difficult subjects at school.

definitions.note: Plural; used for physical substances or raw materials.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per questo lavoro servono materie di buona qualità.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For this job, good-quality materials are needed.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'influenza materna è stata fondamentale nella sua crescita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The maternal influence was crucial in his growth.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho bisogno di una matita per scrivere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a pencil to write.

definitions.note: plural of "matita"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato due matite per la scuola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought two pencils for school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo il matrimonio di mio padre, la mia matrigna è stata molto gentile con me.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After my father's wedding, my stepmother was very kind to me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In questa città ci sono molti matrimoni in primavera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this city there are many marriages in spring.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il loro matrimonio è durato dieci anni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Their marriage lasted ten years.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "matto".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sei matta?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you crazy?

definitions.note: plural masculine form of "matto"; can describe people or things.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono matti a guidare così veloce.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They’re crazy to drive that fast.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci vediamo domani mattina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: See you tomorrow morning.

definitions.note: Often refers to the whole morning as a stretch of time, or to how someone spends the morning.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho passato una mattinata tranquilla a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I spent a calm morning at home.

definitions.note: plural of "mattina"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In queste mattine d’inverno fa molto freddo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On these winter mornings it’s very cold.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci vediamo domani mattino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: See you tomorrow morning.

definitions.note: Often used in an informal, everyday way; it can be playful (“you’re crazy!”) or more serious depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sei matto a guidare così veloce!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re crazy to drive that fast!

definitions.note: Used mainly in more formal or fixed expressions (e.g., “il giornale mattutino”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Leggo il giornale mattutino mentre bevo il caffè.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I read the morning newspaper while I drink coffee.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La frutta è matura.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fruit is ripe.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le ragazze sono già mature per la loro età.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The girls are already mature for their age.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Con l’età arriva anche la maturità.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With age, maturity also comes.

definitions.note: In Italy, la maturità commonly refers to the final exam at the end of high school.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quest’anno devo prepararmi per la maturità.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This year I have to prepare for the high school diploma exam.

definitions.note: Used for both people (emotionally developed) and things like fruit (ready to eat).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo quell’esperienza, è diventato più maturo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After that experience, he became more mature.

definitions.note: Often refers to a wooden stick used as a weapon or as sports equipment (like a baseball bat).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha preso una mazza per difendersi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He took a bat to defend himself.

definitions.note: Often used for a small bunch of flowers, keys, or similar items.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi ha regalato una mazzetta di fiori.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gave me a small bunch of flowers.

definitions.note: In informal/colloquial contexts, it can mean money given illegally to get a favor.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hanno accettato una mazzetta per chiudere un occhio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They accepted a bribe to look the other way.

definitions.note: object pronoun (used after a verb or preposition)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi aiutare me?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you help me?

definitions.note: Unstressed object pronoun form of “mi”; it can mean “me” (direct object) or “to me” (indirect object), depending on the verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi vedi? Sì, me vedi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you see me? Yes, you see me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il meccanico ha riparato la mia macchina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mechanic fixed my car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha vinto una medaglia d’oro alle Olimpiadi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He won a gold medal at the Olympics.

definitions.note: Plural of “medaglia”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha vinto tre medaglie alle Olimpiadi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He won three medals at the Olympics.

definitions.note: Often used in expressions like “la media” (the average) or “in media” (on average).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La media dei voti è sette.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The average grade is seven.

definitions.note: Often refers to newspapers, TV, radio, and online news collectively.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I media parlano di questa notizia tutto il giorno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The media talk about this news all day.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of the adjective “medio”. Not the noun “media” (mass media) in English.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La temperatura media oggi è di 20 gradi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The average temperature today is 20 degrees.

definitions.note: plural of "medico"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I medici lavorano molto in questo ospedale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctors work a lot in this hospital.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo prendere questa medicina dopo pranzo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to take this medicine after lunch.

definitions.note: Can refer to the medical profession or the university subject.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mia sorella studia medicina all’università.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister studies medicine at university.

definitions.note: Commonly used for a medicinal product (often in pharmacies).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo medicinale va preso dopo i pasti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This medicine should be taken after meals.

definitions.note: Plural of "medicina".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo prendere queste medicine ogni giorno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to take these medicines every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il medico mi ha visitato questa mattina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor examined me this morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le medie dei voti sono alte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The averages of the grades are high.

definitions.note: Often used as shorthand for "le scuole medie" (e.g., "andare alle medie").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio fratello va alle medie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother goes to middle school.

definitions.note: Often used critically to mean “not very good.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il film è stato mediocre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie was mediocre.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi sto meglio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I’m feeling better.

definitions.note: Often used with the article: “il meglio” = “the best”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo è il meglio che posso fare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is the best I can do.

definitions.note: Used as a noun, often with an article (e.g., "il meglio").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio il meglio per te.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want the best for you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei una mela, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like an apple, please.

definitions.note: plural of "mela"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compro mele al mercato ogni sabato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I buy apples at the market every Saturday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In giardino c'è un melo pieno di mele.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the garden there is an apple tree full of apples.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa melodia mi rimane in testa tutto il giorno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This melody stays in my head all day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I membri del club pagano una quota annuale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The members of the club pay an annual fee.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei è membro del club.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is a member of the club.

definitions.note: In everyday Italian, this can refer to an arm or a leg (a body limb).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si è fatto male a un membro durante la partita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He injured a limb during the game.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho una buona memoria per i nomi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a good memory for names.

definitions.note: plural of "memoria"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho tante memorie felici della mia infanzia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have many happy memories of my childhood.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo memorizzare queste parole per l’esame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to memorize these words for the exam.

definitions.note: Often used for saving data or information (e.g., on a phone or computer).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il telefono memorizza automaticamente le password.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The phone automatically stores the passwords.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho memorizzato il numero di telefono.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I memorized the phone number.

definitions.native: you memorize, you learn by heart
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Memorizzi già la poesia?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Have you already memorized the poem?

definitions.note: Used in comparisons and quantities; often paired with "più" (more).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei meno zucchero nel caffè.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like less sugar in my coffee.

definitions.note: Used in math or when stating a decrease.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieci meno tre fa sette.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ten minus three is seven.

definitions.note: Used to indicate a smaller amount (less) or a smaller number (fewer). Often used with "di" (e.g., "meno di 10").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho meno tempo oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have less time today.

definitions.note: Often used for a school or workplace dining hall.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi pranzo in mensa con i colleghi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I’m having lunch in the cafeteria with my colleagues.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato una mensola per i libri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a shelf for the books.

definitions.note: Used in the present subjunctive (e.g., after expressions like “I don’t think that…”) or as a formal command (Lei).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non credo che lui menta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't think he’s lying.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La salute mentale è importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Mental health is important.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La sua mentalità è molto aperta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His/Her mindset is very open.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho cambiato idea, ma non ho cambiato mente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I changed my mind, but I didn’t change my mind-set.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non fidarti di lui: mente sempre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t trust him: he always lies.

definitions.note: gerund form of “mentire”; used with “stare” to talk about an action happening right now.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stai mentendo, lo so.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re lying, I know it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Perché menti sempre?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why do you always lie?

definitions.note: This form can be either present indicative or present subjunctive, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non mentiamo: è la verità.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re not lying: it’s the truth.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 1st person singular of "mentire"; common in writing and storytelling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti chiesi la verità, ma mentii.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I asked you for the truth, but I lied.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non devi mentire ai tuoi genitori.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You must not lie to your parents.

definitions.note: Conditional mood (third person singular: “he/she/it would lie”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se lo chiedessi, mentirebbe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I asked him, he would lie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non mentirei mai ai miei amici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would never lie to my friends.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per favore, non provare a mentirmi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please, don’t try to lie to me.

definitions.note: past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Durante l’interrogatorio mentirono per proteggere il loro amico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: During the questioning, they lied to protect their friend.

definitions.note: This form is used with "voi" (you all): it can mean "you (plural) lie" (present tense) or "(you all) lie!" (command).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se mentite, perderete la fiducia di tutti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you lie, you will lose everyone's trust.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha mentito alla polizia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lied to the police.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non mento mai ai miei amici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I never lie to my friends.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi fa male il mento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My chin hurts.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present of "mentire".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non mi fido di loro: mentono sempre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t trust them: they always lie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Leggo mentre aspetto l’autobus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I read while I’m waiting for the bus.

definitions.note: Used to contrast two situations or facts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Io preferisco il tè, mentre lei preferisce il caffè.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prefer tea, whereas she prefers coffee.

definitions.note: Passato remoto (remote past), common in storytelling and writing, especially in southern Italy.
