definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alla fine mentì per proteggere suo fratello.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end, he/she lied to protect his/her brother.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho menzionato il tuo nome durante la riunione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I mentioned your name during the meeting.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Durante la riunione, menzionò il tuo nome.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: During the meeting, he mentioned your name.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quella che hai detto è una menzogna.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What you said is a lie.

definitions.note: Often written as "menu" without the accent, especially in all caps or in casual writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Posso vedere il menù, per favore?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can I see the menu, please?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Che meraviglia vedere il mare al tramonto!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What a wonder to see the sea at sunset!

definitions.note: Often used in expressions like “Che meraviglia!” to mean “How wonderful!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo gelato è una meraviglia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This ice cream is a wonderful thing.

definitions.note: feminine singular form (used with feminine singular nouns)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una giornata meravigliosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a wonderful day.

definitions.note: plural masculine form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I tuoi disegni sono meravigliosi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your drawings are wonderful.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È stato un viaggio meraviglioso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was a wonderful trip.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il mercante vende spezie al mercato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The merchant sells spices at the market.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vado al mercato il sabato mattina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I go to the market on Saturday morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hanno assunto un mercenario per proteggere il convoglio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They hired a mercenary to protect the convoy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci vediamo mercoledì alle tre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: See you on Wednesday at three.

definitions.note: Usually refers to the chemical element; capitalized (Mercurio) when referring to the Roman god or the planet Mercury.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il mercurio è un metallo liquido a temperatura ambiente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Mercury is a liquid metal at room temperature.

definitions.note: Vulgar; used as an exclamation (like “shit!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Merda! Ho dimenticato le chiavi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Shit! I forgot my keys.

definitions.note: Vulgar/strong language; often used as an insult or exclamation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho pestato la merda per strada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I stepped in shit on the street.

definitions.note: Often refers to Southern Italy or the south of a country/region.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La cucina meridionale è molto saporita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Southern cuisine is very flavorful.

definitions.note: Can also be used as the informal (tu) imperative meaning “deserve!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo posto merita una visita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This place deserves a visit.

definitions.note: third-person plural (they)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Queste persone meritano rispetto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These people deserve respect.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hai meritato questo successo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You deserved this success.

definitions.note: Infinitive of "meritare" with the object pronoun "mi" attached ("me").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devi meritarmi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to deserve me.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (voi) form of "meritare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meritate una pausa dopo tutto questo lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You (all) deserve a break after all this work.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (he/she/it deserved; was deserving).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo tutto quello che ha fatto, meritava una pausa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After everything he did, he deserved a break.

definitions.note: Present indicative, second-person singular (tu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meriti una pausa dopo tutto questo lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You deserve a break after all this work.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive, second-person singular (tu), often used after expressions like “è giusto che…”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È giusto che tu meriti una seconda possibilità.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s right that you deserve a second chance.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meritiamo una pausa dopo tutto questo lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We deserve a break after all this work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Merito una pausa dopo tutto questo lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I deserve a break after all this work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha ottenuto una promozione per merito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He got a promotion on merit.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of "meschino"; often used to criticize someone’s behavior or attitude.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Che cosa meschina da dire!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What a petty thing to say!

definitions.note: Often used to describe someone’s character or behavior as small-minded or contemptible.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È stato meschino con i suoi colleghi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was mean with his colleagues.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei mescola il caffè con lo zucchero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She stirs the coffee with sugar.

definitions.note: gerund form; often used to mean “while mixing/stirring.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto facendo la salsa mescolando gli ingredienti in una ciotola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m making the sauce by mixing the ingredients in a bowl.

definitions.note: (voi) imperative plural (used to tell more than one person to do something)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mescolate bene gli ingredienti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Mix the ingredients well.

definitions.note: feminine plural form (often used like an adjective or as a past participle)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le carte sono già mescolate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cards are already mixed.

definitions.note: past participle of “mescolare”; often used like an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho già mescolato gli ingredienti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve already mixed the ingredients.

definitions.note: simple past (passato remoto), third-person singular
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui mescolò lo zucchero nel caffè.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He mixed the sugar into the coffee.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo mese ho molto lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This month I have a lot of work.

definitions.note: plural of "mese".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci vediamo tra due mesi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’ll see each other in two months.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Andiamo a messa domenica mattina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to Mass on Sunday morning.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "mettere"; often used in the passive (agrees with a feminine singular subject) or when the direct object is feminine singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La chiave è stata messa sul tavolo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The key was put on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il messaggero porta una lettera al re.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The messenger brings a letter to the king.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho letto i tuoi messaggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I read your messages.

definitions.note: Used for sending messages, especially by phone (SMS/WhatsApp, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto messaggiando con Luca, poi ti richiamo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m texting Luca, then I’ll call you back.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti mando un messaggio dopo cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'll send you a message after dinner.

definitions.note: Literary/older form of the passato remoto of "mettere" (often equivalent to "mise").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Messe il libro sul tavolo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She put the book on the table.

definitions.note: Past participle plural (typically masculine) of “mettere”; it often appears with a direct object pronoun (e.g., “li ho messi”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Li ho messi sul tavolo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put them on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il cibo messicano è molto piccante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Mexican food is very spicy.

definitions.note: past participle of "mettere"; often used with "avere" to form past tenses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho messo le chiavi sul tavolo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the keys on the table.

definitions.note: Often refers to a skilled occupation or craft (a trade).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fare il falegname è un mestiere che richiede pazienza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Being a carpenter is a job that requires patience.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa sedia è fatta di metallo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This chair is made of metal.

definitions.note: Often used in expressions like “il meteo” (the weather report/forecast).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hai visto il meteo per domani?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Did you see the weather forecast for tomorrow?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un insegnante meticoloso e controlla ogni dettaglio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a meticulous teacher and checks every detail.

definitions.note: Plural of "metodo".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Usiamo metodi diversi per studiare l’italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We use different methods to study Italian.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo metodo è molto semplice.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This method is very simple.

definitions.note: plural of "metro"; used for the unit of length and distances.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La piscina è lunga 25 metri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pool is 25 meters long.

definitions.note: Also used in expressions like “in metro” (= by subway).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vado al lavoro in metro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I go to work by subway.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prendo la metropolitana per andare al lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I take the subway to go to work.

definitions.native: (that) I put, (that) I place, (that) I set
definitions.note: Present subjunctive (congiuntivo presente), 1st person singular of "mettere"; often used after expressions of doubt, desire, or necessity.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vuoi che metta la giacca nell’armadio?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you want me to put the jacket in the closet?

definitions.note: third-person singular present of "mettere" (he/she/it puts)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mette le chiavi in tasca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He puts the keys in his pocket.

definitions.note: gerund form (used like “-ing” in English), often after “stare” to describe an action in progress
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto mettendo i piatti in lavastoviglie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m putting the dishes in the dishwasher.

definitions.native: you will put, you will place
definitions.note: Second-person singular future (tu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani metterai i libri nello zaino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow you will put the books in the backpack.

definitions.note: Often used with a time expression and "ci" (e.g., "metterci un’ora" = to take an hour).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per arrivare in centro, possiamo metterci mezz’ora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: To get downtown, it can take us half an hour.

definitions.note: Often used with direct objects (mettere qualcosa da qualche parte = to put something somewhere).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi mettere il libro sul tavolo?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you put the book on the table?

definitions.note: Used especially with clothing items like glasses, a hat, a jacket.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo mettere la giacca perché fa freddo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to put on my jacket because it’s cold.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “la” (“it” for feminine nouns, or “her”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi metterla sul tavolo?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you put it on the table?

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “lo” = “it” (masculine singular) attached to the verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo metterlo sul tavolo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to put it on the table.

definitions.note: Often used with "a" + infinitive ("mettermi a...") to mean "start" doing something (literally "put myself to...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo mettermi a studiare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to start studying.

definitions.note: Often used as "mettersi a" + infinitive (e.g., mettersi a studiare = to start studying).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È ora di mettersi a lavorare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s time to start working.

definitions.note: Used with clothing items: "mettersi" + article + clothing (e.g., mettersi il cappotto).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Con questo freddo, è meglio mettersi il cappotto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With this cold, it’s better to put on your coat.

definitions.native: to put you, to put yourself
definitions.note: includes the informal pronoun “ti” (= you / yourself). Meaning can be non-reflexive (“put you”) or reflexive depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio metterti in contatto con lei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to put you in touch with her.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani metterà il libro sul tavolo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow he/she will put the book on the table.

definitions.note: Second-person plural ("you" plural) present tense of "mettere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mettete i libri sul tavolo, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put the books on the table, please.

definitions.note: Addressed to 'you' plural (voi). The attached pronoun -la usually means 'it' (feminine noun) or 'her', depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mettetela sul tavolo, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put it on the table, please.

definitions.note: Plural informal command ("you all") with the object pronoun "it" attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mettetelo sul tavolo, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put it on the table, please.

definitions.note: Imperative addressed to “you” (plural) with "vi" = yourselves (e.g., telling a group to put something on).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mettetevi il cappotto!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put on your coat!

definitions.note: Can be used as "you put" (present) or as a command "put!" (imperative), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Metti il libro sul tavolo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put the book on the table.

definitions.note: Also used to make suggestions/requests meaning “let’s …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mettiamo il latte in frigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We put the milk in the fridge.

definitions.note: Informal (tu) command. "-la" is a direct object pronoun meaning “it” (feminine) or “her,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mettila sul tavolo, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put it on the table, please.

definitions.note: Informal (tu) imperative of "mettere" with the direct object pronoun "lo" (= it) attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mettilo sul tavolo, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put it on the table, please.

definitions.note: Informal (tu) command form with the object pronoun mi (“me”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mettimi in lista, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put me on the list, please.

definitions.note: Informal command (tu form), used with the reflexive pronoun “ti,” often for clothing (e.g., “mettiti la giacca”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mettiti la giacca!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put on your jacket!

definitions.note: first-person singular present ("I put / I’m putting")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Metto il libro sul tavolo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the book on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mettono i libri sul tavolo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They put the books on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho mangiato solo metà della pizza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ate only half of the pizza.

definitions.note: Often used in set phrases like “a metà” (halfway) or “nel mezzo/metà” (in the middle).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci vediamo a metà strada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’ll meet halfway.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "mezzo"; used before feminine nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho solo una mezza giornata libera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I only have half a day free.

definitions.note: feminine form (used with feminine nouns or as a feminine noun phrase, e.g., "mezza giornata")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho solo mezza bottiglia d’acqua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I only have half a bottle of water.

definitions.note: used in telling time, referring to 30 minutes past the hour
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono le tre e mezza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s half past three.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci vediamo a mezzanotte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: See you at midnight.

definitions.note: Plural of "mezzo". "mezzi" is often used in "mezzi di trasporto" (means of transport) and more generally to mean the resources/means available.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non abbiamo i mezzi per comprare una casa adesso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We don't have the means to buy a house right now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei una pizza mezzo margherita e mezzo prosciutto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like a pizza half margherita and half ham.

definitions.note: Used mainly in set expressions like "nel mezzo" (= in the middle).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci siamo fermati nel mezzo della strada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We stopped in the middle of the road.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prendo mezzo panino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll have half a sandwich.

definitions.note: Often used in the plural: "mezzi" (e.g., "mezzi di trasporto" = means of transport).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non abbiamo i mezzi per pagare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We don’t have the means to pay.

definitions.note: Often used before a noun in phrases like “mezzo chilo” (half a kilo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei mezzo chilo di mele, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like half a kilo of apples, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci vediamo a mezzogiorno davanti alla stazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: See you at noon in front of the station.

definitions.note: Unstressed object pronoun used before the verb (or attached to it). It can mean “me” (direct object), “to me” (indirect object), or “myself” with reflexive verbs, depending on the verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi vedi?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you see me?

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "mio"; used before a feminine singular noun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa è la mia casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is my house.

definitions.note: feminine singular form; used before a feminine singular noun (e.g. “la mia casa”) or alone to mean “mine” (e.g. “è mia”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa borsa è mia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This bag is mine.

definitions.note: Common in informal speech to emphasize negation, often used with “non” (e.g., “non ... mica”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non sono mica stanco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m not tired at all.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi parlare più vicino al microfono, per favore?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you speak closer to the microphone, please?

definitions.note: In everyday Italian, this noun is often used without an article: “Metti il latte nel microonde.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scalda la pizza nel microonde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Heat up the pizza in the microwave.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Osserviamo la cellula al microscopio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We observe the cell under the microscope.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form (used with feminine plural nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le mie amiche vivono a Roma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My friends live in Rome.

definitions.note: feminine plural form (used with feminine plural nouns, or as a pronoun referring to feminine plural things)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Queste sono le mie scarpe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These are my shoes.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form (used with masculine plural nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I miei amici abitano a Milano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My friends live in Milan.

definitions.note: masculine plural form; used before a noun (“my …”) or on its own (“mine”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I miei amici arrivano domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My friends arrive tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi piace il miele nel tè.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like honey in my tea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La stazione è a due miglia da qui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The station is two miles from here.

definitions.note: plural of the grain "miglio".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In questa zuppa ci sono miglia e verdure.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this soup there is millet and vegetables.

definitions.note: Plural form of "migliaio"; commonly used in the expression "migliaia di" (“thousands of”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono migliaia di persone in piazza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are thousands of people in the square.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “about a thousand” in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci saranno un migliaio di persone alla festa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There will be about a thousand people at the party.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La scuola è a un miglio da qui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The school is a mile from here.

definitions.note: A type of grain.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi cucino il miglio con le verdure.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I’m cooking millet with vegetables.

definitions.note: Short form of "migliore", used before a noun (e.g. "il miglior libro").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo è il miglior ristorante della città.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is the best restaurant in the city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’è stato un miglioramento nel servizio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There has been an improvement in the service.

definitions.note: gerund form (used with "stare" for the present progressive, or to mean "while improving")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto migliorando il mio italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m improving my Italian.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio migliorare il mio italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to improve my Italian.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La situazione è migliorata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The situation has improved.

definitions.note: Used with “voi” (you all).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Con questi esercizi, migliorate ogni settimana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With these exercises, you improve every week.

definitions.note: Command form for “voi” (you all).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Migliorate la pronuncia ripetendo le frasi ad alta voce!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Improve your pronunciation by repeating the sentences out loud!

definitions.note: Feminine plural past participle (often used like an adjective).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le condizioni sono migliorate grazie alle nuove regole.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The conditions have improved thanks to the new rules.

definitions.note: past participle used like an adjective (masculine plural)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Con l’allenamento, i miei risultati sono migliorati.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With training, my results have improved.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho migliorato il mio italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have improved my Italian.

definitions.note: Comparative/superlative form of “buono” (“good”); meaning depends on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo ristorante è migliore di quello.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This restaurant is better than that one.

definitions.note: Future tense (3rd person singular) of "migliorare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Con un po' di pratica, il tuo italiano migliorerà presto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With a bit of practice, your Italian will improve soon.

definitions.note: Often used in sentences with "che" (subjunctive), e.g. "Spero che tu migliori..."; it can also be used as an informal command ("Migliori!").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che tu migliori presto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you get better soon.

definitions.note: Plural form of “migliore”; it can mean either “better” (comparative) or “best” (superlative), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questi ristoranti sono migliori di quelli vicino a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These restaurants are better than the ones near my house.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person singular: “he/she/it improved.” Common in written Italian and storytelling; in speech, the passato prossimo is often used instead.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo la cura, la sua salute migliorò rapidamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the treatment, his health improved quickly.

definitions.note: Vulgar and strongly derogatory; used as an insult. Avoid in polite conversation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non chiamarla mignotta: è un insulto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t call her a whore: it’s an insult.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quel miliardario ha donato molti soldi all’ospedale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That billionaire donated a lot of money to the hospital.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quel miliardario e quel milionario vivono nella stessa città.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That billionaire and that millionaire live in the same city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Un milione di persone vive in questa città.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A million people live in this city.

definitions.note: plural of "milione"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono milioni di persone in questa città.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are millions of people in this city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio padre lavora in un ospedale militare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My father works in a military hospital.

definitions.note: In Italian, the plural is usually "mila" (e.g., duemila = 2,000).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo libro costa mille euro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book costs one thousand euros.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I soldati hanno trovato una mina vicino alla strada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soldiers found a mine near the road.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho ricevuto minacce anonime.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I received anonymous threats.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La sua minaccia non mi spaventa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His threat doesn’t scare me.

definitions.note: present gerund (used like “-ing” in English), often after verbs like “stare”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi stai minacciando?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you threatening me?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non devi minacciare le altre persone.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You must not threaten other people.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La città è stata minacciata da un incendio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The city was threatened by a fire.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La città è minacciata dall’alluvione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The city is threatened by the flood.

definitions.note: can mean "you (plural) threaten" (present tense)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Perché mi minacciate?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you threatening me?

definitions.note: can be a plural command: "(you all) threaten" → "Don’t threaten..."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non minacciate nessuno!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t threaten anyone!

definitions.note: can be the feminine plural past participle/adjective (referring to a group of females or feminine nouns)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le persone minacciate hanno chiamato la polizia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The threatened people called the police.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I testimoni sono stati minacciati.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The witnesses were threatened.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono stato minacciato da uno sconosciuto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was threatened by a stranger.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il paese è minacciato da una tempesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The village is threatened by a storm.

definitions.note: simple past (passato remoto), 3rd person singular: he/she/it threatened
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il ladro minacciò il negoziante con un coltello.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The thief threatened the shopkeeper with a knife.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio nonno era un minatore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather was a miner.

definitions.note: Often used with things like a letter, tone, look, or message.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha ricevuto una lettera minatoria.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She received a threatening letter.

definitions.note: Typically a fairly thick soup, often with vegetables, legumes, pasta, or rice.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stasera mangiamo una minestra calda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tonight we’re eating a hot soup.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In quella regione ci sono molte miniere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In that region there are many mines.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani giochiamo a minigolf con gli amici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we’re playing mini-golf with friends.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In estate si vedono molte minigonne in città.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In summer you see many miniskirts in the city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho un tempo minimo per finire l’esame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a minimum amount of time to finish the exam.

definitions.note: Often refers to a government minister (a member of the cabinet), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il ministro della Salute ha annunciato nuove misure.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The health minister announced new measures.

definitions.note: Often used in comparisons (e.g., "di minore importanza" = "of lesser importance").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo problema è di minore importanza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This problem is of lesser importance.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le opinioni minoritarie meritano rispetto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Minority opinions deserve respect.

definitions.note: plural of "minuto".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho solo cinque minuti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I only have five minutes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aspetta un minuto, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wait a minute, please.

definitions.note: possessive determiner; agrees with the gender and number of the noun (mio/mia/miei/mie)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo è il mio libro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is my book.

definitions.note: Possessive pronoun (used without a following noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo libro è mio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book is mine.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase "prendere la mira" (to take aim).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prendo la mira e tiro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I take aim and shoot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mira il bersaglio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He aims at the target.

definitions.note: Plural of "miracolo".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A volte succedono i miracoli.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sometimes miracles happen.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È stato un vero miracolo che sia arrivato in tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was a real miracle that he arrived on time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se miri in alto, vedi le stelle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you look up, you see the stars.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A colazione mangio yogurt con i mirtilli.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For breakfast I eat yogurt with blueberries.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto) form of "mettere"; common in written Italian and storytelling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mise il libro sul tavolo e uscì.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He put the book on the table and left.

definitions.note: Often used as a strong insult meaning “pathetic” or “contemptible,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi sento miserabile oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel miserable today.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “badly/failing badly,” not only “in poverty.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho fallito miseramente l’esame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I failed the exam miserably.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Molte famiglie vivevano in miseria dopo la guerra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many families lived in poverty after the war.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person plural of "mettere"; common in written narratives.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alla fine misero il libro sul tavolo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end they put the book on the table.

definitions.note: past historic (passato remoto) form of "mettere"; common in written narratives
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Misi le chiavi sul tavolo e uscii.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the keys on the table and went out.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La missione è finita con successo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mission ended successfully.

definitions.note: feminine plural form of "misto"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo ordinato due pizze miste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We ordered two mixed pizzas.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono ancora molti misteri nel mare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are still many mysteries in the sea.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'è una luce misteriosa nella foresta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a mysterious light in the forest.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono luci misteriose nel bosco di notte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are mysterious lights in the woods at night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'è qualcosa di misterioso in quella stanza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There’s something mysterious in that room.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La sua scomparsa è un mistero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His disappearance is a mystery.

definitions.note: Plural of "misura"; can mean measurements or actions taken (measures), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il governo ha annunciato nuove misure di sicurezza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The government announced new security measures.

definitions.note: Plural of "misura"; used for sizes/dimensions or quantified values.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prendo le misure della stanza prima di comprare i mobili.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I take the measurements of the room before buying the furniture.

definitions.note: Often used for flavors, smells, or weather; also for a mild (non-harsh) person or tone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo formaggio ha un sapore mite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This cheese has a mild flavor.

definitions.note: Plural of "mobile" (piece of furniture).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In soggiorno ci sono dei mobili nuovi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is some new furniture in the living room.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La moda cambia ogni stagione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Fashion changes every season.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a fashion model; feminine form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mia sorella lavora come modella a Milano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister works as a model in Milan.

definitions.note: Often used for a physical model, a model/design to copy, or a model (person) who poses for photos or art.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo è il modello che dobbiamo seguire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is the model we have to follow.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "moderato".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha un’opinione moderata su questo tema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a moderate opinion on this topic.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Parla con moderazione durante la riunione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Speak with moderation during the meeting.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La cucina è moderna.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kitchen is modern.

definitions.note: masculine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gli edifici moderni hanno spesso grandi finestre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Modern buildings often have large windows.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo edificio è molto moderno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This building is very modern.

definitions.note: Often used both for a person's character (not boastful) and for something limited/not grand (e.g., a modest house or salary).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una persona modesta e non si vanta mai.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a modest person and never brags.

definitions.note: Plural of "modo".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono molti modi per risolvere questo problema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many ways to solve this problem.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho modificato il documento ieri sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I modified the document last night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non mi piace il tuo modo di parlare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't like your way of speaking.

definitions.note: Usually refers to paperwork you fill out (e.g., an application form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devi compilare questi moduli prima di consegnare la domanda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to fill out these forms before submitting the application.

definitions.note: Can refer to units/parts of a course, system, or device, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il corso è diviso in sei moduli.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The course is divided into six modules.

definitions.note: Usually means an official form/document you fill out.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devi compilare questo modulo e firmarlo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to fill out this form and sign it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il tavolo è in mogano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The table is made of mahogany.

definitions.note: plural of "moglie"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le mogli dei miei amici sono molto simpatiche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My friends’ wives are very nice.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mia moglie lavora in ospedale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My wife works in a hospital.

definitions.note: Can also be used as an informal command to one person (tu): “molla!” = “let go!” / “drop it!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui molla la corda e cade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lets go of the rope and falls.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non mollare la mia mano!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t let go of my hand!

definitions.note: Often used informally for stopping an activity, relationship, or job.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha deciso di mollare il lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He decided to quit his job.

definitions.note: Often used as a command addressed to more than one person (or to one person politely).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mollate la corda!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let go of the rope!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo l’incidente, hanno mollati i freni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the accident, they let go of the brakes.

definitions.note: Common in the expression "ci siamo mollati" (we broke up), referring to ending a romantic relationship or stopping seeing each other.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci siamo mollati l’anno scorso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We broke up last year.

definitions.note: Past participle of "mollare"; often used with "avere" (e.g., "ho mollato" = "I let go / I released").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho mollato la corda e la barca si è allontanata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I let go of the rope and the boat moved away.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of "mollare" (also used as the formal imperative: "molli!")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che tu molli presto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you give up soon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci vediamo al molo alle sei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We'll meet at the pier at six.

definitions.note: feminine singular form; used before feminine singular nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho molta fame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m very hungry.

definitions.note: feminine plural form of the determiner (used before feminine plural nouns)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono molte persone al parco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many people at the park.

definitions.note: feminine plural (used to refer to many women/girls/things; as a pronoun it stands on its own, not before a noun)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non posso venire: ho molte da fare oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't come: I have many things to do today.

definitions.note: masculine plural form; used with masculine plural nouns
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Molti studenti arrivano in anticipo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many students arrive early.

definitions.note: masculine plural form; used as a pronoun to mean “many (people/things)”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Molti pensano che sia una buona idea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many think it’s a good idea.

definitions.native: so much, a great deal of
definitions.note: feminine singular form; used before a feminine singular noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho moltissima pazienza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have so much patience.

definitions.note: Stronger than "molto" (emphatic).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Grazie moltissimo per il tuo aiuto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thank you very much for your help.

definitions.note: Stronger than "molto"; used to emphasize intensity.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi piace moltissimo questa canzone.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like this song very, very much.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono molto felice oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m very happy today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui lavora molto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He works a lot.

definitions.note: As a determiner, it agrees with the noun (molto, molta, molti, molte).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho molto lavoro oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a lot of work today.

definitions.note: Used as a pronoun to mean “a lot/much” (it can stand on its own without a noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ne voglio molto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want a lot of it.

definitions.note: plural of "momento".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono momenti in cui ho bisogno di silenzio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are moments when I need silence.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aspetta un momento, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wait a moment, please.

definitions.note: Often used in everyday Italian to mean a short time or a specific point in time, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non è il momento di parlare di questo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s not the time to talk about this.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il monaco vive in un monastero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The monk lives in a monastery.

definitions.note: Often used after the noun (e.g., “guerra mondiale” = “world war”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La crisi mondiale colpisce molte famiglie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The global crisis affects many families.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il mondo è pieno di persone diverse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The world is full of different people.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho trovato una moneta per terra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found a coin on the ground.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho trovato due monete in tasca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found two coins in my pocket.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui monta a cavallo ogni domenica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He rides a horse every Sunday.

definitions.note: Often used for assembling furniture or equipment.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei monta il mobile nuovo in salotto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She assembles the new piece of furniture in the living room.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani andiamo in montagna.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we’re going to the mountains.

definitions.note: plural of "montagna"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In questa regione ci sono molte montagne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this region there are many mountains.

definitions.note: Gerund form, often used to mean “(while) …-ing.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto montando un mobile nuovo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m assembling a new piece of furniture.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viviamo vicino a un monte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We live near a mountain.

definitions.note: As an adjective, it relates to ethics/values (not the noun “morale” meaning team spirit).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una scelta morale difficile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a difficult moral choice.

definitions.note: Often used critically for someone who focuses on judging others’ behavior.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non fare il moralista: ognuno decide per sé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t be a moralist: everyone decides for themselves.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La coperta è morbida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The blanket is soft.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of "morbido". False friend: it looks like English "morbid" but usually means "soft" (e.g., fabric, pillows).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato delle coperte morbide.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought some soft blankets.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo cuscino è morbido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This pillow is soft.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il bambino ha il morbillo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The child has measles.

definitions.note: Used in the present subjunctive (e.g., after expressions like “spero che…”) and also as the formal imperative (Lei).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che il cane non morda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope the dog doesn't bite.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il cane morde forte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog bites hard.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Attento: quel cane può mordere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Careful: that dog can bite.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto morendo di fame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m dying of hunger.

definitions.note: A strong opioid painkiller used in medicine.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il medico mi ha dato della morfina per il dolore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor gave me some morphine for the pain.

definitions.note: Present tense (noi). Often also used as an exclamation meaning “we’re dying!” (e.g., from laughter).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se non beviamo acqua, moriamo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If we don’t drink water, we die.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se non vai dal medico, morirai.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you don't go to the doctor, you will die.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il pesce è morto ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fish died yesterday.

definitions.note: Conditional present (io) of “morire”; often used figuratively for strong desire or emphasis.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Morirei per un caffè adesso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would die for a coffee right now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Un giorno moriremo tutti, ma oggi siamo qui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: One day we will all die, but today we are here.

definitions.note: Second person plural (voi), future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se non vi fermate, morirete di stanchezza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you don’t stop, you will die of exhaustion.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I soldati morirono durante la guerra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soldiers died during the war.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular, future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se non chiamiamo un medico, morirà.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If we don’t call a doctor, he/she will die.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Un giorno morirò, ma oggi voglio vivere bene.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: One day I will die, but today I want to live well.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form of "morire"; often used in hypothetical clauses after "se" (if).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se lui morisse, sarei devastato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If he died (were to die), I would be devastated.

definitions.note: Common in northern Italy; elsewhere you may also hear "fidanzata".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Giulia è la morosa di Marco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Giulia is Marco’s girlfriend.

definitions.note: Regional (especially Northern Italy) informal term, from singular "morosa".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stasera escono anche le morose.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tonight the girlfriends are coming out too.

definitions.note: Often used for someone who is behind on payments (e.g., rent, bills).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'inquilino è moroso da tre mesi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tenant has been behind on payments for three months.

definitions.note: Common in some regions (especially Northern Italy); elsewhere you may hear "fidanzato" more often.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il mio moroso arriva tra poco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My boyfriend will be here soon.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "mordere" (used with feminine subjects or nouns)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La mano è stata morsa dal cane.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hand was bitten by the dog.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) form of “mordere” (common in narratives, especially in writing).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il cane morse il postino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog bit the mailman.

definitions.note: Past participle of "mordere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono stato morso da un cane.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was bitten by a dog.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho un morso di zanzara sul braccio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a mosquito bite on my arm.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of “morire”; used with “essere” (e.g., “è morta”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La pianta è morta per il freddo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plant died because of the cold.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "morto"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La pianta è morta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plant is dead.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo tutti esseri mortali.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are all mortal beings.

definitions.note: feminine plural form (past participle) of "morire"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le piante sono morte per il freddo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plants died from the cold.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La morte fa parte della vita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Death is part of life.

definitions.note: Past participle (masculine plural) of "morire"; used in compound tenses (e.g., "sono morti") or as an adjective meaning "dead."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I miei nonni sono morti molti anni fa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandparents died many years ago.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono due uccelli morti sulla strada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are two dead birds on the road.

definitions.note: plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In questa tradizione, i morti vengono ricordati ogni anno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this tradition, the dead are remembered every year.

definitions.note: Past participle of “morire”; commonly used with “essere” (e.g., “è morto” = “has died/is dead”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il cane è morto ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog died yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il telefono è morto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The phone is dead.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Suo nonno morì nel 1998.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His grandfather died in 1998.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'è una mosca in cucina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There’s a fly in the kitchen.

definitions.note: plural of "mosca".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono troppe mosche in cucina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are too many flies in the kitchen.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La moschea del quartiere è molto bella.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The neighborhood mosque is very beautiful.

definitions.note: Often used for a move in a game (like chess) or a tactical move/decision.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È stata una mossa intelligente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was a smart move.

definitions.note: Feminine plural past participle of “muovere”; it agrees with a feminine plural noun (often with “essere” or in the passive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le tende erano mosse dal vento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The curtains were moved by the wind.

definitions.note: Depending on context, it can also be the informal command “show!” (tu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mostra la foto a tutti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She shows the photo to everyone.

definitions.note: Used to address someone directly; literally “show” + “to me”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mostrami la foto, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Show me the photo, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi mostrarmi il tuo passaporto, per favore?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you show me your passport, please?

definitions.note: Infinitive with an indirect object pronoun attached (gli = “to him”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo mostrargli la strada.
