definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wrote a note for the teacher.

definitions.note: Common in school contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho preso una nota alta all’esame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got a high grade on the exam.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of the adjective (used with feminine nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una cosa nota.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a well-known thing.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto), used especially in writing and in some regions for completed actions in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Appena entrai, notai il silenzio nella stanza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As soon as I came in, I noticed the silence in the room.

definitions.note: Often used in the sense of becoming aware of something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hai notato qualcosa di strano?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Did you notice something strange?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho notato l’indirizzo sul quaderno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wrote down the address in the notebook.

definitions.note: Past participle of "notare"; often used with "avere" in the passato prossimo (e.g., "ho notato").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho notato un errore nel tuo messaggio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I noticed a mistake in your message.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho scritto delle note sul quaderno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wrote some notes in the notebook.

definitions.note: Commonly used in Italian to mean a laptop computer; it can also mean a notebook (paper) in some contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho lasciato il notebook in ufficio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I left the laptop at the office.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha fatto un progresso notevole in poco tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She made remarkable progress in a short time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho una notizia per te.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have some news for you.

definitions.note: Often used for radio or TV news.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ogni sera guardo il notiziario in TV.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every evening I watch the news on TV.

definitions.note: Plural of "notizia"; often used for news updates or pieces of information.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho delle notizie importanti per te.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have some important news for you.

definitions.note: Often used in set phrases like “è noto” (“it is well-known”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un fatto noto in tutta la città.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a well-known fact throughout the whole city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stanotte ho dormito molto bene.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tonight I slept very well.

definitions.note: plural of "notte".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In estate le notti sono più corte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In summer the nights are shorter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preferisco i voli notturni perché costano meno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prefer night flights because they cost less.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) form, used mainly in written narratives; often corresponds to English simple past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Notò subito l’errore nel documento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She noticed the mistake in the document right away.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono nove persone in classe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are nine people in the class.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho una novità: domani parto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have some news: I’m leaving tomorrow.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of “nudo”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La statua è nuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The statue is nude.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In spiaggia ci sono persone nude.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On the beach there are naked people.

definitions.note: masculine plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In spiaggia alcuni bambini giocano nudi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On the beach some children play naked.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È entrato in mare nudo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He went into the sea naked.

definitions.note: Often used with "non" (double negative): "Non ho nulla" = "I have nothing."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non vedo nulla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t see anything.

definitions.note: plural of "numero"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scrivi i numeri da uno a dieci.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Write the numbers from one to ten.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Qual è il tuo numero di telefono?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is your phone number?

definitions.note: feminine plural form; used with feminine plural nouns
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono numerose ragioni per studiare l’italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many reasons to study Italian.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho numerosi amici in Italia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have many friends in Italy.

definitions.note: present tense (third-person singular) of "nuotare"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui nuota ogni mattina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He swims every morning.

definitions.note: present gerund ("-ing" form)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto nuotando in piscina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m swimming in the pool.

definitions.note: third-person plural present tense (they swim)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In estate nuotano nel lago ogni mattina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In summer they swim in the lake every morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi piace nuotare in piscina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like to swim in the pool.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a swim as an activity or session.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi ho fatto una nuotata in piscina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I went for a swim in the pool.

definitions.note: Usually used with “voi” (you all) in the present tense, or as a plural feminine past participle (e.g., “le gare nuotate”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nuotate ogni mattina in piscina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You swim every morning in the pool.

definitions.note: past participle of "nuotare"; used with "avere" to form the passato prossimo
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho nuotato per mezz'ora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I swam for half an hour.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio fratello è un nuotatore molto veloce.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is a very fast swimmer.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (past), 1st person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da bambino, nuotavo ogni estate al mare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As a child, I used to swim every summer at the sea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sei stanco, ma nuoti ancora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re tired, but you’re still swimming.

definitions.note: Present tense (io) of "nuotare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nuoto ogni mattina in piscina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I swim every morning in the pool.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il nuoto è uno sport completo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Swimming is a well-rounded sport.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto), 3rd person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri Marco nuotò fino all’isola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday Marco swam to the island.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "nuovo"; used with feminine singular nouns
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho una macchina nuova.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a new car.

definitions.note: feminine plural form of “nuovo”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato due scarpe nuove.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought two new shoes.

definitions.note: masculine plural form of "nuovo"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato due libri nuovi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought two new books.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato un telefono nuovo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a new phone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il latte materno nutre il bambino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Breast milk feeds the baby.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Una dieta equilibrata è sempre nutriente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A balanced diet is always nutritious.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'è una nuvola grande nel cielo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a big cloud in the sky.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi ci sono molte nuvole nel cielo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today there are many clouds in the sky.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi il cielo è nuvoloso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today the sky is cloudy.

definitions.note: Used to link two (or more) negatives: “né ... né ...” = “neither ... nor ...”. It can also follow another negative (e.g., “non ... né ...”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non voglio né tè né caffè.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want either tea or coffee.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vuoi tè o caffè?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you want tea or coffee?

definitions.note: Used to call someone’s attention or to express emotion; more literary/formal than “oh” in English in some contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O Marco, vieni qui!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Oh Marco, come here!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il cane è molto obbediente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is very obedient.

definitions.note: Often used with “a” + person/authority: “obbedire a qualcuno”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devi obbedire ai tuoi genitori.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You must obey your parents.

definitions.note: Used with Lei (formal you) as a present subjunctive form, or as an imperative form (formal command).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prego, obbedisca alle istruzioni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please, obey the instructions.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per favore, obbedisci a tua madre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please, obey your mother.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho obbedito alle regole.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I obeyed the rules.

definitions.note: Alternative spelling of “obiettivo” (more common).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il nostro obbiettivo è imparare l’italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our objective is to learn Italian.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La presenza è obbligata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Attendance is mandatory.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form; can also be used as a polite way to say “thank you” (especially as “obbligato/a”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo obbligati a mostrare il biglietto all’ingresso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are required to show the ticket at the entrance.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per entrare, è obbligato il biglietto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: To enter, the ticket is required.

definitions.note: Often used figuratively (e.g., burdened with debts, work, or responsibilities).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È oberato dai debiti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is burdened with debt.

definitions.note: Plural form of "obiettivo".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I nostri obiettivi sono chiari.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our goals are clear.

definitions.note: As an adjective, it often means “impartial” or “based on facts,” not influenced by personal feelings.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cerchiamo una valutazione obiettiva dei risultati.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re looking for an objective evaluation of the results.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il mio obiettivo è imparare l’italiano quest’anno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My goal is to learn Italian this year.

definitions.note: Commonly used in photography to mean a camera lens.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato un nuovo obiettivo per la macchina fotografica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a new lens for the camera.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho un'obiezione: questo piano costa troppo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have an objection: this plan costs too much.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non ho obiezioni, va bene così.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have no objections; it's fine like this.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una buona occasione per imparare l’italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a good opportunity to learn Italian.

definitions.note: plural of “occhio”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho gli occhi marroni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have brown eyes.

definitions.note: Plural form; in Italian it’s usually used in the plural when referring to a pair of glasses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho dimenticato gli occhiali a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I forgot my glasses at home.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase “dare un’occhiata” (“to take a look”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dai un’occhiata a questo messaggio, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take a look at this message, please.

definitions.note: Used as an interjection to warn someone about danger or to be careful.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Occhio! C'è una bici che arriva!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Watch out! There’s a bike coming!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho un granello di sabbia nell’occhio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a grain of sand in my eye.

definitions.note: Often used impersonally (like “it’s necessary”): occorre + infinitive / occorre che + subjunctive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per entrare occorre un biglietto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: To get in, a ticket is needed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’incidente occorre spesso su questa strada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The accident happens often on this road.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo libro occupa molto spazio nello zaino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book takes up a lot of space in the backpack.

definitions.note: Often used with "di": "occuparmi di ..." = "take care of ..." / "deal with ...".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo occuparmi dei bambini stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to take care of the kids tonight.

definitions.note: Reflexive verb; often used with "di" + noun/verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È importante occuparsi della propria salute.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important to take care of your health.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle; often used like an adjective (e.g., a person, seat, room, line)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La sala è occupata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The room is occupied.

definitions.note: feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi Maria è occupata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Maria is busy today.

definitions.note: feminine plural; often used about people (e.g., women) or about things like seats/rooms
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo tutte occupate oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re all busy today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo troppo occupati oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are too busy today.

definitions.note: Past participle of "occupare"; often used in compound tenses and can also describe someone as "busy" (e.g., "Sono occupato").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho occupato questo posto perché era libero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I took this seat because it was free.

definitions.note: Often used to say a person is busy or that something (like a seat, room, or bathroom) is not available.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scusa, sono occupato adesso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry, I’m busy right now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo tavolo occuperà troppo spazio in cucina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This table will take up too much space in the kitchen.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Occupi troppo spazio in garage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You take up too much space in the garage.

definitions.note: Common exclamation expressing surprise, worry, frustration, etc.; often used casually (sometimes written as "Oddio!").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oddio, ho dimenticato le chiavi!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Oh my God, I forgot my keys!

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) form; informal "you".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Perché odi la pioggia?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why do you hate the rain?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Marta odia il traffico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Marta hates traffic.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Odiamo la violenza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We hate violence.

definitions.note: Present indicative, third-person plural (they hate).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Odiano la pioggia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They hate the rain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Odio il traffico al mattino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hate traffic in the morning.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “la” (“her/it”, feminine singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non posso odiarla, anche se mi ha ferito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't hate her, even though she hurt me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non puoi odiarmi per questo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can't hate me for this.

definitions.note: infinitive + the object pronoun “ti” (“you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non voglio odiarti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to hate you.

definitions.note: Used in the imperfect subjunctive, often in hypothetical sentences (e.g., after "se" = "if").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se lui odiasse il suo lavoro, lo cambierebbe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If he hated his job, he would change it.

definitions.note: imperfect subjunctive of "odiare"; used in hypothetical/conditional clauses (e.g., after "se")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se odiassi la pioggia, non vivrei qui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I hated the rain, I wouldn’t live here.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 2nd person plural; common in writing and narratives, less in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da bambini, odiaste quel maestro severo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As children, you (all) hated that strict teacher.

definitions.note: Second person plural (voi) form of "odiare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Perché mi odiate?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why do you hate me?

definitions.note: past participle of "odiare" (often used like an adjective)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un uomo odiato da molti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a man hated by many.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past): used for ongoing/repeated past actions or states.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da bambino odiava la matematica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As a child, he hated math.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da bambini, odiavamo svegliarci presto la domenica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As kids, we hated waking up early on Sundays.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (past habitual/ongoing): describes something that was happening or used to happen in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da bambini odiavano le verdure, ma ora le mangiano volentieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As children they hated vegetables, but now they eat them gladly.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense, 2nd person plural (voi).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da bambini, odiavate andare a letto presto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As children, you hated going to bed early.

definitions.note: Second-person singular, past historic (passato remoto).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da bambino, odiavi le verdure.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As a child, you hated vegetables.

definitions.note: imperfect past (ongoing/repeated action in the past)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da bambino odiavo le verdure.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As a child, I hated vegetables.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani odierà ancora di più questa situazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow he/she will hate this situation even more.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Odio aspettare in fila.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hate waiting in line.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il suo odio per le bugie è evidente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His hatred of lies is obvious.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un commento odioso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a hateful comment.

definitions.note: Can mean either “gives off a smell” or “smells like,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa salsa odora di aglio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This sauce smells like garlic.

definitions.note: Often used with "di" to mean "they smell of ..."; it can also mean "they give off a smell."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le rose odorano di primavera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The roses smell of spring.

definitions.note: present tense (voi): used to say that you (plural) smell of something
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voi odorate di fumo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You smell like smoke.

definitions.note: imperative (voi): used to tell a group to smell something
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Odorate questo fiore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Smell this flower.

definitions.note: Often used with "di" to mean "smelled of" (e.g., "odorava di pane").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La cucina odorava di pane appena sfornato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kitchen smelled of freshly baked bread.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'è un odore strano in cucina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There’s a strange smell in the kitchen.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In cucina ci sono odori deliziosi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are delicious smells in the kitchen.

definitions.note: Used for language, behavior, comments, etc. that may hurt or insult someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quel commento è davvero offensivo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That comment is really offensive.

definitions.note: Often used for a special price or promotion in shops; also used more generally for an offer or proposal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'è un'offerta speciale su queste scarpe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There's a special deal on these shoes.

definitions.note: past participle of "offrire"; often used with "avere" to form compound tenses (e.g. "ho offerto" = "I offered / I have offered")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gli ho offerto un caffè.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I offered him a coffee.

definitions.note: feminine singular (past participle)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Maria è rimasta offesa dalle sue parole.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Maria was offended by his words.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form (used with feminine nouns or with “lei”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei è offesa per quello che hai detto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is offended by what you said.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto) form of "offendere" (used especially in narratives and in some regions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri mi offese davanti a tutti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday he/she offended me in front of everyone.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form. Not the English noun “offense” (in Italian, that’s usually the noun “offesa”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le ragazze erano offese per quelle parole.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The girls were offended by those words.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hai offeso con quelle parole.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You offended me with those words.

definitions.note: masculine singular adjective; often used with "essere" (e.g., "sono offeso")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Marco è offeso per quello che hai detto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Marco is offended by what you said.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive of "offrire"; often used after expressions of desire, doubt, necessity, or to make a polite/formal suggestion.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che offra uno sconto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope that he offers a discount.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il negozio offre uno sconto oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The store offers a discount today.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) present tense of "offrire".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Offri tu il caffè?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you offering (paying for) the coffee?

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 1st person singular: “I offered.” Common in narratives and in some regions in speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Offrii il mio aiuto, ma lui rifiutò.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I offered my help, but he refused.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Posso offrirti un caffè?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can I offer you a coffee?

definitions.native: to give (as a gift/treat), to treat (someone)
definitions.note: Often used when you pay for someone or give something for free (e.g., food/drink).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha offerto la cena a tutti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He treated everyone to dinner.

definitions.note: simple past (passato remoto), third person plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I vicini offrirono aiuto dopo la tempesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The neighbors offered help after the storm.

definitions.note: includes the clitic pronoun “ti” = “to you” (informal singular)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei offrirti un caffè.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to offer you a coffee.

definitions.note: Includes the pronoun “vi” = “to you” (plural) or formal “to you” (one person).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei offrirvi un caffè.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like to offer you a coffee.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person singular: he/she/it offered.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui offrì un caffè a tutti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He offered everyone a coffee.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non lasciare oggetti sul pavimento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t leave objects on the floor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho trovato un oggetto strano sotto il letto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found a strange object under the bed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi non ho tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I don't have time.

definitions.note: Often used as an adverb meaning “today” (even though it can be classified as a noun in some dictionaries).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi ho molto da fare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I have a lot to do.

definitions.note: Used before singular nouns (it doesn’t change for gender or number).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ogni giorno vado a scuola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every day I go to school.

definitions.note: feminine singular (used for women/things that are grammatically feminine)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ognuna ha la sua opinione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Each one has her own opinion.

definitions.note: Usually means “each (person)” or “everyone” in a group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ognuno deve portare il proprio documento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Each person must bring their own document.

definitions.note: Used to express surprise, realization, hesitation, or emotion, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oh, non lo sapevo!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Oh, I didn’t know that!

definitions.note: Informal; commonly used in speech and writing (same as English).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Va tutto ok?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Is everything okay?

definitions.note: Very common and informal; used to agree, confirm, or show you understand.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ok, ci vediamo domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: OK, see you tomorrow.

definitions.note: Common informal interjection; also used to show agreement or that something is acceptable.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Okay, va bene così.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Okay, that’s fine like this.

definitions.note: Can refer to a person from the Netherlands; the same form is also used as an adjective meaning “Dutch.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Un olandese mi ha aiutato alla stazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A Dutch person helped me at the station.

definitions.note: Can also mean the Dutch language; context usually makes it clear.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto imparando l’olandese.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m learning Dutch.

definitions.note: Usually refers to cooking oil; in Italy, unless specified otherwise, it often means olive oil.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Metto un po' di olio nella padella.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put a little oil in the pan.

definitions.note: Plural form of "oliva".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi piacciono le olive nere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like black olives.

definitions.note: Used with a noun or pronoun, usually followed by a preposition like “a” or “il” depending on the expression.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La farmacia è oltre il ponte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pharmacy is beyond the bridge.

definitions.note: Often used in the expression “oltre a”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oltre a Marco, viene anche Sara.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Besides Marco, Sara is coming too.

definitions.note: Often used with a preposition like “oltre a” (= besides, in addition to).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non voglio andare oltre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to go any further.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Camminiamo all'ombra degli alberi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We walk in the shade of the trees.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In ingresso ci sono degli ombrelli per gli ospiti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the entrance there are some umbrellas for the guests.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho dimenticato l’ombrello a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I forgot the umbrella at home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho omesso il tuo nome dalla lista.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I omitted your name from the list.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La polizia sta indagando su due omicidi avvenuti in città.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police are investigating two murders that happened in the city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La polizia sta indagando su un omicidio avvenuto ieri sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police are investigating a murder that happened last night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio zio è omosessuale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My uncle is homosexual.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "onesto".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei è una persona onesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is an honest person.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Onestamente, non ho capito la spiegazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Honestly, I didn’t understand the explanation.

definitions.note: feminine plural form (used with feminine plural nouns)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono persone oneste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are honest people.

definitions.note: plural masculine form of "onesto"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono ragazzi onesti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are honest boys.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una persona onesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is an honest person.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Apprezzo la tua onestà.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I appreciate your honesty.

definitions.note: Often used invariable in Italian (same form for masculine/feminine, singular/plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il corso è disponibile online.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The course is available online.

definitions.note: Used for being connected to the internet or on the web.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi lavoro online.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I work online.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi sento onorata di essere qui oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel honored to be here today.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “honored/pleased” in formal contexts (e.g., “sono onorato di…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono onorato di conoscerla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am honored to meet you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un onore conoscerti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s an honor to meet you.

definitions.note: Often used as a polite/formal title for members of parliament (e.g., "l’onorevole Rossi").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una scelta onorevole.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s an honorable choice.

definitions.note: Used when you make a small mistake or something goes wrong.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oops, ho versato l’acqua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Oops, I spilled the water.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stasera andiamo all’opera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tonight we’re going to the opera.

definitions.note: Often used in set phrases like “opera d’arte” (a work of art).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa è un’opera d’arte famosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is a famous work of art.

definitions.note: Plural of "operaio"; often refers to manual/industrial workers.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gli operai entrano in fabbrica alle sette.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The workers enter the factory at seven.

definitions.note: Past participle of "operare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il chirurgo ha operato il paziente ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The surgeon operated on the patient yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used for both medical/surgical operations and operations in general (e.g., business, military, math).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio nonno domani ha un'operazione al ginocchio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandpa has an operation on his knee tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa è solo la mia opinione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is just my opinion.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le tue opinioni sono importanti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your opinions are important.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una buona opportunità per imparare l’italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a good opportunity to learn Italian.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le due idee sono opposte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The two ideas are opposite.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hanno opinioni opposte sulla questione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They have opposing opinions on the issue.

definitions.note: often used to introduce an alternative option; similar to “o,” sometimes with the sense of “or else.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vuoi il tè oppure il caffè?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you want tea or coffee?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hai un’altra opzione?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have another option?

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quali opzioni abbiamo?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What options do we have?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ora non posso parlare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't talk now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho un'ora per finire il lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have an hour to finish the work.

definitions.note: Common in the fixed expression “ora” meaning “now”; “adesso” is another common word for “now”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ora non posso parlare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't talk now.

definitions.note: Often used in school/university contexts (e.g., an oral exam).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani ho un esame orale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I have an oral exam.

definitions.note: Often used for opening hours: "orario di apertura".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Qual è l’orario del treno per Firenze?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is the train schedule for Florence?

definitions.note: Often used in a religious context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Durante la messa, recitiamo alcune orazioni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: During Mass, we recite some prayers.

definitions.note: Can refer to formal public speaking or a set speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alla cerimonia ci sono state due orazioni molto brevi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the ceremony there were two very short speeches.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nella storia ci sono due orchi che vivono in una grotta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the story there are two ogres who live in a cave.

definitions.note: plural of "orchidea"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In serra coltiviamo orchidee tutto l’anno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the greenhouse we grow orchids all year round.

definitions.note: Can also be used as an informal (tu) command: “order!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ordina una pizza per cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She orders a pizza for dinner.

definitions.note: Can also be used as an informal (tu) command: “tidy up!/arrange!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ordina i documenti sulla scrivania.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She tidies up the documents on the desk.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 1st person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri ordinai una pizza margherita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I ordered a margherita pizza.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto) of "ordinare"; common in writing and in some regions, less in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo il concerto, ordinammo una pizza e tornammo a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the concert, we ordered a pizza and went back home.

definitions.note: Commonly used for ordering food/drinks (e.g., in a restaurant) or ordering goods/services.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei ordinare una pizza, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like to order a pizza, please.

definitions.native: to tidy up, to put in order
definitions.note: Used for organizing or arranging things (often with objects like a room, papers, a desk).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo ordinare la mia scrivania prima di studiare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to tidy up my desk before studying.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una giornata ordinaria.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s an ordinary day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una giornata ordinaria.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s an ordinary day.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "ordinare"; often used with a preceding direct object pronoun (e.g., "l'ho ordinata") or as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'ho ordinata prima che arrivassero gli ospiti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I tidied it up before the guests arrived.

definitions.note: Imperative with the object pronoun “mi” attached; addressed to “you (plural)” (voi).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ordinatemi una pizza, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Order me a pizza, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho ordinato una pizza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ordered a pizza.

definitions.note: Often used for a person/room meaning “tidy” or “well-organized.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La tua scrivania è molto ordinata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your desk is very tidy.

definitions.note: Often used for both “order” (arrangement/organization) and “an order” (a request or command).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'è molto ordine in questa stanza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a lot of order in this room.

definitions.note: Often means “you order” (present indicative, tu). It can also be a present subjunctive form depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando ordini online, controlla l’indirizzo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When you order online, check the address.

definitions.note: Plural of "ordine"; can mean orders (commands) or orders (purchases in a restaurant/shop), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gli ordini del capo sono chiari.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss’s orders are clear.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person singular: “he/she ordered”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il capitano ordinò ai soldati di avanzare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The captain ordered the soldiers to advance.

definitions.note: Plural of "ora" (1 hour; also used for "o'clock" in some time expressions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lavoro otto ore al giorno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I work eight hours a day.

definitions.note: plural of "orecchio"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi fanno male le orecchie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My ears hurt.

definitions.note: plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato degli orecchini nuovi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought new earrings.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho perso un orecchino ieri sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I lost an earring last night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi fa male l’orecchio destro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My right ear hurts.

definitions.note: plural form of "orfano".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo l’incidente, i due bambini sono rimasti orfani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the accident, the two children were left as orphans.

definitions.note: Used as an adjective; it agrees in gender and number with the noun it describes.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da bambino era orfano di padre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As a child, he was fatherless.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da bambino ha vissuto in un orfanotrofio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As a child, he lived in an orphanage.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dobbiamo organizzare la riunione per domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to organize the meeting for tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho organizzato una festa per sabato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I organized a party for Saturday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il progetto è ben organizzato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The project is well organized.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La nostra organizzazione aiuta le famiglie in difficoltà.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our organization helps families in difficulty.

definitions.note: Often used to mean how well something is arranged or planned.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Con un po’ di organizzazione, finiamo il lavoro oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With a bit of planning, we’ll finish the work today.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (also used as the formal imperative with ‘Lei’).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che tu organizzi la festa questo weekend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you organize the party this weekend.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Provo orgoglio per quello che hai fatto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel proud of what you did.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of “orgoglioso” (used with feminine nouns or for a woman/girl)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono orgogliosa di te.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m proud of you.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo orgogliose del nostro lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are proud of our work.

definitions.note: masculine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo orgogliosi del nostro lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are proud of our work.

definitions.note: Often used with “di” + noun/infinitive (e.g., orgoglioso di te, orgoglioso di aver vinto).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono orgoglioso di te.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m proud of you.

definitions.note: Often refers to East Asia/the Middle East or to things from “the East” in general, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi piace la cucina orientale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like Oriental (Eastern) cuisine.

definitions.note: Often means “unique” or “creative,” not just “the first version.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo disegno è davvero originale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This drawing is really original.

definitions.note: plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Queste idee sono davvero originali.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These ideas are really original.

definitions.note: Often used with “di/da” to say where someone or something comes from.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono originario di Napoli.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m originally from Naples.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Qual è l’origine di questa parola?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is the origin of this word?

definitions.note: Often used when talking about where a person comes from (family, country, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha origini italiane, ma vive negli Stati Uniti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has Italian roots, but she lives in the United States.

definitions.note: plural of "origine"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le origini di questa tradizione sono molto antiche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The origins of this tradition are very ancient.

definitions.note: Often used to mean that something has already happened or is no longer changeable ("it’s too late / there’s no turning back").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È ormai troppo tardi per tornare indietro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s already too late to go back.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo anello è d’oro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This ring is made of gold.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In questo negozio vendono orologi di tutti i tipi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this shop they sell all kinds of clocks and watches.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho guardato l’orologio: sono già le otto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I looked at the clock/watch: it’s already eight o’clock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Leggo gli oroscopi ogni mattina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I read horoscopes every morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È stato un giorno orribile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was a horrible day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quei commenti sono orribili.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those comments are horrible.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In montagna abbiamo visto due orsi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the mountains we saw two bears.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'orso vive nel bosco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bear lives in the forest.

definitions.note: Often used for Orthodox Christianity; more generally, it can mean traditional or following established rules.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un ebreo ortodosso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is an Orthodox Jew.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non osa parlare in pubblico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She doesn't dare to speak in public.

definitions.note: Used as an informal command (tu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Osa dire la verità!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Dare to tell the truth!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La stanza era oscura e silenziosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The room was dark and quiet.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non oso chiedere un favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t dare ask a favor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vado in ospedale a trovare un amico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to the hospital to visit a friend.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In questa città ci sono due ospedali.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this city there are two hospitals.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Grazie per la tua ospitalità.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thank you for your hospitality.

definitions.note: Can refer to either a guest (someone invited/hosted) or, in some contexts, a host (someone who receives guests).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo un ospite a cena stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have a guest for dinner tonight.

definitions.note: Plural of “ospite”; can refer to people staying at someone’s home or invited to an event.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gli ospiti arrivano alle otto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The guests arrive at eight.

definitions.note: plural of "osso" (bone)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le ossa del braccio fanno male.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bones in my arm hurt.

definitions.note: present tense (lui/lei)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei osserva i bambini al parco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She watches the children at the park.

definitions.note: imperative (tu)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Osserva il cartello prima di entrare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Look at the sign before you go in.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 1st person singular of "osservare"; common in written narratives.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Osservai il cielo per qualche minuto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I watched the sky for a few minutes.

definitions.note: present gerund ("-ing" form)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stavo osservando gli uccelli nel parco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was observing the birds in the park.
