definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the park we saw two green parrots.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il pappagallo parla e ripete le parole.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The parrot talks and repeats words.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio papà lavora in banca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My dad works at a bank.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il parabrezza della macchina è sporco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car’s windshield is dirty.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per me, questa spiaggia è un paradiso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For me, this beach is a paradise.

definitions.note: Often used in the expression «nei paraggi» meaning “nearby / around here,” sometimes especially about waters near a coast or port.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La nave è nei paraggi del porto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ship is in the vicinity of the port.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo paragrafo è troppo lungo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This paragraph is too long.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo l’incidente, è rimasto paralizzato per mesi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the accident, he remained paralyzed for months.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato un paralume nuovo per la lampada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a new lampshade for the lamp.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei è molto paranoica e pensa che tutti la stiano osservando.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very paranoid and thinks everyone is watching her.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non sono paranoico, ma controllo sempre due volte la porta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm not paranoid, but I always check the door twice.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani c’è una parata in centro per la festa nazionale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow there’s a parade downtown for the national holiday.

definitions.note: Common in sports, especially soccer.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il portiere ha fatto una parata incredibile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The goalkeeper made an incredible save.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi parcheggiare qui per un’ora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can park here for an hour.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho parcheggiato la macchina davanti a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I parked the car in front of the house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’è un parcheggio vicino alla stazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There’s a parking lot near the station.

definitions.note: Can refer to parking as an activity or the act of parking.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il parcheggio è vietato qui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Parking is forbidden here.

definitions.note: simple past (passato remoto), 3rd person singular; common in narratives and in some regions, often replaced by passato prossimo in everyday speech
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Parcheggiò la macchina davanti al supermercato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He parked the car in front of the supermarket.

definitions.note: plural of "parco"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A Roma ci sono molti parchi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In Rome there are many parks.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani andiamo al parco con i bambini.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we’re going to the park with the kids.

definitions.note: Often used impersonally like “pare che…” = “it seems that…”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pare che oggi piova.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It seems that it will rain today.

definitions.note: plural masculine form; used before a noun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho parecchi amici in Italia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have several friends in Italy.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “a lot/quite a bit” in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi ho studiato parecchio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I studied a lot.

definitions.note: Often used broadly for family; to say “parent” (mother or father), use “genitore”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho molti parenti in Sicilia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have many relatives in Sicily.

definitions.note: In Italian, this usually means family members/relations in general (not specifically parents).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani vengono a pranzo i miei parenti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My relatives are coming for lunch tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts (e.g., giving an expert opinion).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei sapere il tuo parere su questa idea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to know your opinion on this idea.

definitions.note: Used for an interior wall or surface; for an exterior boundary wall you often hear "muro".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho appeso un quadro alla parete del soggiorno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hung a picture on the living room wall.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le due squadre sono pari per punti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The two teams are equal on points.

definitions.note: Used for even numbers (2, 4, 6, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Due è un numero pari.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Two is an even number.

definitions.note: Used especially in math to refer to even numbers (e.g., 2, 4, 6).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I pari sono divisibili per 2.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Even numbers are divisible by 2.

definitions.note: 3rd-person singular (he/she/it/you formal) of "parlare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei parla inglese molto bene.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She speaks English very well.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) of "parlare" (io); common in written narratives.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Parlai con il professore dopo la lezione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I spoke with the professor after the lesson.

definitions.native: talk to me, speak to me
definitions.note: Informal singular command (tu) with the object pronoun "mi" (= to me).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Parlami di te.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Talk to me about yourself.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 1st person plural of "parlare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri parlammo a lungo del viaggio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday we talked for a long time about the trip.

definitions.note: Gerund form of "parlare"; often used to mean "while speaking/talking" or "by speaking/talking."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Parlando con lei, ho capito tutto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: By talking with her, I understood everything.

definitions.note: third-person plural present tense of "parlare"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In classe parlano italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In class they speak Italian.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il parlante del telefono non funziona.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The phone’s speaker doesn’t work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi piace parlare con i miei amici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like to talk with my friends.

definitions.native: speak to him, talk to him
definitions.note: Infinitive with the indirect object pronoun “gli” attached (= “to him”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo parlargli stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to talk to him tonight.

definitions.native: talk to her, speak to her
definitions.note: Infinitive with enclitic indirect object pronoun “le” (= to her; also can mean “to them” in formal/polite use).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo parlarle subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to talk to her right away.

definitions.native: talk to me, speak to me
definitions.note: Infinitive with the indirect object pronoun "mi" attached ("to me").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi parlarmi un momento?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you talk to me for a moment?

definitions.native: talk to me, speak to me
definitions.note: Infinitive with the attached pronoun “mi” (“to me”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi parlarmi un momento?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you talk to me for a moment?

definitions.native: talk about it, speak about it
definitions.note: Includes the pronoun “ne” (= “about it / about them” or “of it / of them”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non voglio parlarne adesso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to talk about it now.

definitions.native: talk about it, speak about it
definitions.note: Includes the particle “ne”, which usually means “about it/of it” (replacing “di + something”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non voglio parlarne adesso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to talk about it right now.

definitions.note: Includes the pronoun “ne” (= about it / about them).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dobbiamo parlarne domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to talk about it tomorrow.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto) of "parlare"; often used in stories and historical narration.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo la cerimonia, parlarono con il sindaco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the ceremony, they spoke with the mayor.

definitions.native: to talk to you, to speak to you
definitions.note: includes the pronoun "ti" (= to you, informal singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo parlarti stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to talk to you tonight.

definitions.native: to talk to you, to speak to you
definitions.note: Includes the pronoun “vi” = “to you” (plural), or “to you” in a formal context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo parlarvi subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to talk to you right away.

definitions.note: Imperfetto congiuntivo of "parlare"; used after expressions of doubt, desire, necessity, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Era importante che parlasse con il medico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was important that he/she spoke with the doctor.

definitions.note: Used in the imperfect subjunctive (e.g., in hypothetical sentences after “se”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se parlassi italiano, viaggerei più spesso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I spoke Italian, I would travel more often.

definitions.note: Second-person plural form of “parlare” (used with “voi”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Parlate italiano a casa?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you (all) speak Italian at home?

definitions.note: past participle of "parlare"; commonly used with "avere" to form the past tense (passato prossimo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho parlato con Marco ieri sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I spoke with Marco last night.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense; often means “was …-ing” or “used to …” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Parlava al telefono quando sono arrivato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She was talking on the phone when I arrived.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (past imperfect): often used for ongoing/repeated actions in the past or for setting the scene.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri sera parlavamo di scuola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night we were talking about school.

definitions.note: imperfect (they): describes an ongoing or habitual action in the past
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri sera parlavano al telefono per ore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night they were talking on the phone for hours.

definitions.note: second-person singular (tu) imperfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri parlavi con tua sorella al telefono.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday you were talking to your sister on the phone.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (first person singular): used for an ongoing or habitual action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando ero piccolo, parlavo sempre con i miei nonni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was little, I always talked with my grandparents.

definitions.native: I will speak, I will talk
definitions.note: first-person singular (io), future tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani parlerai con il professore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will talk with the professor.

definitions.note: Conditional mood (present), 3rd person singular (lui/lei/Lei).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se avesse più tempo, parlerebbe con noi ogni giorno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If he had more time, he would speak with us every day.

definitions.note: Future tense (1st person plural) of "parlare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani parleremo del tuo progetto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will talk about your project.

definitions.note: Conditional form: “you” (plural, voi) would speak.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se aveste più tempo, parlereste italiano ogni giorno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you had more time, you would speak Italian every day.

definitions.native: you would speak, you would talk
definitions.note: Second-person singular conditional (tu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se avessi più tempo, parleresti di più con i tuoi amici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you had more time, you would talk more with your friends.

definitions.note: Third-person singular future tense of “parlare” (he/she/it will speak).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani parlerà con il direttore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow he/she will speak with the director.

definitions.native: I will speak, I will talk
definitions.note: First-person singular (io) future tense of "parlare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani parlerò con il professore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will talk with the professor.

definitions.note: Often used with an implied "tu" (informal singular "you"). It can also appear in the present subjunctive (e.g., after "che").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Parli italiano?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you speak Italian?

definitions.note: 1st-person plural present of "parlare"; it can also be used as an invitation meaning "let's talk/speak".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Parliamo italiano a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We speak Italian at home.

definitions.note: Used with "voi"; typically in the present subjunctive after expressions like "è importante che..."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È importante che parliate lentamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that you speak slowly.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of "parlare"; also used as the polite imperative for "loro" (e.g., "Parlino!").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È importante che parlino italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that they speak Italian.

definitions.note: Present tense (1st person singular) of "parlare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Parlo italiano a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I speak Italian at home.

definitions.note: simple past (passato remoto), often used in stories and in some regions instead of the present perfect.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri parlò con il direttore e poi se ne andò.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday he spoke with the director and then left.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non capisco questa parola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t understand this word.

definitions.note: Informal; often used for rude or offensive language.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non dire parolacce davanti ai bambini.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t say swear words in front of the children.

definitions.note: Plural of "parola".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le tue parole mi hanno aiutato molto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your words helped me a lot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per Halloween indosso una parrucca bionda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For Halloween I wear a blonde wig.

definitions.note: This form is used in the present subjunctive (e.g., che io/lui/lei parta) and also as a formal command (Lei) meaning “leave!”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che parta domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope he/she leaves tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used in set phrases like "da parte" (aside) and "a parte" (apart/from the rest).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa è la parte più difficile del compito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is the hardest part of the assignment.

definitions.note: Often used for leaving on a trip or journey.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il treno parte alle otto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train leaves at eight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Luca partecipa alla riunione oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Luca participates in the meeting today.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) form; common in written narration and some regions for past events.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri partecipai alla riunione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I attended the meeting.

definitions.note: Often used with “a” (e.g., “partecipare a una riunione” = “to take part in a meeting”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vuoi partecipare alla riunione domani?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you want to take part in the meeting tomorrow?

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I miei amici parteciparono alla riunione ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My friends participated in the meeting yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ogni anno partecipate alla maratona della città.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every year you participate in the city marathon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho partecipato alla riunione ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I participated in the meeting yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Perché non partecipi alla riunione?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why don’t you participate in the meeting?

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person singular (he/she/it).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Luca partecipò alla riunione ieri sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Luca participated in the meeting last night.

definitions.note: present gerund of "partire"; often used to mean "by leaving/starting" or "leaving/starting (while...)"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Partendo presto, arriveremo in tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Leaving early, we’ll arrive on time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La partenza del treno è alle otto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train’s departure is at eight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il libro è diviso in tre parti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book is divided into three parts.

definitions.native: you leave, you depart, you set off
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Parti domani mattina?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you leaving tomorrow morning?

definitions.note: 1st person plural (“we”): can mean “we leave/are leaving,” and it can also be used as an invitation like “let’s leave.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Partiamo alle otto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We leave at eight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cerco un libro particolare su Roma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m looking for a particular (specific) book about Rome.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una città particolare, diversa dalle altre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a special (unusual) city, different from the others.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi piace particolarmente questo libro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I particularly like this book.

definitions.note: Second-person singular future tense (used with "tu").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani partirai alle otto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow you will leave at eight.

definitions.note: Often used for leaving on a trip or starting a journey.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani mattina partiamo alle otto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow morning we leave at eight.

definitions.native: we will leave, we will depart
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Partiremo domani mattina alle otto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will leave tomorrow morning at eight.

definitions.note: Often used for starting a trip, a journey, or a process (e.g., “partire da…” = “to start from…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Partiremo da Milano e poi andremo a Venezia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will start from Milan and then we will go to Venice.

definitions.native: you (plural) will leave, you (plural) will depart
definitions.note: Future tense, 2nd person plural (voi).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani partirete presto per Roma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow you will leave early for Rome.

definitions.note: simple past (passato remoto), third-person plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Partirono presto per Roma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They left early for Rome.

definitions.note: Future tense (3rd person singular) of "partire".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il treno partirà alle otto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train will leave at eight.

definitions.note: Past participle (feminine singular) of "partire".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Anna è partita ieri sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Anna left last night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho visto una partita di calcio ieri sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I watched a soccer match last night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ragazzi, partite adesso?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Guys, are you leaving now?

definitions.note: Often used for sports matches (e.g., soccer). Not related to English “party.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo visto due partite di calcio ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We watched two soccer matches yesterday.

definitions.note: Past participle (masculine plural) of "partire". Not to be confused with the noun "partiti" meaning "political parties."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono partiti alle otto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They left at eight o’clock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In Italia ci sono molti partiti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In Italy there are many political parties.

definitions.note: Common in sports contexts (e.g., soccer).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo visto due partiti di calcio ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We watched two soccer matches yesterday.

definitions.note: Past participle of "partire". Not to be confused with the noun "partito" meaning "(political) party".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il treno è partito alle otto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train left at eight.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a political party.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il partito ha vinto le elezioni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The party won the election.

definitions.note: Often used for a romantic partner, or for a business/working partner.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il mio partner lavora in un'altra città.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My partner works in another city.

definitions.native: I leave, I'm leaving, I depart
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Parto domani mattina alle sette.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I leave tomorrow morning at seven.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il parto è andato bene e la mamma sta bene.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The delivery went well and the mom is doing well.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Partono alle otto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They leave at eight.

definitions.note: English loanword used in Italian, especially for an event/celebration.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stasera c'è un party a casa mia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tonight there’s a party at my place.

definitions.note: Passato remoto (simple past), common in stories and written narratives (often corresponds to English past tense).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri mattina partì molto presto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday morning he/she left very early.

definitions.note: Often used for something that is not total (e.g., a partial answer, partial payment).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo ricevuto solo una risposta parziale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We received only a partial answer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’edificio è stato riaperto parzialmente dopo i lavori.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The building was partially reopened after the construction work.

definitions.note: Often used for an access pass or a travel/season pass.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo mostrare il pass all’ingresso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to show the pass at the entrance.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il treno passa alle otto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train passes at eight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono ancora due passaggi prima di finire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are still two steps before finishing.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho sottolineato i passaggi più importanti del testo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I underlined the most important passages of the text.

definitions.note: Commonly used for a transit or access pass (e.g., a train pass, backstage pass).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato due passaggi per il treno regionale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought two passes for the regional train.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) of "passare"; common in written stories and narration.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Passai davanti alla scuola e vidi Marco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I passed by the school and I saw Marco.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) of "passare"; often used with time expressions (e.g., "le vacanze", "la giornata").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Passai l’estate in Italia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I spent the summer in Italy.

definitions.note: Informal singular imperative of "passare" with the object pronoun "mi" attached ("to me").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Passami il sale, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Pass me the salt, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stavo passando davanti al supermercato quando ti ho visto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was passing in front of the supermarket when I saw you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gli autobus passano ogni dieci minuti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The buses pass by every ten minutes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho controllato i passaporti prima di partire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I checked the passports before leaving.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho dimenticato il passaporto a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I forgot my passport at home.

definitions.note: Often used for time: "Il tempo passa" = "Time goes by."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il tempo passa in fretta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Time goes by quickly.

definitions.note: Often used with "da": "passare da" = "to stop by (someone’s place)".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Passo da te dopo il lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll stop by your place after work.

definitions.note: Common with "a" + place/person: "passare la giornata a casa" = "to spend the day at home."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio passare più tempo con la mia famiglia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to spend more time with my family.

definitions.note: Includes the attached pronoun “gli” (= to him / to them).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo passargli il sale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to pass him the salt.

definitions.note: Includes the object pronoun “mi” (“to me”) attached to the verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi passarmi il sale?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you pass me the salt?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Passarono davanti alla scuola e continuarono a camminare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They passed in front of the school and kept walking.

definitions.note: Often used with time expressions (e.g., days, hours).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Passarono tre giorni in montagna.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They spent three days in the mountains.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "passare"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La tempesta è passata rapidamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The storm passed quickly.

definitions.note: Used with "voi" (2nd person plural). It can also be used as the plural imperative "passate!" = "go ahead / come in!" depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ogni mattina passate davanti alla scuola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every morning you pass in front of the school.

definitions.note: Feminine plural past participle of "passare" (e.g. "le ore sono passate").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le ore sono passate in fretta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hours passed quickly.

definitions.note: Used as an imperative with “you” (plural): “pass me …”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Passatemi il sale, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Pass me the salt, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I miei passatempi preferiti sono leggere e fare sport.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My favorite pastimes are reading and playing sports.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nel tempo libero, leggere è il mio passatempo preferito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In my free time, reading is my favorite pastime.

definitions.note: past participle plural (often used with essere/avere, or as an adjective meaning “past”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono già passati due giorni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Two days have already passed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono eventi passati.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are past events.

definitions.note: Past participle of "passare"; often used with "avere" (e.g., time spent) or "essere" (e.g., someone/something that has passed by or is gone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho passato una bella giornata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I spent a nice day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il passato è importante per capire il presente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The past is important for understanding the present.

definitions.native: was passing, used to pass, went by
definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past), describing an ongoing or habitual action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ogni mattina passava davanti a casa mia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every morning he/she used to pass in front of my house.

definitions.note: plural of "passeggero"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I passeggeri aspettano il treno sul binario.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The passengers are waiting for the train on the platform.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'è un passeggero che aspetta alla fermata dell'autobus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a passenger waiting at the bus stop.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ogni mattina passeggia nel parco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every morning, he/she takes a walk in the park.

definitions.note: informal command (tu)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Passeggia un po' dopo cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take a walk a bit after dinner.

definitions.note: Gerund form of "passeggiare"; often means "while walking" or "by walking" depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto ascoltando un podcast passeggiando nel parco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m listening to a podcast while walking in the park.

definitions.native: to take a walk, to stroll
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi piace passeggiare nel parco dopo cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like to take a walk in the park after dinner.

definitions.note: Often means a leisurely walk, like a stroll.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Facciamo una passeggiata dopo cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s go for a walk after dinner.

definitions.note: plural of "passeggiata"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Facciamo delle passeggiate dopo cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We go for walks after dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri ho passeggiato nel parco con un amico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I walked in the park with a friend.

definitions.native: was walking, was taking a walk, used to walk
definitions.note: Imperfect tense: describes an ongoing or habitual action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri sera passeggiava nel parco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night he/she was walking in the park.

definitions.native: I walk, I take a walk, I stroll
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo cena passeggio nel parco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After dinner I take a walk in the park.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Facciamo un passeggio dopo cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let's go for a walk after dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani passerai davanti alla scuola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow you will go past the school.

definitions.note: Conditional mood (e.g., for hypotheses, polite requests, or reported speech).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se avesse più tempo, passerebbe a trovarci domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If he had more time, he would stop by to see us tomorrow.

definitions.note: Conditional form (voi): used for hypotheticals, polite suggestions, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se aveste tempo, passereste a trovarci?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you had time, would you stop by to see us?

definitions.note: Second-person singular conditional ("you would..."). Often used for coming by/visiting briefly ("to stop by").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se abitassi più vicino, passeresti a trovarmi più spesso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you lived closer, you would stop by to see me more often.

definitions.note: Third-person singular future tense of “passare” (can refer to time passing or someone/something passing by).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il treno passerà alle otto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train will pass by at eight.

definitions.note: Often used in the subjunctive after “che” (e.g., “spero che tu passi…”); it can also be used as a formal command with “Lei” (e.g., “Passi pure!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che passi presto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you pass by soon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho fatto diecimila passi oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I took ten thousand steps today.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “let’s move on / let’s go on (to the next thing)” in conversation or instructions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Passiamo al prossimo esercizio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let's move on to the next exercise.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha una grande passione per la musica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She has a great passion for music.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Passo davanti alla scuola ogni mattina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I pass in front of the school every morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fai un passo indietro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take a step back.

definitions.note: Used especially to talk about walking or running pace (speed/rhythm).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il suo passo è molto veloce.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His pace is very fast.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho dimenticato la password del mio account.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I forgot my account password.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto), third person singular: “he/she/it passed.” Common in written Italian and in some regions in speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il treno passò alle otto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train passed at eight o’clock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A pranzo mangio spesso la pasta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For lunch I often eat pasta.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In hotel sono inclusi la colazione e due pasti al giorno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the hotel, breakfast and two meals a day are included.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Facciamo un pasto veloce e poi usciamo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s have a quick meal and then go out.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il pastore porta le pecore al pascolo ogni mattina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The shepherd takes the sheep out to graze every morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per cena mangio una patata al forno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For dinner I’m eating a baked potato.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi compro le patate al mercato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I’m buying potatoes at the market.

definitions.note: Often used in the plural. In many contexts, it can refer either to packaged potato chips (patatine in busta) or French fries (patatine fritte).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per favore, una porzione di patatine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A portion of fries, please.

definitions.note: In everyday Italian, this often refers specifically to a driving license (patente di guida).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho dimenticato la patente a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I forgot my driver’s license at home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un tentativo patetico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a pathetic attempt.

definitions.note: In Italian, patetico can mean “moving/poignant” (emotionally touching), not only “pathetic.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un discorso patetico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a moving speech.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ama la sua patria e vuole tornarci un giorno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He loves his homeland and wants to return there one day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il mio patrigno vive con noi da tre anni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My stepfather has been living with us for three years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi piace pattinare sul ghiaccio in inverno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like to skate on the ice in winter.

definitions.note: Plural of "pattino".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato dei pattini nuovi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought new skates.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho paura del buio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m afraid of the dark.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Facciamo una pausa di dieci minuti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s take a ten-minute break.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il pavimento è bagnato, fai attenzione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The floor is wet, be careful.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nel giardino c'è un pavone.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a peacock in the garden.

definitions.note: As an adjective, it describes someone who can wait calmly or tolerate difficulties without getting angry.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sii paziente, l'autobus arriverà presto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Be patient, the bus will arrive soon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il paziente aspetta il medico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The patient is waiting for the doctor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti aspetterò pazientemente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will wait for you patiently.

definitions.note: adjective, plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siate pazienti con i bambini.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Be patient with the children.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In questo reparto ci sono molti pazienti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this ward there are many patients.

definitions.note: Plural form of "paziente" used as a noun meaning a patient person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gli infermieri cercano pazienti gentili e pazienti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The nurses look for kind and patient people.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci vuole pazienza con i bambini piccoli.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It takes patience with small children.

definitions.note: feminine singular form; can be informal and sometimes offensive depending on context
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi mi sento pazza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I feel crazy.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quelle idee sono pazze!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those ideas are crazy!

definitions.note: Often used informally to mean “unbelievable/amazing,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una storia pazzesca!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a crazy story!

definitions.note: Plural form (masculine plural, or mixed-gender plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quei ragazzi sono pazzi!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those boys are crazy!

definitions.note: Plural noun; can be offensive depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non ascoltare quei pazzi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t listen to those crazy people.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sarebbe una pazzia farlo senza pensarci.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It would be madness to do it without thinking about it.

definitions.note: Often used informally; depending on context it can be playful or insulting.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sei pazzo a guidare così veloce!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re crazy to drive that fast!

definitions.note: Can be used informally; depending on context it can sound insulting.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quel pazzo corre in strada senza guardare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That crazy person is running in the street without looking.

definitions.note: Common abbreviation for “personal computer” (computer). Often written as “PC” in Italian too.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato un pc nuovo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a new PC.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non voglio ripetere gli stessi peccati.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to repeat the same sins.

definitions.note: Common interjection used to express regret or disappointment.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Peccato! Non posso venire alla festa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What a pity! I can’t come to the party.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dire una bugia è un peccato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Telling a lie is a sin.

definitions.note: Common in the expression “Che peccato!” to say you’re sorry something happened or didn’t happen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Che peccato! Oggi non posso venire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What a pity! I can’t come today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La pecora mangia l’erba nel prato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sheep eats grass in the meadow.

definitions.note: plural of "pecora"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le pecore pascolano nel prato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sheep graze in the meadow.

definitions.note: Usually used negatively to describe someone who focuses too much on small details or rules.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il professore è un po' pedante e corregge ogni dettaglio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher is a bit pedantic and corrects every detail.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Attenzione: ci sono molti pedoni in questa zona.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Watch out: there are many pedestrians in this area.

definitions.note: Comparative form of "male"; often used with "di" (than).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi sto peggio di ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I feel worse than yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi sto peggio di ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I'm worse than yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used with the article: “il peggio” = “the worst.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo visto il peggio durante la tempesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We saw the worst during the storm.

definitions.note: Alternative form of "peggiore" used before a noun (e.g. "il peggior giorno").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È stato il peggior giorno dell’anno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was the worst day of the year.

definitions.note: Present tense (also used for the imperative “(you) get worse!” depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La situazione peggiora ogni giorno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The situation gets worse every day.

definitions.note: gerund form; often means “while getting worse” or “and it’s getting worse.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La situazione sta peggiorando ogni giorno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The situation is getting worse every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La situazione sta peggiorando.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The situation is getting worse.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo è il risultato peggiore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is the worse result.

definitions.note: Can also mean “worst” depending on context (comparative vs. superlative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È la situazione peggiore di tutte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s the worst situation of all.

definitions.note: plural form (used with masculine or feminine plural nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questi sono i risultati peggiori dell’anno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These are the worst results of the year.

definitions.note: Second person plural (“you” plural). Can be either present tense (“you peel”) or an imperative (“peel!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pelate le patate e poi tagliatele a cubetti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Peel the potatoes and then cut them into cubes.

definitions.note: Past participle of "pelare"; commonly used in compound tenses with "avere" (e.g., "ho pelato" = "I have peeled").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho pelato le patate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I peeled the potatoes.

definitions.note: Often used for food (e.g., tomatoes) to mean the skin has been removed.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho usato un pomodoro pelato per la salsa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I used a peeled tomato for the sauce.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio zio è pelato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My uncle is bald.

definitions.note: Plural of "pelo"; often refers to body hair (including facial hair).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho trovato dei peli sul maglione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found some hairs on the sweater.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho la pelle secca in inverno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have dry skin in winter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il pellicano vola sopra il mare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pelican flies above the sea.

definitions.note: Plural of "pelliccia"; usually refers to coats or garments made of fur.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In inverno alcune persone indossano pellicce.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In winter some people wear fur coats.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha comprato una pelliccia nera per l’inverno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She bought a black fur coat for the winter.

definitions.note: Usually used to mean an individual hair; for hair in general, Italian often uses the plural "capelli".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho un pelo sul maglione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a hair on my sweater.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le pene per questo reato sono severe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The penalties for this crime are severe.

definitions.note: anatomy (sexual term)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il pene è un organo del corpo umano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The penis is an organ of the human body.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hai una penna da prestarmi?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have a pen I can borrow?

definitions.note: Plural of “penna”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato delle penne nuove per la scuola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought some new pens for school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei pensa spesso al futuro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She often thinks about the future.

definitions.note: Used as an informal (tu) command.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pensa prima di parlare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Think before you speak.

definitions.note: Informal (tu) imperative of "pensare" with "ci" (= about it/that).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non rispondere subito: pensaci un attimo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t answer right away: think about it for a moment.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 1st person singular; often used in written narratives and some regions in speech for completed past actions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando lo vidi, pensai che fosse mio fratello.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I saw him, I thought he was my brother.

definitions.note: present gerund of "pensare"; often used to mean “while thinking” or “(I’m) thinking”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto pensando a quello che hai detto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m thinking about what you said.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pensano che sia una buona idea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They think it’s a good idea.

definitions.note: Includes the pronoun “ci” (= “about it/it”), so it refers back to something already mentioned.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo pensarci prima di decidere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to think about it before deciding.

definitions.note: Infinitive "pensare" with the clitic "ci" meaning "about it" / "to it" (often used for decisions or plans).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo pensarci prima di rispondere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to think about it before answering.

definitions.note: Often followed by "che" + a clause (e.g., "penso che...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Penso che domani pioverà.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I think it will rain tomorrow.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive (io/tu): used in hypothetical or dependent clauses (often after “se”, “come se”, “volevo che”, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se pensassi di avere tempo, verrei con te.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I thought I had time, I would come with you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pensate che domani pioverà?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you think it will rain tomorrow?

definitions.note: plural imperative (said to more than one person)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pensate prima di parlare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Think before you speak.

definitions.note: Past participle of "pensare"; often used with an auxiliary verb (e.g., "ho pensato" = "I thought / I have thought").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho pensato a te ieri sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thought about you last night.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (past habitual/ongoing): can also mean “used to think” depending on context.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She was often thinking about his/her future.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pensavano che il museo fosse chiuso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They thought the museum was closed.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (past habitual/ongoing) form; used with “voi”.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You thought you would arrive on time, but there was traffic.

definitions.note: Second-person singular, imperfect tense (tu).

definitions.note: Imperfetto (past habitual/ongoing) of “pensare”; often implies “I was thinking” depending on context.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thought today was Sunday.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have many thoughts today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il tuo pensiero è interessante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your idea is interesting.

definitions.note: Also commonly used to mean a guesthouse/boarding house (a small, usually family-run place to stay).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We booked a guesthouse near the sea.

definitions.note: 1st person singular (io) present tense of "pensare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Penso che domani pioverà.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I think it will rain tomorrow.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto) of "pensare"; common in written narratives and some regions in speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pensò a lungo prima di rispondere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He thought for a long time before answering.

definitions.note: Future tense (3rd person singular) of the reflexive verb "pentirsi"; it’s usually used with "si" (e.g., "si pentirà").

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you do it, he/she will regret it soon.

definitions.note: Past participle of the reflexive verb “pentirsi”; often used with “essere” (e.g., “mi sono pentito”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi sono pentito di quello che ho detto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I regretted what I said.

definitions.note: Usually used reflexively as "pentirsi" (e.g., "mi pento"); often followed by "di" + infinitive.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I regret having told you this.

definitions.note: A general cooking pot (often with handles and a lid).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Metto la pasta nella pentola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the pasta in the pot.

definitions.note: Usually refers to black pepper used as a spice.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi passarmi il pepe, per favore?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Al mercato compro due peperoni rossi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the market I buy two red bell peppers.

definitions.note: Used for the recipient or purpose of something.

definitions.note: Often used before an infinitive to express purpose.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono qui per aiutarti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m here to help you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono due euro per bottiglia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s two euros per bottle.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato una pera al mercato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a pear at the market.

definitions.native: I perceive, I sense, I notice
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Percepisco un odore di fumo nell’aria.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I notice a smell of smoke in the air.

definitions.note: Often written with an accent (perché). It can mean “why” in questions and “because” in answers.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you late? Because there was traffic.

definitions.note: Used in questions (direct or indirect) to ask for a reason.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Perché sei in ritardo?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you late?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono rimasto a casa perché pioveva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I stayed home because it was raining.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non ho studiato, perciò ho preso un brutto voto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn’t study, so I got a bad grade.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo è il percorso più veloce per arrivare in centro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is the fastest route to get downtown.

definitions.note: Often used for an organized program of study or training (e.g., a school or university course).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I chose a course of study in economics.

definitions.note: Used in the present subjunctive (e.g., after expressions like “spero che...”).

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se non stai attento, perde il treno.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto) of "perdere"; often used in narration and in some regions more than in everyday speech.

definitions.note: gerund form of "perdere"; often used to describe an action in progress ("while losing").

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non voglio essere un perdente.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If he doesn’t study, he will fail the exam.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The team suffered a loss in the final.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’azienda ha avuto grandi perdite quest’anno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company had big losses this year.

definitions.note: Present tense (lui/lei) of "perdonare".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She always forgives her friends.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Forgive my delay.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 1st person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alla fine perdonai mio fratello.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end, I forgave my brother.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vuoi perdonarmi?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sei perdonata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are forgiven.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Forgive my lateness.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are forgiven.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope he/she will forgive me soon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti perdonerò, ma non voglio che succeda di nuovo.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I forgive you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti chiedo perdono per il mio errore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ask your forgiveness for my mistake.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person singular; common in written narratives and in some regions in speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alla fine, lo perdonò.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end, she forgave him.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi sono sentita perduta senza il mio telefono.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I felt lost without my phone.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found the lost wallet.

definitions.note: feminine singular form

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I understand perfectly what you're saying.

definitions.note: Past participle (masculine plural) of "permettere"; often used with essere (passive) to mean "are allowed".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like your personality.
