definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This suitcase weighs too much.

definitions.note: Often used figuratively for something that feels like a burden or has an impact.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La decisione pesa su di me.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The decision weighs on me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa valigia è pesante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This suitcase is heavy.

definitions.note: Often used to describe a person, conversation, or situation that feels tedious or annoying.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quel film era davvero pesante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That movie was really boring.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pioveva pesantemente tutta la notte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It rained heavily all night.

definitions.note: Often used to describe awkward movement or lack of grace.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cammina pesantemente dopo la corsa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He walks clumsily after the run.

definitions.note: plural form (masculine or feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le valigie sono pesanti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The suitcases are heavy.

definitions.note: Form of "pesare" used for "you (plural) weigh" (present) or as a plural command ("weigh!").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pesate 70 chili.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You weigh 70 kilos.

definitions.note: Past participle used in compound tenses or as an adjective (masculine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I pacchi sono già pesati.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The packages have already been weighed.

definitions.note: Second-person plural present indicative (voi).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voi pesati molto con lo zaino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You weigh a lot with the backpack on.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei una pesca, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like a peach, please.

definitions.note: Also used in the phrase “andare a pesca” = “to go fishing.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La pesca è vietata in questo lago.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Fishing is forbidden in this lake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio padre pesca ogni domenica mattina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My dad fishes every Sunday morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto pescando al lago con mio padre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m fishing at the lake with my dad.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani andiamo a pescare al lago.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we’re going fishing at the lake.

definitions.native: to pick (at random), to draw (a card/number)
definitions.note: Often used for drawing lots, a card, or a number at random.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pesca una carta e vediamo chi vince.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Draw a card and let’s see who wins.

definitions.note: Past participle of "pescare"; often used to refer to fish that has been caught.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo mangiato del pesce pescato oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We ate some fish caught today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio nonno era un pescatore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather was a fisherman.

definitions.note: plural form of pescatore
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I pescatori tornano al porto al tramonto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fishermen return to the port at sunset.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A cena mangiamo il pesce.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For dinner we eat fish.

definitions.note: plural of "pesce"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nel lago ci sono molti pesci.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many fish in the lake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il peso della valigia è di venti chili.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The weight of the suitcase is twenty kilos.

definitions.note: Used for the name of the currency in several countries (e.g., Mexico, Argentina).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In Messico, paghiamo in pesos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In Mexico, we pay in pesos.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "pessimo"; used for something/someone feminine (or a feminine noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È stata una pessima idea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was a terrible idea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio fratello è molto pessimista sul futuro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is very pessimistic about the future.

definitions.note: plural masculine (or mixed-gender) form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo pessimisti e pensiamo che pioverà.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re pessimistic and we think it will rain.

definitions.note: Superlative of "cattivo" (very bad).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un pessimo film.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a terrible movie.

definitions.note: Past participle of "pestare"; can also be used as an adjective meaning "crushed".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho pestato l'uva per fare il vino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I crushed the grapes to make wine.

definitions.note: simple past (passato remoto), 3rd person singular of "pesare"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il macellaio pesò la carne e mi disse il prezzo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The butcher weighed the meat and told me the price.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il petrolio è una risorsa importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Oil is an important resource.

definitions.note: Plural form; often used like “gossip” in English (as a mass noun) or “pieces of gossip.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non mi piacciono i pettegolezzi in ufficio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t like gossip at the office.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto pettinando i capelli di mia figlia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m combing my daughter’s hair.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi fa male il petto quando respiro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My chest hurts when I breathe.

definitions.note: plural of "pezzo"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi servono due pezzi di carta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need two pieces of paper.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei un pezzo di pizza, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like a piece of pizza, please.

definitions.note: Often used with “di” to mean “a part of” something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa è solo una parte del problema: manca ancora un pezzo importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is only part of the problem: an important part is still missing.

definitions.note: Used with the subjunctive after expressions like "spero che..." ("I hope that...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che ti piaccia questo libro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you like this book.

definitions.note: Often used with an indirect object pronoun (mi/ti/gli/le/ci/vi) to mean "to be pleasing to".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È importante che il regalo le piaccia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that she likes the gift.

definitions.note: Used with the verb piacere: the person who likes something is usually an indirect object (mi/ti/gli/le/ci/vi); the grammatical subject is the thing that is liked.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti piacciamo?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you like us?

definitions.note: Subjunctive form of "piacere"; often used with an indirect object pronoun (mi/ti/gli/le/ci/vi), e.g. "Spero che ti piacciano..." = "I hope you like..."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che ti piacciano questi libri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you like these books.

definitions.note: Used with an indirect object (to someone): e.g., “Ti piaccio” literally “I appeal to you” = “You like me.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti piaccio?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you like me?

definitions.note: Used with what is liked as the grammatical subject: for example, “Mi piacciono i libri” = “I like books” (literally, “Books please me”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi piacciono questi film.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like these movies.

definitions.note: Used with the person who likes something as an indirect object (often with a pronoun like mi/ti/gli/le).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi piace questo libro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like this book.

definitions.note: Gerund of "piacere"; commonly used with an indirect object (mi/ti/gli/le/ci/vi piace) to mean something is pleasing to someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi ha aiutato a scegliere un film che mi stesse piacendo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He helped me choose a movie that I was liking.

definitions.note: Used when meeting someone; literally means “(a) pleasure.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Piacere, sono Marco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Nice to meet you, I’m Marco.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un piacere conoscerti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a pleasure to meet you.

definitions.note: Often used in the expression “per piacere” meaning “please.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi fai un piacere?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you do me a favor?

definitions.note: Often used like “to be pleasing to someone”: mi piace = I like it (literally, “it pleases me”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi piace questo libro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like this book.

definitions.note: Conditional form of "piacere"; used to say what someone would like (literally: "would be pleasing"). Often used with an indirect object pronoun (mi/ti/gli/le/ci/vi/gli) + infinitive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi piacerebbe visitare Roma un giorno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like to visit Rome one day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I piccoli piaceri della vita sono importanti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The small pleasures of life are important.

definitions.native: to please her, to appeal to her
definitions.note: Includes the indirect object pronoun "le" (= to her). Often used about preferences (what someone likes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero di piacerle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope to please her.

definitions.note: Includes the indirect object pronoun “vi” = “to you” (plural or formal). Often used to mean “for you to like (something/someone)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero di piacervi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you like me.

definitions.note: Often used with an indirect object (a + person): e.g. "Ti piacerà..." = "You will like..."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti piacerà questo film.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will like this movie.

definitions.note: Used in the imperfect subjunctive, often in "if"-clauses to express a hypothetical situation (e.g., "If I liked...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se mi piacesse il caffè, lo berrei ogni giorno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I liked coffee, I would drink it every day.

definitions.note: From "piacere". Often used with an indirect object: "mi piacete" literally means "you are pleasing to me" = "I like you (plural)."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi piacete molto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like you a lot. (plural)

definitions.note: Imperfect tense of "piacere" (used like "to be pleasing"; often translates as "liked").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi piaceva questa canzone quando ero bambino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I liked this song when I was a child.

definitions.note: Often used with an indirect object (mi/ti/gli/le/ci/vi/gli): e.g. “mi piacevano” = “I liked / I used to like”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da bambini, ci piacevano molto i cartoni animati.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As children, we really liked cartoons.

definitions.note: From "piacere": the person who likes something is usually expressed with an indirect pronoun (e.g., "mi piace..."); "piacevo" literally means "I was pleasing (to someone)" → "someone liked me."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da bambino piacevo a tutti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As a child, everyone liked me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una serata piacevole.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a pleasant evening.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo camminato piacevolmente lungo il fiume.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We walked pleasantly along the river.

definitions.note: With piacere, the thing/person that is liked is the grammatical subject (e.g., “Mi piaci” literally “You please me” = “I like you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi piaci molto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like you a lot.

definitions.note: Past participle of "piacere"; it often agrees with what is liked (e.g., feminine singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La pizza mi è piaciuta molto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I really liked the pizza.

definitions.note: feminine plural past participle of "piacere" (used with "essere")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le foto ti sono piaciute.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You liked the photos.

definitions.note: Past participle (masculine plural) of "piacere"; often used with "essere" (e.g., "mi sono piaciuti" = "I liked them").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I tuoi regali mi sono piaciuti molto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I liked your gifts a lot.

definitions.note: Past participle of "piacere", often used with "essere" (e.g., "mi è piaciuto" = "I liked it").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi è piaciuto il film.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I liked the movie.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) form; often used with an indirect object (e.g. “le/gli piacque …” = “she/he liked …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le piacque molto il film.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She liked the movie a lot.

definitions.note: Often used for complaining in an annoying or childish way.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Smettila di piagnucolare e dimmi cosa è successo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop whining and tell me what happened.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La Terra è un pianeta del sistema solare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Earth is a planet in the solar system.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I pianeti del nostro sistema solare orbitano intorno al Sole.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The planets in our solar system orbit around the Sun.

definitions.note: Used with the present subjunctive (e.g., after expressions like “spero che...”, “non voglio che...”) or as the formal (Lei) command.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non voglio che pianga.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want him/her to cry.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (lui/lei) of “piangere”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il bambino piange perché è stanco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The child is crying because he is tired.

definitions.note: gerund form; often means “while crying” or “by crying,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È uscito di casa piangendo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He left the house crying.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non voglio piangere davanti a tutti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to cry in front of everyone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando lo saprà, piangerà.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he finds out, he will cry.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (voi), present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Perché piangete?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you crying?

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing/repeated action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri sera piangeva perché era triste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night she/he was crying because she/he was sad.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando guardo quel film, piango sempre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I watch that movie, I always cry.

definitions.note: third-person plural present (they cry/are crying) of "piangere"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I bambini piangono perché sono stanchi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are crying because they are tired.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo due piani per il weekend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have two plans for the weekend.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo edificio ha dieci piani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This building has ten floors.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nel negozio ci sono tre piani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the shop there are three pianos.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/it) present tense of “pianificare”; can also be the formal (Lei) command “plan/schedule.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei pianifica la riunione per domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She plans the meeting for tomorrow.

definitions.note: gerund form; often used after “stare” (e.g., “sto pianificando…”) to mean “I’m planning…”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto pianificando una gita per il weekend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m planning a trip for the weekend.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho pianificato la riunione per domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I planned the meeting for tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi pianifico la settimana prossima.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I plan next week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mia sorella è una pianista molto brava.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is a very good pianist.

definitions.note: Often used to tell someone to do something more gently or to speak/move with less noise.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Parla piano, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Speak softly, please.

definitions.note: Used as an exclamation to tell someone to slow down, be careful, or calm down.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Piano, stai attento!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Easy, be careful!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo un piano per domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have a plan for tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il mio ufficio è al terzo piano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My office is on the third floor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Suono il piano da quando ero bambino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve played the piano since I was a child.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Suono il pianoforte ogni sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I play the piano every evening.

definitions.note: Past historic tense (passato remoto), common in stories and written narratives.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando sentì la notizia, pianse in silenzio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When she heard the news, she cried in silence.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho una pianta sul balcone.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a plant on the balcony.

definitions.note: Often used for a map of a place or the layout of a building (e.g., “pianta della città”, “pianta dell’appartamento”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi darmi la pianta della città?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you give me the map of the city?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ogni primavera pianta fiori sul balcone.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every spring she plants flowers on the balcony.

definitions.note: Informal; used for someone who causes problems or arguments.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non invitare Marco: è un piantagrane.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don't invite Marco: he's a troublemaker.

definitions.note: Informal command (tu). Literally "quit it"; the "-la" refers to what the person is doing (e.g., complaining, joking, shouting).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Piantala di urlare!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop shouting!

definitions.note: Passato remoto (simple past), 1st person plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'anno scorso piantammo due alberi in giardino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last year we planted two trees in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto piantando dei fiori in giardino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m planting some flowers in the garden.

definitions.note: Often used for putting something firmly into the ground (e.g., a stake, a flag).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stanno piantando un palo nel terreno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They’re driving a pole into the ground.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In primavera voglio piantare dei pomodori in giardino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In spring I want to plant some tomatoes in the garden.

definitions.note: Informal: often used to mean leaving someone/something suddenly (e.g., a person, a job, a plan).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi ha piantato davanti al cinema e non è mai arrivato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He ditched me in front of the cinema and never showed up.

definitions.note: Colloquial imperative (plural): used to tell people to stop doing something annoying; literally from the expression “piantarla”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Piantatela di urlare, per favore!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop shouting, please!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho piantato un albero in giardino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I planted a tree in the garden.

definitions.note: Plural of "pianta".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In giardino ci sono molte piante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many plants in the garden.

definitions.note: Used with the subjunctive (e.g., after "che"): can mean "(that) you plant" or "(that) he/she plants," depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che tu pianti un albero in giardino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you plant a tree in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato una piantina di basilico per il balcone.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a basil seedling for the balcony.

definitions.note: Often used for a simple map (e.g., of a city or museum) or a floor plan (e.g., of a house/apartment).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi puoi dare la piantina del museo, per favore?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you give me the museum map, please?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho pianto tutta la notte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I cried all night.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui piantò un albero in giardino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He planted a tree in the garden.

definitions.note: Plural of "piastrella"; usually refers to floor or wall tiles.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In cucina ci sono piastrelle bianche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the kitchen there are white tiles.

definitions.note: Can refer to a physical platform (e.g., a train platform) or a digital/online platform, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci vediamo sulla piattaforma 3.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: See you on platform 3.

definitions.note: Plural of "piatto".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho lavato i piatti dopo cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I washed the dishes after dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho lavato il piatto dopo cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I washed the plate after dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo piatto è molto piccante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This dish is very spicy.

definitions.note: Used for food with strong heat/flavor (like chili).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa salsa è molto piccante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This sauce is very spicy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui picchia la palla con la racchetta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He hits the ball with the racket.

definitions.note: Often used with "alla porta" (at the door).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Qualcuno picchia alla porta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Someone is knocking at the door.

definitions.note: Often used for physical hitting (a person or thing). In some contexts it can imply beating someone up.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non devi picchiare tuo fratello.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You must not hit your brother.

definitions.note: past participle (feminine singular) of "picchiare"; often used in passive constructions to mean someone was beaten/hit
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È stata picchiata dal suo aggressore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was beaten by her attacker.

definitions.note: Often used as a 2nd-person plural command (“you all hit/beat!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non picchiate il cane!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t hit the dog!

definitions.note: Can also be used with “voi” in the present subjunctive (e.g., after “che”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È importante che voi non picchiate nessuno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that you don’t hit anyone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I ragazzi sono stati picchiati.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boys were beaten.

definitions.note: Past participle of "picchiare"; often means "beat up" when referring to a person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È stato picchiato fuori dal locale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was beaten up outside the club.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui picchiava la palla contro il muro.
