definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È difficile poter dire la verità.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s hard to be able to tell the truth.

definitions.note: Used as a modal (auxiliary) verb before another verb in the infinitive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei potere parlare italiano meglio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like to be able to speak Italian better.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il presidente ha molto potere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The president has a lot of power.

definitions.note: Plural of "potere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il presidente ha molti poteri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The president has many powers.

definitions.native: to be able to (do) it, to be able to (do) her
definitions.note: Includes the direct-object pronoun “la” attached to the infinitive; “la” usually means “her” or “it” (feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non penso di poterla vedere domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t think I’ll be able to see her tomorrow.

definitions.native: to be able to do it
definitions.note: Infinitive of "potere" + the direct object pronoun "lo" ("it" or sometimes "him").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero di poterlo fare domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope to be able to do it tomorrow.

definitions.note: includes the attached pronoun "ti" (= you), used before another verb: "poterti + infinitive" (e.g., "poterti aiutare")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero di poterti aiutare domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope I can help you tomorrow.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive of "potere", used in dependent clauses (often after "che") to mean “that (someone) could / might be able to.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Speravo che potesse venire alla festa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was hoping that he could come to the party.

definitions.note: Used in the imperfect subjunctive, often after expressions like "se" (if), "magari" (if only), or in polite/hypothetical statements.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se potessi, verrei con te.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I could, I would come with you.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive of "potere"; often used in hypothetical sentences with "se" (if).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se potessi, verrei con te.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I could, I would come with you.

definitions.note: Often used in hypothetical or uncertain situations (e.g., after "se" or expressions like "speravo che").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se potessimo, verremmo con voi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If we could, we would come with you.

definitions.native: you could, you were able to
definitions.note: Passato remoto (historic past) of "potere", used for past actions mainly in written narratives.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Poteste vedere la città dall’alto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You were able to see the city from above.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (voi) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Potete aiutarmi, per favore?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you help me, please?

definitions.note: Second-person plural (voi) present tense of "potere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Potete chiudere la porta, per favore?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you close the door, please?

definitions.note: Imperfect form; often used with an infinitive to express what someone could do or was able to do in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri non poteva venire alla riunione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday he/she couldn’t come to the meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri non poteva venire a cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday he/she couldn't come to dinner.

definitions.note: Imperfetto, 1st person plural (noi): often implies a past ability or possibility, or “could” in a past context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando eravamo bambini, potevamo giocare fuori fino a tardi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When we were children, we could play outside until late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri non potevano venire alla riunione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday they couldn’t come to the meeting.

definitions.note: Past imperfect tense, 2nd person plural (“you all/you” plural). Often used for ongoing situations in the past or polite/indirect phrasing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Potevate venire prima, ma non avete avuto tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You could have come earlier, but you didn’t have time.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (tu form), often used to talk about ability/possibility in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Potevi venire con noi, ma eri stanco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You could have come with us, but you were tired.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (past) form, used for ongoing/repeated ability or possibility in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da bambino potevo correre per ore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As a child I could run for hours.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense: often means "was able to" or "could" in the past (habitually/for a while).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando ero più giovane, potevo correre molto veloce.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was younger, I could run very fast.

definitions.note: Often used to express possibility or to make a polite suggestion/request.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Potrebbe venire domani?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Could you come tomorrow?

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary with an infinitive to talk about a possible ability or possibility (conditional).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Potrebbero venire domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They could come tomorrow.

definitions.note: First person singular conditional of the auxiliary verb "potere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Potrei venire domani, ma non sono sicuro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I could come tomorrow, but I'm not sure.

definitions.note: First-person plural (noi) form; used to express possibility or make a suggestion politely.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Potremmo andare al cinema stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We could go to the cinema tonight.

definitions.note: Used as a modal auxiliary before an infinitive to express ability/possibility in the future.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani potremo andare al mare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will be able to go to the seaside.

definitions.note: Second person plural (voi), conditional of "potere"; used for polite requests.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Potreste aiutarmi, per favore?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Could you help me, please?

definitions.note: Second person singular (tu), used to make polite requests or suggestions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Potresti aiutarmi con i compiti?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Could you help me with my homework?

definitions.note: Third-person singular future of the modal verb "potere"; it’s used with another verb in the infinitive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani potrà venire con noi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow he/she will be able to come with us.

definitions.note: Future tense (1st person singular) of “potere”; used to express ability or possibility.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani potrò venire alla riunione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will be able to come to the meeting.

definitions.note: past participle of "potere"; used with "avere" to form compound tenses
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non ho potuto venire ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I couldn’t come yesterday.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "povero".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La povera ragazza non ha soldi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The poor girl has no money.

definitions.note: Often used to express pity for someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Povera Maria, ha perso il treno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Poor Maria, she missed the train.

definitions.note: feminine plural form of “povero”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il comune aiuta le famiglie povere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The town helps poor families.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form (can also be used for a mixed-gender group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quei poveri ragazzi non hanno abbastanza soldi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those poor boys don’t have enough money.

definitions.note: Plural noun meaning “poor people” (often used with an article: i poveri).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dobbiamo aiutare i poveri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to help the poor.

definitions.note: Often used either about not having money or to express pity/compassion (like “poor thing”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un ragazzo povero, ma molto generoso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a poor boy, but very generous.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La povertà è un problema serio in molte città.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Poverty is a serious problem in many cities.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'è un pozzo nel cortile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a well in the courtyard.

definitions.note: Very common informal shortening of “poco” (often written with an apostrophe).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aspetta un po’, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wait a bit, please.

definitions.note: Present tense (third-person singular) of "pranzare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui pranza sempre a mezzogiorno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He always has lunch at noon.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 1st person singular: “I had lunch.” Common in narratives and in parts of Italy; in conversation many speakers prefer the passato prossimo (ho pranzato).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri pranzai con i miei nonni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I had lunch with my grandparents.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto), 1st person plural: used especially in writing and in parts of Italy (more common in the South) for completed past actions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri pranzammo insieme al ristorante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday we had lunch together at the restaurant.

definitions.note: Present gerund of "pranzare"; used to mean "while having lunch" or "(is/are) having lunch" depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto pranzando con i miei colleghi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm having lunch with my coworkers.

definitions.native: to have lunch, to eat lunch
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi pranziamo alle due.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today we’re having lunch at two.

definitions.note: Form used with voi (2nd person plural): can be present tense (“you all have lunch”) or the plural imperative (“have lunch!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pranzate alle due?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you all have lunch at two?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho già pranzato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have already had lunch.

definitions.note: Informal: second-person singular (tu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi pranzi a casa o al ristorante?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you having lunch at home today or at the restaurant?

definitions.note: Present tense (noi) of “pranzare”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi pranziamo alle dodici e mezza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today we have lunch at twelve thirty.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi pranzo alle dodici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I have lunch at twelve.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A che ora è il pranzo?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What time is lunch?

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) form, used mainly in written Italian and some regions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri pranzò con i suoi amici al ristorante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday he had lunch with his friends at the restaurant.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Con la pratica, diventi più sicuro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With practice, you become more confident.

definitions.note: Often used for official or administrative matters (e.g., a case file or documents to submit).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo completare la pratica per il permesso di soggiorno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to complete the paperwork for the residence permit.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “basically” in conversation, like summarizing or simplifying a point.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Praticamente, abbiamo finito tutto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Basically, we’ve finished everything.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È praticamente impossibile arrivare in tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s virtually impossible to arrive on time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo praticare l’italiano ogni giorno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to practice Italian every day.

definitions.note: Often used for activities like sports, religion, or a profession (e.g., praticare uno sport).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei pratica yoga due volte a settimana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She does yoga twice a week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pratico italiano ogni giorno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I practice Italian every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo zaino è molto pratico per viaggiare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This backpack is very practical for traveling.

definitions.note: Often used for things that are easy to use or that make something easier.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il supermercato è pratico: è vicino a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The supermarket is convenient: it’s close to home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I bambini giocano nel prato dietro casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children play on the lawn behind the house.

definitions.note: Often used for notice periods (e.g., at work or for contracts): dare il preavviso, periodo di preavviso.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo dare un mese di preavviso prima di lasciare il lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to give one month’s notice before leaving my job.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per precauzione, ho chiuso tutte le finestre prima di uscire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As a precaution, I closed all the windows before going out.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nella lezione precedente abbiamo imparato i numeri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the previous lesson we learned the numbers.

definitions.note: Past participle (plural) of "precipitare"; often used with "essere" to form the past tense for events like falling or crashing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Due aerei sono precipitati in mare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Two planes crashed into the sea.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi serve una risposta precisa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a precise answer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devi lavorare con precisione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to work with precision.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dammi un indirizzo preciso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Give me an exact address.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il leone insegue la sua preda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lion chases its prey.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In questa zona vivono molti predatori.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many predators live in this area.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preferiamo andare a piedi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We prefer to go on foot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È preferibile prenotare in anticipo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s preferable to book in advance.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preferirebbe restare a casa stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She would prefer to stay home tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preferirei restare a casa stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would prefer to stay home tonight.

definitions.note: Second person plural (voi), conditional present.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preferireste cenare fuori o restare a casa?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Would you prefer to eat out or stay at home?

definitions.note: Second person singular (tu), conditional present.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preferiresti andare al mare o in montagna?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Would you prefer to go to the beach or to the mountains?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei preferisce il tè al caffè.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She prefers tea to coffee.

definitions.note: Can be used in statements or questions (e.g., “do you prefer…?”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preferisci il tè o il caffè?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you prefer tea or coffee?

definitions.note: Present tense (io). Often followed by “di” + infinitive or “che” + subjunctive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preferisco il tè al caffè.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prefer tea to coffee.

definitions.note: third-person plural ("they") present tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preferiscono il tè al caffè.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They prefer tea to coffee.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa è la mia canzone preferita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is my favorite song.

definitions.note: Form used with “voi” (you plural): can be present tense (“you prefer”) or an imperative (“prefer!”) depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preferite il tè o il caffè?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you prefer tea or coffee?

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Queste sono le mie canzoni preferite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These are my favorite songs.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questi sono i miei film preferiti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These are my favorite movies.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho preferito restare a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I preferred to stay at home.

definitions.note: as an adjective it agrees in gender and number with the noun it describes
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo è il mio film preferito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is my favorite movie.

definitions.note: noun; usually refers to a male person/thing, or is used generally in informal speech
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il mio preferito è il gelato al cioccolato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My favorite is chocolate ice cream.

definitions.note: imperfect tense (he/she/it preferred; used to prefer)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da bambino preferiva giocare fuori invece di stare in casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As a child, he preferred to play outside instead of staying at home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mia nonna prega ogni mattina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandmother prays every morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi prega di aspettare un momento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She asks me to wait a moment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto pregando per te.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m praying for you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ogni sera prego prima di dormire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every evening I pray before going to sleep.

definitions.note: Often used in polite requests (e.g., "Ti prego" = "Please" / "I’m begging you").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La prego di aspettare un momento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ask you to wait a moment.

definitions.note: Often used to address more than one person (you all), e.g. as a command/invitation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pregate per noi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Pray for us.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho pregato per te ieri sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prayed for you last night.

definitions.note: Often used with "di" + infinitive to mean "asked/begged (someone) to do something."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti ho pregato di aspettarmi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I asked you to wait for me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando ero piccolo, mia nonna pregava ogni sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was little, my grandma prayed every evening.

definitions.note: Also used as a formal/polite "please" (Lei): "Prego, preghi".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preghi per noi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Pray for us.

definitions.note: Often used in the expression "Dio (la) preghi" (may God… / God forbid…).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dio preghi che non succeda di nuovo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: God forbid it happens again.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La mia preghiera è per la tua famiglia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My prayer is for your family.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ogni sera recito le preghiere prima di dormire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every evening I say prayers before going to sleep.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dobbiamo superare i pregiudizi e ascoltarci di più.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to overcome prejudices and listen to each other more.

definitions.note: Often used in polite/formal requests, especially in the phrase “La prego…” meaning “please…”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La prego di aspettare un momento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please wait a moment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prego ogni sera prima di dormire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I pray every evening before going to sleep.

definitions.note: Common reply to "grazie".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: —Grazie! —Prego!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: —Thanks! —You're welcome!

definitions.note: Used to invite someone to proceed (e.g., enter first, speak, sit).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prego, si accomodi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please, have a seat.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prima di partire, pregò in silenzio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Before leaving, he/she prayed in silence.

definitions.note: Often used in more formal or literary contexts; in modern everyday speech, "ha pregato" is more common.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il re lo pregò di restare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The king asked/begged him to stay.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devi premere questo pulsante per accendere la luce.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to press this button to turn on the light.

definitions.note: Also used for pressing a button or key (e.g., on a phone or keyboard).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui premete il pulsante per aprire la porta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He presses the button to open the door.

definitions.note: Can mean either “you press” (present tense) or “press!” (command), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Premi questo pulsante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Press this button.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha vinto il primo premio al concorso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She won first prize in the contest.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho avuto una premonizione che sarebbe successo qualcosa di importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had a premonition that something important would happen.

definitions.note: feminine plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le infermiere sono sempre molto premurose con i pazienti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The nurses are always very caring with the patients.

definitions.note: Often used to describe someone who is thoughtful and shows concern for others.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un infermiere premuroso con tutti i pazienti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a caring, attentive nurse with all the patients.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho premuto il pulsante sbagliato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I pressed the wrong button.

definitions.note: Often used as a formal command (Lei): “Prenda …”. It can also be a present subjunctive form of “prendere”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prenda questo documento, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please take this document.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prende l'autobus ogni mattina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He takes the bus every morning.

definitions.note: past historic (passato remoto), 1st person plural of "prendere"; common in narratives and some regions
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri prendemmo il treno alle sette.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday we took the train at seven.

definitions.note: present gerund of "prendere"; often used to mean "while taking" or "by taking"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto prendendo un caffè.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m having a coffee.

definitions.native: you will take, you will get
definitions.note: Second-person singular future tense (tu form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani prenderai il treno alle otto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow you will take the train at eight.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (loro) future tense of "prendere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani prenderanno l’autobus alle otto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow they will take the bus at eight.

definitions.note: Includes the object pronoun "ci" (= us).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non può prenderci.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She can't catch us.

definitions.note: Very common verb with many uses (e.g., take an object, take a bus, take medicine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Posso prendere questo libro?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can I take this book?

definitions.note: Conditional, 1st person singular (io).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Io prenderei un caffè, ma è troppo tardi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would have a coffee, but it’s too late.

definitions.native: we will take, we will get, we will pick up
definitions.note: Future tense of "prendere" for "we" (noi).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani prenderemo il treno alle otto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will take the train at eight.

definitions.native: to take it, to pick it up
definitions.note: Literally “to take it,” with the direct object pronoun “la” (“it,” often referring to a feminine noun or a situation).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo prenderla in ufficio prima di partire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to pick it up at the office before leaving.

definitions.note: "la" is a direct-object pronoun meaning “it” (referring to a feminine noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi prenderla dal tavolo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can take it from the table.

definitions.native: to get beaten up, to get a beating
definitions.note: Common idiomatic use of "prenderle" (literally "to take them"), where "le" refers to "botte" (blows).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se continui così, le prendi!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you keep it up, you'll get a beating!

definitions.note: Infinitive "prendere" + direct object pronoun "li" (“them”, masculine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo prenderli domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to take them tomorrow.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun "lo" (“it”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi prenderlo dal tavolo, per favore?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you take it from the table, please?

definitions.note: Often used with an infinitive + the attached pronoun “mi” (= me).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vuoi prendermi per mano?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you want to take me by the hand?

definitions.native: to take some, to take some of it/them
definitions.note: Includes the pronoun “ne” (= “some,” “of it,” “of them”), often used with quantities.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio prenderne due.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to take two of them.

definitions.note: Reflexive form of "prendere"; often used for things like taking a break or taking time for yourself.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È importante prendersi una pausa ogni tanto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important to take a break every now and then.

definitions.note: Commonly used with illnesses, especially minor ones (e.g., "prendersi un raffreddore").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È facile prendersi un raffreddore in inverno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s easy to catch a cold in winter.

definitions.note: Infinitive with attached pronoun: prendere + ti (“you”). Often used meaning “pick you up” (e.g., by car).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vengo a prenderti alle otto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll come pick you up at eight.

definitions.note: Includes the clitic pronoun “vi” (= you all).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio prendervi con me.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to take you all with me.

definitions.note: Future tense (lui/lei/Lei). Often also used in the sense of “will get” (e.g., take a bus, get a decision).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani prenderà l’autobus alle otto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow he/she will take the bus at eight.

definitions.note: Future tense (1st person singular) of "prendere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prenderò un caffè prima di uscire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will have a coffee before going out.

definitions.note: Often used for receiving/obtaining something, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prenderò il treno delle otto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will take the eight o'clock train.

definitions.note: Second-person plural present ("you" plural / "you all"), also used as the formal "you" (plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prendete un ombrello: sta piovendo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take an umbrella: it’s raining.

definitions.note: Used as an imperative addressed to more than one person ("you all").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prendetela e mettetela sul tavolo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take it and put it on the table.

definitions.note: Imperative with the object pronoun “le” (= them, feminine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prendetele e mettile sul tavolo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take them and put them on the table.

definitions.note: Plural command (to “voi”); includes the object pronoun “lo” = “it”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prendetelo e mettetelo sul tavolo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take it and put it on the table.

definitions.note: Imperative plural: said to more than one person. “ne” often means “some (of it/them)” or “of it/them”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono dei biscotti sul tavolo: prendetene due.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are some cookies on the table: take two.

definitions.note: Imperative (you all). With "-vi" it means "take for yourselves" / "take (some)".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prendetevi un momento per leggere le istruzioni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take a moment to read the instructions.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (past habitual/ongoing): often means “was taking” or “used to take,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri prendeva l’autobus per andare al lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday he was taking the bus to go to work.

definitions.note: Present tense, 2nd person singular (tu): used to give instructions or talk about what “you” take.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prendi l'ombrello: fuori piove.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take the umbrella; it’s raining outside.

definitions.note: Also commonly used to mean “we’ll have (food/drink)” when ordering.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prendiamo il treno alle otto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We take the train at eight.

definitions.note: Imperative with the direct-object pronoun “la” (= “it/her”, feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prendila e mettila sul tavolo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take it and put it on the table.

definitions.note: Informal (tu) command form of "prendere" with the direct object pronoun "lo" attached (= "it").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prendilo e mettilo sul tavolo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take it and put it on the table.

definitions.note: Informal (tu) imperative with the direct object pronoun “lo” = “it” (masculine singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prendilo e mettilo sul tavolo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take it and put it on the table.

definitions.note: Informal (tu) imperative of "prendere" + "ne" (meaning "some of it/them" or "of it/them").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se ti piacciono i biscotti, prendine due.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you like the cookies, take two (of them).

definitions.note: Imperative with the pronoun “ne” (= “of it/them”). Often used when the quantity is not specified or is implied.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prendine un po’, se hai fame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Have some, if you’re hungry.

definitions.note: Informal singular (tu) imperative with the object pronoun “ti” (= for yourself).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prenditi un momento per respirare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take a moment for yourself to breathe.

definitions.note: Present tense, 1st person singular (io).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prendo un caffè e torno subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll have a coffee and be right back.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they) of "prendere" in the present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ogni mattina prendono il treno per andare al lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every morning they take the train to go to work.

definitions.note: Used for reserving things like a hotel room, a table, tickets, or an appointment.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei prenotare un tavolo per due per stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to book a table for two for tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho già prenotato un tavolo per stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve already booked a table for tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho una prenotazione per due persone alle otto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a reservation for two people at eight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi preoccupa il traffico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The traffic worries me.

definitions.note: Often used with stare (e.g., "stai preoccupando") to mean "you’re worrying (someone)".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi stai preoccupando con queste notizie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re worrying me with this news.

definitions.note: Often translates to “worry” rather than the English verb “preoccupy.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi preoccupano i tuoi ritardi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your delays worry me.

definitions.note: Infinitive with the clitic "ci" (= us/ourselves). Often used like "preoccuparci (per/di qualcosa)" = "to worry (about something)".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non dobbiamo preoccuparci per il futuro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We shouldn’t worry about the future.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively as preoccuparti/preoccuparsi (“to worry”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non voglio preoccupare i miei genitori.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to worry my parents.

definitions.note: This form includes the pronoun “mi” (“me”); it’s commonly used reflexively (like “to worry”) or in the sense “to worry about something.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non voglio preoccuparmi per niente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to worry about anything.

definitions.note: Literally “to worry myself”; includes the clitic pronoun “mi” (= myself). Often used with “di” or “per” to say what you’re worried about.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cerco di non preoccuparmi troppo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I try not to worry too much.

definitions.note: Reflexive verb; often used with “di” + infinitive (e.g., “preoccuparsi di fare…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non ti preoccupare, va tutto bene.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t worry, everything is fine.

definitions.note: Reflexive verb; often used with “di” or “per” (e.g., preoccuparsi di/per qualcosa).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non preoccuparti, va tutto bene.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t worry, everything is fine.

definitions.note: Infinitive with the clitic pronoun “ti” (“yourself/you”), as in “non devi preoccuparti” = “you don’t have to worry.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non devi preoccuparti, va tutto bene.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You don’t have to worry; everything is fine.

definitions.note: Often used as “non preoccuparti” = “don’t worry” (informal, talking to one person). It can also mean “to worry” after verbs like “dovere/potere”: “non devi preoccuparti”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non devi preoccuparti, va tutto bene.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You don’t have to worry; everything is fine.

definitions.native: to worry you (plural), to concern you (plural)
definitions.note: Includes the enclitic pronoun “-vi” = “you (plural)”. It often corresponds to English “to worry you” rather than the literal-looking “to preoccupy you”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non voglio preoccuparvi, ma domani potrebbe piovere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to worry you, but it might rain tomorrow.

definitions.native: to worry you (plural), to concern you (plural)
definitions.note: Includes the pronoun "vi" (= you, plural; or formal "you"). Often used with "non" (e.g., "Non voglio preoccuparvi").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non voglio preoccuparvi, ma dobbiamo parlare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to worry you, but we need to talk.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono un po' preoccupata per l'esame di domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m a bit worried about tomorrow’s exam.

definitions.note: feminine plural form (used with plural feminine nouns or when referring to a group of women)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le ragazze sono preoccupate per l’esame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The girls are worried about the exam.

definitions.note: Often used with "per" to say what someone is worried about. It looks like English "preoccupied," but Italian "preoccupato" usually means "worried/concerned."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo preoccupati per te.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re worried about you.

definitions.note: Often means genuinely worried/concerned in Italian. It looks like English “preoccupied,” which can also mean “distracted/absorbed,” so don’t always translate it that way.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono preoccupato per l’esame di domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m worried about tomorrow’s exam.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono preoccupato per l'esame di domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m worried about tomorrow’s exam.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (past habitual/ongoing); often followed by "mi/ti/lo/la/ci/vi/li/le" (e.g., "mi preoccupava" = "it worried me").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La situazione mi preoccupava molto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The situation was worrying me a lot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho una preoccupazione per il futuro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a worry about the future.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho troppe preoccupazioni in questo periodo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have too many worries these days.

definitions.note: Often used with an object (e.g., “mi preoccupi” = “you worry me”) or reflexively (“ti preoccupi” = “you worry”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi preoccupi quando non rispondi ai messaggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You worry me when you don’t reply to messages.

definitions.note: Often used with a pronoun: "mi preoccupo" = "I worry / I'm worried."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi preoccupo per l’esame di domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m worried about tomorrow’s exam.

definitions.note: third-person singular present (also used for formal “you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei prepara la cena ogni sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She prepares dinner every evening.

definitions.note: past historic (passato remoto), 1st person singular
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri sera preparai la cena per tutti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night I prepared dinner for everyone.

definitions.note: Passato remoto, 1st person plural (used mainly in written Italian and in some regions for past events).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri sera preparammo la cena per tutti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night we prepared dinner for everyone.

definitions.note: gerund form (used like “while/when ...-ing” or to talk about an action in progress)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto preparando la cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m preparing dinner.

definitions.native: to get ready, to prepare ourselves
definitions.note: Includes the pronoun “ci” (“ourselves”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dobbiamo prepararci per l’esame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to get ready for the exam.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo preparare la cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to prepare dinner.

definitions.note: simple past (passato remoto), 3rd person plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I cuochi prepararono la cena in pochi minuti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cooks prepared dinner in a few minutes.

definitions.note: Reflexive verb: it means to make yourself ready for something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo prepararmi per uscire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to get ready to go out.

definitions.native: to prepare you, to get you ready
definitions.note: Infinitive + enclitic pronoun “ti” (= you/yourself, informal singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo prepararti per la festa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to get you ready for the party.

definitions.native: to prepare yourselves, to get ready (you all)
definitions.note: Includes the pronoun "vi" (= you plural). Often used reflexively meaning "to get ready".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dovete prepararvi per l’esame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to get ready for the exam.

definitions.note: feminine singular form (often used as a past participle or adjective).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono preparata per l’esame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am prepared for the exam.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono preparata per l’esame di domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m ready for tomorrow’s exam.

definitions.note: Used with "voi" (you plural): can mean "you prepare" or, as an imperative, "prepare!" (to a group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preparate la cena ogni sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You prepare dinner every evening.

definitions.note: feminine plural form (refers to a group of females or feminine plural nouns)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le valigie sono già preparate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The suitcases are already ready.

definitions.note: Plural (addressing “you all”); reflexive form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preparatevi: il treno parte tra cinque minuti!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Get ready: the train leaves in five minutes!

definitions.note: Often used as a command; it can include the reflexive pronoun (e.g., «Preparati!» = “Get ready!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preparati: stiamo per uscire!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Get ready: we’re about to leave!

definitions.note: Can be the masculine plural past participle/adjective (e.g., «Siamo preparati.»).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo preparati per l’esame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are prepared for the exam.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo preparati per l'esame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are prepared for the exam.

definitions.note: Past participle of "preparare"; used in compound tenses (e.g., passato prossimo) and sometimes as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho preparato la cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prepared dinner.

definitions.note: Often used to mean someone is well-prepared (e.g., has studied) or well-trained.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono preparato per l’esame di domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m prepared for tomorrow’s exam.

definitions.note: Depending on context, it can mean “you prepare” (present indicative) or “that I/you/he/she prepare” (present subjunctive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che tu prepari la cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you prepare dinner.

definitions.note: Can be present tense (“we prepare”) or the informal imperative (“let’s prepare”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prepariamo la cena insieme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We prepare dinner together.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person singular (he/she/it prepared).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri sera preparò la cena per tutti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night he/she prepared dinner for everyone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In italiano, “di” è una preposizione molto comune.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In Italian, “di” is a very common preposition.

definitions.note: Often used for someone who abuses their power or pushes others around.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non essere così prepotente con tua sorella.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t be so bossy with your sister.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "prendere"; often used with "essere" (e.g., "è stata presa")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La decisione è stata presa ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The decision was made yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dov’è la presa per caricare il telefono?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Where is the outlet to charge the phone?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La presa sul manubrio è comoda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The grip on the handlebar is comfortable.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) form of "prendere" (he/she/it took).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri Maria prese il treno alle otto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday Maria took the train at eight.

definitions.note: Often used for introducing a person or presenting something formally.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti presento la mia amica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I introduce you to my friend.

definitions.note: Reflexive: it’s used when you say your name or introduce yourself to someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Piacere, mi presento: sono Luca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Nice to meet you, I’m Luca.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si è presentato in ufficio senza appuntamento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He showed up at the office without an appointment.

definitions.native: to introduce you, to present you
definitions.note: Includes the object pronoun “ti” (“you”, informal singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio presentarti mia sorella.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to introduce you to my sister.

definitions.note: Includes the clitic pronoun “vi” (= to you, plural or formal). Often used to introduce someone to a group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo presentarvi mia sorella.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to introduce you to my sister.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "presentare"; often used with "essere" or in the passive (e.g., "è stata presentata")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Maria è stata presentata al direttore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Maria was introduced to the director.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho presentato Marco ai miei genitori.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I introduced Marco to my parents.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani ho una presentazione in classe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I have a presentation in class.

definitions.note: Often used to mean someone is in attendance (physically present).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono presente alla riunione di oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m present at today’s meeting.

definitions.note: Used as the present subjunctive (che io/tu/lui-lei presenti) and also as the formal imperative (Lei presenti).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È importante che tu presenti Marco ai tuoi genitori.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that you introduce Marco to your parents.

definitions.note: Plural form of "presente"; often used to mean "in attendance" (e.g., at a meeting or in class).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tutti gli studenti sono presenti oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: All the students are present today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho un presentimento: qualcosa andrà storto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a premonition: something will go wrong.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti presento Marco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let me introduce you to Marco.

definitions.note: past historic (passato remoto), he/she/it form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il direttore presentò il nuovo insegnante alla classe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The principal introduced the new teacher to the class.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La tua presenza mi fa piacere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your presence makes me happy.

definitions.note: past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person plural (they) of "prendere"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I bambini presero il treno alle sei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children took the train at six.

definitions.note: Common everyday term; can also mean “preservative” in some contexts, but that’s less common for beginners.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hai un preservativo?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have a condom?

definitions.note: Passato remoto of "prendere" (1st person singular), common in written Italian and storytelling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Presi l'autobus e arrivai in tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I took the bus and arrived on time.

definitions.note: Masculine plural past participle of "prendere" (e.g., "li ho presi" = "I took them").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho presi i biglietti e li ho messi in tasca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I took the tickets and put them in my pocket.

definitions.note: Used for the person in charge of an Italian school (especially middle or high school).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il preside parla con i genitori dopo la riunione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The principal talks with the parents after the meeting.

definitions.note: Used for the head of a country or an organization (e.g., a club, company, or association).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il presidente parlerà in TV questa sera.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui promette di chiamarti domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He promises to call you tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un progetto promettente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a promising project.

definitions.note: Infinitive with the indirect object pronoun “mi” attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi promettermi che verrai domani?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you promise me that you’ll come tomorrow?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te lo prometterò domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will promise you tomorrow.

definitions.note: Second person singular (tu) present tense of "promettere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prometti che mi chiami stasera?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you promise you'll call me tonight?

definitions.note: Present tense (io).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te lo prometto: domani arrivo in tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I promise you: tomorrow I’ll arrive on time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui promise di arrivare in orario.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He promised to arrive on time.

definitions.note: Passato remoto (simple past) of "promettere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Promisero di chiamarmi il giorno dopo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They promised to call me the next day.

definitions.note: simple past (passato remoto), often used in narratives and in some regions of Italy
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti promisi che sarei tornato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I promised you that I would come back.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of "promuovere"; often used with "essere" (e.g., "sono stata promossa").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono stata promossa ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was promoted yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Marco è stato promosso a responsabile del team.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Marco was promoted to team leader.

definitions.note: Commonly used at school to mean a student has passed and moves on to the next grade.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Luca è stato promosso in seconda media.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Luca passed and moved on to the second year of middle school.

definitions.note: Often used for a special offer or discount in shops, as well as for being promoted at work.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'è una promozione sui biglietti del treno questo weekend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There's a promotion (special offer) on train tickets this weekend.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "pronto".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono pronta a partire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m ready to leave.

definitions.note: feminine plural form of "pronto"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le valigie sono pronte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The suitcases are ready.

definitions.note: masculine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siete pronti a partire?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you ready to leave?

definitions.note: Also commonly used on the phone to mean “hello?” (answering a call).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono pronto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m ready.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La pronuncia di questa parola è difficile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pronunciation of this word is difficult.

definitions.note: Can be used as present tense (he/she/it pronounces) or as the informal command (you: pronounce!).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei pronuncia correttamente il tuo nome.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She pronounces your name correctly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi pronunciare questa parola più lentamente?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you pronounce this word more slowly?

definitions.note: Often used in more formal contexts, especially for delivering a speech or making an official statement.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il presidente pronuncerà un discorso domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The president will give a speech tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non credere a quella propaganda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t believe that propaganda.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei propone di andare al cinema stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She suggests going to the cinema tonight.

definitions.note: second-person plural (“you” plural) form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Che cosa proponete per stasera?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What do you propose for tonight?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Propongo di andare al cinema stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I suggest going to the movies tonight.

definitions.note: Informal (used with tu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Che cosa proponi per stasera?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What do you suggest for tonight?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho una proposta per te.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a proposal for you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho proposto un'idea nuova durante la riunione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I proposed a new idea during the meeting.

definitions.note: masculine plural form; agrees with a masculine plural noun (e.g., "i propri" + noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ognuno deve rispettare i propri impegni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Everyone has to respect their own commitments.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "proprio"; used to mean "one’s own" and agrees with a feminine singular noun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha la propria stanza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has her own room.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of "proprio"; it agrees with the noun it refers to and often adds emphasis (like “one’s own”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha la propria stanza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has her own room.

definitions.note: Used as a possessive adjective meaning “one’s own”; it agrees with feminine plural nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ognuno deve rispettare le proprie regole.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Everyone must respect their own rules.

definitions.note: feminine plural form; used with a feminine plural noun (e.g., "le proprie idee").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha le proprie idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has her own ideas.

definitions.note: feminine form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La proprietaria dell’appartamento vive al piano di sotto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The owner of the apartment lives on the floor below.

definitions.note: Often refers to the person who owns a property (house/apartment), i.e., a landlord in rental contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il proprietario dell'appartamento vive al piano di sopra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The owner of the apartment lives upstairs.

definitions.note: Can mean property in general (something owned) or a piece of real estate, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa casa è una mia proprietà.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This house is my property.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La trasparenza è una proprietà del vetro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Transparency is a property of glass.

definitions.note: Often used with a possessive meaning (e.g., "la mia propria casa" = "my own house").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio una stanza tutta mia, proprio mia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want a room all to myself, my very own.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È proprio quello che volevo dire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s exactly what I wanted to say.

definitions.note: Used to emphasize what you’re saying (similar to “really”/“truly”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi dispiace proprio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m really sorry.

definitions.note: Used to show possession or that something belongs to the subject (often with a reflexive meaning, like “his/her/their own”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ognuno ha la propria opinione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Everyone has their own opinion.

definitions.note: In Italy it often refers specifically to cured ham (e.g., prosciutto crudo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei un panino con prosciutto e formaggio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like a sandwich with ham and cheese.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo una breve pausa, possiamo proseguire con la lezione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After a short break, we can continue with the lesson.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da questa prospettiva, il problema sembra più semplice.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: From this perspective, the problem seems simpler.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le prospettive di lavoro sono buone quest'anno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The job outlook is good this year.

definitions.note: Plural of "prospettiva"; often used for future possibilities or expectations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le prospettive per il prossimo anno sono buone.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The prospects for next year are good.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of "prossimo"; often used with feminine nouns (e.g., settimana, volta).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La prossima settimana vado a Roma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Next week I’m going to Rome.

definitions.note: plural masculine form of "prossimo"; used with masculine plural nouns
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci vediamo nei prossimi giorni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’ll see each other in the next few days.

definitions.note: Often used for the next in time (e.g., next week) or the nearest in a sequence.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La prossima fermata è Piazza Roma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The next stop is Piazza Roma.

definitions.note: Can describe something physically nearest or figuratively closest.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La farmacia più prossima è a due isolati da qui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The nearest pharmacy is two blocks from here.

definitions.note: Often used as in "il prossimo" meaning other people/one’s neighbor (in the moral sense).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dobbiamo aiutare il prossimo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We must help our neighbor (others).

definitions.note: Used to refer to the next person/thing in a sequence (often with an article: "il prossimo").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il prossimo, per favore!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Next one, please!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La polizia ha arrestato un uomo che sfruttava una prostituta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police arrested a man who was exploiting a prostitute.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In quella zona ci sono molte prostitute.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In that area there are many prostitutes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il protagonista del film è un detective.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The protagonist of the movie is a detective.

definitions.note: Used in the present subjunctive (e.g., after expressions of desire/necessity like “è importante che…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È importante che la legge protegga i bambini.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that the law protect children.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo cappotto protegge dal freddo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This coat protects from the cold.

definitions.note: present gerund (used like “while …-ing” / “by …-ing”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto proteggendo i miei occhi dal sole.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m protecting my eyes from the sun.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dobbiamo proteggere l'ambiente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to protect the environment.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “la” (= “her/it”, feminine singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo proteggerla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to protect her.

definitions.note: Includes the direct-object pronoun “le” = “them” (feminine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dobbiamo proteggerle dai pericoli.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to protect them from dangers.

definitions.note: Infinitive + direct object pronoun “li” (= them, masculine plural or mixed group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È importante proteggerli dal freddo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important to protect them from the cold.

definitions.native: to protect it, to protect him
definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “lo” (= it/him, masculine singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dobbiamo proteggerlo prima che sia troppo tardi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to protect him before it’s too late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devi proteggermi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to protect me.

definitions.note: reflexive form (used when the subject protects themselves)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È importante proteggersi dal sole.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important to protect yourself from the sun.

definitions.note: Includes the attached pronoun “-ti” = “you” (informal, singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo proteggerti da questo rischio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to protect you from this risk.

definitions.note: Includes the pronoun “vi” = “you” (plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Farò di tutto per proteggervi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll do everything to protect you.

definitions.note: Reflexive use: “vi” can mean “yourselves.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dovete proteggervi dal sole.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You need to protect yourselves from the sun.

definitions.note: Third-person singular future tense (he/she/it will protect).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il casco ti proteggerà la testa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The helmet will protect your head.

definitions.note: Used mainly in scientific/nutrition contexts; often in phrases like “apporto proteico” (protein intake).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo alimento ha un alto contenuto proteico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This food has a high protein content.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le proteine sono importanti per i muscoli.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Proteins are important for muscles.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La mia famiglia è protestante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My family is Protestant.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Molte persone sono scese in piazza per protestare contro la nuova legge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many people took to the streets to protest against the new law.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo protestato contro la nuova legge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We protested against the new law.

definitions.note: plural form of "protesta"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono state molte proteste in città.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There were many protests in the city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando hanno aumentato i prezzi, lui protestò subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When they raised the prices, he protested immediately.

definitions.note: past participle of "proteggere"; often used with "essere" in the passive
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il bambino è protetto dai suoi genitori.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The child is protected by his parents.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Indossare il casco offre una buona protezione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wearing a helmet offers good protection.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani ho una prova di matematica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I have a math test.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hai una prova che lui era lì?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have proof that he was there?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui prova a chiamarti più tardi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tries to call you later.

definitions.note: often used as the informal (tu) imperative: “Try!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prova questo piatto, è buonissimo!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Try this dish, it’s really good!

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) form of “provare”; common in narratives and in some regions for past events.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Provai a chiamarti ieri sera, ma non rispondevi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I tried to call you last night, but you weren’t answering.

definitions.note: Informal (tu) imperative with a direct object pronoun: la (“it”, usually feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non sai se ti piace? Provala!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You don’t know if you like it? Try it!

definitions.note: Past tense (passato remoto), 1st person plural of "provare"; common in writing and in some regions in speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri provammo a chiamarti, ma non rispondevi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday we tried to call you, but you weren’t answering.

definitions.note: Often used with "stare" to mean "I am trying..." (e.g., "sto provando a..."). It can look like English "proving," but it usually means "trying."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto provando a chiamarti da mezz’ora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve been trying to call you for half an hour.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Provano a chiamarti più tardi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They try to call you later.

definitions.note: Often used for clothes (e.g., in a shop).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In negozio provano due giacche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the shop they try on two jackets.

definitions.note: Often used with "ci" to mean trying to do something ("to try at it").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci provo domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'll try tomorrow.

definitions.native: hit on (someone), try it on (with someone)
definitions.note: In informal speech, it can mean flirting with someone or making a move.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sta provando con lei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He's hitting on her.

definitions.native: try (to do it), give it a try
definitions.note: Often used with the idea of making an effort to succeed at something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non sono sicuro, ma posso provarci.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm not sure, but I can try.

definitions.note: Informal; used when someone tries to flirt or make a romantic/sexual advance.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui ci prova sempre con tutte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s always hitting on everyone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio provare a cucinare la pasta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to try to cook pasta.

definitions.note: Often used for tasting food or wine (e.g., “provare un vino”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vuoi provare questo formaggio?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you want to taste this cheese?

definitions.note: Used for trying on clothes (e.g., “provare una giacca”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Posso provare questa camicia?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can I try on this shirt?

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “la” (= it/her, feminine). Often used for food, clothes, or an idea.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vuoi provarla?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you want to try it?

definitions.note: Can look like English “prove,” but it usually means “try” (e.g., try something out).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio provarlo prima di comprarlo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to try it before buying it.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) form; often used in stories and in some regions (especially Southern Italy) instead of the passato prossimo.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Provarono a chiamarmi, ma non risposi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They tried to call me, but I didn’t answer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Provate a chiamarmi più tardi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Try calling me later.

definitions.note: In Italian, provare can also mean “to prove” in the sense of demonstrating something is true.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Provate che avevate ragione.
