definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Prove that you were right.

definitions.note: Plural masculine past participle of "provare"; often used with "avere" (e.g., "abbiamo provati") when referring to masculine plural objects.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Li abbiamo provati ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We tried them yesterday.

definitions.note: past participle of "provare"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho provato questa app ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I tried this app yesterday.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense; often describes an ongoing or repeated action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Provava a chiamarti, ma il telefono era spento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/she was trying to call you, but the phone was off.

definitions.note: imperfect tense (past ongoing/habitual)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Provavo a chiamarti, ma non rispondevi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was trying to call you, but you weren’t answering.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non ci sono prove sufficienti per accusarlo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There isn’t enough evidence to accuse him.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani ho due prove a scuola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I have two tests at school.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they) of “provenire”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Queste informazioni provengono da una fonte affidabile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This information comes from a reliable source.

definitions.note: Third-person singular simple future of "provare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani proverà a chiamarti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow he/she will try to call you.

definitions.note: First-person singular future tense of "provare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani proverò a chiamarti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will try to call you.

definitions.note: Often used with implied "tu". It can also be used as the formal imperative with "Lei" (e.g., "Provi!" = "Try!").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se provi, puoi farcela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you try, you can do it.

definitions.note: Can be present indicative (“we try”) or an informal imperative invitation (“let’s try”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Proviamo a parlare in italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s try to speak in Italian.

definitions.note: Often used with "a" + infinitive (e.g., "provo a...": "I try to..."). It looks like English "prove" but usually means "try".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Provo a chiamarti più tardi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll try to call you later.

definitions.note: Used for emotions or sensations (e.g., "provo gioia": "I feel joy").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Provo molta paura.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel a lot of fear.

definitions.note: Past participle of “provocare”; can also be used as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi ha provocato davanti a tutti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She provoked me in front of everyone.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person singular: “he/she/it caused.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quel commento provocò una discussione accesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That comment caused a heated discussion.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo comprato le provviste per il viaggio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We bought supplies for the trip.

definitions.note: Often used with “a” + infinitive (e.g., “provò a…” = “tried to…”). It can also mean “tested” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri provò a chiamarmi, ma non risposi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday he/she tried to call me, but I didn’t answer.

definitions.note: From the verb "prudere" (to itch). Not related to the English word "prude".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi prude la pelle dopo la doccia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My skin itches after the shower.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sii prudente quando attraversi la strada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Be cautious when you cross the street.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo prudenti quando guidiamo di notte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are careful when we drive at night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guida con prudenza quando piove.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Drive with caution when it rains.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compro le prugne al mercato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I buy plums at the market.

definitions.note: Often used in medical or formal contexts (the everyday word is commonly "prurito" too, but people may also say "prude" for an itch).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho prurito al braccio da ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My arm has been itching since yesterday.

definitions.note: a medical doctor who specializes in mental health
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo psichiatra mi ha consigliato una terapia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The psychiatrist recommended a therapy to me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Studio psicologia all'università.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I study psychology at university.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo stress psicologico può influenzare il sonno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Psychological stress can affect sleep.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo psicologo mi ha aiutato a gestire lo stress.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The psychologist helped me manage stress.

definitions.note: Often used as an insult in everyday speech; in clinical contexts, wording may differ.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non parlare con lui: è uno psicopatico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t talk to him: he’s a psychopath.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci vediamo al pub dopo il lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: See you at the pub after work.

definitions.note: feminine singular form (agrees with a feminine noun)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa biblioteca è pubblica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This library is public.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La casa editrice vuole pubblicare il suo nuovo romanzo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The publishing house wants to publish his/her new novel.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il libro è stato pubblicato nel 2020.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book was published in 2020.

definitions.note: plural masculine form of "pubblico".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I giardini pubblici sono aperti fino alle 20:00.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The public gardens are open until 8:00 p.m.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho visto una pubblicità in TV.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw an advertisement on TV.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un parco pubblico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a public park.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il pubblico applaude alla fine dello spettacolo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The audience applauds at the end of the show.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il museo è aperto al pubblico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The museum is open to the public.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto), 3rd-person singular (he/she/it published).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nel 1998 pubblicò il suo primo romanzo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In 1998, he/she published his/her first novel.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio fratello pratica il pugilato due volte a settimana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother practices boxing twice a week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio fratello è un pugile professionista.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is a professional boxer.

definitions.note: Past participle (feminine singular) of "pugnalare"; it agrees with a feminine direct object (e.g., "l'ha pugnalata" = "he/she stabbed her").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'ha pugnalata in strada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She stabbed her in the street.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'uomo è stato pugnalato davanti al supermercato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The man was stabbed in front of the supermarket.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Durante la lite, lo pugnalò con un coltello.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: During the argument, he stabbed him with a knife.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha alzato i pugni per difendersi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He raised his fists to defend himself.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha chiuso la mano a pugno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He closed his hand into a fist.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi ha dato un pugno nello stomaco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gave me a punch in the stomach.

definitions.note: gerund ("-ing" form), often meaning "while cleaning" or "by cleaning"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto pulendo la cucina adesso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m cleaning the kitchen right now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo pulire la cucina prima di cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to clean the kitchen before dinner.

definitions.note: Used in the present subjunctive (e.g., after expressions like “è importante che...”), and also as a formal command (Lei).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È importante che pulisca la cucina oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that he/she/you (formal) clean the kitchen today.

definitions.note: Present tense (also used for the near future).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui pulisce la cucina ogni sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He cleans the kitchen every evening.

definitions.note: Informal (tu) form; can be used as “you clean” (present) or as the command “clean!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pulisci la tua stanza, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Clean your room, please.

definitions.note: Present indicative, 1st person singular of "pulire".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pulisco la cucina dopo cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I clean the kitchen after dinner.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form of "pulire" (can be 1st or 3rd person singular). Often used after past verbs or in hypothetical "se" (if) clauses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se lui pulisse la cucina, potremmo cenare subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If he were to clean the kitchen, we could have dinner right away.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La cucina è pulita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kitchen is clean.

definitions.note: Second-person plural form (“you all”); can be present tense (“you clean”) or an imperative (“clean!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pulite la cucina, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Clean the kitchen, please.

definitions.note: feminine plural form of the adjective
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le camere sono pulite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rooms are clean.

definitions.note: masculine plural form of the adjective
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I piatti sono puliti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dishes are clean.

definitions.note: Past participle of "pulire". It may look like English "polite", but it means "clean(ed)".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho pulito la cucina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I cleaned the kitchen.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il bagno è pulito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bathroom is clean.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani faccio la pulizia della cucina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I’m doing the cleaning of the kitchen.

definitions.note: Plural; often used for cleaning work/services (e.g., house cleaning).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Faccio le pulizie il sabato mattina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I do the cleaning on Saturday morning.

definitions.note: In Italian, pullman commonly means a coach/long-distance bus (not a train car).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Andiamo a Roma in pullman.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to Rome by coach.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Premi il pulsante rosso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Press the red button.

definitions.note: simple past (passato remoto), 3rd person singular
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri sera pulì la cucina prima di uscire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night, he/she cleaned the kitchen before going out.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non è giusto punire tutti per l’errore di uno solo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It isn’t fair to punish everyone for one person’s mistake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei è stata punita per aver copiato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was punished for copying.

definitions.note: past participle of "punire"; also used as masculine plural adjective meaning "punished"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I ragazzi sono stati puniti per il ritardo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boys were punished for being late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È stato punito per aver copiato durante l’esame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was punished for copying during the exam.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La punizione è stata troppo severa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The punishment was too harsh.

definitions.note: Usually refers to the punk music/culture scene or a person associated with it.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio fratello ascolta musica punk.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother listens to punk music.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La punta della matita si è rotta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tip of the pencil broke.

definitions.note: Gerund form of "puntare"; used for actions in progress ("while aiming/pointing").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sta puntando la torcia verso la porta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She is pointing the flashlight toward the door.

definitions.note: Often used with "a" (e.g., "puntare a" = to aim for, target).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha puntato il dito contro di me.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He pointed his finger at me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devi controllare la punteggiatura prima di consegnare il testo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to check the punctuation before handing in the text.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Qual è il punteggio finale della partita?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is the final score of the game?

definitions.note: plural of "punto".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho preso dieci punti al test.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got ten points on the test.

definitions.note: Used especially in the phrase "punti di sutura" (stitches).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il medico mi ha messo tre punti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor gave me three stitches.

definitions.note: From the verb “puntare” (to aim/point).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Punto a vincere questa partita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m aiming to win this match.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Metti un punto alla fine della frase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put a period at the end of the sentence.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La nostra squadra ha fatto tre punti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our team scored three points.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'autobus oggi è puntuale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus is on time today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Apprezzo molto la tua puntualità.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I really appreciate your punctuality.

definitions.note: Often used for insect stings/bites (e.g., mosquito, bee).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho una puntura di zanzara sul braccio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a mosquito bite on my arm.

definitions.note: Commonly used for medical injections (e.g., a vaccine shot).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani devo fare una puntura.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I have to get an injection.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il giudice punì l’uomo per il crimine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The judge punished the man for the crime.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu, informal); used to express ability or ask/give permission.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi aiutarmi con questo esercizio?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you help me with this exercise?

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (tu) present tense of “potere”; used to ask for permission or ability.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi aiutarmi, per favore?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you help me, please?

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of “puro”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bevo solo acqua pura.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I drink only pure water.

definitions.note: Often used in spoken Italian; it can also mean “even” in some contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vengo pure io.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m coming too.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a member of the Puritan religious movement; can also describe someone with very strict moral views.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I puritani erano molto severi nelle regole morali.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Puritans were very strict in their moral rules.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bevo solo acqua pura.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I only drink pure water.

definitions.note: Used to emphasize that something is nothing more than what is stated (e.g., “pure luck”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È stata pura fortuna.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was sheer luck.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Purtroppo oggi piove e non possiamo uscire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Unfortunately, it’s raining today and we can’t go out.

definitions.note: In everyday Italian, purè most often refers to mashed potatoes (purè di patate).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per cena mangiamo il purè con la carne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For dinner we’re having mashed potatoes with meat.

definitions.note: Golf term (loanword from English).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho sbagliato un putt facile alla buca 18.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I missed an easy putt on the 18th hole.

definitions.note: Very vulgar/offensive word; avoid in polite conversation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha insultato quella donna chiamandola "puttana".
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He insulted that woman by calling her a “whore.”

definitions.note: Very vulgar insult; often used to offend or demean someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non chiamarmi puttana!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t call me a bitch!

definitions.note: Informal/colloquial.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Che puzza in cucina!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What a stink in the kitchen!

definitions.note: Commonly used for unpleasant smells; can also be used figuratively (e.g., something “stinks” meaning it seems suspicious).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Qui puzza di fumo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It smells like smoke in here.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le scarpe puzzano dopo la partita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The shoes stink after the match.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (past) form; describes an ongoing or habitual situation in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando siamo entrati, la stanza puzzava di fumo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When we came in, the room stank of smoke.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In questa stanza ci sono puzzi terribili.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this room there are terrible smells.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Facciamo un puzzle da 500 pezzi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s do a 500-piece puzzle.

definitions.note: Modal auxiliary used with an infinitive to express ability or permission.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui può venire domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He can come tomorrow.

definitions.note: Third-person singular present of "potere"; used for both "he/she/it can" and the formal "you can" (Lei).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Può venire domani?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you come tomorrow?

definitions.note: This form is normally spelled “può” in standard Italian.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puó venire domani?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you come tomorrow?

definitions.note: Often used as a modal auxiliary before another verb (e.g. “può + infinitive”). With “Lei” (formal ‘you’), it can mean ‘you can/may’.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Può venire domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She can come tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used in speech; similar to "qui".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Metti la borsa qua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put the bag here.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato due quaderni per la scuola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought two notebooks for school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho dimenticato il quaderno a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I forgot the notebook at home.

definitions.note: Often used for a framed artwork you hang on a wall.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'è un quadro bellissimo in soggiorno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a beautiful painting in the living room.

definitions.note: Used in expressions like "quadro generale" (general framework/overview).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo bisogno di un quadro generale della situazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need an overall framework of the situation.

definitions.note: More emphatic/literary than the common "qui" (here).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quaggiù fa più freddo che lassù.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Down here it’s colder than up there.

definitions.note: Poetic/literary short form of “quale”; also used in set phrases like “qual è…?”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Qual è il tuo numero di telefono?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is your phone number?

definitions.note: Used with a singular noun in Italian (e.g. "qualche giorno").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho qualche domanda per te.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have some questions for you.

definitions.note: Often used with a following adjective or clause (e.g., “qualcosa di + adjective”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei qualcosa da bere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like something to drink.

definitions.note: feminine singular form (used when referring to a female person or a feminine noun like “persona”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho bisogno di parlare con qualcuna del team.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to talk to someone on the team.

definitions.note: Often means “someone/somebody”; in questions it can also mean “anyone,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'è qualcuno alla porta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There's someone at the door.

definitions.note: Used in questions (often with a noun) and in relative clauses (“the one which/that”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quale libro preferisci?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Which book do you prefer?

definitions.note: Used in questions or to choose among options; it agrees in number: quale (singular), quali (plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quale preferisci, il tè o il caffè?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Which do you prefer, tea or coffee?

definitions.note: Plural form (used with plural nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quali libri vuoi leggere?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Which books do you want to read?

definitions.note: plural form of “quale”; used in questions or relative clauses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quali libri preferisci?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Which books do you prefer?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un tecnico qualificato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s a qualified technician.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per questo lavoro servono qualifiche specifiche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For this job, specific qualifications are required.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo prodotto ha un’ottima qualità.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This product has excellent quality.

definitions.note: Used before a singular noun to mean “any” in a general sense (e.g., “any day/any book”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi scegliere qualsiasi libro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can choose any book.

definitions.note: used before a noun to mean it doesn’t matter which one; agrees in gender/number like an invariable form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi scegliere qualunque libro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can choose any book.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando arrivi?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When are you arriving?

definitions.note: Can also mean “whenever” in some contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando arrivi, chiamami.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When you arrive, call me.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "quanto"; used with feminine singular nouns (e.g., "acqua", "pazienza").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quanta acqua vuoi?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How much water do you want?

definitions.note: feminine plural form of “quanto”; used with feminine plural nouns
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quante persone ci sono alla festa?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How many people are there at the party?

definitions.note: feminine plural form (used with feminine plural nouns or referring to feminine plural things)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quante ne vuoi?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How many do you want?

definitions.note: feminine plural form (used to mean ‘as many as’ when referring to feminine plural things)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prendine quante ti servono.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take as many as you need.

definitions.note: masculine plural form; used with masculine plural nouns or as a pronoun referring to a masculine plural group
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quanti libri hai?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How many books do you have?

definitions.note: plural form, used with masculine plural nouns
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quanti studenti ci sono in classe?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How many students are there in the class?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei una piccola quantità di zucchero, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like a small amount of sugar, please.

definitions.note: Used in questions and exclamations, often with prices or amounts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quanto costa questo libro?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How much does this book cost?

definitions.note: Often used in comparisons/correlations like “quanto più…, tanto più…”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quanto più studio, tanto più capisco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The more I study, the more I understand.

definitions.note: Interrogative determiner; agrees in gender and number with the noun (quanto/quanta/quanti/quante).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quanto tempo hai?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How much time do you have?

definitions.note: Used with "quanto" in comparisons (e.g., "tanto ... quanto" = "as ... as").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho tanti libri quanti ne hai tu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have as many books as you do.

definitions.note: Used in questions and exclamations; agrees in gender/number with the noun it refers to (quanto/quanta/quanti/quante).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quanto costa questo libro?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How much does this book cost?

definitions.native: as much as, what, that which
definitions.note: Can be used as a relative pronoun meaning “what/that which” or “as much as.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho fatto quanto potevo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I did what I could.

definitions.native: as much as, as far as
definitions.note: Used to introduce a comparison or limit (often in the pattern “tanto ... quanto ...”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti aiuto quanto posso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll help you as much as I can.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho quaranta anni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am forty years old.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo il viaggio, ho fatto una quarantena di dieci giorni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the trip, I did a ten-day quarantine.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abito in un quartiere tranquillo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I live in a quiet neighborhood.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È il quarto giorno di viaggio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s the fourth day of the trip.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La mia camera è al quarto piano, ma il quarto è molto silenzioso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My bedroom is on the fourth floor, but the room is very quiet.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho mangiato solo un quarto della pizza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ate only a quarter of the pizza.

definitions.note: Often used with an article (il quarto) to mean ‘the fourth’ in order/position.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo arrivati al quarto posto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We came in fourth place.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono quasi pronto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m almost ready.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho quattordici anni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am fourteen years old.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho quattro fratelli.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have four brothers.

definitions.note: masculine plural form used before nouns starting with s + consonant, z, gn, ps, pn, x, or y (e.g., quegli studenti)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quegli studenti sono in ritardo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those students are late.

definitions.note: masculine plural form of "quello" used before most consonant sounds
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quei ragazzi sono molto simpatici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those boys are very nice.

definitions.note: Demonstrative determiner meaning “that”; used before a masculine singular noun starting with most consonants (e.g., quel libro, quel cane).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quel libro è interessante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That book is interesting.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of “quello”; used before feminine singular nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi piace quella casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like that house.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "quello"; used for a feminine noun or a female person/thing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preferisco quella vicino alla finestra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prefer that one near the window.

definitions.note: feminine plural form of "quello"; used before a noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quelle scarpe sono nuove.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those shoes are new.

definitions.note: feminine plural demonstrative pronoun (refers to feminine plural nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preferisco quelle, non queste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prefer those, not these.

definitions.note: plural masculine form of "quello"; used for groups of males or mixed gender
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quelli sono i miei amici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those are my friends.

definitions.note: demonstrative determiner; agrees in gender and number with the noun it refers to
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preferisco quello zaino blu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prefer that blue backpack.

definitions.note: Demonstrative pronoun, often contrasted with "questo" (this one).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preferisco quello.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prefer that one.

definitions.note: Not standard Italian spelling; likely a typo for “questa” (feminine singular of “questo”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quesra è la mia borsa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is my bag.

definitions.note: This form is not standard Italian; it’s likely a misspelling of “questo”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hai scritto "quesro" invece di "questo".
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You wrote "quesro" instead of "questo".

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "questo"; used before feminine singular nouns
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa casa è molto bella.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This house is very beautiful.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa è la mia amica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is my friend.

definitions.note: feminine plural form of "questo"; used before feminine plural nouns
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Queste scarpe sono nuove.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These shoes are new.

definitions.note: feminine plural form of “questo” (used with feminine plural nouns or as a pronoun)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preferisco queste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prefer these.

definitions.note: plural masculine form of "questo"; used before a masculine plural noun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questi libri sono interessanti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These books are interesting.

definitions.note: masculine plural form of "questo"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questi sono i miei amici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These are my friends.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una questione importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s an important issue.

definitions.note: Plural of "questione"; often means a matter/problem to discuss or solve.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dobbiamo risolvere alcune questioni prima di partire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to sort out a few issues before leaving.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo libro è interessante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book is interesting.

definitions.note: Demonstrative pronoun used to refer to something close to the speaker (masculine singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo è il mio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This one is mine.

definitions.note: refers to this place (where the speaker is)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Resta qui con me.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stay here with me.

definitions.note: Often used to introduce a conclusion or result; it can also be used in speech like “so…” to move the conversation forward.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non ho studiato, quindi ho preso un brutto voto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn’t study, so I got a bad grade.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho quindici anni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am fifteen years old.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo è il quinto capitolo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is the fifth chapter.

definitions.note: Often used for an assigned limit or allotment (e.g., a sales quota), or for someone’s share (quota) of a cost.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo raggiunto la quota di vendita questo mese.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We reached the sales quota this month.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La mia routine quotidiana inizia alle sette.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My daily routine starts at seven.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho rabbia per quello che è successo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m angry about what happened.

definitions.note: Medical term (a disease).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il cane ha la rabbia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog has rabies.

definitions.note: Usually a sports racket (e.g., tennis, badminton).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato una nuova racchetta da tennis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a new tennis racket.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) present tense of "raccogliere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Raccogli le foglie dal prato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You pick up the leaves from the lawn.

definitions.note: gerund form ("-ing"), often used to mean "while picking up/collecting".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto raccogliendo le foglie in giardino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m picking up the leaves in the garden.

definitions.note: Often used for physically gathering things (e.g., from the ground) or collecting items in one place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi raccogliere i tuoi libri da terra?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you pick up your books from the floor?

definitions.note: Used for gathering crops or fruit when they are ready.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In autunno raccogliamo le mele.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In autumn we harvest the apples.

definitions.note: 2nd person plural form ("you all"); it can be used as a present tense form or as a command (imperative), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per favore, raccogliete i vostri rifiuti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please pick up your trash.

definitions.note: Used in the present subjunctive (e.g., after expressions like “spero che…”) and also as the formal (Lei) imperative.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che lei raccolga tutti i documenti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope she collects all the documents.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto) form; common in narratives and in some regions, often corresponding to English simple past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Raccolse le chiavi da terra e uscì.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He picked up the keys from the ground and left.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto), third-person plural: “they …” (often used in stories and historical narration).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alla fine della giornata raccolsero le foglie nel giardino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the end of the day they collected the leaves in the garden.

definitions.native: I gathered, I collected, I picked up
definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 1st person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Raccolsi le chiavi da terra e tornai a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I picked up the keys from the ground and went home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I raccolti sono stati abbondanti quest'anno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The harvests were plentiful this year.

definitions.note: Often used for collections of texts (e.g., poems, short stories).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho letto due raccolti di poesie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I read two collections of poems.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho raccolto le mele in giardino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I picked the apples in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quest'anno il raccolto di mele è stato abbondante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This year the apple harvest was abundant.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo ristorante mi è stato raccomandato da un amico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This restaurant was recommended to me by a friend.

definitions.note: Often used with mail: “posta/pacco raccomandato” = registered mail/parcel.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho spedito un pacco raccomandato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sent a registered parcel.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi serve una raccomandazione per questo ristorante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a recommendation for this restaurant.

definitions.note: third-person singular present ("he/she/it tells") or informal singular imperative ("tell!")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Racconta sempre storie divertenti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She always tells funny stories.

definitions.note: Informal command form with the pronoun “ci” (“us”) attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Raccontaci cosa è successo ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tell us what happened yesterday.

definitions.note: Informal (tu) command form with the pronoun mi (“to me”) attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Raccontami la tua giornata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tell me about your day.

definitions.note: Often used for telling a story or recounting events.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi puoi raccontare cosa è successo?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you tell me what happened?

definitions.note: Used when explaining something in words, often with details.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Racconta la tua giornata in poche parole.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Describe your day in a few words.

definitions.note: 2nd-person plural (voi) form with the pronoun “ci” (“us”); often used as an imperative.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Raccontateci cosa è successo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tell us what happened.

definitions.note: Imperative (plural “you”): said to more than one person. “-mi” means “to me.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Raccontatemi cosa è successo ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tell me what happened yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti ho raccontato tutto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I told you everything.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu racconti sempre la verità.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You always tell the truth.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti racconto tutto domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll tell you everything tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi piace leggere un racconto prima di dormire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like reading a story before going to sleep.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto), often used in stories and in writing for completed past actions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri sera mi raccontò tutta la storia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night he/she told me the whole story.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho raddoppiato la dose.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I doubled the dose.

definitions.note: Reflexive: means “to shave oneself.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi devo radermi prima di uscire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to shave before going out.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In inverno accendiamo il radiatore in camera da letto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In winter we turn on the radiator in the bedroom.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ascolto la radio ogni mattina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I listen to the radio every morning.

definitions.note: Often used for bread that is no longer fresh.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo pane è raffermo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This bread is stale.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto raffreddando la minestra prima di metterla in frigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m cooling the soup before putting it in the fridge.

definitions.note: Refers to the common cold (a mild illness), not cold temperature.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho preso il raffreddore e oggi resto a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I caught a cold and I’m staying home today.

definitions.note: often used for a young woman; can also mean “girlfriend” depending on context
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quella ragazza studia italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That girl studies Italian.

definitions.note: plural of "ragazza"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le ragazze sono in biblioteca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The girls are in the library.

definitions.note: Masculine plural of "ragazzo"; can also refer to a mixed group of boys and girls (like "guys" in English).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ragazzi, andiamo al parco!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Guys, let's go to the park!

definitions.note: Often refers to a girl in her early teens; can also be used affectionately.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quella ragazzina va a scuola in bicicletta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That girl goes to school by bike.

definitions.note: Diminutive form; often suggests a young age or a slightly informal/affectionate tone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La ragazzina gioca in giardino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The girl is playing in the garden.

definitions.note: Plural form; often refers to young boys or young teenagers in an informal, everyday way.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I ragazzini giocano a calcio nel parco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boys are playing soccer in the park.

definitions.note: Often implies a young age; can be slightly informal/affectionate depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quel ragazzino gioca al parco ogni pomeriggio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That little boy plays at the park every afternoon.

definitions.note: Often used informally to mean “guy” or “kid,” not only for a young boy.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quel ragazzo è molto simpatico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That boy is very nice.

definitions.note: third-person singular (he/she/it)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il treno raggiunge Roma alle 18:30.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train reaches Rome at 6:30 p.m.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo tre ore di cammino raggiungemmo il rifugio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After three hours of walking, we reached the shelter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Possiamo raggiungere la stazione a piedi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We can reach the station on foot.

definitions.note: Includes the attached pronoun "lo" (= him/it, masculine singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo raggiungerlo prima che parta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to reach him before he leaves.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Con i mezzi pubblici, questi luoghi sono facilmente raggiungibili.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With public transportation, these places are easily reachable.

definitions.note: past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person singular: “he/she/it reached”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Finalmente raggiunse la stazione in tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Finally, he reached the station in time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho raggiunto la stazione in dieci minuti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I reached the station in ten minutes.

definitions.note: Third-person singular present (he/she/it reasons/thinks).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui ragiona con calma prima di decidere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He thinks calmly before deciding.

definitions.note: Informal singular imperative (a command): “think!” / “use your head!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ragiona un momento: non è una buona idea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Think for a moment: it’s not a good idea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il tuo ragionamento è chiaro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your reasoning is clear.

definitions.note: Often used for thinking in a logical, step-by-step way.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prova a ragionare prima di rispondere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Try to think before answering.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non capisco la ragione del suo ritardo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t understand the reason for his delay.

definitions.note: Used in expressions like “avere ragione” (“to be right”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hai ragione: questa è la strada giusta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re right: this is the correct street.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi sembra una proposta ragionevole.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It seems like a reasonable proposal to me.

definitions.note: plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le tue richieste sono ragionevoli.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your requests are reasonable.

definitions.note: Plural of "ragione".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono molte ragioni per studiare l’italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many reasons to study Italian.

definitions.note: 1st person plural present of "ragionare"; it can mean "we ..." or be used like an encouragement: "let's ..."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ragioniamo un attimo prima di decidere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let's think for a moment before deciding.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'è una ragnatela nell'angolo del soffitto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a spiderweb in the corner of the ceiling.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In giardino ci sono molti ragni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many spiders in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'è un ragno in bagno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There’s a spider in the bathroom.

definitions.note: It can also be used as an informal command: “slow down!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il traffico rallenta vicino al ponte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Traffic slows down near the bridge.

definitions.note: Gerund of "rallentare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto rallentando perché c’è traffico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m slowing down because there’s traffic.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devi rallentare quando piove.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to slow down when it rains.

definitions.note: Used for "you (plural)" in the present tense or as a command.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Rallentate, per favore!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Slow down, please!

definitions.note: Feminine plural past participle (e.g., with "essere").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le auto sono rallentate a causa del traffico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cars slowed down because of traffic.

definitions.note: Often used as a formal command (to Lei) or as the present subjunctive of “rallentare.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Rallenti, per favore: c'è un pedone.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Slow down, please: there’s a pedestrian.

definitions.note: Loanword from Japanese; commonly refers to a Japanese noodle soup dish.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A pranzo mangio spesso il ramen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For lunch I often eat ramen.

definitions.note: Somewhat literary/old-fashioned.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Un ramingo bussò alla porta chiedendo un po’ d’acqua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A drifter knocked on the door asking for some water.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'è una rana nello stagno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a frog in the pond.

definitions.note: Used in Italian mainly as a loanword for an American-style cattle farm.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hanno comprato un ranch in Texas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They bought a ranch in Texas.

definitions.note: Often used for a lasting, bitter feeling from a past hurt or offense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non provo rancore, ma non dimentico quello che è successo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't feel resentment, but I don't forget what happened.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nel laghetto ci sono molte rane.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many frogs in the pond.

definitions.note: Often used for incoherent or confused speech, especially by someone who is ill or very old.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il paziente ha iniziato a rantolare parole senza senso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The patient started to ramble incoherent words.

definitions.note: Usually refers to the music genre (hip-hop/rap).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ascolto spesso il rap in macchina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I often listen to rap in the car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi compro due rape al mercato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I'm buying two turnips at the market.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of “rapido”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei è molto rapida a capire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very quick to understand.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo finire rapidamente questo lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to finish this work quickly.

definitions.note: plural masculine form of “rapido” (used with masculine plural nouns)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono studenti rapidi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are fast students.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un treno rapido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a fast train.

definitions.note: Often used for a robbery involving force or threat (e.g., a mugging or armed robbery).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’è stata una rapina in banca ieri sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There was a bank robbery last night.

definitions.note: past participle used with feminine singular nouns (e.g., "la banca")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La banca è stata rapinata ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bank was robbed yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono stato rapinato ieri sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was robbed last night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il bambino è stato rapito ieri sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The child was kidnapped last night.

definitions.note: Often used figuratively to mean being completely fascinated or absorbed.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ero rapito dalla musica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was captivated by the music.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La polizia sta cercando i rapitori.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police are looking for the kidnappers.

definitions.note: Plural of "rapporto"; often used for personal, social, or professional relationships.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho buoni rapporti con i miei vicini.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a good relationship with my neighbors.

definitions.note: Plural of "rapporto"; used for written reports (e.g., at work or school).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo consegnare due rapporti entro domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to hand in two reports by tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il rapporto tra i due fratelli è molto forte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The relationship between the two brothers is very strong.

definitions.note: Often used for a written report (for example, for work or school).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo finire il rapporto entro domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to finish the report by tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questi dati rappresentano la situazione attuale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These data represent the current situation.

definitions.note: Present tense, 1st person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Io rappresento la mia classe al consiglio degli studenti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I represent my class on the student council.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "raro".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una specie rara.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a rare species.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vado raramente al cinema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I rarely go to the cinema.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In questa zona ci sono rari uccelli migratori.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this area there are rare migratory birds.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un uccello raro in questa zona.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a rare bird in this area.

definitions.note: Often used as a past participle with "essere" (e.g., "mi sono rasato") to mean "I shaved"; it can also be used as an adjective meaning "clean-shaven."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi sono rasato stamattina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I shaved this morning.

definitions.note: usually used with "la barba" (the beard) or "le gambe" (the legs).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ogni mattina rasi la barba.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every morning you shave your beard.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono dei ratti nel seminterrato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are rats in the basement.

definitions.note: Commonly used in legal or news contexts (e.g., "ratto di persona").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La polizia ha arrestato due persone per ratto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police arrested two people for kidnapping.

definitions.note: Often used to mean a group of people or animals; for people, it can sound outdated or offensive depending on context, so be careful.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non esistono razze superiori o inferiori.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are no superior or inferior races.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo visto una razza nuotare vicino alla riva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We saw a stingray swimming near the shore.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dobbiamo combattere il razzismo in tutte le sue forme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We must fight racism in all its forms.
