definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to risk missing the train.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho rischiato tutto per aiutarti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I risked everything to help you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un rischio inutile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s an unnecessary risk.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È troppo rischioso guidare così veloce.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s too risky to drive that fast.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person singular (he/she/it).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Rischiò tutto per aiutare un amico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He risked everything to help a friend.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho riscritto la email per renderla più chiara.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I rewrote the email to make it clearer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo riscrivere il testo perché ci sono molti errori.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to rewrite the text because there are many mistakes.

definitions.note: Passato remoto (remote past), most common in written Italian and in some regions for completed actions in the distant past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando lo vide, rise e se ne andò.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he saw him, he laughed and walked away.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person plural: “they laughed”. Common in narratives and in some regions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando sentì la battuta, tutti risero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When they heard the joke, everyone laughed.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando lo vide cadere, risero tutti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When they saw him fall, they all laughed.

definitions.note: Often used to describe a person who is shy/quiet and doesn’t share much, or a situation/info that is confidential.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui è una persona molto riservata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a very reserved person.

definitions.note: Past participle of "ridere"; used with "avere" (e.g., "ho riso"). Not to be confused with the noun "riso" meaning "rice".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho riso molto durante il film.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I laughed a lot during the movie.

definitions.note: Used as the past participle of "ridere" (to laugh), e.g. in compound tenses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho riso tutta la sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I laughed all evening.

definitions.note: past participle used with avere (e.g., “ho riso” = “I laughed / I have laughed”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho riso molto ieri sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I laughed a lot last night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preferisco il riso alla pasta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prefer rice to pasta.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il suo riso era contagioso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His/Her laughter was contagious.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person singular; common in written narratives and some regions in speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo ore di lavoro, risolse il problema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After hours of work, he/she solved the problem.

definitions.note: Past participle (masculine plural) of "risolvere"; often used with "essere" or as an adjective to describe masculine plural nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I problemi sono finalmente risolti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The problems are finally solved.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho risolto il problema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I solved the problem.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei risolve il problema in pochi minuti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She solves the problem in a few minutes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dobbiamo risolvere questo problema subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to solve this problem right away.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani risolveremo questo problema insieme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will solve this problem together.

definitions.note: plural of "risorsa"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non abbiamo abbastanza risorse per finire il progetto oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We don't have enough resources to finish the project today.

definitions.note: Plural of "risparmio" (money you have saved).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I miei risparmi sono in banca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My savings are in the bank.

definitions.note: Imperative form meaning you ask someone not to make you do/suffer something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Risparmiami questa fatica, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Spare me this effort, please.

definitions.note: gerund form; often used to mean doing something while saving money or by saving money
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto risparmiando per comprare una macchina nuova.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m saving up to buy a new car.

definitions.note: Often used for saving money or resources; can also mean “to spare” (e.g., time, effort).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto cercando di risparmiare per un viaggio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to save for a trip.

definitions.note: Often used with money, time, or resources.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho risparmiato molti soldi questo mese.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saved a lot of money this month.

definitions.note: Used when someone avoids harm, effort, or an unpleasant experience.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hai risparmiato una lunga discussione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You spared me a long discussion.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto) of "risparmiare"; common in writing and in some regions, while everyday speech often uses passato prossimo.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'anno scorso risparmiò abbastanza soldi per comprare una macchina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last year he/she saved enough money to buy a car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il medico disse che l'operazione risparmiò il nervo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor said the operation spared the nerve.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui rispetta sempre le regole.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He always respects the rules.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense (“they respect”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Rispetto le regole, e anche loro le rispettano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I respect the rules, and they respect them too.

definitions.note: Often used both for people (show respect) and for rules/agreements (comply with).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dobbiamo rispettare le regole.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to respect the rules.

definitions.note: Past participle of "rispettare"; often used like an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il professore è molto rispettato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The professor is very respected.

definitions.note: imperfect tense (past), 3rd person singular (he/she/it)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da giovane, rispettava sempre i suoi genitori.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he was young, he always respected his parents.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (io): used for ongoing/repeated actions in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da bambino, rispettavo sempre le regole.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As a child, I always respected the rules.

definitions.note: Often used as a formal command (Lei form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Rispetti le regole, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please respect the rules.

definitions.note: first-person plural (noi), present tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Rispettiamo le regole della scuola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We respect the school rules.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Rispetto le regole.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I respect the rules.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase “rispetto a …” to mean “compared to / with respect to …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Rispetto a ieri, oggi fa più caldo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Compared to yesterday, today it’s warmer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tratta tutti con rispetto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Treat everyone with respect.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei è sempre molto rispettosa con tutti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is always very respectful with everyone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un ragazzo sempre rispettoso con tutti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s a boy who is always respectful to everyone.

definitions.note: Often used after "che" in the present subjunctive (e.g., "Spero che lei risponda") or as a formal command to "Lei" (e.g., "Risponda, per favore").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che lei risponda presto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope that she answers soon.

definitions.note: third-person singular present (he/she/it answers) of "rispondere"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui risponde subito alle domande.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He answers the questions right away.

definitions.note: gerund form (used like “while answering/responding” or “by answering/responding”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto rispondendo alle tue domande.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m answering your questions.

definitions.note: Often used with “a” for the person you answer (e.g., “rispondere a qualcuno”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi rispondere a questa domanda?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you answer this question?

definitions.note: Future tense (he/she/it will).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti risponderà domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She will answer you tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti risponderò domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will answer you tomorrow.

definitions.note: Used with “voi” (you plural). Depending on context it can be present tense (“you answer/are answering”) or an imperative (“answer!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Perché non rispondete alle mie domande?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why aren’t you answering my questions?

definitions.note: Informal singular (tu) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Rispondi al telefono, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Answer the phone, please.

definitions.note: Informal (tu) command: imperative + "mi" (to me).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Rispondimi, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Answer me, please.

definitions.note: Present tense, 1st person singular (io).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti rispondo subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'll answer you right away.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto), common in written Italian (stories, history), especially for completed actions in the distant past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alla fine rispose con una sola parola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end, he/she answered with a single word.

definitions.note: passato remoto (simple past), used mainly in writing and in some regions of Italy
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando sentirò la domanda, risposero subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When they heard the question, they answered right away.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), common in written narratives and some regions; often corresponds to 'I answered' in English.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando mi chiese il nome, risposi subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he asked me my name, I answered right away.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La tua risposta è corretta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your answer is correct.

definitions.note: plural of "risposta"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le tue risposte sono corrette.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your answers are correct.

definitions.note: Past participle of "rispondere"; commonly used with "avere" (e.g., "ho risposto").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho risposto alla tua domanda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I answered your question.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a physical fight (often in public) involving multiple people.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È scoppiata una rissa fuori dal bar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A brawl broke out outside the bar.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Andiamo al ristorante stasera?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Shall we go to the restaurant tonight?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono molti ristoranti in questa zona.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many restaurants in this area.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo ristrutturato l'appartamento l'anno scorso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We renovated the apartment last year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nel 2019 ristrutturò la casa dei nonni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In 2019, he/she renovated his/her grandparents’ house.

definitions.note: Plural of "risultato".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I risultati dell’esame saranno pubblicati domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The exam results will be published tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il risultato dell’esame è arrivato oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The result of the exam arrived today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il treno ha dieci minuti di ritardo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train is ten minutes late.

definitions.note: Often used for picking up something that is ready for you (e.g., an order, a package, documents).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo ritirare il pacco in posta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to pick up the package at the post office.

definitions.note: Common with money (e.g., from an ATM) or for withdrawing something from circulation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio ritirare cento euro dal bancomat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to withdraw one hundred euros from the ATM.

definitions.note: Used for taking back something said or offered (e.g., a statement, a complaint, an invitation).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha deciso di ritirare la sua denuncia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He decided to withdraw his complaint.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho ritirato i soldi al bancomat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I withdrew the money at the ATM.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo brano ha un ritmo veloce.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This piece has a fast rhythm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Marco ritorna a casa alle sei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Marco comes back home at six.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stavo ritornando a casa quando mi hai chiamato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was coming back home when you called me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani ritornare a casa presto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I’ll return home early.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "ritornare"; often used with "essere" in compound tenses
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Maria è ritornata a casa tardi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Maria came back home late.

definitions.note: form used with "voi" (you plural), e.g. as an imperative: "Ritornate!"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ritornate a casa presto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come back home soon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Marco è ritornato a casa tardi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Marco came back home late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ritornerà domani mattina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She will return tomorrow morning.

definitions.native: I will return, I will come back
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ritornerò a casa dopo il lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will return home after work.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (2nd person singular) of "ritornare"; often used after expressions like "spero che" (I hope that).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che tu ritorni presto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you come back soon.

definitions.note: Used with "voi" in the present subjunctive (e.g., after expressions like "è importante che...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È importante che ritorniate presto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that you come back soon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il ritorno a casa è previsto per domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The return home is scheduled for tomorrow.

definitions.note: past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person singular; common in narratives and formal writing
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo molti anni, ritornò nel suo paese natale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After many years, he returned to his hometown.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho appeso un ritratto di mia nonna in salotto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hung a portrait of my grandmother in the living room.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 1st person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo molti anni, ritrovai una vecchia foto in soffitta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After many years, I found an old photo again in the attic.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani ho una riunione alle dieci.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I have a meeting at ten.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani ho due riunioni in ufficio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I have two meetings at the office.

definitions.note: Present tense (noi) of "riuscire"; often followed by "a" + infinitive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Riusciamo a finire il lavoro oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We manage to finish the work today.

definitions.note: Often used with “a” + infinitive (e.g., “riuscire a fare…” = “to manage to do…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono riuscito a finire il lavoro in tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I managed to finish the work on time.

definitions.note: Used in the imperfect subjunctive, often after expressions like "se" (if) or "speravo che" (I hoped that).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Speravo che riuscisse a finire il lavoro oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hoped that he/she would manage to finish the work today.

definitions.native: you (all) can, you (all) manage, you (all) succeed
definitions.note: Second-person plural form ("voi").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Riuscite a finire i compiti oggi?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you (all) finish the homework today?

definitions.note: Feminine plural past participle, used with "essere" (e.g., "sono riuscite").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le ragazze sono riuscite a trovare la strada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The girls managed to find the way.

definitions.note: past participle used with essere (e.g., “siamo riusciti a…”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo riusciti a finire il lavoro in tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We managed to finish the work on time.

definitions.note: past participle of "riuscire"; often used with "essere" (e.g., "sono riuscito a...")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono riuscito a finire il lavoro in tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I managed to finish the work on time.

definitions.note: Imperfect past; often implies repeated/ongoing ability or attempts in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non riusciva a dormire la notte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She couldn't sleep at night.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense of "riuscire" (often used with "a" + infinitive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non riuscivamo a trovare le chiavi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We couldn't find the keys.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past, ongoing/repeated). Often followed by “a” + infinitive (e.g., riuscivo a capire).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da piccolo riuscivo a nuotare per un’ora senza fermarmi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was little, I was able to swim for an hour without stopping.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person singular of "riuscire".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alla fine riuscì a trovare le chiavi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end, he/she managed to find the keys.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci siamo seduti sulla riva del fiume.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We sat on the riverbank.

definitions.note: Often used for seeing someone again (e.g., after some time) or seeing something another time (e.g., a film).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero di rivederti presto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope to see you again soon.

definitions.native: see her again, see it again
definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “la” (= her/it, feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero di rivederla presto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope to see her again soon.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “lo” (“him” or “it”) attached to the verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero di rivederlo presto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope to see him again soon.

definitions.note: Infinitive with the pronoun “ti” (you) attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non vedo l’ora di rivederti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t wait to see you again.

definitions.note: Includes the object pronoun “vi” = “you” (plural, or formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero di rivedervi presto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope to see you again soon.

definitions.note: second-person singular ("you") in the future tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani rivedrai i tuoi amici al parco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow you will see your friends again at the park.

definitions.note: Future tense (noi) of "rivedere"; often used when you expect to meet someone again.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci rivedremo domani mattina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will see each other again tomorrow morning.

definitions.native: will see again, will meet again
definitions.note: Future tense (he/she/it). Used for seeing someone/something again; can also mean meeting again.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono sicuro che ti rivedrà presto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm sure he/she will see you again soon.

definitions.native: I will see again, I will meet again
definitions.note: First-person singular (io) future tense of "rivedere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti rivedrò domani in ufficio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll see you again tomorrow at the office.

definitions.note: Often used for making information known, especially something previously secret or unknown.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non posso rivelare il segreto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t reveal the secret.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "rivelare" (often used in the passive or as an adjective)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La verità è stata rivelata ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The truth was revealed yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il segreto è stato rivelato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The secret was revealed.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alla fine rivelò la verità a tutti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end, he/she revealed the truth to everyone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato una rivista di viaggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a travel magazine.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato due riviste alla stazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought two magazines at the station.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho rivisto il film ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I watched the movie again yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used for something checked and corrected (e.g., a text or document).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il documento è stato rivisto dal professore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The document was reviewed by the professor.

definitions.note: Used when you want something returned to you (something you had before).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Rivogliamo i nostri soldi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We want our money back.

definitions.note: Used to say you want something returned to you (or back the way it was).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Rivoglio il mio libro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want my book back.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Rivogliono i soldi che hanno prestato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They want back the money they lent.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense form of "rivolere"; it implies someone used to want something again or still wanted it back.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo averlo lasciato andare, lo rivoleva con sé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After letting him go, she wanted him back with her.

definitions.note: Often used with "a" to mean addressing someone (e.g., "rivolgo una domanda a..." / "mi rivolgo a...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi rivolgo al professore per chiedere aiuto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I turn to the professor to ask for help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La rivolta è iniziata dopo l’annuncio del governo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The uprising began after the government’s announcement.

definitions.note: Past participle (feminine singular) of "rivoltare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho lasciato la giacca rivolta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I left the jacket turned inside out.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of the adjective; it often appears with “a” (e.g., “rivolta a …”) meaning “addressed to …”.

definitions.note: Very common and informal; often used as a vague word for objects, belongings, or items.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "romantico".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This song is very romantic.

definitions.note: plural masculine form (or mixed group)

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Luca and Marco are very romantic.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il ristorante ha un'atmosfera molto romantica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The restaurant has a very romantic atmosphere.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi piacciono i romanzi gialli.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like mystery novels.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio zio è un romanziere famoso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My uncle is a famous novelist.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto leggendo un romanzo molto interessante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm reading a very interesting novel.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Luca rompe il bicchiere per sbaglio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Luca breaks the glass by accident.

definitions.note: Commonly used both literally (breaking an object) and figuratively (breaking a rule, an agreement, a relationship).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho rotto il bicchiere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I broke the glass.

definitions.note: As a color adjective, it is usually invariable: una camicia rosa, due camicie rosa.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato una camicia rosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a pink shirt.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho regalato una rosa a mia madre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I gave my mother a rose.

definitions.note: As a noun, it refers to the color.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il rosa è il mio colore preferito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Pink is my favorite color.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nel giardino ci sono rose rosse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the garden there are red roses.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Metto un po’ di rosmarino sulle patate al forno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put a bit of rosemary on the baked potatoes.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "rosso"; used with feminine singular nouns
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato una macchina rossa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a red car.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato due rose rosse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought two red roses.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi sono messa il rossetto rosso prima di uscire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put on red lipstick before going out.

definitions.note: masculine plural form of "rosso"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I fiori sono rossi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The flowers are red.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho una macchina rossa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a red car.

definitions.note: As a noun, it refers to the color red.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il rosso è il mio colore preferito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Red is my favorite color.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of the adjective.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ball is round.

definitions.note: often used for the shape of objects (e.g., a table, face, ball)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il tavolo è rotondo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The table is round.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of the past participle of “rompere”; often used like an adjective.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "rotto".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La finestra è rotta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The window is broken.

definitions.note: past participle (feminine plural) of "rompere"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le finestre sono rotte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The windows are broken.

definitions.note: feminine plural form of "rotto".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le finestre sono rotte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The windows are broken.

definitions.note: masculine plural past participle/adjective of "rompere"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I bicchieri sono rotti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The glasses are broken.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I broke the glass.

definitions.note: Often used for something that no longer works or has been damaged.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The phone is broken.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My morning routine includes a coffee and a walk.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha un rovescio molto potente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has a very powerful backhand.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’auto rovesciò il bidone della spazzatura.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car knocked over the trash can.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il castello è in rovina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The castle is in ruins.

definitions.note: Often used figuratively for a serious downfall or failure.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La rovina dell'azienda è arrivata all'improvviso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company's collapse came suddenly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La pioggia rovina il picnic.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rain ruins the picnic.

definitions.note: Often used for damaging something, or for spoiling a plan, situation, or mood.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non voglio rovinare la sorpresa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to ruin the surprise.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho rovinato il telefono.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ruined the phone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il mio piano è rovinato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My plan is ruined.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo visitato le rovine di un antico castello.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We visited the ruins of an ancient castle.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se piove, rovinerà la festa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If it rains, it will ruin the party.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È importante che tu non rovini tutto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that you don’t ruin everything.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person singular of "rovinare"; common in written stories and history.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La pioggia rovinò la festa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rain ruined the party.

definitions.note: Rare/nonstandard form; in Italian you will much more often see "rancio" with the same meaning (especially in a military context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo la marcia, i soldati hanno mangiato il rrancio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the march, the soldiers ate their mess hall meal.

definitions.note: Onomatopoeia used especially in comics to represent snoring.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ru… ru… sta già dormendo sul divano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Snore… snore… he’s already sleeping on the couch.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Qualcuno mi ruba la bicicletta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Someone steals my bike.

definitions.note: Also used as the informal (tu) command form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non ruba i soldi!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t steal the money!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Qualcuno mi ha rubato la bicicletta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Someone stole my bicycle.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “la” (“it” for a feminine noun, or “her”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non puoi rubarla: non è tua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can't steal it: it's not yours.

definitions.note: Infinitive with the direct object pronoun “lo” attached (= “it”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non voglio rubarlo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to steal it.

definitions.note: Includes the object pronoun “mi” (= me). Often used with what is being stolen: “rubarmi + [something]”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non puoi rubarmi la macchina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can’t steal my car from me.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto), 3rd person plural: “they stole”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I ladri rubarono i gioielli durante la notte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The thieves stole the jewels during the night.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "rubare"; used with feminine singular nouns or in passive forms
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La mia borsa è stata rubata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My bag was stolen.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "rubato".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hanno restituito la borsa rubata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They gave me back the stolen bag.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hanno restituito i documenti rubati.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They gave me back the stolen documents.

definitions.note: In English, “rubato” is also a musical term meaning a flexible tempo (not related to this meaning).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hanno rubato la bici ieri sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They stole my bike last night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se avesse l’occasione, ruberebbe dei soldi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If he had the chance, he would steal some money.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non rubo mai.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I never steal.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto) of "rubare"; common in narratives and formal writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri notte rubò una bicicletta davanti alla stazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night he stole a bicycle in front of the station.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gioco a rugby ogni sabato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I play rugby every Saturday.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like a rum, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'è troppo rumore qui dentro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There’s too much noise in here.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At night I hear strange noises in the house.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "rumoroso".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La strada è rumorosa di notte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The street is noisy at night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I bambini ridevano rumorosamente in cortile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children were laughing noisily in the courtyard.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il bar era molto rumoroso ieri sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bar was very noisy last night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nel film, ha un ruolo importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the movie, he has an important role.

definitions.note: Often used for a job or function in an organization.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Qual è il tuo ruolo in azienda?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is your position in the company?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La ruota della bicicletta è bucata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bicycle wheel is flat.

definitions.note: plural of "ruota"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le ruote della bici sono sgonfie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bike’s wheels are flat.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) form of “rompere”; common in narration and writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per la rabbia ruppe il telefono.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In his anger, he broke the phone.

definitions.note: Passato remoto (simple past), 1st person singular: “I broke.” Common in writing and in some regions for past events.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da bambino ruppi il braccio giocando a calcio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As a child I broke my arm playing soccer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'è un ruscello dietro la casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There’s a stream behind the house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio padre russa molto di notte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My father snores a lot at night.

definitions.note: Informal command (tu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Russa pure, tanto io non riesco a dormire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Go ahead and snore, I can’t sleep anyway.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La mia amica è russa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My friend is Russian.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Russian tourists often visit Rome.

definitions.note: plural noun: people from Russia

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Russians live in Russia.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a person, language, or thing from Russia; it also agrees in gender and number (russo/russa/russi/russe).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il mio vicino è russo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My neighbor is Russian.

definitions.note: As a noun, it refers to a Russian person; for a woman you often hear “russa” (feminine form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Conosco un russo che vive a Milano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I know a Russian man who lives in Milan.

definitions.note: Often used with the article: “il russo” = “Russian (the language)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto imparando il russo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m learning Russian.

definitions.note: Used as a conversational filler, like when getting someone's attention or introducing what you’re about to say.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sa, oggi non posso venire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You know, I can’t come today.

definitions.note: Often used with an infinitive to mean “knows how to.”

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She knows how to speak English.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci vediamo sabato mattina.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La sabbia è calda sotto i piedi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sand is warm under my feet.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Did you take the shopping bags?

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you give me a bag, please?

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wisdom also comes from experience.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are wise pieces of advice.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is a wise woman.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hai agito saggiamente e hai evitato problemi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You acted wisely and avoided problems.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio nonno è un uomo saggio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather is a wise man.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho scritto un saggio sulla storia d’Italia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wrote an essay about the history of Italy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il saggio del villaggio dava sempre buoni consigli.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The village sage always gave good advice.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo sai che oggi è domenica?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you know that today is Sunday?

definitions.note: Used to talk about knowing how to do something (ability/skill).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sai nuotare?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you swim?

definitions.note: Informal: used with "tu" (2nd person singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo sai già?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you already know it?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A cena abbiamo bevuto del sake.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At dinner we drank some sake.

definitions.note: Rare/literary shortened form of “sale” (the usual word for “salt”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nella ricetta serve un pizzico di sal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the recipe you need a pinch of salt.

definitions.note: Poetic/archaic shortened form of the imperative “sali” (tu) from “salire”; often seen in older texts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sal sul monte prima che faccia buio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Go up the mountain before it gets dark.

definitions.note: Often used for public or functional spaces (e.g., a waiting room, an exhibition hall, a living room).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci vediamo nella sala d’attesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: See you in the waiting room.

definitions.note: Most commonly used for a regular wage paid by an employer.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha un buon salario e lavora in centro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has a good salary and works downtown.

definitions.note: past participle of "salare"; often used with "avere" to form past tenses
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho salato la pasta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I salted the pasta.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo formaggio è molto salato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This cheese is very salty.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tieni la corda saldamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hold the rope firmly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Metti poco sale nella pasta, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put a little salt in the pasta, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'ascensore sale al quinto piano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The elevator goes up to the fifth floor.

definitions.note: present gerund; often means “while going up / as (someone) is going up.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto salendo le scale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going up the stairs.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that you go up right away.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sali le scale ogni giorno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You go up the stairs every day.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) form, used mainly in narratives and in some regions of Italy.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Salii le scale di corsa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ran up the stairs.

definitions.note: Often used for going up (stairs, hills) or getting on board (a bus/train/plane).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo salire le scale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to go up the stairs.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When you go up into the mountains, bring water and a jacket.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Go up the stairs quietly, please.

definitions.note: Past participle of "salire" used with "essere"; agrees with masculine plural subjects.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo saliti al terzo piano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We went up to the third floor.

definitions.note: Past participle of "salire"; often used with "essere" (e.g., "sono salito").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono salito le scale di corsa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ran up the stairs.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per cena mangiamo salsiccia e patate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For dinner we eat sausage and potatoes.

definitions.note: Not related to English “salt” (it comes from “saltare” = to jump).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il gatto salta sul tavolo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat jumps onto the table.

definitions.note: Informal singular command (tu). Not related to English “salt”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Salta qui!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Jump here!

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), often used in stories and in some regions instead of the past tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando sentii il rumore, saltai dalla sedia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I heard the noise, I jumped out of my chair.

definitions.note: present gerund (used like English “-ing”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto andando a casa saltando nelle pozzanghere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going home jumping in the puddles.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il gatto sa saltare molto in alto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat can jump very high.

definitions.note: Often used for skipping something (like a meal, a class, or a step).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi ho saltato la colazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I skipped breakfast.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei è saltata giù dal muretto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She jumped down from the little wall.

definitions.note: Often used in cooking (e.g., “saltata in padella” = sautéed in a pan).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho mangiato verdura saltata in padella.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ate vegetables sautéed in a pan.

definitions.note: Usually means “you (plural) jump”; it can also be used as the plural command “jump!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando sentite la musica, saltate!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When you hear the music, jump!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono saltato sul letto per scherzo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I jumped on the bed as a joke.

definitions.note: Often used for skipping something (a class, a meal, a step).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho saltato il pranzo perché non avevo fame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I skipped lunch because I wasn’t hungry.

definitions.note: Used in cooking for quickly frying/stir-frying in a pan.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho saltato il pollo in padella con le verdure.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sautéed the chicken in a pan with the vegetables.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando senti la musica, salti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When you hear the music, you jump.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ogni mattina salto la corda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every morning I jump rope.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho fatto un salto sopra la pozzanghera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I jumped over the puddle.

definitions.note: Common in the phrase “fare un salto” = to drop by briefly.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Faccio un salto al supermercato e torno subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll drop by the supermarket and come right back.

definitions.note: simple past (passato remoto), 3rd person singular: “he/she/it jumped”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il gatto saltò sul tavolo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat jumped onto the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Saluta i tuoi amici quando li vedi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Greet your friends when you see them.

definitions.note: Often used in phrases like “effetto salutare” (a beneficial effect).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Una passeggiata dopo cena è salutare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A walk after dinner is beneficial.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ricordati di salutare i tuoi nonni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Remember to greet your grandparents.

definitions.native: to greet me, to say hello to me
definitions.note: Infinitive of "salutare" with the object pronoun "mi" attached (= "me").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi salutarmi quando arrivi?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you greet me when you arrive?

definitions.note: Often used with "voi" (you plural / formal you).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando entrate, salutate tutti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When you come in, greet everyone.

definitions.note: past participle of "salutare"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho salutato la mia professoressa questa mattina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I greeted my teacher this morning.

definitions.note: Used when raising glasses for a toast (literally “health”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Salute!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Cheers!

definitions.note: Often said after someone sneezes (literally “health”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Salute! Hai starnutito forte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Bless you! You sneezed loudly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La salute è importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Health is important.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase “mandare i saluti” = “to send regards.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti mando i miei saluti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I send you my regards.

definitions.note: Used with the subjunctive (e.g., after expressions like “I hope that…”) or as a formal command with “Lei” (e.g., “Lei saluti…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che tu saluti tutti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you greet everyone.

definitions.note: Often used as a closing in letters, emails, or messages (e.g., “Cordiali saluti”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Saluti a tutti!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Greetings to everyone!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Un saluto a tutti!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Greetings to everyone!

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd-person singular of “salutare”; common in written stories and historical narration.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Salutò i vicini e poi entrò in casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He greeted the neighbors and then went into the house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa app salva le password in modo sicuro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This app saves passwords securely.

definitions.note: Used as a command (imperative, tu form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Salva il documento prima di chiudere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Save the document before closing.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 1st person singular of "salvare"; common in writing and storytelling, less common in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando ho visto l'incendio, salvai il cane dal fumo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I saw the fire, I saved the dog from the smoke.

definitions.note: Used for saving files/data (computers) and also for saving/rescuing people.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ricordati di salvare il documento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Remember to save the document.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “la” (“her” or “it” for a feminine noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dobbiamo salvarla prima che sia troppo tardi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to save her before it's too late.

definitions.note: “-le” is a feminine plural object pronoun (“them,” referring to feminine plural nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dobbiamo salvarle prima che sia troppo tardi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to save them before it’s too late.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “li” (= “them,” masculine plural or mixed group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dobbiamo salvarli prima che sia troppo tardi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to save them before it’s too late.

definitions.note: Includes the object pronoun “li” = “them” (masculine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo salvarli prima di chiudere il documento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to save them before closing the document.

definitions.note: Includes the direct-object pronoun “lo” (= him/it).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dobbiamo salvarlo prima che sia troppo tardi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to save him before it’s too late.

definitions.note: Infinitive with the clitic pronoun “mi” attached; often used after a modal verb (e.g., dovere, potere).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo salvarmi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to save myself.

definitions.note: object pronoun "ti" = "you" (informal singular) attached to the verb
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio salvarti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to save you.

definitions.note: Includes the pronoun "vi" (= you plural; also used as formal singular in some contexts).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio salvarvi prima che sia troppo tardi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to save you before it’s too late.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "salvare"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La foto è stata salvata sul computer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The photo was saved on the computer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il salvataggio dei bambini è stato rapido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rescue of the children was quick.

definitions.note: Used for both the present tense “you (plural) save” and the plural imperative “save!” (addressing more than one person).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Salvate il documento prima di chiudere il programma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Save the document before closing the program.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I file sono stati salvati sul computer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The files were saved on the computer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho salvato il file.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saved the file.

definitions.note: Usually used as a title for Jesus (il Salvatore). Also a male first name.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gesù è il Salvatore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Jesus is the Savior.

definitions.note: A neutral/polite greeting; often feels a bit more formal than “ciao.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Salve, come posso aiutarla?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hello, how can I help you?

definitions.note: Third-person singular future tense of "salvare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui salverà il documento prima di chiudere il computer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will save the document before shutting down the computer.

definitions.note: Used for the present subjunctive (e.g., after expressions like “spero che…”) and also as the formal (Lei) imperative.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che tu mi salvi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you save me.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto) form of "salvare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il pompiere salvò il bambino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The firefighter saved the child.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) of “salire” (he/she/it went up). Common in narratives; in everyday speech many speakers use the past tense (passato prossimo) instead.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Salì le scale in silenzio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He went up the stairs in silence.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "sano".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo la febbre, ora mi sento sana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the fever, I feel healthy now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prendo un sandwich al prosciutto e formaggio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll have a ham and cheese sandwich.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'è sangue sul pavimento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is blood on the floor.

definitions.note: Often used for wounds or injuries (literally “to bleed”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wound is still bleeding.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi sono tagliato un dito e sto sanguinando.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I cut my finger and I’m bleeding.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form of "sano".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I bambini sono sani e felici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are healthy and happy.

definitions.note: Often used with an infinitive to mean “know how to.”

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They know how to speak Italian.

definitions.note: 3rd person plural (they) present tense of "sapere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Loro sanno la risposta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They know the answer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo la febbre, mi sento di nuovo sano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the fever, I feel healthy again.

definitions.note: As an adjective it means “holy.” It can also refer to a “saint” in religious contexts.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is a very holy church.

definitions.note: present gerund of "sapere"; often used like “knowing …” or “while knowing …”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sapendo la verità, non posso mentire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Knowing the truth, I can't lie.

definitions.note: Shortened infinitive of "sapere", used especially before clitic pronouns (e.g., "saperlo").

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to know how to do it too.

definitions.native: to know (how to), to be able to
definitions.note: Poetic/older shortened infinitive of "sapere"; most commonly used in fixed expressions like "il saper fare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il saper parlare bene in pubblico è utile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Knowing how to speak well in public is useful.

definitions.note: Used for knowing facts or information, or knowing how to do something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: So parlare italiano, ma non so scrivere bene.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can speak Italian, but I don’t know how to write well.

definitions.note: Infinitive with the direct-object pronoun “la” attached (refers to a feminine noun, or “it”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devi saperla per superare l’esame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to know it to pass the exam.

definitions.note: This is the verb sapere with the object pronoun lo (“it”) attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio saperlo subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to know it right away.

definitions.native: to know about it, to know about them
definitions.note: Includes the particle “ne”, which refers to something already mentioned (often translated as “about it/them”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non voglio saperne niente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to know anything about it.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form of “sapere”, used in hypothetical clauses (often after “se”) and after certain expressions of doubt/feeling.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If he/she knew it, he/she would tell you.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive of "sapere" (used in hypotheticals like "if ... knew" and after certain expressions).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you knew the truth, you wouldn't say this.

definitions.note: Often used as “if you knew…” (imperfect subjunctive, voi). It can also be a literary/simple past form meaning “you (plural) knew/found out.”

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you knew the truth, you would change your mind.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (voi) form; used for talking to more than one person, or as a polite form in some regions/contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sapete dove si trova la stazione?

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past), used for ongoing/repeated states or background information.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando ero piccolo, sapeva sempre cosa dire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was little, he always knew what to say.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (past habitual/ongoing): often implies repeated/ongoing knowing or background information in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sapevamo la risposta, ma non l’abbiamo detta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We knew the answer, but we didn’t say it.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (they/you-plural/formal you plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sapevano già la verità.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They already knew the truth.

definitions.note: Second person plural (voi), imperfect tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sapevate già la verità?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Did you already know the truth?

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (tu form), used for ongoing/background knowledge in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sapevi già la risposta?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Did you already know the answer?

definitions.note: Imperfetto (past habitual/ongoing): can mean “I knew” or “I used to know,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sapevo che oggi saresti arrivato in ritardo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I knew that today you would arrive late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi serve del sapone per lavarmi le mani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need some soap to wash my hands.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo gelato ha un sapore buonissimo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This ice cream has a really good flavor.

definitions.note: feminine singular form

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This soup is very tasty.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo sugo è davvero saporito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This sauce is really tasty.

definitions.note: Used mainly in the present subjunctive (e.g., che lui/lei sappia) and can also be used as a formal command (Lei sappia…).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che lui sappia la verità.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope he knows the truth.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non lo sappiamo ancora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We don’t know yet.

definitions.note: Used with another verb in the infinitive (e.g., “sappiamo nuotare” = “we can swim”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We can speak a little Italian.

definitions.note: present subjunctive, 3rd person plural (“that they know”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È importante che sappiano la verità.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that they know the truth.

definitions.note: Second-person plural present subjunctive (also used as the plural formal imperative: “you all should know”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che sappiate la verità.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you know the truth.

definitions.note: Conditional (3rd person singular) of "sapere"; also used as a polite form ("would you know...") in questions.

definitions.note: Conditional (present), 1st person singular of "sapere".

definitions.note: Future tense of "sapere" (to know).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will know the truth.

definitions.note: Future tense (3rd person singular) of “sapere”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani saprà la verità.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow he/she will know the truth.

definitions.note: Past participle of "sapere"; commonly used with "avere" in the passato prossimo to mean you found out something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho saputo la verità ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found out the truth yesterday.

definitions.note: Second-person singular future (tu) of "essere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani sarai a casa?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Will you be at home tomorrow?

definitions.note: Future tense (3rd person plural) of "essere"; used for "they will be" and "you (plural) will be" depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani saranno a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow they will be at home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il suo commento era davvero sarcastico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His comment was really sarcastic.

definitions.note: Conditional present (3rd person singular) of "essere"; also used as an auxiliary in the conditional perfect.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se avessi più tempo, sarebbe più facile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I had more time, it would be easier.

definitions.note: Conditional mood, 3rd person plural (they/you all/formal you would be). Used as an auxiliary with a past participle to form the conditional perfect.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sarebbero arrivati prima, ma c'era traffico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They would have arrived earlier, but there was traffic.

definitions.note: Conditional present (io). Often used in polite phrases or hypothetical situations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sarei felice di aiutarti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would be happy to help you.

definitions.note: Conditional mood (noi). Used for hypothetical situations and in polite/indirect statements.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Saremmo più felici con meno stress.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We would be happier with less stress.

definitions.note: Future tense (1st person plural) of "essere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani saremo a casa alle otto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will be at home at eight.

definitions.note: Conditional mood, 2nd person plural (voi). Often used in polite forms or hypothetical situations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se veniste prima, sareste più rilassati.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you came earlier, you would be more relaxed.

definitions.note: Second-person singular conditional form of “essere”; often used as an auxiliary to form the conditional perfect.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Saresti arrivato prima, ma c’era traffico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You would have arrived earlier, but there was traffic.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (voi) future of "essere"; used as an auxiliary or as the main verb "to be".

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary with a past participle to form the future perfect (futuro anteriore).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When you arrive, he will have already left.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular future tense of “essere” (to be).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani sarà una bella giornata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow it will be a beautiful day.

definitions.note: Future simple, 1st person singular of "essere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani sarò a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will be at home.

definitions.note: First person singular, simple future of "essere".

definitions.note: Plural of "sasso".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother plays the saxophone in a band.

definitions.note: present gerund (ongoing action) of "sbadigliare"

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I yawned during the lesson.

definitions.native: you’re wrong, you make a mistake

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you make a mistake, you can try again.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry, I think I’m making a mistake.

definitions.native: to make a mistake, to be wrong
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho sbagliato e mi dispiace.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I made a mistake and I’m sorry.

definitions.native: to miss (a target), to get wrong
definitions.note: Commonly used with things like a bus/train stop, a number, or an answer.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hai sbagliato la risposta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You got the answer wrong.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form (often used like an adjective, e.g. with a feminine noun such as “risposta” or “idea”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La risposta è sbagliata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The answer is wrong.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La risposta è sbagliata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The answer is wrong.

definitions.native: you (plural) are wrong, you (plural) make a mistake
definitions.note: Used with “voi” (you all).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sbagliate sempre i conti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You always get the calculations wrong.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le risposte sono sbagliate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The answers are wrong.

definitions.note: Past participle of "sbagliare"; often used as an adjective meaning "wrong".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hai sbagliato numero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You dialed the wrong number.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La risposta è sbagliata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The answer is wrong.

definitions.native: was wrong, was making a mistake
definitions.note: imperfect tense (ongoing or habitual action in the past)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pensavo che avesse ragione, ma sbagliava.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thought he was right, but he was wrong.

definitions.native: I was wrong, I made a mistake
definitions.note: imperfect tense (used for ongoing or habitual past actions/states)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pensavo di avere ragione, ma sbagliavo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thought I was right, but I was wrong.

definitions.native: I’m wrong, I make a mistake
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scusa, sbaglio spesso quando sono stanco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry, I often make mistakes when I’m tired.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho fatto uno sbaglio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I made a mistake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono rimasto sbalordito dalla notizia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was astonished by the news.

definitions.note: Usually used with "di" + noun/pronoun: "sbarazzarci di ...".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dobbiamo sbarazzarci di queste vecchie scatole.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to get rid of these old boxes.

definitions.note: Often used as "sbarazzarsi di" (= to get rid of something/someone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio sbarazzarmi di questi vecchi vestiti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to get rid of these old clothes.

definitions.note: Often used with "di" (e.g., sbarazzarsi di qualcosa = get rid of something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È difficile sbarazzarsi di questa macchia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s hard to get rid of this stain.

definitions.note: Past participle (feminine singular) of "sbarazzare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La cantina è stata sbarazzata dei vecchi scatoloni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The basement was cleared of the old boxes.

definitions.note: Often used as an informal command (to one person), usually followed by “di” (e.g., “sbarazzati di…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sbarazzati di quei vestiti vecchi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Get rid of those old clothes.

definitions.note: Often used with a direct object (e.g., "ho sbarazzato i vecchi mobili" = "I got rid of the old furniture").
