definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho sbarazzato i vecchi mobili.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got rid of the old furniture.

definitions.note: Often used with "di" to mean "get rid of" something (e.g., "sbarazzarsi di...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che tu sbarazzi la cucina prima di cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you clear the kitchen before dinner.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si sbarazzò dei vecchi vestiti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He got rid of the old clothes.

definitions.note: Used in contexts like “che lui/lei sbatta…” (subjunctive) and also as the formal command form (Lei) in some cases.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non voglio che sbatta la porta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want him/her to slam the door.

definitions.note: Often used for doors, windows, or other objects making a loud impact.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non sbattere la porta!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t slam the door!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sbatto la porta quando esco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I slam the door when I leave.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho sbattuto la porta perché ero arrabbiato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I slammed the door because I was angry.

definitions.note: Informal and usually derogatory/slang.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non voglio avere problemi con gli sbirri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to have trouble with the cops.

definitions.note: Informal, often derogatory/slang term for a police officer.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non parlare con lo sbirro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t talk to the cop.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In primavera sbocciano i fiori nel giardino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In spring, the flowers bloom in the garden.

definitions.native: take care of it, deal with it
definitions.note: Often used informally to mean “get it done” (finish a task or handle something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo sbrigarci oggi, prima di sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to take care of it today, before evening.

definitions.native: to take care of, to deal with
definitions.note: Often used with an object like “una faccenda” (a task/errand) or in expressions like “sbrigare una pratica” (handle some paperwork).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo sbrigare alcune cose prima di uscire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to take care of a few things before going out.

definitions.note: Pronominal/reflexive verb; very common in the imperative (e.g., “Sbrigati!” = “Hurry up!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dobbiamo sbrigarci, il treno parte tra dieci minuti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to hurry up; the train leaves in ten minutes.

definitions.note: Includes the pronoun “vi” (= yourselves/you all), from reflexive “sbrigarsi”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dovete sbrigarvi, è tardi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to hurry up; it’s late.

definitions.note: Informal command to more than one person ("voi"); literally "get yourselves done" / "get moving".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dai, sbrigatevi o perderemo il treno!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come on, hurry up or we'll miss the train!

definitions.note: Informal (used with "tu"); literally "get yourself done/finished".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sbrigati, siamo in ritardo!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hurry up, we're late!

definitions.native: take care of (it), deal with (it), handle (it)
definitions.note: Present subjunctive, 2nd person singular (tu) of “sbrigare”; often used after expressions like “è meglio che…” or “penso che…”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È meglio che tu sbrighi questa pratica oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s better if you take care of this paperwork today.

definitions.note: Informal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo la festa era sbronzo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the party he was drunk.

definitions.note: Can mean “he/she peels” (present) or “peel!” (informal command).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui sbuccia una banana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He peels a banana.

definitions.note: present gerund ("-ing" form), often used to mean "while peeling"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto sbucciando una mela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m peeling an apple.

definitions.note: Used for removing the skin/peel from fruits or vegetables.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi sbucciare la mela, per favore?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you peel the apple, please?

definitions.note: Past participle of "sbucciare"; often used like an adjective (e.g., "una mela sbucciata").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho mangiato una banana sbucciata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ate a peeled banana.

definitions.note: simple past (passato remoto), 3rd person singular
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui sbucciò una mela e la mangiò subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He peeled an apple and ate it right away.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti va di giocare a scacchi dopo cena?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you feel like playing chess after dinner?

definitions.note: Often used for payments, bills, documents, or subscriptions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La scadenza del pagamento è domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The payment deadline is tomorrow.

definitions.note: Past participle (feminine singular) of "scadere", commonly used for things like documents, cards, and deadlines.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La carta di credito è scaduta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The credit card has expired.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Metti i piatti sullo scaffale, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put the plates on the shelf, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha scagliato una pietra contro la finestra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He threw a stone at the window.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le scale sono in fondo al corridoio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The stairs are at the end of the hallway.

definitions.native: scale (e.g., a musical scale, a measurement scale)
definitions.note: Often used in phrases like “scala musicale” (musical scale) or “scala di misura” (measurement scale).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa mappa è in scala 1:10.000.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This map is at a scale of 1:10,000.

definitions.native: to climb, to scale (a mountain, a wall)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vogliamo scalare quella montagna domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We want to climb that mountain tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used for amounts (money, points, taxes, discounts).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi scalare questa spesa dalle tasse?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you deduct this expense from the taxes?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho scalato la montagna ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I climbed the mountain yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le scale sono molto ripide.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The stairs are very steep.

definitions.note: Refers to the weighing device (e.g., bathroom or kitchen scales).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato una bilancia digitale, ma le scale non funzionano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a digital scale, but the scales don’t work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo scambiato i posti a sedere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We swapped seats.

definitions.note: Often used with “per” (e.g., “scambiare X per Y”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti ho scambiato per mio fratello.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I mistook you for my brother.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I due studenti scambiarono i libri alla fine della lezione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The two students exchanged the books at the end of the lesson.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho ricevuto la valigia scambiata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I received the swapped suitcase.

definitions.note: Often used with “per”: “scambiata per …” = “mistaken for …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’ho scambiata per sua sorella.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I mistook her for her sister.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ogni settimana scambiate i libri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every week you swap books.

definitions.note: (plural command)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scambiate i posti, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Swap seats, please.

definitions.note: (past participle, feminine plural)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le valigie sono state scambiate all’aeroporto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The suitcases were swapped at the airport.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I documenti sono stati scambiati.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The documents were exchanged.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho scambiato due parole con lei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I exchanged a few words with her.

definitions.note: Often used with “per” (e.g., “scambiare qualcuno per…” = “to mistake someone for…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti ho scambiato per tuo fratello.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I mistook you for your brother.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Facciamo uno scambio: io prendo questo libro e tu prendi quello.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s make an exchange: I’ll take this book and you take that one.

definitions.note: simple past (passato remoto) of "scambiare"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scambiò la sua maglietta con quella di un amico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He exchanged his T-shirt with a friend's.

definitions.note: simple past (passato remoto) of "scambiare"; often used with "per" (e.g., "scambiare X per Y")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La scambiò per sua sorella.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He mistook her for her sister.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La notizia ha causato uno scandalo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The news caused a scandal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È stato un comportamento scandaloso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was a scandalous behavior.

definitions.note: Often masculine in Italian: lo scanner.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato uno scanner per digitalizzare i documenti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a scanner to digitize the documents.

definitions.note: Used for an unmarried man; the feminine form is "scapola".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio zio è uno scapolo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My uncle is a bachelor.

definitions.note: Present tense (3rd person singular) of "scappare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il cane scappa dal giardino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog runs away from the garden.

definitions.note: simple past (passato remoto) form; common in narratives and in some regions
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando vidi il cane, scappai subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I saw the dog, I ran away immediately.

definitions.note: present participle/gerund of “scappare”; used with “stare” for an action in progress or on its own as “while running away/escaping”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto scappando perché ho paura.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m running away because I’m scared.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono scappato perché avevo paura.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ran away because I was scared.

definitions.note: Past participle of "scappare"; often used with "essere" (e.g., "è scappata").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il mio gatto è scappata stanotte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My cat ran away tonight.

definitions.note: Can be used for “you (plural) run away/escape” (present) or as a command to “you all” (imperative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se vedete un pericolo, scappate!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you see danger, run away!

definitions.note: Feminine plural past participle (e.g., with essere: “sono scappate”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le ragazze sono scappate di casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The girls ran away from home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I ladri sono scappati dalla finestra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The thieves ran away through the window.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il gatto è scappato di casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat ran away from home.

definitions.note: simple past (passato remoto) of "scappare"; common in narratives and in some regions, while everyday speech often uses passato prossimo ("è scappato")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando vide il cane, scappò subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he saw the dog, he ran away immediately.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In cucina ci sono degli scarafaggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are some cockroaches in the kitchen.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In cucina c'è uno scarafaggio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a cockroach in the kitchen.

definitions.note: Often used for batteries (e.g., "batteria scarica" = dead battery).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La batteria del telefono è scarica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The phone battery is dead.

definitions.note: Gerund form: often means “(while) downloading / in the process of downloading.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto scaricando un'app sul telefono.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m downloading an app on my phone.

definitions.note: Gerund form: often means “(while) unloading / in the process of unloading.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sta scaricando le valigie dal taxi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s unloading the suitcases from the taxi.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi scaricare l'app sul tuo telefono.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can download the app on your phone.

definitions.note: Often used for unloading goods from a vehicle (e.g., a truck).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dobbiamo scaricare le valigie dalla macchina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to unload the suitcases from the car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho scaricato l’app sul telefono.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I downloaded the app on my phone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho scaricato le valigie dalla macchina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I unloaded the suitcases from the car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi manca una scarpa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m missing a shoe.

definitions.note: Plural of "scarpa".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo comprare nuove scarpe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to buy new shoes.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of "scarso"; used to describe something that is insufficient or of low quality/amount.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La qualità è scarsa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The quality is poor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo risorse scarse in questo periodo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have scarce resources during this period.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il servizio qui è scarso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The service here is poor.

definitions.note: Used for something that has been thrown away or not accepted (e.g., an item, an idea, a proposal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho scartato la proposta perché era troppo costosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I rejected the proposal because it was too expensive.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Metti i biscotti nella scatola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put the cookies in the box.

definitions.note: plural of "scatola"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato due scatole di biscotti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought two boxes of cookies.

definitions.note: Often refers to a photo; feminine singular past participle.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La foto è stata scattata ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The photo was taken yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho scattato una foto al tramonto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I took a photo at sunset.

definitions.note: Often used for alarms or mechanisms (e.g., “è scattato l’allarme”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È scattato l’allarme antincendio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fire alarm went off.

definitions.note: Often used like English “-ing” forms, especially with “stare” (e.g., “sto scavando” = “I’m digging”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto scavando una buca in giardino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m digging a hole in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dobbiamo scavare una buca in giardino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to dig a hole in the garden.

definitions.note: Past participle of "scavare"; often used with "avere" or as an adjective (e.g., "una grotta scavata").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho scavato una buca in giardino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I dug a hole in the garden.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto), 3rd person singular of "scavare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I cani scavò una buca in giardino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog dug a hole in the garden.

definitions.note: second-person singular (tu) present indicative; also used as the imperative (tu)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scegli tu il film stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You choose the movie tonight.

definitions.note: third-person singular (he/she/it) of "scegliere"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei sceglie un gelato alla fragola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She chooses a strawberry ice cream.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devi scegliere un libro da leggere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to choose a book to read.

definitions.native: to choose some (of them), to choose one (of them)
definitions.note: Includes the particle “ne”, meaning “of it/of them” (used when the thing chosen is already mentioned or implied).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono tanti colori; devo sceglierne uno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many colors; I have to choose one (of them).

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani sceglierò un regalo per mia sorella.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will choose a gift for my sister.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (voi) present tense; also used as the plural imperative (“choose!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scegliete un film da guardare stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Choose a movie to watch tonight.

definitions.note: Imperative with the particle "ne", meaning "of them/some" (refers to something previously mentioned).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se ti piacciono questi biscotti, scegline due.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you like these cookies, choose two (of them).

definitions.note: Used for the present subjunctive (e.g., after expressions like “spero che…”) and also as the formal (Lei) command form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che scelga il colore giusto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you choose the right color.

definitions.note: first-person singular present tense ("I choose")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi scelgo un libro da leggere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I choose a book to read.

definitions.note: simple past (passato remoto), 3rd person singular of "scegliere"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alla fine scelse il vestito blu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end, he/she chose the blue dress.

definitions.note: past historic (passato remoto), 1st person singular
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alla fine scelsi il treno invece dell’aereo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end I chose the train instead of the plane.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "scegliere"; it agrees with a feminine noun (e.g., "la macchina scelta").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La candidata è stata scelta per il lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The candidate was chosen for the job.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hai una scelta difficile da fare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have a difficult choice to make.

definitions.note: Plural of "scelta".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho tante scelte, ma non so quale fare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have many choices, but I don’t know which one to make.

definitions.note: Past participle of "scegliere"; used in compound tenses (e.g., "ho scelto") and sometimes as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho scelto questo libro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I chose this book.

definitions.note: Often insulting; use with care.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non essere scemo: controlla prima di attraversare la strada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t be stupid: check before crossing the street.

definitions.note: Often insulting; use with care.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non fare lo scemo!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don't be an idiot!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa è la scena più bella del film.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is the most beautiful scene in the movie.

definitions.note: Often refers to making a public scene or an exaggerated emotional outburst.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha fatto una scenata al ristorante davanti a tutti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She made a scene at the restaurant in front of everyone.

definitions.note: Often used in the present subjunctive (e.g., after verbs like “spero che…”). It can also be the formal command form (Lei) meaning “go down/come down.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che scenda presto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope he/she comes down soon.

definitions.native: to go down, to come down
definitions.note: Often used for moving downward (stairs, a mountain) or getting off/out of a vehicle.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo scendere alla prossima fermata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to get off at the next stop.

definitions.note: addressed to “you” plural (you all)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scendete le scale piano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Go down the stairs slowly.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) present tense; also used as an informal imperative (“come down!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scendi le scale con calma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come down the stairs slowly.

definitions.native: I go down, I come down
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scendo le scale lentamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I go down the stairs slowly.

definitions.note: Often used for getting off a bus, train, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scendo alla prossima fermata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I get off at the next stop.

definitions.note: Used mainly for films and TV (a written plan of scenes and dialogue).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La sceneggiatura del film è molto ben scritta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The film's screenplay is very well written.

definitions.note: Used for the law-enforcement official; sometimes also used for the sheriff character in Western stories.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo sceriffo sta cercando il ladro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sheriff is looking for the thief.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of "scendere" (typically used with "essere").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Maria è scesa dal treno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Maria got off the train.

definitions.note: past historic (passato remoto) form of "scendere"; common in written narratives
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scese le scale in silenzio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He went down the stairs in silence.

definitions.note: past historic (passato remoto) form of "scendere"; used for getting off a bus/train, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scese dal treno alla stazione centrale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He got off the train at the central station.

definitions.note: Past simple (passato remoto), 3rd person plural of "scendere"; common in narratives and historical accounts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo cena scesero in strada per fare una passeggiata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After dinner they went down to the street for a walk.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) of "scendere" for "I" (io).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scesi le scale in silenzio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I went down the stairs quietly.

definitions.note: past participle (masculine singular) of "scendere"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono sceso dal treno alla stazione centrale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got off the train at the central station.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of the adjective
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei è scettica riguardo a quella storia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is skeptical about that story.

definitions.note: feminine plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le mie amiche sono scettiche riguardo alla nuova proposta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My friends are skeptical about the new proposal.

definitions.note: plural masculine form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono scettici riguardo a questa promessa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are skeptical about this promise.

definitions.note: Often used with “di” + noun/infinitive (e.g., “scettico di/di fare qualcosa”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono scettico su questa proposta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m skeptical about this proposal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo schermo del computer è molto grande.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The computer screen is very big.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Usa lo schermo per proteggere il viso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Use the shield to protect your face.

definitions.note: Can also be used as the informal (tu) imperative: “Scherza!” = “Joke!/You’re joking around!” (often said as “Stai scherzando?” = “Are you kidding?”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui scherza sempre con i suoi amici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s always joking with his friends.

definitions.note: gerund (often used like “just joking”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stavo solo scherzando.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was just joking.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stavo solo scherzando!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was just joking!

definitions.native: are you kidding, are you joking
definitions.note: Often used as a 2nd-person singular form (tu) to ask if someone is joking; it can also be a noun meaning “jokes,” but here the lemma indicates the verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scherzi? Non può essere vero!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you kidding? It can’t be true!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Era solo uno scherzo!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was just a joke!

definitions.note: past participle of "schiaffeggiare"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui è stato schiaffeggiato davanti a tutti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was slapped in front of everyone.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), often used in written narratives for completed actions in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando lo vide mentire, lo schiaffeggiò davanti a tutti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When she saw him lie, she slapped him in front of everyone.

definitions.note: Often used for vehicles (or someone/something) hitting something hard; can also be used more generally for ‘to smash’ or ‘to shatter.’
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'auto schiantò contro il muro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car crashed into the wall.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nella storia, la schiava viveva senza libertà.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the story, the female slave lived without freedom.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In passato, molti schiavi lavoravano nelle piantagioni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the past, many slaves worked on plantations.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nel XIX secolo la schiavitù fu abolita in molti paesi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the 19th century, slavery was abolished in many countries.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nell’antica Roma, molti uomini erano schiavi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In ancient Rome, many men were slaves.

definitions.note: Refers to the back of the body (not the “back” of an object).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi fa male la schiena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My back hurts.

definitions.note: Often used to describe someone’s way of speaking/attitude: honest and direct.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Apprezzo il tuo modo di parlare schietto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I appreciate your straightforward way of speaking.

definitions.note: Often used in the expression “Che schifo!” meaning “How disgusting!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Che schifo, questo latte è andato a male!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How disgusting, this milk has gone bad!

definitions.note: feminine singular form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quella cucina è davvero schifosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That kitchen is really disgusting.

definitions.note: Informal/strong; can be used literally (food, smells) or as an insult about a person/behavior.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Che schifo: questo panino è schifoso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How disgusting: this sandwich is gross.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La schizofrenia è una malattia mentale che richiede cure e supporto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Schizophrenia is a mental illness that requires care and support.

definitions.note: Often used for someone who is hard to please (especially about food or cleanliness).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio fratello è molto schizzinoso con il cibo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is very picky about food.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho fatto uno schizzo del progetto prima di iniziare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I made a sketch of the project before starting.

definitions.note: Often used for a sudden spray of liquid (e.g., water, paint).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Uno schizzo d’acqua mi ha bagnato la camicia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A splash of water got my shirt wet.

definitions.note: Plural; singular is "sci" (a ski).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato degli sci nuovi per andare in montagna.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought new skis to go to the mountains.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sciacquò i bicchieri e li mise ad asciugare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She rinsed the glasses and put them to dry.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato uno scialle di lana per l’inverno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a wool shawl for the winter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I passeggeri sono saliti sulla scialuppa di salvataggio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The passengers got into the lifeboat.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le scialuppe sono pronte per l’emergenza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lifeboats are ready for the emergency.

definitions.note: Usually used for groups of insects (especially bees).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Uno sciame di api è entrato in giardino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A swarm of bees came into the garden.

definitions.note: gerund of "sciare"; often used to mean "while skiing"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi sono fatto male sciando ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got hurt while skiing yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani andiamo a sciare in montagna.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we’re going skiing in the mountains.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho messo la sciarpa perché fa freddo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put on the scarf because it’s cold.

definitions.note: past participle of "sciare"; often used with "avere" to form the past tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho sciato tutto il weekend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I skied all weekend.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La scienza ci aiuta a capire il mondo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Science helps us understand the world.

definitions.note: plural of "scienza"; often used for school subjects or fields of study.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A scuola studiamo le scienze e la matematica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At school we study science and math.

definitions.note: plural of "scienziato"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gli scienziati studiano il cambiamento climatico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Scientists study climate change.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio zio è uno scienziato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My uncle is a scientist.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Allo zoo ho visto una scimmia molto intelligente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the zoo I saw a very intelligent monkey.

definitions.note: Plural of “scimmia”. In everyday Italian it can refer to monkeys in general; for great apes you may also hear “scimmie antropomorfe” or “grandi scimmie”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Allo zoo ho visto due scimmie molto curiose.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the zoo I saw two very curious monkeys.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of “sciocco” (used to describe a woman or a feminine noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una decisione sciocca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a silly decision.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La notizia è stata scioccante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The news was shocking.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono ancora scioccata da quello che è successo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m still shocked by what happened.

definitions.note: feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Erano tutte scioccate dalla notizia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were all shocked by the news.

definitions.note: plural masculine (or mixed-gender) form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo rimasti scioccati dalla notizia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We were shocked by the news.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono scioccato da quello che è successo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m shocked by what happened.

definitions.note: feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non fate domande sciocche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t ask silly questions.

definitions.note: Plural form of "sciocchezza".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non dire sciocchezze!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don't say nonsense!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una domanda sciocca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a silly question.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non fare lo sciocco!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t be a fool!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il burro si scioglie nella padella.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The butter melts in the pan.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui scioglie il nodo con calma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He unties the knot calmly.

definitions.note: gerund of “sciogliere” (used like “-ing”, often with “stare”: “sto sciogliendo” = “I’m melting/dissolving”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto sciogliendo il burro in una padella.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m melting the butter in a pan.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "sciogliere"; agrees with a feminine singular noun (e.g. "la neve è sciolta")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La neve è sciolta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The snow has melted.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il burro è sciolto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The butter is melted.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il nodo è sciolto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The knot is untied.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani c’è uno sciopero dei trasporti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow there is a transport strike.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Attento: il pavimento è bagnato e puoi scivolare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Careful: the floor is wet and you can slip.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "scivolare" (often used with "essere")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei è scivolata sul pavimento bagnato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She slipped on the wet floor.

definitions.note: past participle of "scivolare"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono scivolato sul ghiaccio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I slipped on the ice.

definitions.note: feminine singular form (used with feminine singular nouns)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La strada è scivolosa dopo la pioggia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The road is slippery after the rain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Attento: il pavimento è scivoloso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Careful: the floor is slippery.

definitions.note: plural of "scoiattolo".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nel parco ci sono molti scoiattoli.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the park there are many squirrels.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho visto uno scoiattolo nel parco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw a squirrel in the park.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form; often used to describe things related to school (e.g., "vita scolastica").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La vita scolastica può essere stressante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: School life can be stressful.

definitions.note: feminine plural form; used with feminine plural nouns (e.g., “attività scolastiche”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le attività scolastiche iniziano a settembre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: School activities start in September.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form; can also be used as mixed-gender plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gli eventi scolastici iniziano a settembre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: School events start in September.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “school-related” or “academic,” especially in phrases like “anno scolastico” (school year).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'anno scolastico inizia a settembre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The school year starts in September.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho fatto una scommessa con un amico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I made a bet with a friend.

definitions.native: challenge (something you try to achieve, a risky plan)
definitions.note: Often used figuratively for a risky goal or plan, not just gambling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aprire quel negozio è stata una scommessa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Opening that shop was a challenge (a gamble).

definitions.note: past participle of "scommettere"; often used with "avere" to form the past tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho scommesso dieci euro sulla mia squadra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bet ten euros on my team.

definitions.note: Often used with “su” to mean “bet on” (e.g., scommettere su una squadra).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non scommetto mai sui soldi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I never bet money.

definitions.note: Commonly used both for literal betting (money) and figuratively to mean “I’m sure / I’m willing to guess.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scommetto dieci euro che vincerà la nostra squadra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bet ten euros that our team will win.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Queste scarpe sono scomode.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These shoes are uncomfortable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il gatto è scomparso ieri sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat disappeared last night.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of "scomparire"; used with feminine subjects (often with "essere").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La chiave è scomparsa ieri sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The key disappeared last night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I documenti sono scomparsi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The documents have disappeared / are missing.

definitions.note: Past participle of “scomparire”; often used like an adjective to mean someone or something is no longer present.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il gatto è scomparso da ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat has been missing since yesterday.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto) of "scomparire"; common in writing and in some regions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il gatto scomparve nel giardino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat disappeared in the garden.

definitions.note: Often used for defeating an opponent (in sports, war, or competition).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La nostra squadra ha sconfitto gli avversari.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our team defeated the opponents.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo la sconfitta, la squadra ha promesso di allenarsi di più.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the defeat, the team promised to train more.

definitions.note: feminine plural past participle of "sconfiggere"; used with feminine plural subjects or as an adjective
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le nostre squadre sono state sconfitte in finale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our teams were defeated in the final.

definitions.note: past participle of “sconfiggere”; often used with “essere” or “avere” in compound tenses
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Li abbiamo sconfitti in finale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We defeated them in the final.

definitions.note: Past participle of "sconfiggere"; often used with "avere" (e.g., "ho sconfitto...") or as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo sconfitto la squadra avversaria.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We defeated the opposing team.

definitions.note: Often used to strongly plead with someone (e.g. “Ti scongiuro…” = “I beg you…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti scongiuro, non andare via.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I beg you, don’t go away.

definitions.note: Used when talking about preventing something bad from happening.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Con questa decisione scongiuro un rischio maggiore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With this decision, I avert a bigger risk.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non parlare con gli sconosciuti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t talk to strangers.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un numero sconosciuto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s an unknown number.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per me questa strada è sconosciuta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This street is unfamiliar to me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho parlato con uno sconosciuto alla fermata dell’autobus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I talked to a stranger at the bus stop.

definitions.note: Often describes actions or decisions made without thinking about the consequences.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È stato sconsiderato guidare così veloce con la pioggia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was reckless to drive so fast in the rain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo prodotto è scontato del 20%.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This product is discounted by 20%.

definitions.note: Commonly used to say something is assumed too easily or is not as obvious as people think.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non dare nulla per scontato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t take anything for granted.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Con questa tessera hai uno sconto del 10%.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With this card you get a 10% discount.

definitions.note: Often used to describe someone who is easily irritated or unfriendly.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi Marco è un po' scontroso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today Marco is a bit grumpy.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Era sconvolta dopo aver sentito la notizia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was shocked after hearing the news.

definitions.note: plural masculine form; can also be used for mixed-gender groups.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo la notizia, siamo rimasti sconvolti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the news, we were left shocked.

definitions.note: Often used to describe being emotionally shaken by bad news or an event.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono sconvolto da quello che è successo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m shocked by what happened.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vado al lavoro in scooter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I go to work on a scooter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prendo la scopa e pulisco il pavimento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I take the broom and clean the floor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri mattina scopai il pavimento della cucina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday morning I swept the kitchen floor.

definitions.note: Vulgar/slang usage.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quella notte scopai con la mia ragazza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That night I had sex with my girlfriend.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo scopare la cucina prima di cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to sweep the kitchen before dinner.

definitions.note: Very informal/vulgar slang; can sound crude or offensive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui vuole solo scopare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He just wants to have sex.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho scopato il pavimento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I swept the floor.

definitions.note: Vulgar/slang meaning of "scopare" in Italian.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho scopato con lui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had sex with him.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La scoperta di questa medicina ha salvato molte vite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The discovery of this medicine has saved many lives.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le scoperte scientifiche hanno cambiato il mondo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Scientific discoveries have changed the world.

definitions.note: Past participle of "scoprire"; used in compound tenses (e.g., "ho scoperto").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho scoperto un errore nel documento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I discovered a mistake in the document.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo scopo di questo esercizio è imparare nuove parole.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The purpose of this exercise is to learn new words.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il palloncino può scoppiare se lo gonfi troppo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The balloon can burst if you blow it up too much.

definitions.note: Often used for something that starts suddenly, like a war, a fire, or an argument.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È scoppiata una discussione durante la riunione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: An argument broke out during the meeting.

definitions.note: Past participle of "scoppiare" (feminine singular); often used with "essere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La gomma è scoppiata durante il viaggio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tire burst during the trip.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il pneumatico è scoppiato in autostrada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tire burst on the highway.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) form; common in stories and news, less in everyday conversation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La bomba scoppiò durante la notte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bomb exploded during the night.

definitions.note: Usually used in the present subjunctive (e.g. “che io/lei scopra”) or as the formal (Lei) command “Scopra!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che lei scopra la verità.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope she finds out the truth.

definitions.note: Can mean “you discover” (present tense) or “discover!” (command), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scopri la verità.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Discover the truth.

definitions.note: past historic (passato remoto), 1st person singular
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scoprii la verità troppo tardi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I discovered the truth too late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio scoprire la verità.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to discover the truth.

definitions.note: Includes the object pronoun “lo” (“it”, masculine singular) attached to the verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio scoprirlo subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to find it out right away.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scoprirà la verità presto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She will discover the truth soon.

definitions.note: Second-person plural present ("you" plural) of "scoprire"; also used as the formal "you" (Lei/Loro) in some contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scoprite la verità domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will find out the truth tomorrow.

definitions.note: Passato remoto (simple past), used often in narratives and in some regions of Italy.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nel 1492 Colombo scoprì l’America.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In 1492 Columbus discovered America.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person plural; often used in written narratives for completed past actions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le critiche lo scoraggiarono, ma continuò comunque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The criticisms discouraged him, but he kept going anyway.

definitions.note: Often used like an adjective to describe how someone feels.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo l'esame, mi sono sentito scoraggiato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the exam, I felt discouraged.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo l’esame, ero scoraggiato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the exam, I was discouraged.

definitions.note: Can be literal (a shorter route) or figurative (a quicker way to do something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prendiamo una scorciatoia per arrivare prima a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s take a shortcut to get home sooner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scorda spesso le chiavi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He often forgets his keys.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) form, common in narratives and some regions; often replaced by "ho scordato" in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scordai il tuo nome per un attimo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I forgot your name for a moment.

definitions.note: simple past (passato remoto), 3rd person plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo la festa, scordarono il suo compleanno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the party, they forgot his birthday.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "scordare"; used to agree with a feminine noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho lasciato la borsa scordata a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I left the bag forgotten at home.

definitions.note: Can also be used as the plural imperative: “forget!” (addressing more than one person).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voi scordate sempre le chiavi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You all always forget the keys.

definitions.note: Often used as a command, especially in the expression “Scordati (di) …” = “Forget about …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scordati di quella storia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Forget about that story.

definitions.note: Past participle used in the plural (e.g., in passive forms).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I documenti sono stati scordati a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The documents were forgotten at home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho scordato le chiavi a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I forgot the keys at home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il pianoforte è scordato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The piano is out of tune.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se non lo scrivi, lo scorderà.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you don’t write it down, he/she will forget it.

definitions.note: Informal singular (tu) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Perché scordi sempre le chiavi?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why do you always forget your keys?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scordo spesso i nomi delle persone.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I often forget people’s names.

definitions.note: Passato remoto (simple past), often used in narratives and in some regions instead of the present perfect.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri scordò le chiavi a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday he forgot his keys at home.

definitions.note: Colloquial and considered vulgar.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho scoreggiato in ascensore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I farted in the elevator.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho visto uno scorpione sotto una pietra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw a scorpion under a rock.

definitions.note: Often used for liquids (water, blood), time, or traffic moving smoothly.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il fiume scorre veloce dopo la pioggia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The river flows fast after the rain.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (past continuous/habitual) form of "scorrere"; often used for liquids (water, blood) or time passing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il fiume scorreva lentamente vicino al paese.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The river was flowing slowly near the town.

definitions.note: Often used with time words (e.g., settimana scorsa = last week).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il mese scorso ho cambiato lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last month I changed jobs.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo una scorta d’acqua per due giorni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have a supply of water for two days.

definitions.note: Often used for police or bodyguards accompanying someone or something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il camion viaggia con una scorta armata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The truck travels with an armed escort.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È stato scortese con il cameriere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was rude to the waiter.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) form of "scuotere" (used mainly in written narratives, especially for past events).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il cane scosse la testa e l’acqua finì dappertutto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog shook its head and water ended up everywhere.

definitions.note: Often used to describe someone emotionally shaken after a bad event.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo l'incidente, era ancora scosso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the accident, he was still shaken.

definitions.note: past participle of "scuotere"; can also be used like an adjective (e.g., "sono scosso" = "I’m shaken/upset").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho scosso la bottiglia prima di aprirla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I shook the bottle before opening it.

definitions.note: Commonly used in Italian to mean adhesive tape (brand name turned generic).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi passi lo scotch, per favore?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you pass me the Scotch tape, please?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei un bicchiere di scotch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like a glass of Scotch whisky.

definitions.note: Usually used as an invariable noun (often plural: i/le scout).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mia sorella è una scout.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is a Scout.

definitions.note: Often used in sports/business for someone who searches for talent.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo scout della squadra segue i giovani giocatori.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The team scout follows young players.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio nonno è scozzese.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandpa is Scottish.

definitions.note: Commonly used loanword in Italian; often also said as "schermata" or "cattura dello schermo".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi mandi uno screenshot dell’errore?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you send me a screenshot of the error?

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) form, common in written narratives.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri sera scrisse una lettera a sua madre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night he/she wrote a letter to his/her mother.

definitions.note: Passato remoto (3rd person plural) of "scrivere"; common in narratives and formal writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nel diario scrissero tutto quello che era successo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the diary they wrote everything that had happened.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 1st person singular of "scrivere"; common in storytelling and some regions, less in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri sera scrissi una lettera a mia nonna.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night I wrote a letter to my grandmother.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of “scrivere”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La lettera è stata scritta ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The letter was written yesterday.

definitions.note: feminine plural past participle of "scrivere"; often agrees with a feminine plural noun (and may appear with "essere" in passive forms).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le istruzioni sono scritte in italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The instructions are written in Italian.

definitions.note: plural form (masculine)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho letto i messaggi scritti ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I read the messages written yesterday.

definitions.note: masculine plural past participle of "scrivere"; often used like an adjective (e.g., "documenti scritti").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho letto i documenti scritti in italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I read the documents written in Italian.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il messaggio è scritto in italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The message is written in Italian.

definitions.note: past participle of “scrivere”; used in compound tenses (e.g., passato prossimo) and sometimes as an adjective
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho scritto una lettera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wrote a letter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio padre è uno scrittore e lavora da casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My father is a writer and works from home.

definitions.note: plural of “scrittore”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gli scrittori presentano i loro libri alla fiera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The writers present their books at the fair.

definitions.note: Feminine form; used for a woman who writes books/articles.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mia sorella è una scrittrice e pubblica romanzi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is a writer and she publishes novels.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La sua scrittura è molto chiara.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His/Her writing is very clear.

definitions.note: Used for the present subjunctive (e.g., after expressions like “it’s important that…”) and also as a formal command with Lei (“Write…, please.”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È importante che lei scriva subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that you write right away.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho messo il computer sulla scrivania.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the computer on the desk.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In ufficio ci sono tre scrivanie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the office there are three desks.

definitions.note: Present tense form of "scrivere" (used with "lui/lei/Lei").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scrive una lettera ogni settimana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She writes a letter every week.

definitions.note: gerund of "scrivere"; often used for actions in progress (like "while writing" or "I am writing")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto scrivendo una email.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am writing an email.

definitions.note: Future simple (second person singular) of "scrivere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani mi scriverai un messaggio?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Will you write me a message tomorrow?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi piace scrivere lettere agli amici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like to write letters to my friends.

definitions.note: Future tense, second person plural (voi).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani scriverete una lettera al vostro insegnante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow you will write a letter to your teacher.

definitions.note: Includes the indirect object pronoun “gli” (= to him).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo scrivergli stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to write to him tonight.

definitions.native: to write to her, to write to them
definitions.note: The ending "-le" is an attached pronoun meaning "to her" or "to them" (indirect object).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio scriverle una lettera domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to write her a letter tomorrow.

definitions.note: Here "-le" can also mean "them" (feminine plural direct object), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo scriverle stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to write them tonight.

definitions.note: Infinitive with attached indirect object pronoun: "to me".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi scrivermi quando hai tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can write to me when you have time.

definitions.note: Infinitive + indirect object pronoun “ti” (to you).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo scriverti stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to write to you tonight.

definitions.note: Includes the pronoun “vi” (= to you, plural; also used as a polite/formal “to you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo scrivervi una email domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to write you an email tomorrow.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/it) future tense of "scrivere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani scriverà una lettera a sua nonna.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow he/she will write a letter to his/her grandmother.

definitions.note: future tense (io) of "scrivere"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani scriverò una email al professore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will write an email to the professor.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (voi) present tense; also used as the polite form for “you” (formal, singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scrivete la risposta qui, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Write the answer here, please.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (past): describes an ongoing/habitual action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri sera scriveva una lettera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night he/she was writing a letter.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) present tense of "scrivere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scrivi sempre in modo molto chiaro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You always write very clearly.

definitions.note: Present tense (io).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scrivo un'email a mia sorella.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I write an email to my sister.

definitions.note: Usually used in expressions like “avere scrupoli” (to have scruples) or “senza scrupoli” (without scruples).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non ho scrupoli a dirti la verità.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have no qualms about telling you the truth.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un impiegato scrupoloso e controlla ogni dettaglio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a meticulous employee and checks every detail.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il cavaliere alza lo scudo per proteggersi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The knight raises the shield to protect himself.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La scultura in piazza è molto famosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sculpture in the square is very famous.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mia sorella va a scuola in autobus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister goes to school by bus.

definitions.note: plural of "scuola"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le scuole in questa città sono molto buone.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The schools in this city are very good.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of “scuro”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La stanza è scura.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The room is dark.

definitions.note: Plural form (masculine plural or mixed-gender plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I corridoi sono scuri di notte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The corridors are dark at night.

definitions.note: Often used for colors, rooms, or times of day with little light.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In questa stanza è troppo scuro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this room it’s too dark.

definitions.note: Informal (used when speaking to one person you address as “tu”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scusa, puoi ripetere?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry, can you repeat that?

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase “una scusa” (an excuse). Not to be confused with “scusa!” as an interjection meaning “sorry/excuse me.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non è una scusa valida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s not a valid excuse.

definitions.note: Often used as an informal way to apologize or to get someone’s attention; can also mean “excuse” in the sense of “excuse me.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scusa, ho dimenticato di chiamarti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry, I forgot to call you.

definitions.note: Informal (used with tu); literally “excuse me/forgive me.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scusami, puoi ripetere?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Excuse me, can you repeat that?

definitions.note: Often used at the start of a sentence to politely apologize (e.g., for being late).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scusando il ritardo, iniziamo subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry for the delay, let’s start right away.

definitions.native: to excuse us, to excuse ourselves
definitions.note: "ci" means "us/ourselves" here (object/reflexive pronoun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dobbiamo scusarci per il ritardo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to apologize for the delay.

definitions.note: Often used to apologize or to get someone's attention (e.g., “Scusa!” = “Excuse me!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi scusarmi?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you forgive me?

definitions.note: Literally “to excuse me” (scusare + mi). Often used to apologize.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo scusarmi per il ritardo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to apologize for the delay.

definitions.native: to excuse me, to apologize to me
definitions.note: Infinitive verb form with the object pronoun attached: scusare + mi (“me”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo scusarmi con te per ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to apologize to you for yesterday.

definitions.note: Reflexive form; often used as “scusarsi per …” (to apologize for …) or “scusarsi con …” (to apologize to …).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi devo scusare per il ritardo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to apologize for being late.

definitions.native: to apologize to you, to excuse you
definitions.note: Includes the object pronoun "ti" (= you).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Volevo scusarti per quello che ho detto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wanted to apologize to you for what I said.

definitions.native: to apologize to you (plural), to excuse you (plural)
definitions.note: Reflexive/with object pronoun: "-vi" means "you" (plural) or formal "you" (plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo scusarvi per il ritardo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to apologize to you for the delay.

definitions.note: Past participle (feminine singular) of “scusare”; often agrees with a feminine direct object (e.g., “l’ho scusata” = “I excused/forgave her”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'ho scusata subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I forgave her right away.

definitions.note: Form used with voi (you plural) and also as a polite/formal way to address someone (e.g., in a shop). Often used to get someone’s attention.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scusate, dov'è la stazione?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Excuse me, where is the station?

definitions.note: Plural/formal command: said to more than one person, or to one person using “voi” (very formal/old-fashioned).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scusatemi, potete ripetere?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Excuse me, can you repeat?

definitions.note: Plural/formal command: can be used to apologize to more than one person, or with “voi”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scusatemi per il ritardo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry for the delay.

definitions.note: Reflexive imperative (addressed to “you” plural: you all).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scusatevi subito per quello che avete detto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Apologize right away for what you said.

definitions.note: Informal (used with "tu"); literally "excuse yourself."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scusati per il ritardo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry for being late.

definitions.note: Past participle (masculine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I ragazzi sono già scusati.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boys are already excused.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho scusato Marco per il ritardo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I excused Marco for being late.

definitions.note: Often used with the reflexive form “scusarsi” (e.g., “mi sono scusato” = “I apologized”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi sono scusato per l’errore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I apologized for the mistake.

definitions.note: Plural form of “scusa.” Often used to apologize (e.g., “Scuse!” = “Sorry!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scuse, ho sbagliato numero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry, I dialed the wrong number.

definitions.note: Often used in polite requests (like “would you excuse me?”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scusereste il ritardo?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Would you excuse the delay?

definitions.note: Formal/polite form (Lei) of "scusare"; often used to get someone’s attention or to apologize.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scusi, può ripetere, per favore?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Excuse me, can you repeat, please?

definitions.note: Also used to politely get attention or to excuse yourself (e.g., before asking a question).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scusiamo, dov'è la stazione?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Excuse us, where is the station?
