definitions.note: Often used as “mi scuso …” to mean “I’m sorry / I apologize …” (fairly formal/polite).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi scuso per il ritardo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I apologize for the delay.

definitions.note: Passato remoto (simple past), used mainly in written Italian or storytelling; often replaced by passato prossimo in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alla fine scusò tutti per il ritardo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end, he apologized to everyone for the delay.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei è sdraiata sul divano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is lying down on the couch.

definitions.note: Often used to describe someone’s position (e.g., on a bed, sofa, or the ground).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il gatto è sdraiato sul divano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat is lying down on the sofa.

definitions.note: Past simple (passato remoto) of "sdraiare"; often used in writing (and in some regions) for completed past actions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La madre sdraiò il bambino sul letto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mother laid the child down on the bed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se piove, resto a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If it rains, I’ll stay at home.

definitions.note: Clitic form of "si" used before another object pronoun (e.g., se lo, se ne). In English it often corresponds to himself/herself/themselves depending on context, and is sometimes not translated literally.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se lo ricorda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She remembers it.

definitions.note: reflexive pronoun (used for 3rd person); often appears before the verb
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se lo ricorda bene.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She remembers it well.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La camicia è secca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The shirt is dry.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho riempito il secchio d’acqua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I filled the bucket with water.

definitions.note: Often used for things with little or no moisture (skin, clothes, weather).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo la doccia, i capelli sono secco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the shower, the hair is dry.

definitions.note: Common for foods like crackers or biscuits.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questi biscotti sono secco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These biscuits are crisp.

definitions.note: plural of "secolo"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo castello è rimasto in piedi per secoli.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This castle has remained standing for centuries.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nel XXI secolo, la tecnologia cambia rapidamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the 21st century, technology changes rapidly.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa è la seconda volta che vengo qui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is the second time I come here.

definitions.note: Plural of "secondo" (unit of time).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aspetta due secondi, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wait two seconds, please.

definitions.note: Plural of "secondo" in the sense of a "secondo piatto" in an Italian meal (often meat or fish).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per cena abbiamo ordinato due secondi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For dinner we ordered two main courses.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo è il mio secondo giorno a Roma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is my second day in Rome.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Secondo me, questo ristorante è il migliore del quartiere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: According to me, this restaurant is the best in the neighborhood.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aspetta un secondo, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wait a second, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il medico mi ha prescritto un sedativo per dormire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor prescribed me a sedative to sleep.

definitions.note: Informal/colloquial in many contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi fa male il sedere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My butt hurts.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi sedere qui, per favore?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you sit here, please?

definitions.note: Infinitive with the clitic pronoun “mi” attached (“to sit myself”); commonly used after another verb (e.g., voglio/posso/devo sedermi).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio sedermi qui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to sit down here.

definitions.note: Reflexive verb; used for the action of sitting down (getting seated).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È meglio sedersi qui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It's better to sit here.

definitions.note: Infinitive of "sedere" with the object pronoun "ti" (= you). Often used like "to sit down" / "to take a seat" when telling someone to sit.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi sederti qui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can sit here.

definitions.note: Includes the clitic pronoun “vi” (= “there”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non voglio sedervi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to sit there.

definitions.note: 2nd person plural (“voi”): can be present tense (“you sit/are sitting”) or an imperative (“sit!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sedete, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sit down, please.

definitions.note: Imperative form addressed to more than one person (“you all”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sedetevi, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sit down, please.

definitions.note: Passato remoto (simple past), most common in written Italian (stories, history), especially in some regions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sedetti vicino alla finestra e aspettai il treno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sat down near the window and waited for the train.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense: describes an ongoing or habitual past action/state.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sedeva vicino alla finestra e leggeva un libro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She was sitting near the window and was reading a book.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa sedia è molto comoda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This chair is very comfortable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho sedici anni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am sixteen years old.

definitions.note: Plural of "sedia".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono quattro sedie in cucina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are four chairs in the kitchen.

definitions.note: Often used for a car seat or a seat as part of something (e.g., a chair, bicycle, stadium).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il sedile dell’auto è molto comodo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car seat is very comfortable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si è sentito sedotto dal suo fascino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He felt seduced by her charm.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of “sedere”; used with “essere” (e.g., for a feminine subject).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Maria è rimasta seduta vicino alla finestra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Maria stayed seated near the window.

definitions.note: Feminine singular; can describe a woman/girl or any feminine noun. Not related to English “sedate”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La ragazza rimane seduta vicino alla finestra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The girl remains seated near the window.

definitions.note: Feminine plural past participle of "sedere"; often used with "essere" (e.g., "sono sedute").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le ragazze sono sedute in prima fila.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The girls are seated in the front row.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le persone sedute vicino alla finestra stanno leggendo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The people sitting near the window are reading.

definitions.note: Masculine plural past participle of "sedere"; often used with "essere" to mean "to be sitting/seated."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo seduti qui, vicino alla finestra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are sitting here, near the window.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form (used for groups of men or mixed groups).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo seduti al tavolo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are seated at the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui è seduto vicino alla finestra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is sitting near the window.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi serve una sega per tagliare questo ramo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a saw to cut this branch.

definitions.note: Often used for scoring points/goals in sports.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Segna un gol al primo tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She scores a goal in the first half.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho visto un segnale di stop all’incrocio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw a stop sign at the intersection.

definitions.note: Plural of "segnalibro"; usually means the physical bookmark you put in a book.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato due segnalibri nuovi per questo romanzo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought two new bookmarks for this novel.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho segnato la pagina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I marked the page.

definitions.note: Often used in sports (e.g., scoring a goal/point).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha segnato un gol al primo tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He scored a goal in the first half.

definitions.note: Often used for signing a document (e.g., a form or contract).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se segni qui, la richiesta è completa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you sign here, the request is complete.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se segni ancora, vinciamo la partita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you score again, we’ll win the match.

definitions.note: Plural of "segno".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vedo dei segni sulla porta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see some signs on the door.

definitions.note: Plural of "segno".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono segni di matita sul foglio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are pencil marks on the sheet of paper.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'è un segno sulla porta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a mark on the door.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo segno significa "pericolo".
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This symbol means “danger.”

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "segreto".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa informazione è segreta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This information is secret.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hanno deciso segretamente di cambiare piano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They secretly decided to change the plan.

definitions.note: female form; often used for a woman who works as an office assistant.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La segretaria risponde al telefono tutto il giorno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The secretary answers the phone all day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il segretario risponde alle email e organizza gli appuntamenti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The secretary answers emails and organizes appointments.

definitions.note: Often refers to the office/service (e.g., at a school or company) rather than the person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La segreteria è aperta fino alle 16:00.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The administrative office is open until 4:00 p.m.

definitions.note: Plural of "segreto".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non voglio rivelare i miei segreti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to reveal my secrets.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un incontro segreto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a secret meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo è un segreto: non dirlo a nessuno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is a secret: don’t tell anyone.

definitions.note: Used with the subjunctive (e.g. after expressions like “spero che…”) or as a formal command (“Lei segua…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che mi segua fino all’uscita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you follow me to the exit.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I seguaci del cantante lo aspettano fuori dal teatro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The singer’s followers are waiting for him outside the theater.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il cane segue il padrone.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog follows its owner.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “while following” or “by following,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto seguendo le istruzioni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m following the instructions.

definitions.note: Often used in fixed phrases like "il giorno seguente" (the following day) or "la settimana seguente" (the next week).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La settimana seguente siamo partiti per Roma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The following week we left for Rome.

definitions.note: Plural form; used before a plural noun (e.g., "i giorni seguenti").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nei giorni seguenti, abbiamo ricevuto una risposta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the following days, we received an answer.

definitions.note: Can be used with "tu" as either "you follow" (present) or "follow!" (imperative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Segui la strada e poi gira a destra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Follow the road and then turn right.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seguiamo il professore fino all'aula.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We follow the professor to the classroom.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 1st person singular (“I followed”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seguii le istruzioni e tutto andò bene.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I followed the instructions and everything went well.

definitions.note: Imperative (informal singular) + object pronoun “mi” (= me).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seguimi, ti porto a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Follow me, I'll take you home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo l’introduzione, seguiranno alcune domande.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the introduction, some questions will follow.

definitions.note: Often used both for physically following someone/something and for following along (e.g., a lesson, instructions, a story).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi seguire questa strada fino al centro?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you follow this road to the city center?

definitions.native: to follow her, to follow it
definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “la” (= “her” or “it” for a feminine noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non posso seguirla adesso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t follow her right now.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “li” (“them”, masculine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non posso seguirli adesso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't follow them right now.

definitions.native: to follow it, to follow him
definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “lo” (= it/him, masculine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È difficile seguirlo quando parla così in fretta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s hard to follow him when he speaks so fast.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi seguirmi, per favore?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you follow me, please?

definitions.note: Often used when you mean “understand what I’m saying” or “keep up” in a conversation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi segui? Puoi seguirmi?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you following me? Can you follow me?

definitions.note: infinitive with the attached object pronoun “mi” (“me”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi seguirmi, per favore?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you follow me, please?

definitions.note: Passato remoto (they …); common in narratives and some regions for past events.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seguirono la guida fino al museo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They followed the guide all the way to the museum.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular, future tense (he/she/it will follow).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il cane seguirà il suo padrone fino a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog will follow its owner all the way home.

definitions.note: Simple future, 1st person singular (io).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani seguirò la lezione online.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will follow the online lesson.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "seguire"; it can agree with a preceding feminine direct object pronoun (e.g., "l'" = "la").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'ho seguita fino a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I followed her all the way home.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (voi): can be present tense (“you follow”) or an imperative (“follow!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seguíte le istruzioni, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Follow the instructions, please.

definitions.note: Command addressed to more than one person (voi form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seguitemi, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Follow me, please.

definitions.note: Past participle of "seguire" (masculine plural); used in compound tenses or as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo seguiti da un cane fino a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are followed by a dog all the way home.

definitions.note: past participle of "seguire"; often used with "avere" to form the passato prossimo (e.g., "ho seguito").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho seguito il tuo consiglio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I followed your advice.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (ongoing/habitual action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Marco seguiva il professore in silenzio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Marco was following the professor in silence.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti seguo fino a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll follow you to your house.

definitions.note: Often used for classes, lessons, or training programs.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seguo un corso di italiano online.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m taking an online Italian course.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present indicative of "seguire".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I bambini seguono l’insegnante in silenzio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children follow the teacher in silence.

definitions.note: Passato remoto (historic past) of "seguire"; common in written narratives.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il cane seguì il bambino fino a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog followed the child home.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (“you are”); can also be used as an auxiliary with a past participle (e.g., in the passive: essere + participle).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sei invitato alla festa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are invited to the party.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho sei libri sul tavolo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have six books on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho selezionato il file giusto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I selected the right file.

definitions.note: Common loanword from English; in Italian it’s usually masculine: un selfie.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho fatto un selfie davanti al Colosseo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I took a selfie in front of the Colosseum.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of the adjective
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La natura qui è davvero selvaggia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Nature here is truly wild.

definitions.note: plural masculine form (used with masculine plural nouns or mixed groups)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In questa zona vivono molti animali selvatici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many wild animals live in this area.

definitions.note: Often used for plants, animals, or places; for people it can mean “uncivilized” or “untamed,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In montagna abbiamo visto un cavallo selvatico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the mountains we saw a wild horse.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il semaforo è rosso, quindi dobbiamo fermarci.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The traffic light is red, so we have to stop.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sembra una buona idea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It seems like a good idea.

definitions.note: third-person plural (they) in the present tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sembrano stanchi dopo il viaggio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They seem tired after the trip.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sembri stanco oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You seem tired today.

definitions.note: Imperfetto congiuntivo (subjunctive imperfect) of "sembrare"; often used after expressions of doubt/opinion or in hypothetical past contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non pensavo che sembrasse così stanco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn’t think he seemed so tired.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive (used after expressions like "temevo che...", "pensavo che...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Temevo che sembrassi stanco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was afraid you seemed tired.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "sembrare"; agrees with a feminine subject (often used with "essere")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi è sembrata una buona idea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It seemed like a good idea to me.

definitions.note: Present tense (voi) of “sembrare”; used to address a group (plural “you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sembrate stanchi oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You all seem tired today.

definitions.note: Past participle of "sembrare"; often used with "essere" (e.g., "è sembrato...") or as an adjective-like form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi è sembrato molto stanco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He seemed very tired to me.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past), often used for descriptions or ongoing situations in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sembrava stanco dopo il lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He seemed tired after work.

definitions.note: imperfect tense (3rd person plural)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I bambini sembravano stanchi dopo la scuola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children seemed tired after school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri sembravate stanchi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday you looked tired.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (tu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sembravi stanco ieri sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You seemed tired last night.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (past habitual/ongoing) form: often used for descriptions in the past or how something appeared.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da lontano sembravo più alto nelle foto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: From far away, I seemed taller in the photos.

definitions.note: Conditional mood; often used to express uncertainty or reported information.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sembrerebbe che domani piova.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It would seem that it will rain tomorrow.

definitions.note: often used with informal "tu" ("you"), and also after "che" in the present subjunctive
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sembri stanco oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You seem tired today.

definitions.note: Present indicative, 1st person plural of "sembrare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sembriamo stanchi oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We seem tired today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sembro stanco oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I seem tired today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho piantato un seme nel giardino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I planted a seed in the garden.

definitions.note: Used mainly in school/university contexts; more generally, it can mean a six-month period.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il primo semestre inizia a settembre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The first semester starts in September.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho piantato i semi in giardino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I planted the seeds in the garden.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a floor that is partly underground (often at street level with windows).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vivono in un seminterrato vicino alla stazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They live in a basement near the station.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una ricetta semplice.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a simple recipe.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te lo dico semplicemente: non posso venire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m telling you simply: I can’t come.

definitions.note: plural form (masculine or feminine), used to describe more than one thing/person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le istruzioni sono semplici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The instructions are simple.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Apprezzo la semplicità della tua spiegazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I appreciate the simplicity of your explanation.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sarò sempre con te.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will always be with you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preferisco la senape al ketchup.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prefer mustard to ketchup.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il senato voterà la legge domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The senate will vote on the law tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used in the plural (i seni) to mean “breasts.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si è fatta male al seno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She hurt her breast.

definitions.note: Used especially in fixed expressions like “in seno a” (= within/among) and in literary contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Teneva il bambino stretto al seno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She held the baby close to her chest.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho una strana sensazione che oggi pioverà.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “la”, meaning “it” (referring to a feminine noun). Often used for sensations (e.g., movement, vibration).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The floor is dirty.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of “sportivo” (used to describe a woman or a feminine noun).

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La sposa arriva tra pochi minuti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bride will arrive in a few minutes.

definitions.note: Used as a noun meaning “wife,” especially in formal or traditional contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mia sposa lavora in ospedale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My wife works in a hospital.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui sposa Maria domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He marries Maria tomorrow.

definitions.note: gerund form of "sposare"; it describes an action in progress (often translated with “-ing”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m marrying Laura next month.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They can’t marry us without the documents.

definitions.note: Often used in the sense of ‘to marry someone’ (e.g., Sposare Marco).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vuoi sposare Luca?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you want to marry Luca?

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “la” (= her).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vuole sposarla l'anno prossimo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wants to marry her next year.

definitions.note: Infinitive with the direct object pronoun "lo" attached (refers to a male person).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vuole sposarlo l’anno prossimo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She/He wants to marry him next year.

definitions.note: Includes the object pronoun “mi” (= “me”) attached to the verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vuoi sposarmi?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you want to marry me?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vuoi sposarmi?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Will you marry me?

definitions.note: simple past (passato remoto), 3rd person plural: “they married”

definitions.note: Reflexive verb (used with an auxiliary like “essere” in compound tenses).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sposiamo a giugno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re getting married in June.

definitions.note: Includes the object pronoun "ti" = "you" (informal).

definitions.note: Can also be reflexive/reciprocal (“-vi” = “yourselves/each other”), meaning that you (plural) get married.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you want to get married, we can organize a small ceremony.

definitions.note: feminine singular form; used for a married woman or as the feminine singular past participle of “sposare”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mia sorella è sposata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is married.

definitions.note: feminine singular; used for a woman
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Giulia è sposata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Giulia is married.

definitions.note: Can be present tense ("you all marry") or the plural imperative ("marry!") addressed to more than one person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sposatevi se vi amate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Get married if you love each other.

definitions.note: Feminine plural past participle/adjective (refers to a group of women).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le mie amiche sono sposate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My friends are married.

definitions.note: feminine plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le mie sorelle sono sposate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sisters are married.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono sposati da cinque anni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They have been married for five years.

definitions.note: plural form (used for more than one person)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Luca e Sara sono sposati da cinque anni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Luca and Sara have been married for five years.

definitions.note: Used as an adjective, or as the past participle of "sposare" in compound tenses (often with the reflexive form "sposarsi").

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Marco has been married for two years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Marco è sposato da cinque anni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Marco has been married for five years.

definitions.note: second-person singular (tu) future tense; informal "you"

definitions.note: Second-person plural future: used with “voi” (you all).

definitions.note: Depending on context, it can mean “you marry” (tu sposi) or be a present subjunctive form (e.g., che io/lui/lei sposi = “that I/he/she marry”).

definitions.note: Often used reflexively (sposarsi) to mean “to get married.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sposiamo a giugno.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo sposo aspetta la sposa davanti alla chiesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The groom is waiting for the bride in front of the church.

definitions.note: Often used for moving something from one place to another, or for rescheduling (like an appointment).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you move the chair near the table?

definitions.native: move, get out of the way

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She is studying for the exam.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stamattina ho bevuto un caffè.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This morning I drank a coffee.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La stampa di questo libro è di alta qualità.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The printing of this book is high quality.

definitions.note: Used to refer to news media collectively.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La stampa ha parlato molto di questa notizia.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato una stampante nuova per l’ufficio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a new printer for the office.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho stampato il documento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I printed the document.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "stanco".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm getting tired.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo il viaggio, lei era stancata.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That job tired me.

definitions.note: feminine plural form

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re tired after the walk.

definitions.note: plural masculine form (also used for mixed-gender groups)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo il viaggio, siamo tutti stanchi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the trip, we are all tired.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La lunga camminata lo stancò molto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The long walk tired him a lot.

definitions.note: Often used unchanged in Italian, especially in formal/technical contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo è il modello standard.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is the standard model.

definitions.note: Gerund form of “stare”; often used in expressions like “stando così…” (= “being like this… / if things stay like this…”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Staying at home today, I can rest.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary with the gerund to form the present continuous (stare + gerund).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stanno mangiando.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are eating.

definitions.note: From "stare"; often used for location or a temporary state (not the same as "essere").

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are in the garden.

definitions.note: means “this night” (the night that is coming or is currently happening)

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tonight I’m going to bed early.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La mia stanza è piccola ma luminosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My room is small but bright.

definitions.note: plural of stanza (a room)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In questo hotel ci sono cinquanta stanze.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this hotel there are fifty rooms.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a famous person (e.g., a movie or music star).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quella cantante è una star in Italia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That singer is a star in Italy.

definitions.note: Shortened form of “stare”, often used in informal speech or set phrases (e.g., “star bene”, “star zitto”). Not related to the English noun “star”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meglio star zitti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Better to stay quiet.

definitions.native: you will be, you will stay

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow you will stay at home all day.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary with the gerund to form the present progressive (stare + gerund), like English “to be” + “-ing”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto leggendo un libro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am reading a book.

definitions.note: Often used to talk about someone’s condition (e.g., how someone is doing) or being located somewhere.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto bene, grazie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m well, thanks.

definitions.native: we will be, we will stay

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani staremo a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will stay at home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho starnutito tutto il giorno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sneezed all day.

definitions.note: future tense (lui/lei/Lei): can mean being in a place/state (“will be”) or remaining somewhere (“will stay”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow he/she will stay at home all day.

definitions.native: I will be, I will stay
definitions.note: First person singular (io), simple future of “stare”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani starò a casa tutto il giorno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will stay at home all day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stasera andiamo al cinema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tonight we’re going to the movies.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "essere" used with compound tenses (e.g., "sono stata")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono stata a Roma due volte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have been to Rome twice.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "essere"; used with feminine singular subjects (e.g., "Maria è stata...")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Maria è stata molto gentile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Maria has been very kind.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “run/owned by the state” (e.g., schools, roads, companies).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio padre lavora in un'azienda statale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My father works in a state-run company.

definitions.note: Used as the auxiliary form of "essere" with a feminine plural subject in the passato prossimo (e.g., "siete state" = "you (plural) were/have been").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siete state in ritardo ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You (plural) were late yesterday.

definitions.note: feminine plural past participle of "essere"; used with a feminine plural subject (e.g., "Siamo state...")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo state a Roma per tre giorni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have been in Rome for three days.

definitions.note: Past participle feminine plural of "stare"; used with "essere" in compound tenses and agrees with a feminine plural subject.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo state molto bene in vacanza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have been very well on vacation.

definitions.note: Second-person singular present (tu) of "stare"; often used for temporary states or how someone is feeling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Come state oggi?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How are you (all) today?

definitions.note: Imperative plural form meaning “stay” and “me” as an object pronoun (“stay with me / stay close to me”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Statemi vicino, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stay close to me, please.

definitions.note: Past participle of "essere" used with "essere" as an auxiliary; it agrees with the subject (masculine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo stati molto occupati oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have been very busy today.

definitions.note: past participle (plural masculine) of "essere"; used in compound tenses (e.g., "siamo stati")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo stati a Roma due volte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have been to Rome twice.

definitions.note: plural of "stato"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gli Stati Uniti sono molto grandi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The United States are very large.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le statistiche mostrano un aumento dei prezzi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The statistics show an increase in prices.

definitions.note: Past participle of essere, used to form compound tenses (e.g., sono stato = I have been).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono stato a Roma due volte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have been to Rome twice.

definitions.note: Past participle of "essere" (to be). Often used with "essere" to form compound tenses (e.g., "sono stato" = "I have been").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono stato a Roma due volte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have been to Rome twice.

definitions.note: Usually means a political state (country or region).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'Italia è uno Stato membro dell'Unione Europea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Italy is a member state of the European Union.

definitions.note: Often used in set phrases like "in buono stato" (in good condition).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La bici è in ottimo stato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bike is in excellent condition.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'è una statua nella piazza principale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a statue in the main square.

definitions.note: plural of "statua"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nel parco ci sono statue antiche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the park there are ancient statues.

definitions.note: Used for people or things from the United States.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono statunitense, ma vivo in Italia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m American, but I live in Italy.

definitions.note: Often used with a gerund (e.g., "stava + -ando/-endo") to mean "was ...-ing".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stava dormendo quando hai chiamato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was sleeping when you called.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (imperfect tense) of “stare”; often used for ongoing states or situations in the past (e.g., where someone was, how someone was feeling).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stava a casa perché non stava bene.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She was at home because he/she wasn’t feeling well.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (past habitual/ongoing) form of "stare" used as an auxiliary (e.g., with a gerund to form the past progressive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stavamo parlando quando mi hai chiamato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We were talking when you called me.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense of "stare" used as an auxiliary (e.g., "stare + gerund" for ongoing actions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stavano guardando la TV quando hai chiamato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were watching TV when you called.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense of "stare" (they/you plural). Often used with a location or to form the progressive (stare + gerund).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stavano a casa quando ha iniziato a piovere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were at home when it started to rain.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (past habitual/ongoing), 2nd person plural (voi). Used as an auxiliary to form the progressive with a gerund.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stavate studiando quando ho chiamato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You were studying when I called.

definitions.note: Often used with a gerund (stare + gerund) to talk about an action in progress in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stavi studiando quando ti ho chiamato?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Were you studying when I called you?

definitions.note: Imperfetto (first-person singular) of “stare”, used as an auxiliary with the gerund to form the past progressive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stavo studiando quando mi hai chiamato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was studying when you called me.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (past) form of "stare"; used for ongoing states/situations in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stavo a casa quando mi hai chiamato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was at home when you called me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stavolta arrivo puntuale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This time I’ll arrive on time.

definitions.note: Most often used for train stations (stazione ferroviaria).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La stazione è vicino al centro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The station is near the city center.

definitions.note: Often a fence made of stakes or slats (a palisade-style fence).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'è uno steccato di legno intorno al giardino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a wooden fence around the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da bambino, lo stegosauro era il mio dinosauro preferito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As a child, the Stegosaurus was my favorite dinosaur.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Di notte vedo una stella molto luminosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At night I see a very bright star.

definitions.note: plural of "stella"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Di notte si vedono molte stelle nel cielo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At night you can see many stars in the sky.

definitions.note: Plural of "stellina"; often used for small star-shaped items (e.g., pasta or decorations).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per Natale abbiamo appeso delle stelline alla finestra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For Christmas we hung some little stars on the window.

definitions.note: Informal “you” form (tu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stendi i panni sul balcone.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hang the clothes out on the balcony.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "stesso"; often used for emphasis meaning "the very/same (person/thing)".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato la stessa borsa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought the same bag.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form; often used with an article (e.g., “la stessa”) to mean “the same one.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prendo la stessa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'll take the same one.

definitions.note: Used after a pronoun for emphasis (e.g., “lei stessa” = “she herself”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei stessa ha detto di sì.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She herself said yes.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary with the gerund to form a past progressive idea in the subjunctive (e.g., “stesse + gerund”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pensavo che stesse dormendo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thought he was sleeping.

definitions.note: Used in the imperfect subjunctive (e.g., after se/if, or in dependent clauses expressing doubt, possibility, wish).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se lui stesse meglio, verrebbe alla festa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If he were feeling better, he would come to the party.

definitions.note: feminine plural form of "stesso" (used to agree with feminine plural nouns)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo le stesse idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have the same ideas.

definitions.note: Imperfetto congiuntivo (subjunctive imperfect) of "stare", used after expressions of doubt, desire, or necessity; often corresponds to English "were" in hypothetical or reported contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dubito che stessero a casa ieri sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I doubt they were at home last night.

definitions.note: Subjunctive imperfect of "stare"; often used in "stare + gerund" to form the past subjunctive progressive (e.g., "se stessi andando" = "if I were going").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se stessi lavorando, non potrei rispondere al telefono.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I were working, I couldn't answer the phone.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form of “stesso”; often used for emphasis after a noun or pronoun (meaning “the very same”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo gli stessi gusti musicali.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have the same musical tastes.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form of "stesso"; used for emphasis ("themselves") or to mean "the same".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hanno scelto gli stessi colori.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They chose the same colors.

definitions.note: Often used with the definite article (il/lo/la/i/le) to mean “the same (one/thing)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo la stessa idea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have the same idea.

definitions.note: Used after a noun or pronoun for emphasis (like “myself/yourself/himself”, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'ho fatto io stesso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I did it myself.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) form of “stare” (3rd person singular), common in narratives and formal writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Durante la tempesta, stette in casa e aspettò.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: During the storm, he/she stayed at home and waited.

definitions.note: Used mainly as the present subjunctive of "stare" (often after "che"), including as an auxiliary with the gerund to form the progressive (e.g., "che stia facendo").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È importante che stia lavorando oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that he/she be working today.

definitions.note: Form of "stare" used in the present subjunctive (e.g., after "penso che", "è importante che"); it can also be used as a formal (Lei) command.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Penso che Luca stia bene oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I think Luca is doing well today.

definitions.note: 1st-person plural present of "stare", used as an auxiliary (commonly to form the present continuous with "stare" + gerund).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stiamo studiando per l’esame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are studying for the exam.

definitions.note: Present indicative, 1st person plural of “stare”. Often used to describe a temporary state or location.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stiamo bene, grazie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re doing well, thanks.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary with a gerund to form the progressive (e.g., “stiano + gerund”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che stiano studiando adesso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope they are studying right now.

definitions.note: Used with the subjunctive (e.g., after expressions like “I hope that…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che stiano bene.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope they are well.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (voi) of "stare", often used after "che" to express a wish, doubt, or possibility.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che stiate bene.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you are well.

definitions.note: Common in Italian as an English loanword, especially for a USB drive (“chiavetta USB”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho salvato il file sulla stick.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saved the file on the USB stick.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi piace il suo stile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like his style.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mia sorella vuole diventare stilista.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister wants to become a fashion designer.

definitions.note: Most commonly used to mean “I value / I respect” when talking about a person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti stimo molto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I respect you a lot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prendo uno stipendio mensile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I earn a monthly salary.

definitions.note: Present tense form of "stirare"; used for ironing clothes.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei stira la camicia prima del lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She irons the shirt before work.

definitions.note: Present tense form of "stirare"; can also mean to stretch or pull something taut.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui stira la corda per fissarla bene.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He pulls the rope tight to fasten it well.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "stirare"; used with feminine nouns (e.g., "camicia", "maglietta").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La camicia è già stirata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The shirt is already ironed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho stirato la camicia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ironed the shirt.

definitions.note: Often used for family origin/ancestry; can also refer more generally to a “line” or “stock” of people.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viene da una stirpe di musicisti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She comes from a lineage of musicians.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person singular: “he/she/it ironed.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri mia madre stirò tutte le camicie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday my mother ironed all the shirts.

definitions.note: plural of “stivale”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato degli stivali nuovi per l'inverno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought some new boots for the winter.

definitions.note: Used with a gerund (e.g., "sto + -ando/-endo") to form the present continuous ("am ...-ing").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto studiando per l'esame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am studying for the exam.

definitions.note: First-person singular present of "stare". Often used with a gerund to mean "I am (doing)" (e.g., "sto studiando" = "I'm studying").

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm at home today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho mal di stomaco dopo pranzo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a stomachache after lunch.

definitions.note: Often used for someone who feels mentally foggy or disoriented (e.g., from shock, lack of sleep, noise, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo la notizia, ero completamente stordito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the news, I was completely dazed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Raccontami una storia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tell me a story.

definitions.note: Often refers to the subject/field of history (e.g., at school), or the history of a place/period.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A scuola studiamo storia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At school we study history.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un edificio storico del centro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a historic building in the city center.

definitions.note: plural of "storia"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi piacciono le storie di avventura.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like adventure stories.

definitions.note: Often used for something not straight (a line, a nail, a leg, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il quadro è storto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The picture is crooked.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La strada è molto trafficata oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The road is very busy today.

definitions.note: plural of "strada"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le strade del centro sono strette.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The streets in the city center are narrow.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "strano"; used to describe a feminine noun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una storia strana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a strange story.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stranamente, oggi non ho fame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Strangely, I'm not hungry today.

definitions.note: feminine plural form of “strano”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho avuto idee strane oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had strange ideas today.

definitions.note: Past participle of "strangolare"; often used with "essere" to form the passive, or as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'uomo è stato strangolato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The man was strangled.

definitions.note: plural masculine (or mixed-gender) form of "strano"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono rumori strani in casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are strange noises in the house.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form; used to describe a woman or a feminine noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei è straniera, ma parla bene italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is foreign, but she speaks Italian well.

definitions.note: feminine form of "straniero".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quella straniera parla italiano molto bene.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That foreign woman speaks Italian very well.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of the adjective (used with feminine plural nouns, or for a group of women/girls).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le studentesse straniere parlano italiano molto bene.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The foreign (female) students speak Italian very well.

definitions.note: plural masculine form; can also be used as a noun meaning “foreigners” depending on context
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono molti studenti stranieri nella mia classe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many foreign students in my class.

definitions.note: plural form of “straniero”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In questa città ci sono molti stranieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this city there are many foreigners.

definitions.note: Often used about people or things from another country.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In questa città ci sono molti studenti stranieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this city there are many foreign students.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un po' strano, ma funziona.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It's a bit strange, but it works.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie is extraordinarily beautiful.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le misure straordinarie sono state approvate ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The extraordinary measures were approved yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi devo fare due ore straordinarie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I have to do two hours of overtime.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hai fatto un lavoro straordinario!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You did an extraordinary job!

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of "strappare"; often used like an adjective (e.g., "la pagina è strappata").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La pagina è strappata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The page is torn.

definitions.note: Usually means “you (plural) tear/rip” (present) or “tear/rip!” (plural command).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Perché strappate le pagine del libro?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you tearing the pages out of the book?

definitions.note: Past participle of "strappare"; often used with "avere" to form the past (e.g., "ho strappato" = "I tore").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho strappato la pagina per sbaglio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I tore the page by accident.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’è uno strappo nella tua maglietta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There’s a tear in your T-shirt.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto) of "strappare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Strappò la pagina dal quaderno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She tore the page out of the notebook.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo bisogno di una strategia per vincere la partita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need a strategy to win the game.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nella storia, la strega vive in una casa nel bosco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the story, the witch lives in a house in the woods.

definitions.note: plural of "strega"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nella fiaba ci sono due streghe cattive.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the fairy tale there are two evil witches.

definitions.note: Often used for a male magic-user; can be literal (in stories) or figurative for someone very skilled.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nella fiaba, lo stregone lancia un incantesimo sul castello.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the fairy tale, the wizard casts a spell on the castle.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nel villaggio, tutti avevano paura della stregoneria.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the village, everyone was afraid of witchcraft.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo lavoro è molto stressante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This job is very stressful.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi sono molto stressato per il lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I’m very stressed because of work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa strada è stretta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This road is narrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I due argomenti sono strettamente collegati.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The two topics are closely connected.

definitions.note: feminine plural form of "stretto"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le strade del centro storico sono molto strette.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The streets in the historic center are very narrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I jeans sono troppo stretti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The jeans are too tight.

definitions.note: Often used with people: "amici stretti" = "close friends".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo amici stretti da anni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’ve been close friends for years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa strada è troppo stretta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This road is too narrow.

definitions.note: Often used in expressions like "un amico stretto" (= a close friend).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un mio amico stretto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s a close friend of mine.

definitions.note: Past participle of "stringere"; it can look like English "strict" but usually means physically "tight" (or figuratively "close").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho stretto la cintura perché mi cadeva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I tightened my belt because it was falling down.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was a moving speech.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non toccate il vetro, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t touch the glass, please.

definitions.note: Imperative form with the direct object pronoun “lo” attached (used with “voi” = plural you / formal you).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take off your shoes before coming in.
