definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is the translation into English.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le traduzioni di questo libro sono disponibili in molte lingue.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The translations of this book are available in many languages.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), often used in stories and in some regions for completed past actions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui tradì la fiducia dei suoi amici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He betrayed his friends' trust.

definitions.note: Often refers to road traffic or congestion; it can also mean “illegal trafficking” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'è molto traffico stamattina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There’s a lot of traffic this morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La tragedia ha colpito tutta la città.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tragedy affected the whole city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prendiamo il traghetto per andare sull’isola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re taking the ferry to go to the island.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "tragico".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una storia tragica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a tragic story.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una storia tragica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a tragic story.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo quasi al traguardo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re almost at the finish line.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prendo il tram per andare al lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I take the tram to go to work.

definitions.note: Used especially for the plot of a book, film, or TV series.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La trama del film è molto interessante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plot of the movie is very interesting.

definitions.note: Used to express the means or channel used to do something; often followed by a noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho inviato i documenti tramite email.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sent the documents via email.

definitions.note: plural of “tramonto”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In inverno, i tramonti arrivano presto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In winter, sunsets come early.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guardiamo il tramonto dal balcone.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We watch the sunset from the balcony.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il bambino cammina sui trampoli al parco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The child walks on stilts at the park.

definitions.note: Often used with “che” (tranne che) or with a noun/pronoun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tutti sono venuti, tranne Marco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Everyone came except Marco.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "tranquillo".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo l'esame, mi sento tranquilla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the exam, I feel calm.

definitions.note: masculine plural; can also be used to address a mixed group
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ragazzi, state tranquilli: andrà tutto bene.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Guys, stay calm: everything will be fine.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi sono tranquillo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I am calm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hanno messo una trappola per i topi in cucina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They put a trap for mice in the kitchen.

definitions.note: Often used with time: "il tempo trascorre" = "time passes".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il tempo trascorre in fretta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Time passes quickly.

definitions.note: Often used with a time expression (e.g., an afternoon, the summer) to mean “to pass/spend time.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo trascorso tutta la giornata al mare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We spent the whole day at the beach.

definitions.note: Often used with a period of time (e.g., a day, the summer) or with time expressions like "il tempo".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Trascorrerà l’estate al mare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She will spend the summer at the seaside.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Come trascorrete il fine settimana?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How do you spend the weekend?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Come trascorri il weekend?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How do you spend the weekend?

definitions.note: Often used with a time expression (e.g., hours, days) or with "il tempo".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Trascorro molto tempo con la mia famiglia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I spend a lot of time with my family.

definitions.note: Often seen as a narrative past tense (passato remoto), especially in written stories.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Trascorse l’estate al mare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She spent the summer at the seaside.

definitions.note: Used mainly in storytelling/writing; it’s the remote past (passato remoto) of "trascorrere" for "they".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Trascorsero tre anni prima che tornasse a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Three years passed before he came back home.

definitions.note: Past participle of "trascorrere"; often used with "avere" to talk about time spent.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I giorni che abbiamo trascorsi a Roma sono stati bellissimi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The days we spent in Rome were wonderful.

definitions.note: Past participle of "trascorrere"; commonly used with "avere" to talk about time spent.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho trascorso una bella giornata con i miei amici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I spent a lovely day with my friends.

definitions.note: Often used for writing something exactly as it is spoken or written (e.g., audio, notes, text).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo trascrivere l’intervista entro stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to transcribe the interview by tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho trascurato i miei amici negli ultimi mesi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I neglected my friends in the last few months.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per troppo lavoro, trascurò la famiglia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Because of too much work, he neglected his family.

definitions.note: gerund form; often used with “stare” to describe an action in progress
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto trasferendo i file sul computer nuovo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m transferring the files to the new computer.

definitions.note: Often used for moving something/someone to another place; also used for transferring money, data, or a person to another office/team/school.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani devo trasferire i file sul nuovo computer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I have to transfer the files to the new computer.

definitions.native: you will transfer, you will move
definitions.note: Second-person plural future tense (voi) of "trasferire".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani trasferirete i file sul nuovo computer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow you will transfer the files to the new computer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devono trasferirmi in un altro ufficio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They have to transfer me to another office.

definitions.note: past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person plural (“they transferred/moved”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nel 2010 trasferirono la sede a Milano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In 2010 they moved the headquarters to Milan.

definitions.note: Reflexive verb; often used for moving house or moving to a different city/country.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi sono trasferito a Milano per lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I moved to Milan for work.

definitions.native: transfer to you, move to you
definitions.note: Infinitive with the clitic "vi" (= to you, plural/formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dobbiamo trasferirvi i file entro stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to transfer the files to you by this evening.

definitions.note: Infinitive with the direct-object clitic "vi" (= you, plural/formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il medico ha deciso di trasferirvi in un altro reparto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor decided to transfer you to another ward.

definitions.note: past participle (feminine singular) of "trasferire"; often used with "essere" for movement or change of workplace/department
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo l’estate, Maria è stata trasferita a Milano per lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the summer, Maria was transferred to Milan for work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ogni mese trasferite i soldi sul conto risparmio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every month you transfer the money to the savings account.

definitions.note: Used to address more than one person (voi).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Trasferite questi file nella nuova cartella.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Move these files into the new folder.

definitions.note: Feminine plural past participle, often used with a passive form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le pratiche sono state trasferite in un altro ufficio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The documents were transferred to another office.

definitions.note: Past participle used with masculine plural subjects or objects (e.g., “i documenti trasferiti”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I pazienti sono stati trasferiti in un altro ospedale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The patients were transferred to another hospital.

definitions.note: Past participle of "trasferire"; often used with "essere" for being transferred (e.g., by a company) or moved (to another place).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono stato trasferito a Milano per lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was transferred to Milan for work.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo l’università, si trasferì a Milano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After university, they moved to Milan.

definitions.note: Can be present tense (he/she/it transforms) or the informal singular command (transform!).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il sole trasforma l'acqua in vapore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sun transforms the water into vapor.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "trasformare"; used in compound tenses and passive forms.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La città è stata trasformata in pochi anni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The city was transformed in a few years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il quartiere è stato trasformato negli ultimi anni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The neighborhood has been transformed in recent years.

definitions.note: simple past (passato remoto), third-person singular (he/she/it)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La pioggia trasformò la strada in un fiume.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rain turned the street into a river.

definitions.note: Commonly used for changing residence (moving to a new home).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani dobbiamo traslocare in un nuovo appartamento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we have to move to a new apartment.

definitions.note: gerund form; often used to mean “while transporting/carrying.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto trasportando le scatole in macchina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m carrying the boxes to the car.

definitions.note: Often used for moving people or things from one place to another, especially by vehicle.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dobbiamo trasportare i mobili nella nuova casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to transport the furniture to the new house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il trasporto pubblico in questa città è efficiente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Public transportation in this city is efficient.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il libro tratta un argomento importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book deals with an important topic.

definitions.native: they deal with, they treat, they handle
definitions.note: Present tense (3rd person plural) of "trattare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In questa lezione trattano un tema importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this lesson they deal with an important topic.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of "trattare"; often used with "essere" to form the passive (e.g., "è stata trattata").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La pratica è stata trattata ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The case was handled yesterday.

definitions.note: Past participle of "trattare". Not to be confused with the noun "trattato" meaning "treaty".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho trattato il problema con molta attenzione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I handled the problem with a lot of care.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I due paesi hanno firmato un trattato di pace.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The two countries signed a peace treaty.

definitions.note: A formal written work, often academic or philosophical.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto leggendo un trattato di filosofia per l’università.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m reading a treatise on philosophy for university.

definitions.note: Used with “di” to say what a book, article, conversation, etc. was about.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il libro trattava di storia italiana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book was about Italian history.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il medico trattava molti pazienti ogni giorno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor was treating many patients every day.

definitions.note: Often used for physically stopping someone/something from moving, or for holding back emotions (e.g., laughter, tears).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo trattenere il cane perché corre verso la strada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to hold the dog back because it’s running toward the street.

definitions.note: passato remoto (historic past) form of "trattenere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si trattenne dal ridere durante la riunione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He held back from laughing during the meeting.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "trattenere"; agrees with a feminine noun (e.g., "somma", "ragazza").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La somma è stata trattenuta dalla banca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The amount was withheld by the bank.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi ha trattenuto al lavoro fino a tardi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She kept me at work until late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È importante che tu tratti bene i clienti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that you treat customers well.

definitions.note: Can also be used as an imperative meaning “let’s handle/deal with …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Trattiamo questo problema domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’ll deal with this problem tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il medico trattò il paziente con molta attenzione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor treated the patient with a lot of attention.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo l’incidente, ha avuto un trauma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the accident, he had a trauma.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si è sentito travolto dalle emozioni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He felt overwhelmed by emotions.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il pedone è stato travolto da un'auto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pedestrian was run over by a car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho tre fratelli.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have three brothers.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il biglietto costa trecento euro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ticket costs three hundred euros.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho tredici anni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am thirteen years old.

definitions.note: Used in Italian especially for longer walks in nature/mountains; often treated as a masculine noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani facciamo trekking in montagna.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we’re going hiking in the mountains.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La terra trema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ground shakes.

definitions.note: gerund form (used like “-ing” in English)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono rimasto lì tremando dal freddo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I stayed there trembling from the cold.

definitions.note: Often used for shaking from cold, fear, or strong emotion.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi tremano le mani dal freddo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My hands are shaking from the cold.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per la paura, tremava tutto il corpo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Out of fear, his whole body was trembling.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le sue mani tremavano dal freddo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His hands were shaking from the cold.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of "tremendo"; can be used both negatively (very bad) or positively (very impressive), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una notizia tremenda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s terrible news.

definitions.note: Often used as an intensifier meaning “very” (not necessarily something negative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono tremendamente felice di vederti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m tremendously happy to see you.

definitions.note: In everyday Italian it often emphasizes something very negative (like “terrible/awful”), but it can also mean “very big/intense.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri ho avuto un mal di testa tremendo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I had a tremendous (terrible) headache.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo in tremila alla manifestazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are three thousand of us at the demonstration.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I treni partono ogni mezz’ora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The trains leave every half hour.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prendo il treno alle otto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I take the train at eight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho trenta anni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am thirty years old.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase “una trentina di …” to mean an approximate number.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'erano una trentina di persone alla riunione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There were about thirty people at the meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il tribunale apre alle nove.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The court opens at nine.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono triste oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m sad today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho provato una grande tristezza dopo la sua partenza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I felt great sadness after his departure.

definitions.note: plural form (masculine or feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono tristi perché devono partire domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are sad because they have to leave tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La squadra ha vinto un trofeo importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The team won an important trophy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La troia ha appena avuto dei piccoli.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sow just had some piglets.

definitions.note: Very vulgar and offensive insult in Italian; avoid using it.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non chiamarla troia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t call her a slut.

definitions.note: Commonly used in Italian for someone who posts provocative or offensive messages online to upset others.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non rispondere: è solo un troll.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t reply: it’s just a troll.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Suona la tromba nella banda della scuola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He plays the trumpet in the school band.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio fratello suona il trombone nella banda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother plays the trombone in the band.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of "troppo"; used with feminine singular nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'è troppa gente in questa stanza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are too many people in this room.

definitions.note: feminine plural form of "troppo"; used with feminine plural nouns
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono troppe persone in questa stanza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are too many people in this room.

definitions.note: plural masculine form of "troppo"; used with masculine plural nouns
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono troppi libri sul tavolo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are too many books on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hai parlato troppo in classe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You talked too much in class.

definitions.note: Agrees in gender and number when used as a determiner (e.g., troppo, troppa, troppi, troppe).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho troppo lavoro oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have too much work today.

definitions.note: Used as a pronoun to mean an excessive amount (instead of modifying a noun or adjective).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ne hai preso troppo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You took too much of it.

definitions.note: plural of "trota"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nel fiume ci sono molte trote.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many trout in the river.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei trova sempre le chiavi nella borsa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She always finds the keys in her bag.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 1st person singular (io). Common in written narratives; in everyday speech many people use passato prossimo instead.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alla fine trovai le chiavi sotto il divano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end I found the keys under the sofa.

definitions.note: Informal singular (tu) imperative with the object pronoun mi (“me”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se hai bisogno di aiuto, trovami dopo la lezione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you need help, find me after the lesson.

definitions.note: passato remoto (past historic) of "trovare"; means "we found"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alla fine trovammo la chiave sotto il tappeto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end we found the key under the doormat.

definitions.note: third-person plural (they) form of "trovare"; can mean to find or to discover something
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non trovano le chiavi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They can't find the keys.

definitions.note: Here, "ci" means "us" (direct object).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se vuoi trovarci, siamo sempre in biblioteca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you want to find us, we’re always in the library.

definitions.note: Here, "ci" means "there" (a place).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi piace trovarci la mattina, quando c’è poca gente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like being there in the morning, when there aren’t many people.

definitions.note: "ci" is an object pronoun meaning "us" here; used often in phrases like "puoi trovarci..." (you can find us...).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi trovarci in ufficio fino alle cinque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can find us in the office until five.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non riesco a trovare le chiavi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t manage to find the keys.

definitions.note: Includes the direct-object pronoun "la" attached to the verb; it can mean "it" (feminine noun) or "her".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo trovarla prima di stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to find it/her before tonight.

definitions.note: Includes the direct-object pronoun “le” = “them” (feminine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo trovarle prima di partire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to find them before leaving.

definitions.note: Infinitive "trovare" with the direct object pronoun "li" (= them) attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo trovarli prima di stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to find them before tonight.

definitions.note: Infinitive of "trovare" with the direct object pronoun "li" attached (="them").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo trovarli prima di sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to find them before evening.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “lo” (“it/him”) attached to the verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo trovarlo subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to find it/him right away.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi trovarmi alla stazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can find me at the station.

definitions.note: Often used with the meaning “be/feel” in contexts like “trovarmi bene/male” (feel good/bad) or “trovarmi in…” (find myself in…).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero di trovarmi bene nel nuovo lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope I’ll feel good in the new job.

definitions.note: Infinitive of "trovare" with the clitic pronoun "mi" (“me/myself”) attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Posso trovarmi in difficoltà se non studio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can find myself in trouble if I don’t study.

definitions.note: past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person plural

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a human error.

definitions.note: Used to describe behavior or treatment that shows compassion.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was very kind/humane with us.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gli umani hanno bisogno di dormire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Humans need to sleep.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una persona umile e gentile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a humble and kind person.

definitions.note: Infinitive with the attached pronoun “ci” (ourselves/us).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I felt humiliated in front of everyone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Apprezzo la sua umiltà.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I appreciate his humility.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi sono di buon umore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I'm in a good mood.

definitions.note: masculine singular indefinite article (used before most masculine singular nouns)

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a dog.

definitions.note: feminine singular indefinite article (used before feminine singular nouns)

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of "uno"; used before feminine singular nouns (as an article) or as the number "one".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei una mela, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like an apple, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono undici studenti in classe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are eleven students in the class.

definitions.note: Refers to Hungary (language, people, or things from Hungary); as an adjective it agrees in gender and number with the noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La cucina ungherese è molto saporita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hungarian cuisine is very flavorful.

definitions.note: Can refer to a man or a woman; context makes it clear.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio nonno è ungherese.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather is Hungarian.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto imparando l’ungherese.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m learning Hungarian.

definitions.note: Plural of "unghia".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi sono tagliato le unghie ieri sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I cut my nails last night.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "unico".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei è l’unica persona che mi capisce.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is the only person who understands me.

definitions.note: feminine plural form of "unico"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hanno idee uniche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They have unique ideas.

definitions.note: plural masculine form of "unico".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono gli unici studenti della classe che parlano inglese.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are the only students in the class who speak English.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È figlio unico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is an only child.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un'esperienza unica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It's a unique experience.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A scuola devo indossare l’uniforme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At school I have to wear the uniform.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A scuola, gli studenti devono indossare uniformi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At school, the students must wear uniforms.

definitions.native: you will join, you will unite
definitions.note: future tense (tu form) of "unire".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani unirai le tue forze alle nostre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow you will join your strength with ours.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Possiamo unire le forze e finire prima.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We can join forces and finish earlier.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devi unire questi due file in uno solo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You need to merge these two files into one.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani unirete le due parti del progetto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow you will join the two parts of the project.

definitions.native: to join me, to unite with me
definitions.note: Object pronoun “mi” means “me” (e.g., “to join me” or “to join with me,” depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi unirmi al gruppo?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you add me to the group?

definitions.note: Reflexive verb; often used with “a” (to join someone) or “a/in” (to join a group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vogliamo unirci al gruppo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We want to join the group.

definitions.note: Used with the direct-object pronoun "ti" (you).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio unirti al nostro gruppo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to add you to our group.

definitions.note: Includes the clitic pronoun “vi” = “you” (plural) or formal “you.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio unirvi al gruppo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to add you to the group.

definitions.native: to join there, to join in there
definitions.note: Includes “vi” meaning “there” (in that place).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È bello unirvi amici nuovi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s nice to join new friends there.

definitions.note: Future tense (3rd person singular) of "unire".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La nuova regola unirà tutti gli studenti nello stesso progetto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The new rule will unite all the students in the same project.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (io) of “unire”; also used as the formal imperative “(Lei) unisca” meaning “join/unite” in polite commands.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che io unisca le due parti del discorso con una buona conclusione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope that I join the two parts of the speech with a good conclusion.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo ponte unisce le due sponde del fiume.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This bridge connects the two sides of the river.

definitions.note: Informal singular command (tu): “join (me/us)” / “come along.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Unisciti a noi per cena!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Join us for dinner!

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "unire"; used to agree with a feminine singular noun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La famiglia è rimasta unita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The family stayed united.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lavoriamo insieme per unire le persone.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We work together to unite people.

definitions.note: imperative (you all) + "vi" = "yourselves"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ragazzi, unitevi e finite il lavoro insieme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Guys, join together and finish the work together.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho unito i due documenti in un unico file.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I joined the two documents into a single file.

definitions.note: Plural form; can refer to university students or to things connected to a university, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gli studenti universitari spesso studiano in biblioteca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: University students often study in the library.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form; often refers to a female university student or something related to a university.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mia sorella è universitaria.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is a university student.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “university student” in context (e.g., uno studente universitario).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mia sorella è una studentessa universitaria.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is a university student.

definitions.note: In Italian, "università" usually refers to a university (higher education institution).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mia sorella studia medicina all’università.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister studies medicine at university.

definitions.note: Used before masculine singular nouns that start with s+consonant (e.g., uno studente), z (e.g., uno zaino), gn (e.g., uno gnomo), ps (e.g., uno psicologo), or x/y.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C'è uno studente in classe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a student in the classroom.

definitions.note: Used as the number “one” and as the masculine singular indefinite article before masculine singular nouns (like “un libro” = “a book”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho uno zaino nuovo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a new backpack.

definitions.note: Used as an indefinite pronoun meaning “one” (a person), similar to English “one/you” in general statements.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Uno non sa mai cosa può succedere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You never know what can happen.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) form; common in writing and storytelling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Unì i due gruppi in una sola squadra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She joined the two groups into a single team.

definitions.note: Used before feminine singular nouns that start with a vowel (elision of “una”: un’ + amica).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho un’amica italiana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have an Italian friend.

definitions.note: plural of "uomo"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono molti uomini in piazza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many men in the square.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quell’uomo è molto gentile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That man is very kind.

definitions.note: plural of "uovo" (egg)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi servono due uova per la torta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need two eggs for the cake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A colazione mangio un uovo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For breakfast I eat an egg.

definitions.note: Informal loanword from English; used to mean an extra lift in energy or mood.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi mi serve un up per finire il lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I need a boost to finish the work.

definitions.note: Usually written lowercase in Italian when referring to the language; uppercase when referring to the people (gli Urdu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto imparando l'urdu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m learning Urdu.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una questione urgente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s an urgent matter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo parlarti urgentemente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to talk to you urgently.

definitions.note: Somewhat medical/formal; in everyday speech Italians often say "fare pipì".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Di solito urino prima di uscire di casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I usually pee before leaving the house.

definitions.note: Often means “he/she/it shouts” (present tense); it can also be used for formal “you shout.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui urla quando è arrabbiato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He shouts when he is angry.

definitions.note: gerund form (used for “while shouting/yelling” or “by shouting/yelling”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È entrato urlando e tutti si sono spaventati.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He came in shouting and everyone got scared.

definitions.note: Often implies a loud or angry/strong voice.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non urlare, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t shout, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando videro il cane, urlarono per la paura.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When they saw the dog, they shouted out of fear.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho urlato perché non mi sentivi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I shouted because you couldn’t hear me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando vedo un ragno, urlo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I see a spider, I scream.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho sentito un urlo nella notte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I heard a scream in the night.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto), 3rd person singular: “he/she shouted.” Common in writing and storytelling; in speech you often hear “ha urlato.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando vide il ladro, urlò e chiamò la polizia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he saw the thief, he shouted and called the police.

definitions.note: Depending on context, it can also be the informal singular command “use!” (tu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Marta usa questa app per studiare l’italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Marta uses this app to study Italian.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto usando il computer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m using the computer.

definitions.note: third-person plural ("they") present tense of "usare"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In Italia usano spesso il contante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In Italy they often use cash.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi usare il mio telefono?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you use my phone?

definitions.note: includes the direct object pronoun “la” (“it” referring to a feminine noun) attached to the verb
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devi usarla ogni giorno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to use it every day.

definitions.note: "lo" is an object pronoun meaning “it” (usually referring to a masculine noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Posso usarlo per tagliare il pane?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can I use it to cut the bread?

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "usare"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho usato una chiave usata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I used a used key.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato una bici usata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a used bike.

definitions.note: plural “you” (voi).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quale app usate per studiare l’italiano?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Which app do you use to study Italian?

definitions.note: past participle feminine plural; often used in passive forms (e.g., “sono usate”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Queste espressioni sono usate spesso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These expressions are used often.

definitions.note: Past participle of "usare"; often used with "avere" to form the past tense (passato prossimo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho usato il computer ieri sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I used the computer last night.

definitions.note: past tense (imperfect): “was using / used to” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando ero piccolo, usava sempre la stessa bicicletta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was little, he always used the same bicycle.

definitions.note: Gerund of "uscire"; used with "stare" to mean an action in progress (e.g., "sto uscendo" = "I’m going out").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto uscendo di casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m leaving the house.

definitions.native: we go out, let's go out
definitions.note: Present tense: “we go out”; can also be used as an invitation meaning “let’s go out.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Usciamo stasera?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are we going out tonight?

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) form of "uscire"; common in narratives and some regions, less common in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo cena uscii a fare una passeggiata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After dinner I went out for a walk.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto) of "uscire"; commonly used in narratives, especially in written Italian.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri sera uscimmo dopo cena e tornammo tardi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night we went out after dinner and came back late.

definitions.note: Often used with “di” to mean “go out of (a place)”: “uscire di casa”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stasera voglio uscire con gli amici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tonight I want to go out with my friends.

definitions.native: will go out, will leave, will come out
definitions.note: Future tense (3rd person singular) of "uscire"; can refer to a person leaving or something coming out (e.g., a book, results).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il treno uscirà dalla stazione alle 18:00.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train will leave the station at 6:00 p.m.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of "uscire"; used with "essere" in compound tenses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Maria è uscita alle otto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Maria went out at eight.

definitions.note: Form used with “voi” (you plural); it can also be used as a plural command (“go out!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Uscite di casa alle otto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You leave the house at eight.

definitions.note: Past participle of "uscire" (used with "essere"); this form agrees with a masculine plural subject (e.g., "noi", "loro").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siamo usciti presto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We went out early.

definitions.note: Past participle of "uscire"; commonly used with "essere" (e.g., "sono uscito").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono uscito presto ieri sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I went out early last night.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) form of “uscire” used mainly in written Italian and some regions; corresponds to “he/she went out” in English depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo cena, uscì di casa in silenzio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After dinner, he went out of the house quietly.

definitions.note: Present indicative, 2nd person singular (tu) of "usare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu usi spesso il telefono per lavorare?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you often use your phone for work?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Usiamo questa app ogni giorno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We use this app every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Di notte si sente cantare l’usignolo nel giardino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At night you can hear the nightingale singing in the garden.

definitions.note: 1st-person singular present (io).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo uso ogni giorno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I use it every day.

definitions.note: Often used in fixed expressions like "in uso" (in use) and "fare uso di" (to make use of).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo telefono è ancora in uso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This phone is still in use.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un uso comune salutare quando si entra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a common custom to say hello when you enter.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto) of "usare" (used mainly in narratives, books, or some regional speech).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri usò il mio telefono per chiamare sua madre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday he used my phone to call his mother.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo dizionario è molto utile per chi studia l’italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This dictionary is very useful for people who study Italian.

definitions.note: plural (masculine or feminine), agreeing with a plural noun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questi consigli sono molto utili.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These pieces of advice are very useful.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Utilizza questa app ogni giorno per studiare italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She uses this app every day to study Italian.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto pagando utilizzando la mia carta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m paying using my card.

definitions.note: third-person plural (they) of "utilizzare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Utilizzano questa app ogni giorno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They use this app every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi utilizzare il mio computer per un'ora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can use my computer for an hour.

definitions.note: Includes the attached pronoun “-la” (= “it” for a feminine singular direct object; sometimes “her” depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Possiamo utilizzarla per aprire la porta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We can use it to open the door.

definitions.note: Infinitive + direct object pronoun "lo" (= "it"); common after verbs like "devo", "posso", "voglio".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Posso utilizzarlo per il progetto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can use it for the project.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person plural (they). Common in narratives and formal writing; in everyday speech people often use the passato prossimo instead.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I tecnici utilizzarono un nuovo software per risolvere il problema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The technicians used new software to solve the problem.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "utilizzare"; often used with "essere" in passive forms or as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa macchina è stata utilizzata solo due volte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This machine has been used only twice.

definitions.note: Often the "voi" form (plural "you"), used for commands (imperative) or for "you use" (present tense).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Utilizzate questa app ogni giorno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Use this app every day.

definitions.note: Feminine plural past participle, agreeing with a feminine plural noun (e.g., "le parole utilizzate").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le parole utilizzate nell’esercizio sono semplici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The words used in the exercise are simple.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo metodo è molto utilizzato in Italia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This method is widely used in Italy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se utilizzi l’app ogni giorno, impari più in fretta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you use the app every day, you learn faster.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per questo esercizio utilizziamo una calcolatrice.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For this exercise we use a calculator.

definitions.note: Often sounds more formal than "uso" (from "usare").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Utilizzo questa app per studiare italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I use this app to study Italian.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'utilizzo del cellulare è vietato in classe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The use of cell phones is forbidden in class.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person singular (“he/she/it used”). Common in writing and narratives; in everyday speech people often use the passato prossimo instead.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Utilizzò il computer per finire il progetto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He used the computer to finish the project.

definitions.note: Used with a past participle (va + participle) to express necessity, like “needs to be done”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo modulo va compilato oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This form must be filled out today.

definitions.note: Present tense of "andare" (to go); used with lui/lei/Lei.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei va al lavoro in autobus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She goes to work by bus.

definitions.note: Often used to ask or say how something is going ("Come va?") or whether something works.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Come va oggi?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How’s it going today?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quest'estate vado in vacanza al mare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This summer I'm going on vacation to the seaside.

definitions.note: Plural of “vacanza”; often used for time off from work/school (e.g., summer/Christmas holidays).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quest'estate andiamo in vacanze al mare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This summer we're going on vacation to the seaside.

definitions.note: In informal speech, it can also be a strong insult toward a woman.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La vacca mangia l’erba nel prato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cow eats grass in the meadow.

definitions.note: Plural of "vacca"; can be insulting if used about people.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Al pascolo ci sono cinque vacche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are five cows grazing in the pasture.

definitions.note: Informal singular imperative of "andare" + "ci" ("there").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se vuoi capire, vacci di persona.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you want to understand, go there in person.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho fatto il vaccino ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got the vaccine yesterday.

definitions.native: (that) I go, (that) you go, (that) he/she goes
definitions.note: Present subjunctive of "andare"; it’s used after expressions like "penso che", "è importante che", "prima che".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È importante che vada subito a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that he/she goes home right away.

definitions.native: may they go, let them go
definitions.note: Present subjunctive, 3rd person plural of "andare"; often used after expressions of doubt, desire, necessity, or to give a (polite/indirect) command.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È meglio che vadano a casa adesso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s better that they go home now.

definitions.note: Present tense form of "andare" used with "io" (I).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vado a scuola in autobus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I go to school by bus.

definitions.note: Very vulgar and offensive; used as an insult.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vaffanculo, non voglio più sentirti!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Fuck you, I don't want to hear from you anymore!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho un'idea vaga di quello che è successo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a vague idea of what happened.

definitions.note: Present tense, second person singular (tu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vai a scuola in autobus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You go to school by bus.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Una valanga ha bloccato la strada di montagna.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: An avalanche blocked the mountain road.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo libro vale dieci euro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book is worth ten euros.

definitions.note: Used for things like tickets, coupons, and documents.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo biglietto vale fino a giugno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This ticket is valid until June.

definitions.note: Often used in set phrases like “ne vale la pena” (“it’s worth it”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo quadro vale molto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This painting is worth a lot.

definitions.note: Common in formal contexts (rules, documents, tickets).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il biglietto vale fino a domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ticket is valid until tomorrow.

definitions.native: was worth, used to be worth
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo telefono valeva 200 euro l'anno scorso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This phone was worth 200 euros last year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che questo regalo valga qualcosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope this gift is worth something.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La tua risposta è valida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your answer is valid.

definitions.note: Often used for documents, tickets, IDs, and deadlines.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo biglietto è valido fino a domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This ticket is valid until tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used to describe a solution, method, or argument that works well.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una soluzione valida per il problema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s an effective solution to the problem.

definitions.note: Often used for a work bag/briefcase; can also mean a small suitcase depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho messo i documenti nella valigetta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the documents in the briefcase.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho messo i vestiti nella valigia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the clothes in the suitcase.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le valigie sono già in macchina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The suitcases are already in the car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vivono in una valle tra le montagne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They live in a valley between the mountains.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo quadro ha un grande valore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This painting has great value.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I valori della nostra azienda sono importanti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The values of our company are important.

definitions.note: Often used in practical contexts like prices, measurements, or data.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Controlla i valori nella tabella.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Check the figures in the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un soldato valoroso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a brave soldier.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dobbiamo valutare tutte le opzioni prima di decidere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to evaluate all the options before deciding.

definitions.note: Often used for estimating the monetary value of something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Un esperto può valutare la casa prima della vendita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: An expert can appraise the house before the sale.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La valutazione del progetto sarà pronta domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The evaluation of the project will be ready tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nei film, i vampiri hanno paura della luce del sole.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In movies, vampires are afraid of sunlight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nel film c'è un vampiro che vive in un castello.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the movie there is a vampire who lives in a castle.

definitions.note: past participle of "vandalizzare"; often used with "essere" (to be) as in "è stato vandalizzato".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il muro è stato vandalizzato durante la notte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wall was vandalized during the night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei un gelato alla vaniglia, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like a vanilla ice cream, please.

definitions.note: Often used with "a" + infinitive to mean "go to (do something)".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vanno a comprare il pane.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They go to buy bread.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense of "andare" (used for "they" or polite "you" plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vanno al lavoro ogni mattina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They go to work every morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui vanta sempre i suoi successi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He always boasts about his successes.

definitions.note: Plural of "vantaggio".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I vantaggi di studiare ogni giorno sono evidenti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The advantages of studying every day are clear.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo nuovo lavoro è un grande vantaggio per me.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This new job is a big advantage for me.

definitions.note: plural form; used before a plural noun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho letto vari articoli su questo argomento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I read several articles on this topic.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I prezzi variano da negozio a negozio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Prices vary from store to store.

definitions.note: feminine plural form of “vario”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo provato varie soluzioni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We tried various solutions.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form; used before a plural feminine noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho letto varie notizie interessanti oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I read various interesting news stories today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Faccio il bagno nella vasca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I take a bath in the bathtub.

definitions.note: Used for a container that holds water or another liquid (e.g., a fish tank, a water basin).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La vasca dei pesci è in salotto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fish tank is in the living room.

definitions.note: Plural of "vasca".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nel bagno ci sono due vasche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the bathroom there are two tubs.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Metto i fiori nel vaso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the flowers in the vase.

definitions.note: Common in everyday Italian, especially for a glass of water or wine.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei un vaso d’acqua, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like a glass of water, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Metto le tazze sul vassoio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the cups on the tray.

definitions.note: Often used for very large areas or abstract things like a “vasto problema” (a vast problem).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il deserto è vasto e silenzioso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The desert is vast and silent.

definitions.note: Command form: informal singular imperative of "andarsene" (used to tell one person to leave).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vattene subito!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Go away right now!

definitions.note: Clitic pronoun form of "vi", used especially before another clitic pronoun (e.g., "ve lo", "ve ne").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ve lo dico subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m telling you right away.

definitions.note: plural masculine form of "vecchio"; used for a group of men or mixed gender.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I miei nonni sono vecchi, ma molto attivi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandparents are old, but very active.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "vecchio".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La mia nonna è vecchia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandmother is old.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In vecchiaia, mio nonno cammina più lentamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In old age, my grandpa walks more slowly.

definitions.note: feminine plural form of "vecchio"; used with feminine plural nouns
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quelle sedie sono vecchie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those chairs are old.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo libro è molto vecchio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book is very old.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quel vecchio vive da solo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That old man lives alone.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive of "vedere" (used after expressions like "spero che...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che tu veda la differenza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you see the difference.

definitions.note: Usually used with the subjunctive (e.g. after "che") meaning "that they see"; it can also be used as a formal/plural command.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che vedano il problema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope they see the problem.

definitions.note: third-person singular (he/she/it) present tense of "vedere"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui vede una macchina rossa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He sees a red car.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto), 1st person plural of "vedere"; common in writing and in some regions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri vedemmo un film molto bello.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday we saw a very nice movie.

definitions.note: Gerund of "vedere"; often means "while seeing" or "by seeing," depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vedendo la pioggia, ho preso l’ombrello.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Seeing the rain, I took the umbrella.

definitions.note: Often used with ci in expressions like “non riesco a vederci (bene)” = “I can’t see (well)”. Depending on context, ci can also refer to “us/each other/there”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non riesco a vederci bene senza occhiali.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't see well without glasses.

definitions.native: to be able to see, to see (well)
definitions.note: Often used when talking about eyesight or visibility (e.g. in the dark, without glasses).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Senza occhiali non riesco a vederci.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Without glasses I can’t see (well).

definitions.native: to see each other, to meet (up)
definitions.note: Commonly used to talk about meeting someone (often with a time: domani, stasera, ecc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Possiamo vederci domani?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can we see each other tomorrow?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio vedere il mare domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to see the sea tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used with movies/TV or when looking at something for a while.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stasera vogliamo vedere un film.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tonight we want to watch a movie.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “la” (“her” or “it” for a feminine noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero di vederla domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope to see her tomorrow.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “la” (= “her” or “it” for feminine nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non posso vederla oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t see her/it today.

definitions.note: Infinitive of "vedere" with the direct object pronoun "le" (= them, feminine plural) attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo vederle domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to see them tomorrow.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “li” (= them, masculine plural or mixed group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio vederli domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to see them tomorrow.

definitions.note: Infinitive + attached direct object pronoun: vedere + li (= them).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei vederli domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to see them tomorrow.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun "lo" (= "him" or "it", masculine singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non posso vederlo oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't see him today.

definitions.note: Infinitive "vedere" + clitic pronoun "mi" (me). Often used after modal verbs (e.g., "puoi", "vuoi").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi vedermi domani?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you see me tomorrow?

definitions.note: Infinitive + attached object pronoun (mi = “me”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi vedermi domani?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you see me tomorrow?

definitions.note: infinitive + direct object pronoun “ti” (“you”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero di vederti domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope to see you tomorrow.

definitions.note: Infinitive of "vedere" with the direct object pronoun "ti" (you) attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non vedo l'ora di vederti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't wait to see you.

definitions.note: Includes the object pronoun “vi” (= you plural, or formal you).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero di vedervi domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope to see you tomorrow.

definitions.note: "vi" is the object pronoun for "you" (plural) and is also used as a polite form for "you" (singular) in some contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero di vedervi presto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope to see you soon.

definitions.note: "vi" can also mean "there" (referring to a place).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non posso vedervi da qui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t see there from here.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form, often used in hypothetical clauses (e.g., after "se" or "che").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se vedesse il problema, capirebbe subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If he saw the problem, he would understand right away.

definitions.note: Second person plural (voi) present tense of "vedere"; also used as formal "you" in some contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vedete quella casa bianca?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you (all) see that white house?

definitions.note: Imperfect past (ongoing or habitual action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da casa, vedeva il mare ogni mattina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: From home, she/he used to see the sea every morning.

definitions.note: First-person singular, imperfect tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da bambino, vedevo spesso le stelle dalla finestra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As a child, I often saw the stars from the window.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) present of "vedere"; often used to point something out (like "you see," / "look").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vedi quella macchina rossa?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you see that red car?

definitions.note: Also commonly used to mean “let’s see.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vediamo il film stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re watching the movie tonight.

definitions.note: 1st person singular (io) present tense of “vedere”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vedo un cane nel parco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see a dog in the park.

definitions.note: Third-person plural ("they") present tense of "vedere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vedono la montagna dalla finestra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They see the mountain from the window.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo molti anni di matrimonio, è rimasta vedova.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After many years of marriage, she became a widow.

definitions.note: Second-person singular simple future of "vedere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vedrai che andrà tutto bene.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’ll see that everything will be fine.

definitions.note: future tense, 1st person plural of "vedere"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani vedremo il nuovo film al cinema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will see the new movie at the cinema.

definitions.note: Second person plural (voi), future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se venite domani, vedrete la città con più calma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you come tomorrow, you will see the city more calmly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani vedrà i suoi amici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow he/she will see his/her friends.

definitions.note: First-person singular future tense of "vedere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani vedrò il medico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will see the doctor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dalla terrazza ci sono due vedute sul mare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: From the terrace there are two views of the sea.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form; used for a woman or a feminine noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mia sorella è vegana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is vegan.

definitions.note: Plural form (masculine plural, or mixed-gender group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I miei amici sono vegani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My friends are vegan.

definitions.note: Used for both people and things (e.g., a vegan person or vegan food).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio fratello è vegano e non mangia carne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is vegan and doesn't eat meat.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei è vegetariana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is vegetarian.

definitions.note: feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le opzioni vegetariane sono chiaramente indicate nel menu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The vegetarian options are clearly indicated on the menu.

definitions.note: plural masculine form; used for a group of men or a mixed-gender group
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I miei amici sono vegetariani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My friends are vegetarian.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio fratello è vegetariano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is vegetarian.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo veicolo è molto comodo per viaggiare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This vehicle is very comfortable for traveling.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il vento gonfia la vela della barca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wind fills the boat's sail.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Accendo una vela sul tavolo.
