definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I light a candle on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Attenzione: quella sostanza è veleno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Careful: that substance is poison.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form (used with feminine nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quella pianta è velenosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That plant is poisonous.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form; can describe things that contain poison or animals that inject venom.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Attenzione: questi funghi sono velenosi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Careful: these mushrooms are poisonous.

definitions.note: Often used for poisonous substances or toxic/venomous animals; it can also be used figuratively for “malicious” words or comments.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quel serpente è velenoso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That snake is venomous.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il treno è molto veloce.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train is very fast.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Parla veloce quando è nervoso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He speaks quickly when he’s nervous.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Parla velocemente perché ha fretta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He speaks quickly because he's in a hurry.

definitions.note: plural form (masculine or feminine)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le auto veloci consumano più benzina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Fast cars use more gasoline.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La velocità massima su questa strada è 50 km/h.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The maximum speed on this road is 50 km/h.

definitions.note: Used in the present subjunctive (e.g., after expressions like "spero che...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che lui venda la macchina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope he sells the car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui vende la sua macchina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He sells his car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto vendendo la mia vecchia bici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m selling my old bike.

definitions.note: Future tense (2nd person singular) of "vendere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani venderai la tua bici?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Will you sell your bike tomorrow?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio vendere la mia macchina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to sell my car.

definitions.native: to sell it, to sell her
definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “la” (feminine singular), meaning “it” (for a feminine noun) or “her.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei venderla domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like to sell it tomorrow.

definitions.note: Infinitive "vendere" with the direct object pronoun "li" (= them) attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dobbiamo venderli prima della fine del mese.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to sell them before the end of the month.

definitions.note: Third-person singular future tense of "vendere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani venderà la sua macchina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow he/she will sell his/her car.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (voi) form of "vendere" in the present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vendete le mele al mercato ogni sabato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You sell the apples at the market every Saturday.

definitions.note: Often used for a personal or long-standing desire for revenge.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha giurato vendetta contro chi lo ha tradito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He swore revenge against the person who betrayed him.

definitions.note: past historic (passato remoto), third-person singular
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nel 2005 vendette la sua macchina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In 2005, he/she sold his/her car.

definitions.note: past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nel 1998 vendettero la loro casa al mare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In 1998 they sold their house by the sea.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) form, used especially in written stories and in some regions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri vendetti la mia vecchia bici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I sold my old bike.

definitions.note: present tense (tu): “you sell”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vendi la tua bici?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you selling your bike?

definitions.note: imperative (tu): “sell!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vendi questo libro online.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sell this book online.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vendiamo frutta fresca al mercato ogni sabato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We sell fresh fruit at the market every Saturday.

definitions.note: Plural of "vendita".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le vendite sono aumentate questo mese.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sales increased this month.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il venditore mi ha mostrato un modello più economico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The salesperson showed me a cheaper model.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vendo la mia bici domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m selling my bike tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Al mercato vendono frutta e verdura fresca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the market they sell fresh fruit and vegetables.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle; often used in the passive with essere/venire or as an adjective
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La casa è stata venduta la settimana scorsa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The house was sold last week.

definitions.note: feminine plural past participle of "vendere"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le case sono state vendute ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The houses were sold yesterday.

definitions.note: past participle (masculine plural) of “vendere”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I biglietti sono già stati venduti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tickets have already been sold.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho già venduto la macchina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve already sold the car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le vene delle mani sono molto visibili.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The veins in the hands are very visible.

definitions.note: Used with a past participle to form a passive construction (equivalent to English “being + past participle”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stava venendo interrogato dalla polizia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was being questioned by the police.

definitions.note: gerund form of “venire”; often used like “while coming/when coming” or to form the present continuous with “stare” (e.g., “sta venendo” = “is coming”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto venendo a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m coming home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci vediamo venerdì sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: See you Friday evening.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary with a past participle to form the passive voice (often in more formal Italian), especially in the subjunctive after expressions like “è importante che…”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È importante che venga rispettata la legge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that the law be respected.

definitions.note: Used either in the present subjunctive (e.g., after "che") or as a formal command (Lei form), like “Come!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Venga qui, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come here, please.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary to form the passive voice (often emphasizing the action).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che i documenti vengano firmati oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope the documents are signed today.

definitions.note: present subjunctive, 3rd person plural (used after expressions of doubt, desire, necessity, etc.)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che vengano alla festa stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope they come to the party tonight.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary with a past participle to form the passive (similar to “to get” / “to be” in English), often emphasizing the action happening.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vengo chiamato spesso dal mio capo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I get called often by my boss.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “I’m coming” (e.g., in response to someone calling you).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vengo subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m coming right away.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary with a past participle to form the passive voice.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I documenti vengono firmati dal direttore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The documents are signed by the director.

definitions.note: third-person plural present tense of “venire”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vengono a casa mia ogni sabato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They come to my house every Saturday.

definitions.note: Present tense (noi) of "venire"; it can also mean "we are coming" depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Veniamo a casa dopo la scuola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We come home after school.

definitions.note: Used with "che" in the present subjunctive for "voi" (you plural/formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che veniate alla festa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you come to the party.

definitions.note: Poetic/archaic shortened form of “venire”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo sento venir da lontano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hear him coming from far away.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary to form the passive voice (often instead of “essere”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il lavoro deve venire fatto oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The work must be done today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vengo a casa tua alle otto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm coming to your house at eight.

definitions.note: Infinitive of "venire" with the attached pronoun "mi" (= to me). Often used before another infinitive (e.g., "venirmi a prendere" = come pick me up).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi venirmi a prendere alle otto?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you come pick me up at eight?

definitions.note: Used with a past participle to form the passive in the imperfect subjunctive (e.g., "venisse fatto" = "were done").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se la porta venisse aperta, entrerei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If the door were opened, I would come in.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive of "venire"; used after expressions like "speravo che...", "volevo che...".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Speravo che venisse alla festa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hoped he would come to the party.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form (used in hypothetical clauses like “if …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se venissi domani, saremmo molto felici.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you came tomorrow, we would be very happy.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 2nd person plural of "venire"; common in writing and storytelling, less in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Veniste qui molto tempo fa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You came here a long time ago.

definitions.note: Second-person plural form (“you all”); can be present tense or the imperative.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Venite spesso qui?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you come here often?

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing/repeated action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ogni estate veniva al mare con noi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every summer he/she used to come to the sea with us.

definitions.note: imperfect past (they)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ogni estate venivano al mare con noi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every summer they used to come to the seaside with us.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary in the passive voice (more common in formal/literary Italian), like English “was” in “was done/was made.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Venne arrestato dalla polizia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was arrested by the police.

definitions.note: Third-person singular passato remoto of "venire"; common in narration/literary Italian (often corresponds to "è venuto/a" in everyday speech).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Poi venne a casa mia e mi raccontò tutto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Then he came to my house and told me everything.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary with a past participle to form a passive meaning (often in narratives).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Venne ro arrestati dalla polizia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were arrested by the police.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) form of "venire"; common in written narratives and formal storytelling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Venero a trovarci la settimana scorsa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They came to visit us last week.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary with a past participle to form a passive meaning (literary/less common).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Venni invitato alla festa, ma non potei andare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was invited to the party, but I couldn’t go.

definitions.note: Passato remoto (historic past), 1st person singular of "venire"; common in narratives and some regions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando venni a sapere la verità, rimasi in silenzio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I found out the truth, I stayed silent.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho venti euro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have twenty euros.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Accendo il ventilatore perché fa caldo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I turn on the fan because it’s hot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi c’è molto vento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today there’s a lot of wind.

definitions.note: past participle (feminine singular), often used with essere in compound tenses
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei è venuta ieri sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She came last night.

definitions.note: feminine plural past participle of "venire"; often used with "essere" in compound tenses
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le ragazze sono venute ieri sera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The girls came last night.

definitions.note: Masculine plural past participle of "venire"; commonly used with "essere" in compound tenses (e.g., "sono venuti").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I miei amici sono venuti a casa mia ieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My friends came to my house yesterday.

definitions.note: Past participle of "venire"; often used with "essere" and agrees in gender/number ("venuto" = masculine singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono venuto a casa presto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I came home early.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una storia vera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a true story.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono veramente stanco oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m really tired today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi piace la maglietta verde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like the green T-shirt.

definitions.note: used as a noun: the color green
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il verde è il mio colore preferito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Green is my favorite color.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il giudice ha letto il verdetto in tribunale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The judge read the verdict in court.

definitions.note: plural form (masculine or mixed gender) of "verde"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato due peperoni verdi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought two green peppers.

definitions.note: Usually used as an uncountable noun in Italian (e.g., “mangiare verdura” = “eat vegetables”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo comprare la verdura per la cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to buy vegetables for dinner.

definitions.note: Plural form of "verdura"; often used to mean vegetables in general.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mangio verdure ogni giorno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I eat vegetables every day.

definitions.note: feminine plural form of "vero"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono storie vere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are true stories.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho provato vergogna dopo aver mentito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I felt shame after lying.

definitions.note: Commonly used with the reflexive pronoun “si”: “si vergogna” = “is ashamed.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lui si vergogna di parlare in pubblico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is ashamed to speak in public.

definitions.note: Usually used with a direct object (shaming someone). For “to be ashamed,” Italian typically uses the reflexive form “vergognarsi.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non voglio vergognare la mia famiglia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to shame my family.

definitions.note: Reflexive verb (used with reflexive pronouns like mi/ti/si).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi vergogno di quello che ho detto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m ashamed of what I said.

definitions.note: Infinitive of the reflexive verb "vergognarsi" with the object pronoun "ti" attached ("yourself"). Often used in phrases like "Dovresti vergognarti!"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dovresti vergognarti!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You should be ashamed of yourself!

definitions.note: In modern Italian this meaning is most commonly expressed with the reflexive form: “si vergognava”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vergognava di quello che aveva detto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She was ashamed of what he/she had said.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing/repeated in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da bambino, mi vergognavo quando dovevo parlare davanti alla classe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As a child, I was ashamed/embarrassed when I had to speak in front of the class.

definitions.note: Most often used reflexively as “mi vergogno (di ...)” = “I’m ashamed (of ...)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi vergogno di quello che ho detto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m ashamed of what I said.

definitions.note: feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È stata una decisione vergognosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was a shameful decision.

definitions.note: feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Che situazione vergognosa!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What an embarrassing situation!

definitions.note: plural masculine form of "vero"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questi fatti sono veri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These facts are true.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prima di inviare il modulo, fai una verifica dei dati.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Before sending the form, do a check of the data.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi verificare l’indirizzo, per favore?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you check the address, please?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo fatto alcune verifiche prima di firmare il contratto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We did some checks before signing the contract.

definitions.note: Common in school contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani ho due verifiche di matematica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I have two math tests.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dimmi la verità, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tell me the truth, please.

definitions.note: Usually written with the accent as “verità”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dimmi la verità.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tell me the truth.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’è un verme nella mela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There’s a worm in the apple.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono vermi nel compost.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are worms in the compost.

definitions.note: Often refers to a protective or glossy coating (like varnish), but can also mean paint in general depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La vernice è ancora fresca, non toccarla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The paint is still fresh, don’t touch it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una storia vera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a true story.

definitions.note: Used as a short interjection to ask for confirmation (like “right?” or “really?”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani vieni con noi, vero?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re coming with us tomorrow, right?

definitions.note: Often used with the article: "il vero" = "the truth".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dimmi il vero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tell me the truth.

definitions.note: This form is from the verb "venire" (not "essere"); it means "you will come" (future, 2nd person singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani verrai alla festa?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Will you come to the party tomorrow?

definitions.note: Future simple (futuro semplice), 2nd person singular (tu) of “venire”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani verrai con noi?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Will you come with us tomorrow?

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary with a past participle to form the passive voice (e.g., “verranno aperte” = “will be opened”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le porte verranno aperte alle otto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doors will be opened at eight.

definitions.note: 3rd person plural (they) future tense of "venire".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani verranno a casa nostra per cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow they will come to our house for dinner.

definitions.note: Conditional form of “venire” (used for hypotheticals or polite requests).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se avesse tempo, verrebbe con noi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If he had time, he would come with us.

definitions.note: Second person plural future tense of "venire".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani verrete a cena da noi?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Will you (all) come to dinner at our place tomorrow?

definitions.note: Second person plural future tense of "venire".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A che ora verrete in stazione?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What time will you (all) arrive at the station?

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary in passive constructions (venire + past participle).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La cena verrà servita alle otto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Dinner will be served at eight.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular future of "venire" (he/she/it will come).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Verrà domani mattina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She will come tomorrow morning.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary with a past participle to form a passive meaning (similar to English “be” in the passive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Verrò contattato domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will be contacted tomorrow.

definitions.note: First-person singular, simple future of "venire".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani verrò a casa tua dopo il lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will come to your house after work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho versato l’acqua, ma era già versata sul pavimento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I poured the water, but it was already spilled on the floor.

definitions.note: Often used for money (e.g., a sum that has been paid into an account).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La quota è già stata versata sul conto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fee has already been paid into the account.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Marta è molto versatile: sa cucinare, riparare le cose e parlare tre lingue.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Marta is very versatile: she can cook, fix things, and speak three languages.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho versato l’acqua nel bicchiere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I poured the water into the glass.

definitions.note: Often used with money (e.g., paying a fee or depositing money into a bank account).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho versato 50 euro sul conto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I deposited 50 euros into the account.

definitions.note: Form of "versare" (e.g., present subjunctive, or formal "Lei" command). Not related to English "verse(s)".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È importante che tu versi l’acqua lentamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that you pour the water slowly.

definitions.native: verses, lines (of a poem or song)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi piace leggere i versi di questa poesia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like reading the lines of this poem.

definitions.note: Used especially for the sounds animals make.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Di notte si sentono i versi dei lupi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At night you can hear the wolves’ cries.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preferisco questa versione del testo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prefer this version of the text.

definitions.note: used with a noun/pronoun to indicate direction (often like “in the direction of”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Andiamo verso casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s go toward home.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto) form of “versare” (common in writing and in some regions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Versò il vino nei bicchieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She poured the wine into the glasses.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto) form of “versare”, used especially for payments/deposits.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Versò un acconto di cento euro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She paid a deposit of one hundred euros.

definitions.note: Plural form; often used when talking about having dizzy spells (e.g. “avere le vertigini”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho le vertigini quando mi alzo troppo in fretta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I get dizzy when I stand up too fast.

definitions.note: Often used with a direct object (someone being dressed).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei veste il bambino ogni mattina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She dresses the child every morning.

definitions.note: Present gerund of "vestire"; often used with "stare" (e.g., "sto vestendo" = "I’m getting dressed / I’m dressing...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto vestendo i bambini.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m dressing the children.

definitions.note: Often used with a direct object (e.g., vestire un bambino = dress a child). When used reflexively (vestirsi), it means “to get dressed.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vesto i bambini prima di uscire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I dress the children before going out.

definitions.native: to get dressed, to dress oneself
definitions.note: Reflexive verb; it means putting clothes on yourself (not dressing someone else).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi vesto in fretta ogni mattina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I get dressed quickly every morning.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "vestire"; used with "essere" or in passive-like meanings
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si è vestita in fretta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She got dressed quickly.

definitions.note: feminine singular
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lei è sempre vestita di nero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is always dressed in black.

definitions.note: feminine plural; used to describe women or feminine plural nouns
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le bambine sono già vestite per la festa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The girls are already dressed for the party.

definitions.note: Informal (tu) command, from the reflexive verb "vestirsi".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vestiti in fretta!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Get dressed quickly!

definitions.note: plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I bambini sono già vestiti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are already dressed.

definitions.note: Plural of "vestito"; often used generally for clothing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo comprare dei vestiti nuovi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to buy some new clothes.

definitions.note: past participle of "vestire"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho vestito il bambino in fretta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I dressed the child quickly.

definitions.note: Adjective (masculine singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando è arrivato, era già vestito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he arrived, he was already dressed.

definitions.note: Often refers to a (typically women’s) dress; more generally it can mean an item of clothing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho comprato un vestito nuovo per la festa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a new dress for the party.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) form, used mainly in written narratives and in some regions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando arrivò la notizia, si vestì in fretta e uscì.
