definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mia sorella vive a Milano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister lives in Milan.

definitions.note: feminine plural form (e.g., "le tradizioni vive")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le tradizioni sono ancora vive.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The traditions are still alive.

definitions.note: gerund form of "vivere"; often used to describe an action in progress (like English "while ...-ing").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sto vivendo a Roma da due mesi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve been living in Rome for two months.

definitions.note: Often used in more formal contexts (e.g., “essere vivente” = “living being”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È l’animale vivente più veloce sulla terra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s the fastest living animal on Earth.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio vivere in Italia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to live in Italy.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form of "vivere"; often used after expressions like "se" (if) or "volevo che" (I wanted that).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se vivesse qui, sarebbe più felice.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If he lived here, he would be happier.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (voi) present tense of "vivere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vivete in centro o in periferia?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you live downtown or in the suburbs?

definitions.note: Second-person plural (voi) present tense; can express an ongoing action depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In questo momento vivete una situazione difficile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Right now you are living through a difficult situation.

definitions.note: imperfect tense (past), used for an ongoing/habitual action in the past
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando ero piccolo, viveva in campagna.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was little, he/she was living in the countryside.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (past), used for ongoing/repeated actions or descriptions in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando eravamo bambini, vivevamo in campagna.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When we were kids, we lived in the countryside.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past, ongoing/habitual) for “they”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando eravamo studenti, vivevano in un appartamento vicino all’università.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When we were students, they lived in an apartment near the university.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (imperfect tense), 2nd person plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando eravate studenti, vivevate vicino all’università.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When you were students, you lived near the university.

definitions.note: second person singular, imperfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando eri a Roma, vivevi vicino al Colosseo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When you were in Rome, you lived near the Colosseum.

definitions.note: First-person singular, imperfect (past habitual/ongoing) of "vivere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando vivevo a Roma, prendevo il caffè al bar ogni mattina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I lived in Rome, I would have coffee at the café every morning.

definitions.note: Present tense (tu form) of "vivere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dove vivi?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Where do you live?

definitions.note: Imperative (tu form) of "vivere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vivi il momento!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Live in the moment!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I tuoi nonni sono ancora vivi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your grandparents are still alive.

definitions.note: Often used for colors (e.g., "colori vivi").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preferisco colori vivi in estate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prefer vivid/bright colors in the summer.

definitions.note: Present tense (noi) form of "vivere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viviamo a Milano da due anni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have been living in Milan for two years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vivo a Milano da tre anni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I live in Milan (and have lived there) for three years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È ancora vivo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is still alive.

definitions.note: Often used for bright colors or an energetic tone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il colore è molto vivo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The color is very vivid.

definitions.note: present tense (they)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vivono a Milano da tre anni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They have lived in Milan for three years.

definitions.note: Future tense (3rd person singular): “he/she/it will live.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se mangia bene, vivrà più a lungo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If he eats well, he will live longer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ognuno ha i suoi vizi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Everyone has their vices.

definitions.note: Often used for a child or person who gets everything they want.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una bambina molto viziata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is a very spoiled child.

definitions.note: Can describe food or something that has gone bad or been contaminated.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'acqua è viziata, non berla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The water is tainted—don’t drink it.

definitions.note: Often used for a child or someone who has been indulged too much.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un ragazzo viziato e pretende sempre tutto subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s a spoiled boy and he always expects everything right away.

definitions.note: Also used for food or products that are no longer good.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo latte è viziato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This milk has gone bad.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fumare è un vizio difficile da lasciare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Smoking is a bad habit that's hard to quit.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devo studiare il vocabolario per l’esame di italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to study the vocabulary for the Italian exam.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho cercato questa parola nel vocabolario.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I looked up this word in the dictionary.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In italiano ci sono cinque vocali: a, e, i, o, u.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In Italian there are five vowels: a, e, i, o, u.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho riconosciuto la sua voce al telefono.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I recognized his voice on the phone.

definitions.note: Often used in set phrases like “una voce del menu” or “una voce della lista”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa voce del menu non funziona.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This menu item doesn’t work.

definitions.note: Plural of "voce".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sento delle voci nella stanza accanto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hear voices in the next room.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preferisco la vodka liscia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prefer vodka straight.

definitions.note: Often used in phrases like "avere voglia di" (to feel like / want to do something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho voglia di un caffè.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel like having a coffee.

definitions.note: Used with "che" + subjunctive (e.g., after verbs like "spero", "penso", "è possibile"). It can also act as a modal meaning "want to".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che tu voglia venire con noi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you want to come with us.

definitions.note: Subjunctive form of "volere" (used often after "che", e.g. "spero che..."). It can also be used as a formal imperative ("Voglia...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spero che tu voglia venire domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you want to come tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vogliamo andare al mare domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We want to go to the seaside tomorrow.

definitions.note: First-person plural present tense of "volere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vogliamo un caffè, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We want a coffee, please.

definitions.note: Often used before an infinitive to make a suggestion (literally: "we want to...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vogliamo andare al cinema stasera?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Shall we go to the cinema tonight?

definitions.note: present subjunctive, 3rd person plural (used after expressions like “è importante che…”, “penso che…”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È importante che vogliano partire presto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that they want to leave early.

definitions.note: Very formal/polite request, usually followed by an infinitive (e.g., “vogliate attendere”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vogliate attendere un momento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please wait a moment.

definitions.note: Often used in very formal or polite requests (especially in writing), where it can sound like “please” + verb (e.g., “Vogliate…” = “Please…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vogliate chiudere la porta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please close the door.

definitions.note: Often used with an infinitive to mean “want to …”; it can sound more direct than “vorrei” (“I would like”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio andare a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to go home.

definitions.note: Present tense, 1st person singular (io) of "volere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio un caffè, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want a coffee, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vogliono andare a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They want to go home.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense of “volere” (used with “they” or “you all”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vogliono andare al cinema stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They want to go to the cinema tonight.

definitions.note: Second-person plural pronoun (“you all”). In some contexts (especially older or regional), it can also be used as a formal singular “you”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voi siete pronti?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you all ready?

definitions.note: Present tense (lui/lei) or imperative (tu) of "volare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L'aereo vola sopra la città.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plane flies over the city.

definitions.note: gerund form of "volare"; often used like English "-ing" (e.g., "while flying")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho visto un'aquila volando sopra la valle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw an eagle flying over the valley.

definitions.note: Can mean “they fly” or “you (plural) fly,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gli uccelli volano alto nel cielo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The birds fly high in the sky.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abbiamo visto un disco volante nel cielo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We saw a flying saucer in the sky.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tieni le mani sul volante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Keep your hands on the steering wheel.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho preso un volante all’ingresso del museo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I picked up a flyer at the entrance of the museum.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi piace volare in aereo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like to fly on a plane.

definitions.note: 2nd person plural (voi) present tense of "volare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se avete le ali, volate molto in alto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you have wings, you fly very high.

definitions.note: 2nd person plural (voi) imperative of "volare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Volate con calma e restate insieme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Fly calmly and stay together.

definitions.note: past participle of "volare"; used with "essere" in compound tenses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sono già volato a Roma due volte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have already flown to Rome twice.

definitions.note: Often used as a friendly way to accept or say you’re happy to do something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ti aiuto volentieri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll gladly help you.

definitions.note: Poetic/old shortened form of "volere" (infinitive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È difficile voler cambiare subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s hard to want to change right away.

definitions.note: Shortened form of "volere", common before another infinitive (e.g. "voler fare"); can sound more literary or formal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È inutile voler convincerlo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s useless to want to convince him.

definitions.note: Often used as a modal (auxiliary) before another verb: "volere + infinitive" = "want to + verb".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio andare a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to go home.

definitions.note: Often used with an infinitive: "voglio + infinitive" = "I want to + verb".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voglio volere meno cose e vivere più semplicemente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to want fewer things and live more simply.

definitions.note: Common in expressions like "che cosa vuoi dire?" = "what do you mean?".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Che cosa vuole dire questa parola?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What does this word mean?

definitions.note: Conditional present, 1st person singular (io).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Volerei in Italia domani, ma non ho i soldi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would fly to Italy tomorrow, but I don't have the money.

definitions.note: Infinitive of "volere" with the direct object pronoun "lo" attached ("it").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Posso volerlo, ma non posso averlo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can want it, but I can't have it.

definitions.note: Subjunctive (imperfect) form of "volere"; often used after "se" (if) or when expressing wishes/uncertainty.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se volesse venire, sarebbe il benvenuto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If he wanted to come, he would be welcome.

definitions.note: Subjunctive imperfect form of “volere”, often used after “che” to express what someone wanted or would have wanted in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non credevo che volesse venire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn’t think he wanted to come.

definitions.note: Used in the imperfect subjunctive (io/tu), often in sentences like “if I/you wanted …” (se volessi …).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se volessi, potrei aiutarti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I wanted, I could help you.

definitions.note: Can be the 2nd person plural (voi) passato remoto of "volere" (often in writing/literature).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alla fine voleste andare via.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end you wanted to leave.

definitions.note: Can be the 2nd person plural (voi) imperfect subjunctive of "volere" (often after "se", "benché", etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se voleste venire, sareste i benvenuti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you wanted to come, you’d be welcome.

definitions.note: Used with an infinitive to say what someone wants to do.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Volete andare al cinema stasera?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you want to go to the cinema tonight?

definitions.note: Second-person plural ("you" plural/formal) present tense of "volere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Volete un caffè?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you want a coffee?

definitions.note: Imperfect form of "volere" used as a modal auxiliary before another verb (e.g., "voleva andare" = "wanted to go").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voleva andare a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wanted to go home.

definitions.note: Imperfetto (past) form of "volere"; often used for ongoing/repeated wanting in the past, or as a polite/softened request.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri voleva andare al mare, ma pioveva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday he/she wanted to go to the sea, but it was raining.

definitions.note: Imperfect (noi): often translated as “we wanted” or “we used to want,” frequently followed by an infinitive (“wanted to …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Volevamo comprare una casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We wanted to buy a house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri volevamo andare al cinema, ma pioveva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday we wanted to go to the cinema, but it was raining.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Volevano partire presto, ma era troppo tardi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They wanted to leave early, but it was too late.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense: describes an ongoing or habitual wanting in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da piccoli volevano sempre andare al parco dopo scuola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When they were little, they always wanted to go to the park after school.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (voi) imperfect of "volere"; often used with an infinitive (e.g., "volevate andare" = "you wanted to go").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Volevate andare al cinema, ma era troppo tardi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You wanted to go to the cinema, but it was too late.

definitions.note: second-person plural (“you” plural) imperfect
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri volevate andare al mare, ma pioveva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday you wanted to go to the sea, but it was raining.

definitions.note: Often used with an infinitive to mean “wanted to …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Volevi andare al cinema, ma eri stanco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You wanted to go to the cinema, but you were tired.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (informal singular “you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cosa volevi dire?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What did you want to say?

definitions.note: Often used to make polite requests or introductions (e.g. “volevo chiederti…” = “I wanted to ask you…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Volevo un caffè, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wanted a coffee, please.

definitions.note: Imperfect past (io) of "volere"; often used for a past desire or intention, or to make a request sound polite.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Volevo parlarti un momento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wanted to talk to you for a moment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Con questo biglietto voli a Roma domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With this ticket you fly to Rome tomorrow.

definitions.note: Plural of "volo".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono molti voli per Roma oggi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many flights to Rome today.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto) form of "volere"; common in written narratives and formal storytelling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando lo vide, volle parlarle subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he saw her, he wanted to talk to her right away.

definitions.note: past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri vollero partire presto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday they wanted to leave early.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il mio volo parte alle otto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My flight leaves at eight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I volontari aiutano durante la raccolta di cibo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The volunteers help during the food drive.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Faccio volontariato ogni sabato mattina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I do volunteering every Saturday morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La partecipazione al corso è volontaria.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Participation in the course is voluntary.

definitions.note: As an adjective, it describes someone who offers to do something without being paid or required.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È un assistente volontario nella biblioteca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a volunteer assistant at the library.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio fratello è un volontario in ospedale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is a volunteer at the hospital.

definitions.note: Often used for willpower, intention, or determination (not usually for a last will/testament).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci vuole molta volontà per smettere di fumare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It takes a lot of willpower to quit smoking.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non ho la volontà di uscire stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't feel like going out tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho visto una volpe nel bosco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw a fox in the woods.

definitions.note: plural of "volpe" (fox)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Di notte, nel bosco, si vedono spesso le volpi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At night, in the woods, you often see foxes.

definitions.note: Very common in set phrases like "una volta" (= once) and "a volte" (= sometimes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È la prima volta che vengo qui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s the first time I come here.

definitions.note: Often used as an imperative (“Turn!”) or as “he/she turns,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Volta a destra al semaforo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Turn right at the traffic light.

definitions.note: Can be used as a command to more than one person (“you” plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voltate a destra al semaforo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Turn right at the traffic light.

definitions.note: Plural of "volta" (e.g., how many times something happens).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono andato due volte questa settimana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I went there two times this week.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive, often used after "che" (e.g., "È importante che tu volti...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È importante che tu volti a destra al semaforo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that you turn right at the traffic light.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho visto molti volti felici alla festa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw many happy faces at the party.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il suo volto è familiare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His/Her face looks familiar.

definitions.note: Can mean the volume (sound level) or a book volume (one book in a series).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puoi abbassare il volume, per favore?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you turn down the volume, please?

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of "volere"; often used like an adjective (e.g., a planned/intended choice).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È una decisione voluta da tutti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a decision wanted by everyone.

definitions.note: Feminine plural past participle of "volere"; often used like an adjective (e.g., "le modifiche volute" = "the desired changes").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le modifiche volute dal direttore sono state approvate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The changes wanted by the director were approved.

definitions.note: Masculine plural past participle of "volere"; often agrees with a masculine plural noun (e.g., "i documenti voluti").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha comprato i libri voluti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He bought the books he wanted.

definitions.note: Common in the impersonal expression "ci sono voluti" + time/number (e.g., "Ci sono voluti tre giorni" = "It took three days").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono voluti tre giorni per finire il lavoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It took three days to finish the work.

definitions.note: Past participle of "volere" (used for compound tenses like passato prossimo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho voluto parlare con te.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wanted to talk to you.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person singular of “volare”; common in narration and writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: L’aereo volò sopra le montagne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plane flew over the mountains.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi sento male: devo vomitare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel sick: I have to throw up.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho vomitato dopo cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I vomited after dinner.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo il viaggio in barca, vomitò subito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the boat trip, he/she vomited right away.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they) future tense of "volere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani vorranno partire presto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow they will want to leave early.

definitions.note: Used to express a wish or a polite request; it’s the conditional form of “volere”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrebbe un caffè, per favore?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Would you like a coffee, please?

definitions.note: 3rd person singular conditional of “volere” (used for polite requests or hypothetical desires).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrebbe un caffè, per favore?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Would you like a coffee, please?

definitions.note: Often used as a polite way to ask for something (common in orders and requests).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei un caffè, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like a coffee, please.

definitions.note: Conditional form of “volere”, commonly used for polite requests.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei un caffè, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like a coffee, please.

definitions.note: Conditional of "volere" used for polite requests or to express a desire.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorremmo un tavolo per due, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We would like a table for two, please.

definitions.native: we would like, we would want
definitions.note: Conditional form of “volere” used for polite requests or wishes.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorremmo un tavolo per due, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We would like a table for two, please.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (voi) conditional form, often used for polite requests or suggestions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: VorrestE un caffè o un tè?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Would you like a coffee or a tea?

definitions.note: Conditional, 2nd person plural (voi).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: VorrestE una tazza di tè?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Would you like a cup of tea?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorresti venire con noi?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Would you like to come with us?

definitions.note: Often used to make a polite request or offer.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorresti un caffè?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Would you like a coffee?

definitions.note: 3rd person singular future of "volere"; often used to mean "will" (to indicate future or intention).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrà venire con noi domani.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She will want to come with us tomorrow.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular future of "volere".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani vorrà parlare con te.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow he/she will want to talk to you.

definitions.note: Possessive determiner used when addressing more than one person (voi) or as a formal “your.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dov'è la vostra casa?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Where is your house?

definitions.note: feminine singular form (formal or plural “you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È la vostra casa?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Is it your house?

definitions.note: plural feminine form; used with feminine plural nouns
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dove sono le vostre chiavi?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Where are your keys?

definitions.note: Plural feminine form, used with feminine plural nouns (formal or plural “you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le vostre borse sono qui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your bags are here.

definitions.note: plural masculine form (used with masculine plural nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dove sono i vostri libri?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Where are your books?

definitions.note: Plural form (masculine) of the possessive pronoun/adjective meaning 'your' for 'voi' (you all / formal you).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questi libri sono vostri.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These books are yours.

definitions.note: Plural form used with "voi"; it can also be used as a formal singular "your" (as in letters or formal situations).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È vostro questo libro?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Is this book yours?

definitions.note: Used to address more than one person (plural “you”). It agrees in gender and number with the noun it refers to (e.g., vostro/vostra/vostri/vostre).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo è il vostro libro?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Is this your book?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mia sorella vota alle elezioni comunali.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister votes in the local elections.

definitions.note: Can also be used as an informal singular command (tu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vota con attenzione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Vote carefully.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani vado a votare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I'm going to vote.

definitions.note: Simple past (passato remoto), 3rd person plural, of "votare".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I cittadini votarono per il nuovo sindaco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The citizens voted for the new mayor.

definitions.note: Second-person plural ("you all") present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Votate sempre alle elezioni comunali?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you always vote in the local elections?

definitions.note: Second-person plural ("you all") command (imperative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Votate per il vostro candidato preferito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Vote for your preferred candidate.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho già votato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve already voted.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domenica voterai alle elezioni comunali.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On Sunday you will vote in the municipal elections.

definitions.note: third person singular (he/she/it) in the future tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Domani voterà alle elezioni comunali.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow he/she will vote in the local elections.

definitions.note: Used most commonly as the present subjunctive (e.g., “che tu voti” = “that you vote”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È importante che tu voti alle elezioni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that you vote in the election.

definitions.note: Plural of "voto".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I voti saranno contati stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The votes will be counted tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho già espresso il mio voto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have already cast my vote.

definitions.note: Used especially for school/university grades.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho preso un buon voto all’esame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got a good grade on the exam.

definitions.note: Past historic (passato remoto), 3rd person singular of “votare”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ieri il Parlamento votò la nuova legge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday Parliament voted on the new law.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dopo l’operazione mi sentivo ancora vulnerabile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the operation I still felt vulnerable.

definitions.note: Used with an infinitive to mean “want to …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vuoi un caffè?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you want a coffee?

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vuoi un caffè?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you want a coffee?

definitions.note: Common in speech and writing as a shortened form of “vuole” (he/she/it wants).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Non vuol venire con noi stasera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She doesn't want to come with us tonight.

definitions.note: Often used in the expression “vuol dire” (= “means”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Che cosa vuol dire questa parola?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What does this word mean?

definitions.note: Often used before an infinitive as a modal/auxiliary verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vuole andare a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She wants to go home.

definitions.note: Can also mean “you want” when addressing someone formally (Lei).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vuole andare a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She wants to go home.

definitions.note: Commonly used in the expression “ci vuole” to mean “it takes / it is needed.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci vuole tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It takes time.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "vuoto".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La bottiglia è vuota.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bottle is empty.

definitions.note: feminine plural form of "vuoto"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le bottiglie sono vuote.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bottles are empty.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il bicchiere è vuoto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The glass is empty.

definitions.note: Often used with the definite article: “il vuoto” (the void/emptiness).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: C’è un vuoto nel mio stomaco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There’s an empty feeling in my stomach.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per colazione mangio un waffle con sciroppo d'acero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For breakfast I eat a waffle with maple syrup.

definitions.note: Usually refers to the green Japanese horseradish paste served with sushi.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorrei un po' di wasabi, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like a little wasabi, please.

definitions.note: Often used like in English; common in expressions like "il web" (the web).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho trovato questa ricetta sul web.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found this recipe on the web.

definitions.note: Commonly used in Italian; often written as two words: "week end".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo weekend vado al mare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This weekend I’m going to the seaside.

definitions.note: Usually refers to the movie/book genre about the American Old West.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stasera guardiamo un western.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tonight we’re watching a western.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preferisco il whisky senza ghiaccio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prefer whisky without ice.

definitions.note: Often used as an invariable masculine noun in Italian (il windsurf).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: D’estate faccio windsurf al mare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the summer I do windsurfing at the sea.

definitions.note: Used to express surprise, admiration, or excitement.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wow, che bello questo posto!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wow, this place is so beautiful!

definitions.note: Used in Italian as an English loanword, especially for the sport/entertainment shown on TV.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio fratello guarda il wrestling in TV ogni settimana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother watches wrestling on TV every week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il bambino suona lo xilofono a scuola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The child plays the xylophone at school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hanno comprato uno yacht nuovo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They bought a new yacht.

definitions.note: Japanese currency; in Italian it’s usually invariable (same form in singular and plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questo ristorante accetta anche gli yen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This restaurant also accepts yen.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Faccio yoga due volte a settimana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I do yoga twice a week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mangio uno yogurt a colazione.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I eat a yogurt for breakfast.

definitions.note: Chinese currency unit (the renminbi).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quanto costa in yuan?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How much does it cost in yuan?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho messo i libri nello zaino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the books in my backpack.

definitions.note: plural of "zampa"; used especially for animals (and sometimes jokingly for people’s hands/feet).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Il cane ha le zampe sporche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog has dirty paws.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stanotte una zanzara mi ha punto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A mosquito bit me last night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In estate ci sono troppe zanzare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In summer there are too many mosquitoes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La zebra corre nella savana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The zebra runs in the savanna.

definitions.note: plural of "zebra"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Al safari abbiamo visto due zebre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On the safari we saw two zebras.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho zero euro in tasca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have zero euros in my pocket.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mia zia vive a Firenze.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My aunt lives in Florence.

definitions.note: plural of “zio”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: I miei zii vivono a Milano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My uncles live in Milan.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mio zio vive a Firenze.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My uncle lives in Florence.

definitions.note: Often used to tell a woman or girl to be quiet (feminine form); can sound rude depending on tone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zitta, per favore: sto ascoltando.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Shh, please: I’m listening.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "zitto"; often used as an instruction meaning “be quiet.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stai zitta, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Be quiet, please.

definitions.note: feminine plural form of "zitto" (said especially to people/animals to tell them not to speak or make noise)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bambine, state zitte per favore!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Girls, please be quiet!

definitions.note: Plural form of "zitto"; often used as an informal command meaning “be quiet!” when addressing more than one person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: State zitti, per favore!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Be quiet, please!

definitions.note: Often used as an invariable adjective/adverb meaning “be quiet!” (e.g., “Stai zitto!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stai zitto, per favore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Be quiet, please.

definitions.note: Used to tell someone to be quiet; can sound blunt or rude depending on tone and context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zitto! Sto ascoltando.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Quiet! I'm listening.

definitions.note: Same meaning as in English; commonly used in movies, games, and horror contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nel film c'è uno zombie che cammina lentamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the movie there is a zombie that walks slowly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Questa zona è molto tranquilla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This area is very quiet.

definitions.note: plural of "zona"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ci sono zone della città molto tranquille.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are areas of the city that are very quiet.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Andiamo allo zoo domenica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s go to the zoo on Sunday.

definitions.note: Gerund of "zoppicare"; describes an action in progress (often like “while limping”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È entrato in casa zoppicando.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He came into the house limping.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per Halloween compriamo una zucca grande.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For Halloween we buy a big pumpkin.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vuoi un po' di zucchero nel caffè?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you want a little sugar in your coffee?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Per cena preparo una zuppa calda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For dinner I’m making a hot soup.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary in compound tenses (passato prossimo) with certain verbs (often movement/state changes) and with reflexive verbs.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Marco è arrivato in ritardo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Marco has arrived late.

definitions.note: In standard Italian this form is written «è» (with a grave accent).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: È già tardi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It is already late.

definitions.note: Nonstandard spelling; in standard Italian this form is written “è”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oggi ê tardi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today it is late.
